## 2026-10-27 — A read-aloud refusal stops at once when the phone leaves the app, and the withheld sentence is finally drawn

**Decided:** three corrections to the 2026-10-27 typed read-aloud, all phone-side, no new route and no new control. **It fails closed on an unknown route:** the wiring asked `PrivateAloud.route(header) != null` for "do we know the route?", but `route()` answers `SILENT_ROUTE` for a missing or unreadable header and can never answer null - so `ReadAloud.Facts.mayRead`'s "unknown is never spoken" branch was dead code and an answer whose route facts were unknown could be read aloud. `routeOrNull(header)` is the null-able reader now; `route()` delegates to it and keeps its old meaning for the voice path. **It stops when the phone leaves the app:** `MainActivity` observes `ON_STOP` (the phone locking, HOME, another app) and stops the read at once, and the read loop re-asks the live lock before every sentence, because the "locked" fact was a snapshot taken when the answer arrived. **The withheld sentence is drawn:** the one fixed sentence "It's on your screen." appears where the Read aloud control would have been, and nothing beyond it, when a privacy rule withholds the read; a locked phone or a stale link draws nothing. That last clause corrects the earlier 2026-10-27 typed-read-aloud entry, which said a locked phone and a stale link keep their words on screen with that sentence - the shipped screen shows it only for privacy, and the other two cases are not what that sentence says.

**Why:** an audit of #892 found the gate's fail-closed branch dead and the promised refusal sentence unshowable, so the record said something the screen could not do. The Lead ruled on 2026-10-27 that leaving the app stops a read immediately rather than pausing it, and that a refusal is one sentence on screen rather than silence.

**Proven by:** `ReadAloudRouteFailClosedTest` (the wiring asks a reader that can say it does not know, and `routeOrNull`'s null path), `ReadAloudTest` (the one sentence, and nothing offered beside it) and `ReadAloudWiringTest` (the `ON_STOP` stop and the live lock re-read), all run off-device by the full `:app:testDebugUnitTest` suite. The phone drive is a field-test row, not a pass: when this entry was written, no APK built from the fix had been driven. **Corrected 2026-10-27, after the drive:** CI's APK of this PR's own head (`3eabe74c4`, run `40513029611`, `versionName 0.2.2906`, sha256 `64155E6640EC019A1D083DBC4B96BB3077317DF1499AE4134031A34AF292AA1A`) was driven on the owner's phone at 14:03-14:05Z, about 25 minutes before the squash merge of `67089d2` at 14:30:24Z - a field-drive record, not a CI pass. That APK is the PR head's build, not the merged tree: `main` gained #877 (`f4f5af130`) before the squash. The squash's own build was installed and driven too, and it is that later drive - not the PR-build one - that proves row 135: `jarvis-client-67089d2.apk` (v0.2.2908, sha256 `5542ff957084aca820527cc4bc11a46b9fc2b092b3d7f49eb7456603c050f5a1`, from main's `Jarvis client` run `40521754536`) with a HOME key while a sentence was playing paused and stopped the track 25 ms after the app's own window went invisible, 19,328 frames into a clip whose natural end needed 28,581. The earlier PR-build drive's teardown was the previous sentence's natural end, 130 ms before HOME was injected, so it is not cited for row 135. Matrix rows 133 and 136 are **DRIVEN** from the PR-build drive, row 135 from the later merged-build drive, all with their limits stated there; the withheld sentence (row 134) and the unknown-route fail-closed path stay **NOT-TESTABLE**.


## 2026-10-27 — A rotation does not stop a read: a configuration change is not leaving

**Decided:** The Lead ruled on 2026-10-27 that **rotation must not stop a read.** A configuration change is not leaving the app - the screen is still in front of the owner, showing the answer being read - and the old behaviour was an accident of `ON_STOP` also firing for a rotation, not a decision. The `ON_STOP` observer in `MainActivity` now skips a configuration change with the same test `onStop()` already uses for the lock session, and the stop stays in that observer rather than moving into `MainActivity.onStop()`, because an existing test pins `Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP` in `MainActivity.kt`.

**Why:** the read-aloud follow-up of 2026-10-27 found that turning the phone sideways cut a read off. "Away" now means the activity is gone or another app is in front, not that the layout changed.

**Proven by:** the follow-up PR #899 (merged as `aaad48540` at 17:07:20Z on 2026-10-27)'s `ReadAloudWiringTest` - `a rotation does not stop a read that is still on screen` pins the guard's **presence** at its own source line, not its polarity (measured: an inverted guard still passes the test), because a JVM unit test cannot simulate a configuration change; `a locked or backgrounded phone stops the read` keeps the other side pinned, also as a source pin. The whole phone unit suite is 2,706 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped. **Not proven:** the rotation behaviour on a real phone - the field-test matrix has no row for it and no phone was driven for it, so it is not a pass.


## 2026-10-27 — Major capabilities become model presets, and the two cards get one job each

**The owner's directive, in their own words:** *"for major things like therapist, or others, id likee them to be presets that choose the best local ai models to load for their purpose and these are added to the preset menu as a choice. do the same for the other strong integrated tools"*.

**What was built.** Four capability rows joined the five focus presets in `backend/jarvis_presets.py`, after them in the menu: **Reflective Coach** (`reflect`, talking a difficult thought through), **Pictures & Screens** (`pictures`, reading a screenshot or picture), **Documents & Notes** (`documents`, long reading, notes and study) and **Browser & Forms** (`browser`, long pages and multi-step form work). Fast's model changed from `qwen3:8b` to **`qwen3.5:4b`** on the RTX 2080 SUPER (the `coding` lane) at the **16,384**-token window that lane serves. The four capability rows all load **`qwen3.5:9b` on the RTX 2060 12 GB**: Reflective Coach, Documents & Notes and Browser & Forms at **196,608** tokens - the measured General setup, 44.9 tokens a second, 9.17 GB of video memory and no spill - and Pictures & Screens at **32,768**, whose window and speed are not separately measured (the model's vision capability is documented). They are choices in the one Presets menu both apps draw; no route, no screen and no store was added for any of them.

**Why the two cards get one job each.** The 196,608-token window fits only on the 12 GB 2060 (Qwen3.5's recurrent layers keep no KV cache), so every capability row that needs the long window runs there. The 8 GB 2080 SUPER is the display card, and Fast's small 4B model leaves it about 4 GB of video memory in use - measured 2026-10-10 on that same card: 77.1 tokens a second and 4.15 GB at a 65,536-token window, the file 3.16 GB on disk - which leaves headroom for Windows, DWM and WebView2. Coding's 30B model uses both cards only while it is applied.

**The honesty limits, said plainly.** The long-window capability rows share the measured General setup; **no model on this PC has been measured for reflective quality**, and this entry claims none. **Reflective Coach is a model choice only:** it is not a therapist, gives no diagnosis, keeps no therapy record, and carries no store, no route and no network - crisis help stays exactly where it already is. A matching tenth personality's wording is a separate owner decision and is **not** part of this change. Fast's 77.1 tokens a second is a measurement at a 65,536-token window while its lane serves 16,384, so it is evidence of the card's headroom rather than a promise at the served window.

**A preset the owner chooses is the mechanism.** There is no automatic per-feature model switching, and this change adds none: applying a preset is the only way a model changes, and an apply that needs a different model raises the existing ONE approval card (`switch_model`, the SAME card the model switch already used); if that model is already the one loaded, the switch reports nothing to change and the choice is saved without a card. Two things were deliberately left out because they need no preset: Live and Medical already pin their own models and lanes, and Reminders, the research/price radar and crisis help call no model at all.

## 2026-10-27 — The Reflective Coach is a tenth personality, and what it deliberately does not do

**What was decided.** The owner asked for "major things like therapist" to be presets that choose the right local model and appear in the Presets menu. The model half landed earlier the same day (the entry above); this entry records the wording half that entry deliberately left out: a tenth built-in personality, **Reflective Coach** (`reflect`).

**What the wording can and cannot do.** Its prompt block (348 characters; the assembled `<jarvis_persona>` block measures 635 typed / 722 spoken with its own dials and 729 with the longest word on every dial, against the 750-character cap) reflects first, asks one gentle question at a time, suggests a step only when asked, refuses diagnosis, prescription and medicine advice, refuses to call itself a therapist, refuses to promise secrecy, and says plainly that it keeps no therapy record. That is prompt-level only: no Python filter checks a diagnosis or a medicine directive, and nothing here is clinical judgement. The block has no phone number and no crisis script, because the crisis message is code-owned.

**What stays code-owned.** `jarvis_wellbeing.py`'s 988/911 reply, its `NOTE` to the model, and `jarvis_manner.prompt_block(crisis_active=True)` - which returns the calm crisis block *instead of* all persona text - are untouched. `backend/test_manner.py` proves, for each of the ten built-ins, that the crisis answer is the same calm block and that no persona carries "988", "911", "nine eight eight", "crisis", "suicide", "self-harm", "hotline" or "lifeline". There is still exactly one crisis message, in one place.

**Why a built-in and not "My Personalities".** The creator path is forbidden to write safety text: it stores a 240-character style line, and its own prompt says never to write about safety. A coach that may not say "I am not a therapist" is not the safe version.

**Out of scope, deliberately.** No thought-record store, no `therapy.db`, no diagnosis or medication regex, no risk scoring, no PHQ-9/GAD-7, no mood tracking, no session summary, no export to the medical record, no new route, no screen, no network, no model call, no approval card. This keeps the 2026-09-26 wellbeing review's exclusion of an "AI therapist", CBT course or questionnaire ("Not a clinician; several US states ban AI therapy; the APA (Nov 2025) calls chatbots' crisis help 'limited and unpredictable'"). A personality is words in the same chat the owner already had; it remembers nothing of its own.

**Both apps, by construction.** The personality is a row in the one `/api/manner` answer the HUD Presets menu, desktop Settings and the phone's chat path already read; the local desktop grid copy in `personalities.js` is the fallback for an older PC. No client release, no new route, no permission change.

**Proven by.** `backend/test_manner.py` (581 passed with a clean config folder), `python -B tools/check_personalities.py` (47 passed), `backend/test_personality_creator.py` (132 passed), `backend/test_wellbeing.py` (213 passed), and the generated copies rewritten by `tools/gen_personalities.py` and `tools/gen_plain_error_cases.py`, with `tools/check_stale_twins.py` and `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` (121 passed) holding the byte-identical twins. **Not proven:** any model's reflective quality (no such measurement exists), and the desktop settings page was not driven locally (the Playwright harness is not installed here; CI's `frontend` job is its first run).

## 2026-10-27 — The Galaxy's eight looks are drawn in 3D, and the Galaxy opens on the Planetary Orrery

**The owner's request, in their own words:** *"none of the galaxy on the current jarvis hud look like the one that gemini made… i would to simplify all the galaxy options… add an option to hide the galaxy under the Galaxy Options menu."* They chose **"Port Gemini's exact 3D look (Recommended)"** and chose **Planetary Orrery as the default look**. The hide-the-galaxy switch and the rest of the Galaxy Options menu are a **separate workstream**: this change is the visual engine, and it adds only the mount point that menu will move (the Look control that already existed, plus the chosen look's two own buttons beside it).

**What was built.** The HUD's Galaxy now draws through one three.js scene, the same shape the reference page has: the page is not eight engines, it is ONE 32-node scene with eight coordinate systems over it, and that is what was ported - its eight arrangements at its own radii and wave amplitudes, its palettes and its `FogExp2` density 0.0016, its ACES exposure 1.25, its camera position and look-at per look, its guide bodies (ecliptic rings; cortical plates with apical trunks, forked twigs and basal roots; four nebula wells inside a 3,200-point cloud; a 72-step double helix with base-pair rungs and a laser disk on the time axis; a radar floor with zone rings, crosshairs, a rotating sweep and a containment dome; tree baselines; one zen halo), its 1,800-star sky and its five animation branches. The look ids are **the repository's own eight** - the ones `galaxy-presets.js`, the Look control and the Brain window's chips already use (`planetary-orbit`, `neural-arbor`, `nebula`, `dna-helix`, `radar-dome`, `star-map`, `clean-tree`, `zen-ring`) - so the 3D engine and the flat fallback name the same picture, and no list exists twice. The module is `jarvis-desktop/src/galaxy-cosmos.js`, served from `backend/static/` and carried by the published base exactly like `galaxy-presets.js` was, with one `STATIC_ASSETS` key. three.js itself is copied into this repository by its own PR; **this** change adds the page's `<script src="/three.min.js" defer>` and the matching `STATIC_ASSETS` key together, which is the only state where the closed whitelist and the page agree in both directions. The engine loads it from this origin only - never a CDN - and stays on the flat picture when it is absent.

**Why the fallback is the flat picture of the same look.** A machine without WebGL, a page served without three.js, and an owner who asked for reduced motion must all still see a real picture, not a blank one. Because the two engines share one list of look ids, each of those cases draws the flat layout of the look that was chosen, and the counts line says which engine is drawing (`data-galaxy-engine`). The same idle rule the page already had stops the 3D loop the moment the Galaxy leaves the screen: `shouldRun()` gates every frame, so a hidden map draws nothing - which is the part of the coming "hide the galaxy" switch this engine had to honour in advance.

**The three fields `/api/graph` does not send were derived, not invented.** Gemini's Nebula keys on `cluster`, its DNA helix on `timestamp` and its Radar dome on `secRing`, and `/api/graph` sends none of them. The wells are the HUD's own saved groups (Facts, Knowledge, Projects, Sources); the helix's order is any real date found in a node's `meta`/`detail` text, falling back to id order and saying so; the radar's three rings are **kinds of thing** - Jarvis itself, what it can do, what it has saved - and are **not** a claim about safety or taint, which is what the reference page's rings mean. At most 240 names and 360 links are drawn, and a ring that cannot hold its names at a readable spacing grows outward instead of crowding, which is one of two deliberate deviations from the page's own numbers (the other is the frame, below) and only bites on a picture far larger than the 32 names it was drawn for.

**What this does not claim.** It is not pixel-identical to the Gemini page: the 16-glyph icon studio is not ported (labels stay the page's own label pass, with its budgets), stars and the nebula cloud come from a seeded generator so the sky is stable rather than different every load, and the guide-line opacities are the page's own numbers but the tone mapping does the rest. **Nothing here is measured on the owner's PC** - the frame rate of 240 names through WebView2, and how the glow looks on his monitor, are unknown until he looks; CI's browser run is the first time this draws in a browser at all beyond the desk. There is no Android counterpart and none is wanted: `/api/graph` stays off the phone, and the phone's read-only Galaxy picture (the 2026-10-26 decision) is a separate, deterministic drawing.

**Proven by:** `jarvis-desktop/tests/galaxy-cosmos.mjs` (35 pure checks: the eight ids against `BUILT_PRESETS`, every palette and camera against the reference page number by number, the derived fields, Gemini's geometry at Gemini's size, the guide bodies counted, the seeded sky, the budgets, the two controls per look, and the framing and fog checks described below) and `tests/hud-galaxy-looks.mjs`, which now drives the flat fallback deliberately through reduced motion, checks the owner's default look opens, and - when `three.min.js` is beside the page - drives all eight 3D looks, proves the node buttons ride the 3D camera through a drag, and proves the engine stops drawing when the Galaxy leaves the screen. The delivered page stayed byte-identical in its three copies, and `backend/test_hud_static.py`, `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py`, `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` and `tools/check_stale_twins.py` pass with the new served files in all four lists.


## 2026-10-27 — The Galaxy's frame is fitted to every real name, and the fog follows the camera

**Why this exists.** The owner approved the exact 3D port but named one defect it must fix: the reference page, and this HUD's old gallery picture, put names outside the frame. The verified capture of `2745274a9`'s constellation left four of forty real names stranded away from the cluster and unlabelled (`e:4`, `e:5`, `e:6`, `e:8`); Gemini's own page crops itself at 1440x900 - its nebula puts six of thirty-two names off-frame - and its labels are about 30 px tall under a banner that covers a third of the picture. "Port the look" was never "port that".

**The rule.** Every name's centre is kept inside `FRAME_FILL` = 82% of the half-frame: the outer 9% of the width and the height is the body's own radius, the 10-14 px label above it, and air. The camera is Gemini's own whenever the picture already fits that; otherwise it backs straight away from the same look-at along the same direction until the outermost real name is exactly on the line, so the angle never changes and only the distance does. The fit is per point and exact (depth `d - s`, offset `x_c`), not a bounding-sphere guess, so a flat ring and a tall helix are each framed for their own shape. The radius-only form (a caller with no positions) uses the conservative whole-sphere rule. `cameraFrame` is pure; `tests/galaxy-cosmos.mjs` proves the rule at 32, 120 and 240 names in all eight looks, at 1440x900 and on the HUD's real stage shapes, around the orrery's orbit, including room for the label above every name.

**Three consequences, all measured.**
- **The scroll wheel can no longer snap the camera into a big picture.** The zoom ceiling follows the framed distance (`max(620, frame * 2.5)`) instead of a fixed 620 units; with 240 names a fixed cap would jump thousands of units inward on the first notch.
- **The far plane follows the frame.** The page's 2,000 units is right for a 250-unit camera; at the 240-name budget the tree is framed at 2,587 and the helix at 1,653, and a fixed far plane put the whole tree behind the far plane - no bodies, no buttons - until `camera.far` grew with the frame. This was measured in the browser probe, not guessed.
- **The two looks that used to turn the whole scene now turn the camera around its target.** The nebula and the helix rotated `scene.rotation.y` every frame, which turned the bodies but not the page's projection - so the labels and buttons drifted off their names - and it also rotated names out of the fitted frame (measured: 1.006 of the half-frame at 135 degrees, i.e. just off screen). For an unlit scene, moving the camera around the target is the same picture, and the labels, the buttons and the frame all follow it. The page's own `project()` now also reads each body's WORLD position, so a future scene rotation cannot reintroduce the drift.

**The fog is the page's density, scaled only when the frame pulls back.** Gemini's `FogExp2` density 0.0016 suits a camera about 250 units out; at 2,587 units it keeps about 0.0015% of the light, which is a black picture. The density becomes `0.0016 * min(1, 250 / frameDistance)`, so every picture Gemini's own camera frames keeps his exact density, and every pulled-back picture keeps the same depth cue: about 85% of the far edge survives at any size (proved in the same test file).

**Proven by:** the same `galaxy-cosmos.mjs` (35 checks, 3 of them the framing rule and the fog), and a headless-Chromium probe on the real page at 1440x900 which found every one of 240 name buttons inside the stage in all eight looks (worst margin 70 px on a 960x773 stage) and every one of the 120-name inline budget likewise. **What this does not claim:** at 240 names the tree and the helix are wide layouts, so their bodies are small (their labels stay the page's 10-14 px); every name is inside the frame and remains a real button, but 240 names on one stage is dense, and how it reads on the owner's monitor is still unmeasured. The Brain window's separate SVG constellation (the surface the four stranded names were captured on) is not this page and is unchanged by this port.

## 2026-10-27 — Pinned chats, and the owner's tags presented as projects in the HUD's History panel

**The owner's ask, in their own words:** *"Id like a history tab with a column icon that opens up a menu that looks like all the coversations in the deepseek harness on desktop for the jarvis HUD, like the screenshot. ... both should have pinnable chats, project organization by chat, and more"*.

**Decided: a pin is ONE flag on a conversation, not a list in either app.** The pin is a `pinned` column in the same encrypted `chat-history.db` that holds every other History fact, changed by a new metadata route `POST /api/history/pin {"id": "<conversation id>", "pinned": true|false}` and read back as `pinned` on every list, open and search row. Neither the desktop nor the phone keeps a pin list of its own, so a chat pinned on one is pinned on the other, and a restart changes nothing. The route raises **no approval card** and loosens nothing: pinning is the owner's own tidying, the same class of change as filing a chat under a tag (§99), and it stores no text - the only text in that table, the title, stays sealed exactly as it was. Its refusals are exact (a body that is not exactly `{"id", "pinned"}`, a `pinned` that is not a JSON boolean, an id that is not a string / is empty / is longer than 128 characters = `400`; a chat that is gone = `404`, with nothing written and so no ghost row; the history cannot be opened = `503`), and pinning twice is pinning once. Contract: `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §18.3. The phone's client half is a separate lane and is not in this change.

**Decided (the Gemini ruling of the same day): a pin carries its MOMENT, and the Pinned group is ordered by it.** A second column, `pinned_at` (epoch seconds, or null), is what the route answers with and what every list, open and search row carries beside `pinned`; the Pinned group is drawn **`pinned_at DESC, updated_at DESC`**. Two consequences are deliberate: a chat that receives a message never jumps above one that was pinned after it (the pin is the order, not the chat's time), and pinning an already-pinned chat keeps its FIRST `pinned_at` - pinning twice is pinning once, all the way down. Neither app derives that order from its own state; both read the two fields the PC sends.

**Decided (the same ruling): while the private view is hidden, this route cannot be used to look for a chat.** With App lock or "Hide memory lists and chat history" on, `GET /api/history` withholds EVERY row - the pinned ones included, because a pin is still a title - and keeps only the switch, the counts and `{"hidden": true, "hidden_count": n}`; and `POST /api/history/pin` answers **`423` for every id**, before it looks at one. A `200` ("pinned it") against a `404` ("no such chat") would be an oracle telling a caller whether a chat exists on a locked PC, which is the thing App lock is for. The server's own list route applies that withholding through `jarvis_private_view` (the Q1 hook of 2026-10-20; the hook is absent = unlocked), so the browser HUD, the phone and the desktop get ONE answer, and the desktop keeps its own belt-and-braces redaction on top.

**Decided: the existing chat tags ARE the "projects".** The owner asked for "project organization by chat"; Jarvis already has chat tags (`docs/CHAT-TAGS-DESIGN.md`, both apps), so the panel groups by them - one collapsible section per tag, in the tag registry's order, with its icon, name and count - and adds **no second concept and no second store**. Chats with no tag are shown under **"Untagged"**, the word both apps already use, rather than being hidden. A chat whose tag was deleted elsewhere is shown there too, not lost.

**Decided: the HUD may pin, file and delete ONE chat itself, and nothing more.** The panel's row menu offers Open, Pin/Unpin, Move to project (one of the owner's existing tags, or none) and Delete, through ONE new Rust command `hud_history_act` that carries only an action, one chat id and that action's own value. It is refused while the private lists are hidden (a title is the owner's words) and held on a stale link (rule 4), exactly like the Brain's own tag and mark commands, and it raises no card. There is no delete-all, no clear-list and no route this command can be talked into sending; creating a new tag stays the phone's and the Brain's for now. Deleting from the HUD deletes the chat only - forgetting the facts it taught stays the Brain's own flow.

**Decided: the row words and the three request shapes are ONE module both windows import.** The ruling was to share the row-action helpers between `jarvis_hud.html` and `brain.js` like the Reminders `hud-actions.js`, so pin/file/delete cannot drift. `jarvis-desktop/src/history-actions.js` is that module: the action labels (including "Delete", which the Brain's own History row now reads from it), the three sentences of the delete confirmation, and the args/body a write sends. `history-view.js` re-exports the sentence it used to own, so the Brain keeps reading the same words from the same place, and a stand-alone second copy of either sentence is what the ruling forbids. On the PC side `hud_act_body` shares `tag_chat_body` and `delete_body` with the Brain's own commands, so the BODIES cannot drift either - a Rust test compares both surfaces' output for the same chat. The HUD's module is loaded with `<script type="module">` (still ONE external file: the page's inline count and every CSP hash are unchanged) because a classic script cannot import a shared module.

**Decided (the same ruling): the sidebar's keyboard and screen-reader behaviour is part of the contract.** A row is a `<div role="listitem">` holding TWO SIBLING buttons - the chat and its `...` - never a button inside a button; the age is a real `<time datetime title>`, and a clock ahead of the PC is clamped so no row can say "in 3 minutes"; a group header is a `<button aria-expanded>` and toggling one keeps the keyboard on that header; Escape closes the row menu and puts focus back on the `...`, a second Escape closes the sidebar and puts it back on the left column's History icon; "Show N more" moves focus to the first chat it revealed; and the page's global Space push-to-talk bails for `#history-sidebar, input, textarea, button, [role="menu"]` and for an open sidebar, so Space inside the panel is the panel's.

**Decided: the HUD's reads join its fixed allow-list, with the query checked in ONE place.** The HUD page holds no pairing token (apps security audit M2), so its reads go through `hud_proxy::hud_get`, which allows exact paths. Three History reads were added - `/api/history`, `/api/history/conversation?id=`, `/api/history/tags` - and their query is parsed and rebuilt by `brain/history.rs::history_read_path` (each parameter at most once, values in the PC's own shapes, `before` kept as the digits written so no `f64` can print an exponent). While App lock or "Hide memory lists" is on, the same redaction the Brain's History tab uses applies: the list keeps its counts and loses its conversations, a tag keeps its id and count and loses its name, and an opened chat is refused whole. A test pins that the page cannot make a History read of any other shape.

**Why this is the fourth lane, and what it will meet.** It changes `jarvis_hud.html` (the left rail), `lib.rs`, `build.rs`, `capabilities/hud.json`, `permissions/surfaces.toml` and `package.json`'s `test:ui` list - the same files the HUD bug fixes (lane 1), the Galaxy options menu (#909) and the 3D Galaxy port (#910, after #907) touch. It is based on `main` at `2745274a9` deliberately so one rebase covers it: the sidebar is one new module pair plus a small hook in the page, and nothing in it depends on those lanes.

**The limits, recorded here rather than discovered later:** the panel's search matches a chat's NAME only (searching what was said is the Brain's, §71); a fork of a pinned chat keeps the pin and its `pinned_at`, like its tag and project; a support/chatbot/comparison record opens read-only and the next message starts a new chat rather than being filed into that record; nothing in this change is deployed to the owner's PC yet (a rebuild, `apply-patches.ps1` and the HUD whitelist deploy are needed), and the panel has not been driven in WebView2 - its pure logic and the page/Rust wiring are tested in Node and Rust, not in a running window.

## 2026-10-27 — A home-screen widget ends in words, never a spinner; and the release-build hole behind it

**The owner's bug, in their words:** every Jarvis widget sat **"buffering indefinitely"** on their Pixel and on the OnePlus CPH2419, while the phone app itself was connected and drawing live PC data.

**What was actually wrong - and it was not the widget code, and not the network.** The spinner was the launcher's `initialLayout`: Glance's own `glance_default_loading_layout`, whose whole content is a bare ProgressBar. It stayed there because **no Glance update ever ran in a release build.** Glance composes a widget inside a WorkManager `SessionWorker`; WorkManager builds its default `InputMerger` by loading `androidx.work.OverwritingInputMerger` **by name** and calling `Class.newInstance()` on it; R8 had removed that class's no-arg constructor, because nothing in any static call graph calls it. `androidx.work`'s own consumer rule - `-keep class * extends androidx.work.InputMerger`, read out of `work-runtime-2.7.1.aar`'s `proguard.txt` in this PC's Gradle cache - keeps the class and its name, and not its constructors. So every worker failed with `Could not create Input Merger`, `provideGlance` never ran, and every widget kept the launcher's ProgressBar for ever. The app was unaffected because the app never uses WorkManager directly. This is the **same reflective hole as the `androidx.room.RoomDatabase` keep rule already in `proguard-rules.pro`, one call further along**: that rule stopped the release build crashing at launch, and this one lets the widget jobs run at all.

**Decided:** (1) `proguard-rules.pro` keeps constructors on every `androidx.work.InputMerger` subclass. (2) A widget must always end in a state that says something - real content, an explicit empty state, or an explicit error - so `WidgetStates` has **no loading state at all**, and every draw of all five widgets goes through it. (3) Every wait a widget makes is bounded - 4 s to start the runtime, 8 s for the PC's widget answer - and running out is an error sentence, not an open-ended wait. (4) The layout shown before the first update is `res/layout/widget_initial.xml` ("No update yet - open Jarvis to connect") for all five widgets, as `initialLayout` **and** `previewLayout`, because a spinner is a promise that something is coming and that promise was exactly what broke. (5) App lock's "hide the card's own words" rule moved out of the composable into `ApprovalWidgetRules.cardTitle`/`cardDetail`, so it is checked on the JVM instead of by reading the drawing code.

**Deliberately not done.** No new dependency: WorkManager was already there, transitively, and is now usable. No second poller: the app's existing `EventService` fills `pending`, and `JarvisRuntime`'s `widgetJob`/`boardJob` already redraw every widget on every link, queue, stale and App-lock change, so a background refresh would duplicate them. Nothing starts `EventService` from a widget draw - a background foreground-service start is restricted, and a home-screen tap is not consent to begin listening. No backend route, and no change to the widget data contract with the PC.

**Proven by:** the connected OnePlus CPH2419 on 2026-10-27. `adb shell am broadcast -a androidx.glance.appwidget.action.DEBUG_UPDATE -n com.jarvis.client/.widget.ApprovalWidgetReceiver` made the app's own process log `Trouble instantiating + androidx.work.OverwritingInputMerger`, `java.lang.InstantiationException: java.lang.Class<...> has no zero argument constructor` and `Could not create Input Merger`, thirty milliseconds after the broadcast - the widget update path, failing. The installed APK's own `classes.dex` (pulled from the phone) has `Landroidx/work/OverwritingInputMerger;` with **no `<init>` at all**, while `androidx.glance.session.SessionWorker`'s public `(Context, WorkerParameters)` constructor is present. `WidgetStatesTest` proves the terminal-state machine, the bounds and the App-lock rule (14 tests), and the whole `:app:testDebugUnitTest` suite runs locally on the Android toolchain: **2,720 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped**. A local `:app:assembleRelease` (the same R8 configuration CI uses) builds, and the new APK's `classes.dex` was dumped again: `OverwritingInputMerger` now has a `PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR <init>()V`, and its resource table has `initialLayout` and `previewLayout` both at `layout/widget_initial` - a LinearLayout with two TextViews and no ProgressBar.

**Not proven:** the widgets on a phone. No APK built from this branch has been installed - a locally built release APK can only be installed over the owner's CI build if its version code and key match, and getting it wrong costs the pairing token - so the field-test step is CI's APK, add all five widgets, and expect terminal states.

## 2026-10-27 — Settings loses its "Everyday" and "Rare" bands, its search ranks by the words that matched, and the tray's update row lands on the update card

**The owner, in their own words:** *"when i right click the jarvis tray icon, click on update available, it only opens the settings page"* and *"when i search update in the settings page on the jarvis desktop, updates is not the first thing that comes up, its considered rare in the settings, get rid of the general clasification of everyday settings with things like everyday or rare in settings, search bar should search for matching terms"*.

**Decided, the destination.** The tray's "Update available — v…" row opens Settings AT the Updates card, not at the top of Settings and not on a second updater surface. `windows.rs` gained the Settings twin of the Brain's place mechanism: `SETTINGS_PLACES` (one place, `"updates"`), `SETTINGS_PLACE_EVENT` (`"settings-place"`) and `show_settings_at`, which stores the place and then calls `show_settings`, so App lock is asked exactly as before. An open window is told by event and is never reloaded, so nothing typed in it is lost; a new window is built at `settings.html#updates`; either way the card is scrolled to and its first control focused. The tray row still never checks, downloads or installs - the install button on the card is still the owner's press.

**Decided, the classification.** The Everyday and Rare bands are removed from `settings.html` and from its jump list. Every card, section id, anchor and jump link stays; the jump list is one unlabelled group of every editable card, then the one labelled read-only group. The one heading left, "What Jarvis does", is a fact about those cards (they report, they change nothing) rather than a guess about how often they are needed. `tests/first-run-settings.mjs` and `tests/spending.mjs` were re-pointed at that shape rather than deleted: they still hold their cards and links, just not to a frequency band.

**Decided, the search.** Search orders what it finds by where the words matched: the card's own title or a name the menus catalogue already answers to for it (exact, then prefix, then a typo), then its labelled rows, then its detail text; ties go to the shorter title, then the title itself. Nothing reads the section, the old band or the page's document order, and the remaining group heading is put away while a search is on so the results are one ranked list. "update" was added to the Updates card's names in `jarvis_menus.py` (and the published base, and the generated catalogue both apps read), so "open update" names it as well as typing it in the box.

**Why.** The band had become a claim about the owner's life rather than a description of a card, and it was wrong about the one card the report was about: Updates sat under "Rare", and searching "update" drew it FIFTH - behind four cards that merely mention updating - because results kept page order, which is document-order weighting wearing no label. "Search bar should search for matching terms" only means something if the card named "Updates" comes first for "update". A destination also has to be a place the page really has, which is why the tray's row names the card's own id rather than a second updater window.

**Proven by:** `windows.rs`'s `only_a_named_place_is_a_place_in_settings` and `the_settings_place_event_is_one_name_in_both_languages` (that last one reads `settings-place.js`, so the Rust event name and the page's are held together from both sides; the `settings.html#updates` literal itself is read by `tools/check_invoke_grants.py`, which refuses to judge a window whose page it cannot name - a helper hiding that literal failed the audit, caught and fixed on this branch); `tray.rs`'s `the_update_row_opens_the_updates_card_and_settings_stays_plain`; `backend/test_settings_registry.py` rewritten for the new shape and run in full (732 checks, 0 failed) with `JARVIS_BACKEND` unset so it checks this repository's copy; the browser-free `jarvis-desktop/tests/settings-place.mjs`; the extended `tests/settings-search.mjs` (including "searching 'update' lists Updates first", the alias check, the tie-break check and a browser-free check of the exported `cardRank`/`compareMatches`); and two new checks in `tests/updates.mjs`, one opening `settings.html#updates` (the fragment door) and one emitting `settings-place` at an open page (the event door), both asserting the card is scrolled to, focus is inside it, and a place the page does not have is ignored. Gates at the desk: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check/clippy --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `cargo test --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` with `JARVIS_SKIP_WINDOW_TESTS=1`, `tools/gen_menu_cases.py --check`, the three base/twin checks, and every settings-related desktop suite. **Not proven:** what the owner sees in a packaged build - the scroll and focus checks are local headless-Chromium interaction evidence, not a drive of an installed app, and no screenshot is claimed as a pass. The tray row itself was not clicked on the owner's PC; the dispatch is pinned in Rust tests and in the browser test's source read.

## 2026-10-27 — A release build is checked for the classes R8 is asked for by name

**Decided:** the release APK gets a dex assertion in CI. `tools/check_apk_reflective_keeps.py`, run by the `Jarvis client` workflow's existing `build` job immediately after `assembleRelease`, so it covers every pull request that touches the client and not only `main` — no new job and no new required check. It reads the APK's own `classes*.dex` in plain Python (no SDK, no device, no `dexdump`) and fails when a class this app creates **by name** has lost the constructor reflection calls: `androidx.work.OverwritingInputMerger` and `androidx.work.ArrayCreatingInputMerger` (WorkManager stores the class name in a work request and runs `Class.forName(...).newInstance()`), `androidx.glance.session.SessionWorker` (WorkManager's `WorkerFactory` rebuilds a Worker from the name in the request) and `androidx.work.impl.WorkDatabase_Impl` (Room looks its generated database up by name; the keep rule at `proguard-rules.pro:76` fixed the earlier launch crash). A family sweep also fails any concrete `*InputMerger` or `*Database_Impl` the dex carries without a no-arg constructor, so a subclass nobody has listed is caught too. The failure names the class and says "reflective instantiation hole - see proguard-rules.pro". It deliberately does **not** fall back to the debug APK: R8 does not run there, so a pass against it would prove nothing.

**Why:** on 2026-10-27 the release build stripped `OverwritingInputMerger`'s no-arg constructor. WorkManager builds its InputMerger reflectively, so **every** home-screen widget update died with "Could not create Input Merger" and all five widgets sat on the launcher spinner for ever - while every unit test and the debug build were green. PR #908 added the keep rule. The identical thing had already happened to Room's `WorkDatabase_Impl`, which crashed the app at launch; that one was fixed by hand and nothing stopped the next. A missing keep rule cannot fail the Gradle build, so the only thing that can catch it is looking at the artifact that ships.

**Proven by local builds, both directions.** A release APK of this tree with PR #908's InputMerger keep applied passes in 0.82 s (6,824 classes parsed, all four targets and both sweeps OK). The same tree **without** that keep fails in 0.63 s (6,815 classes): `FAIL: reflective instantiation hole - androidx.work.OverwritingInputMerger`, `its constructor <init>()V is missing (the class itself is there)`, and the same for `ArrayCreatingInputMerger`; `dexdump` on that `classes.dex` independently shows the class with no `<init>` at all. A third build, with the keep applied but the Room keep rule removed, fails naming `androidx.work.impl.WorkDatabase_Impl` (6,581 classes), and `dexdump` again agrees - so the prior instance is guarded, not just the one that bit. `--self-test` proves the judgement and the wording with fabricated inventories, including an unlisted concrete `*InputMerger` that must be reported and an abstract one that must not. CI cost: under a second on the release APK the job already builds.

**Not proven, and not claimed:** the table knows only the reflective entry points listed in it, plus the two family sweeps - a future reflective hole in a class nobody has listed will still ship, and adding one is a one-line entry with a comment. The check reads the dex R8 produced, so it asserts the result; it cannot tell whether the keep rules themselves are the right ones. And a build signed with a throwaway key still passes it: signing stays the separate step above it.

## 2026-10-27 — A phone answer's Right/Wrong moves behind a chevron, pins are kept on the phone, and the chat says where its other chats are

**The owner's request, in their own words:** *"also, i dont want a 'was this
answer right' on every response from jarvis. put a carrot that opens a menu on
each chat that has this, along with a pin message button that pins the message
and remembers it and can be found easily in a new menu. also where can i find
old jarvis chats? and how do i open new ones?"*

**Decided: the always-visible mark block goes, and a per-message menu carries
it instead.** The persistent "Was this right?" row under every finished answer
on Home is removed. Each Jarvis answer - the one on screen AND each answer
folded into the thread above it - now carries a drawn chevron at the end of
its own "Jarvis" line; that chevron opens a small dialog that is about that
ONE message and holds exactly two things: the same Right / Wrong pair (`feedback.patch`,
unchanged - one mark per answer, the chosen one tapped again takes it back, a
mark never changes memory, and the desktop's own unavailable, busy and
not-connected sentences are kept word for word) and **Pin message / Unpin
message**. A folded answer has no `turn_id` in the thread (the thread keeps words),
so its menu carries the pin and no marks: the chevron is never a dead control.
The mark still goes out over the same `/api/feedback/mark` route; no route, request or server
behaviour changed.

**Decided: a pin is the phone's own bookmark, not the PC's.** The pinned
words, the chat they came from (the conversation id and the owner's question,
which is what makes "which chat" readable) and when it was pinned are kept on
THIS PHONE in a private `SharedPreferences` file (`data/ChatPins.kt` holds the pure rules, `data/PinnedChatStore.kt` is the thin
store) - no new backend route, nothing sent to the PC, and the desktop's kept
chat history is untouched. A new **Pinned messages** screen, opened from the
chat's More menu, lists them newest first, each row with Unpin and Open chat;
Open chat opens History at that one conversation rather than copying History.
The list hides under "Hide memory lists and chat history" through the same `HiddenSection`
every other memory list uses, survives a restart, holds at most 100 pins, and
**refuses rather than dropping an older pin** - the menu says the cap in words
instead of silently forgetting something the owner saved. A temporary chat
(and a game the PC made temporary) may not be pinned at all, because the PC
keeps nothing of it and the phone must not keep a copy either.

**Decided: the old chats and a new chat are named where the owner looks.** The
shared More menu now leads with **New chat**, a labelled **Earlier chats**
(the row that already existed, until now with nothing under it saying where it
goes) and **Pinned messages**; "New chat" is the idle timer's own reset (`ChatSession.newConversationSaid`)
and not a second mechanism, and it is the same word the row under a finished
answer now uses. An empty chat says once, above the box, that the old chats
are in More and that a new chat is there too - he asked both questions on the
same day, so the answer is written where he was already looking. History stays
one screen: nothing is duplicated.

**Why.** The owner had said three times over that the feedback pair was noise
on every answer, and could not find History from the chat even though the row
had been in the More menu since 2026-10-25 - a row with no line under it, in a
menu he had never opened, is not a door. Pins are deliberately phone-local
because the alternative (a new route plus a PC-side store) would have been a
backend change to serve a bookmark, against the project's rule that a client
adds no route it does not need; keeping them local also means the same "hide
the memory lists" switch governs them, with no second privacy model to keep in
step.

**Proven by:** `data/ChatPinsTest` (JVM: one pin per message however it was reached, newest
first, the cap refusing instead of dropping, the cut at 2000 characters, a
corrupt file costing only the rows it damaged, ages that never read backwards,
and the words a temporary chat is refused with) and `ChatMenuTest` (source pins: the old
block is gone from `Reply`, the menu holds the marks and the pin, every answer row
has the named chevron, the pin store has no route and says it is kept on the
phone, the list is behind `HiddenSection`, History is opened at one chat and not copied,
the chat rows are in the More menu in order, and the chevron is named and
48dp). The existing `LearningTest` (`Feedback.viewFor`, `nextMark`, the mark body) and `ChatMarkTest` are unchanged and
still pass, because the mark's own rules did not move. **Proven at the desk,
2026-10-27:** the whole `:app:testDebugUnitTest` suite was run on this PC against this branch (JDK
17, the cached Gradle 9.6.0 and Android SDK 36, `--offline`), so - unlike most phone
changes in this project - this one is compiled and tested before CI rather
than by CI. **Not proven, and not claimed:** the menu, the chevron and the new
screen have not been driven on a phone - no field-test row was added and none
is claimed as a pass; and pins are not shown on the desktop HUD, which has no
feedback control either - the one-sided-on-purpose reason is written down in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8, beside the HUD chat box's existing limits (no History, no
Incognito, no New conversation).
## 2026-10-28 — "Hide memory lists and chat history" blocks desktop captures on its own, and the pairing token stays as it is

**The owner's decision, in their own words (answering question P-2 of the 2026-10-27 privacy audit):** *"hide-lists alone must block desktop captures"*, and on the shared pairing token, *"Legacy shared token stays as-is (do not change it)."*

**What was decided.** On the PC, "Windows Hello for memory lists and chat history" is now a capture block in its own right, with App lock off and with the owner sitting at the machine. Before this, it could never block anything: `capture_blocked_from` asked "is the owner here" first, and that answer is always "yes" while App lock is off (because `app_locked` returns false whenever `security.app_lock` is false), so the hidden-lists reason and the settings' own reason were both unreachable behind it. The hidden state is now checked above that return, in the same place the pairing code's reason already was - a code and a hidden list are the two things whose whole promise is that their words are not on another screen.

**The cost, said plainly, because it was chosen with the cost in view.** While that setting is on, `private_hidden` is true unless a Show was passed by Windows Hello and a covered window still has focus. So desktop captures are blocked nearly all of the time for an owner who has the setting on - including a screenshot they take themselves while sitting at the PC. That is what the phone already does (its rule is `s.appLock || s.privateLists`, with no "the owner is here" exception) and what `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 has claimed about the desktop since 2026-10-11. The alternative - leaving the rule as it was and correcting the document - was offered as the second option and declined.

**What did NOT change, on purpose.** The pairing token is still ONE shared secret for every device, minted and stored exactly as it was; nothing about its lifetime, storage, logging or the pairing flow was touched, and no second token was introduced. The audit's sibling report on secrets (`.dsh-scratch/AUDITS-2026-10-27/partner-secrets.md`) is where that question lives, and this decision leaves it where the owner put it.

**The rest of the same audit's fixes, recorded here only as what they were.** P-1 (the High one): the HUD's memory graph outlived the hide, so `private-hidden` is now broadcast to every window and the HUD page forgets every word it holds before re-reading `/api/graph` redacted - see the changelog fragment for 2026-10-28. P-3: the phone's one-time backup recovery code raises `FLAG_SECURE` while it is drawn. P-5: the two toasts that carried the PC's own words go through `notify_guarded`. P-6: the two documents that contradicted the code are corrected. P-7: Live's and Resume's notifications are redacted by the shared `notificationsLocked` rule. **P-4 was not a bug:** the report's mechanism does not exist - in Tauri 2 a page's global `listen()` registers with the target `Any`, and `match_any_or_filter` lets an `Any` listener through every filter, so the widget's listener already fired before this change (`tauri-2.12.5/src/event/listener.rs:346`); the report's claim that the event never reached it is wrong, and the broadcast keeps the property by construction rather than by subtlety.

**Proven by.** `cargo test --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (1,030 passed; the three `%TEMP%` failures this PC always has, documented in `CLAUDE.md`), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets` and `cargo clippy -D warnings`; the phone's whole JVM suite, `jarvis-client/gradlew.bat --offline :app:testDebugUnitTest`: 2,709 tests in 251 classes, 0 failures, including the three new ones this change added; `node tests/csp-inline.mjs`, `node tests/hud-safety.mjs` and `python -B backend/test_hud_static.py` (42 passed); and `node tests/hud.mjs`: **147 checks, 0 failed**, including the new P-1 page test. That last one needed the node `playwright` package, which is not a dependency of this package - it was installed with `npm i --no-save` and driven the Chromium already on this PC through the harness's own `JARVIS_TEST_CHROME` override, so the page, the CSP and the inline script exercised are the real ones. Two runs of that suite were needed: the check's first two versions failed on their own fixtures (a browser-side name used in a Node assertion, then the inspector asserted open after `setTrace` had closed it by design), and both fixes are their own commits on the branch. **Not proven here:** the desktop app itself was not run, so no window probe beyond the suite's own, and nothing on the phone was driven on hardware - the JVM suite is predicate proof, not device proof. **Shown, not only asserted:** the hidden state was rendered in the real page and read back (`p1-before.png` / `p1-after.png`, in this branch's scratch folder under `.dsh-scratch/AUDITFIX-PRIVACY-2026-10-28/`) - before it, four node buttons with `Owner's sister is called Priya (Facts)` and `Priya (Knowledge)`, the inspector open on the sentence and `Priya` in the search box; after it, two buttons, the inspector back to `-`, an empty search box, the counts line saying the lists are hidden, and the readouts still 41 / 3 / 12.
## 2026-10-28 — A backup never claims data it cannot restore, and a damaged settings file fails closed

**What was decided (the data-integrity audit's F1-F5, implemented).** Five rules now hold, and each is a behaviour change rather than a comment:

1. **A backup carries the chat-history key only when that key PROVES itself** against the `meta` `check` row of the database riding beside it (F1). The provider is split: `jarvis_chat_log.get_existing_key()` reads the Credential Manager entry and never makes one, `get_or_create_key(db_path)` makes one ONLY for a brand-new, empty `chat-history.db` (and refuses in plain words over a history that already holds anything), and `verify_key_opens_db(db_path, key_bytes)` is the AES-GCM check-row proof. `counts.chat_history_key` now means "a key that opens the archived history is inside". When the history holds rows and the key is missing or does not verify, the database is **left out** of the archive rather than carried unreadable: `counts.excluded_dbs` names it as `"chat-history.db (encryption key missing or mismatched in Windows Credential Manager)"`, and the result sentence reads **"Backed up N databases, except chat-history.db (...), left out to prevent an unreadable backup."** A restore refuses to write a chat-history key into Credential Manager unless that key opens the chat history **now on this PC**, and it refuses to overwrite the live `chat-history.db` at all when neither the archive's key nor this PC's current key opens the staged database - the live file and the live key stay exactly as they were, `applied.chat_history_refused` is set, and the receipt NAMES the database. The restore card says it too when the archive has no chat history in it. The SAME read-only rule now covers the review decks' and medical store's keys (`_study_decks_key_b64`, `_medical_key_b64`): both used to call a provider that mints, so a missing key put a fresh one into the archive beside a `study.db`/`health.db` sealed with the old one - an unopenable database reported as a complete backup. No readable key now means no file, which is what `test_backup.py` already expected. **The two other sealed stores get the same rule**: `study.db` and `health.db` are left out when their own key cannot be read, and since 2026-10-28 they are **named** in `counts.excluded_dbs` as `"study.db (encryption key missing or unreadable in Windows Credential Manager)"` / `"health.db (...)"` - the old `continue` dropped them silently, so an archive could lack the owner's decks or his medical record and still read as complete. An empty store of either kind is left out without a line, because nothing in it can be lost.
2. **A database whose snapshot failed is named, never silently dropped** (F4): the same `excluded_dbs` list, with `"memory.db (could not be read)"`, and the same "Backed up N databases, except ..., left out to prevent an unreadable backup" sentence instead of a bare "Backed up." The same field drives the desktop panel's preview sentence, so the panel and the backend cannot disagree.
3. **A damaged `manner.json` refuses every write** (F3). Absent and unreadable are now different answers on the write path: absent is a fresh folder and is fine; unreadable keeps the damaged bytes as `manner.json.corrupt-<stamp>`, changes nothing, and answers in plain words telling the owner to fix or delete it. Every successful write keeps the previous valid file as `manner.json.bak`. The #881 merge shape is untouched - a partial patch still keeps every key it does not name - and switching a personality still applies that preset's dials, as it always did.
4. **Every way a chat is deleted scrubs receipts** (F2): a retention sweep, and a "Forget a time frame" whose ten-minute Undo expired, now purge the deleted conversations' words out of `receipts.db` exactly as a hand delete does - the expiry purge runs then, not at take-out time, because a scrub cannot be undone and those ten minutes are a real Undo. The 200-turn cap is gone, so a long chat's later words are purged too; `jarvis_receipts.purge_many` does a whole list in one pass per 200 words, so a big sweep does not re-read the table once per word.
5. **Changing the retention window sweeps BEFORE it saves** (F5). A sweep that fails saves nothing and answers 500 saying the deletion failed and the window was not saved; a save that fails after a successful sweep answers 500 with the number already deleted. Neither is ever answered with "could not save the setting" about a window that really changed.

**Why:** each of the five was a claim the code could not keep. A `.jbak` that says it carries your chats and cannot open them is worse than one that says it does not; a backup that drops `memory.db` without a word is the one archive you would reach for when `memory.db` is already damaged; a single silent write after a truncated `manner.json` wiped every saved personality; a delete that leaves the words in another store is not a delete; and "could not save the setting" over a window that had already saved and deleted hid a half-applied change.

**Proven by:** `backend/test_backup.py` (**553 passed**, including the new key-works / key-wrong / key-missing cases, the named `study.db`/`health.db` exclusions, the left-out-database message, the mint guard on the provider, the restore-over-live refusal and its mixed case, and the restore receipt that names a refused `chat-history.db`), and the nine-suite run that covers the rest - `backend/run_suites.py test_chat_log.py test_manner.py test_receipts.py test_forget_range.py test_api_doc.py test_data_backup.py test_shipped_modules.py test_records_encoding.py test_roll_changelog.py test_no_scratch_in_the_tree.py` - **2,256 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (the skip is that runner's own visible-browser opt-out, not a pass; `test_data_backup.py` was re-run after the last change: 152 passed, 1 skipped). Twins and records: `python -B tools/check_stale_twins.py` (all files match), `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` (123 passed) and `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` (39 passed), `tools/roll_changelog.py --check` (9 fragments OK), `git diff --check` clean. **Not proven:** the panel's preview sentence was not driven here - the Playwright harness is not installed on this PC, so CI's `frontend` job is its first run; no live backend was deployed or restarted for this change, so every suite ran against the hermetic staged copy `backend/run_suites.py` builds; and the audit's **F6 stays open** - the ten-minute Undo still lives in the backend's memory, so a restart inside the window drops the held chats and the receipts scrub for them never runs (the chats are gone either way; only their words in old receipts could remain). The receipts scrub is best-effort by design, as it has been since 2026-10-18: a store that cannot be reached is not allowed to fail a delete. The three `git` copies of the F1-era tests that this branch replaced are gone, not disabled: no `skip` or `ignored` covers any of them.
## 2026-10-28 — Deny on the home-screen widget denies; only a card that says deny needs the app opens the app

**The owner's rule, in their own words:** *"tapping deny on the widget should deny it, except in cases of needing extra approval like a finger print or a confirm deny or approve for extra important decisions."*

**What went wrong, from the field.** On CI APK **v0.2.2979** (main after #908), with the phone in App lock / private view, the approvals widget showed "Needs your OK / A decision is waiting" with **Deny** and **Review**. The owner tapped **Deny** and it only **opened the app** - no denial was sent. The cause was one line of pure rules: `ApprovalWidgetRules.denyActsDirectly(hidden, denyOk) = !hidden && denyOk`. App lock, "Hide memory lists and chat history", **and settings that could not be read at all** (which fail closed and count as hidden) all routed that tap to `actionStartActivity<MainActivity>()`.

**What this replaces.** The 2026-09-28 decision above that "under App lock, the widgets' buttons open the locked app first, in both apps". It is replaced **for Deny on the phone's approval widget only**. Hiding the card's words is a display rule, not a deny rule: a refusal is the safe direction, cannot approve anything, and costs at most a retry. The quick-link widget's buttons and the desktop widget's tiles keep the 2026-09-28 rule unchanged.

**What was decided.**
1. **Deny acts directly whenever the card allows an unread deny** - `notice?.denyOk != false`, which includes a row with no `notice` at all (an older desktop) - **including while the widget is hidden.** `denyActsDirectly` now takes `denyOk` alone; `hidden` is deliberately not a parameter any more.
2. **A card that needs extra approval draws no Deny.** When the server says so itself (`deny_ok: false` - a denial the desktop wants confirmed, by a fingerprint, a PC-only check or another step), the widget draws **one** action that opens the app: **"Deny in app"** on a visible card, so the tap cannot be mistaken for a denial that already happened, and **"Review"** while locked, where the card says nothing about what is waiting. There is never a button labelled Deny that only opens the app.
3. **The locked wording is unchanged:** "Needs your OK / A decision is waiting", with the card's title and reason hidden (`cardTitle`/`cardDetail`, 2026-10-27).
4. **PC-only is not a deny problem.** The phone's `JarvisRuntime.decide` gates only `approve && item.pcOnly`, and the PC agrees: `jarvis_owner_check.py` says "Deny never comes here: POST /api/deny is passed straight to the owner's", so a PC-only card's deny really does work from the phone and the widget keeps offering it. Only the server's own `deny_ok: false` moves Deny into the app. Approve still only ever opens the app, and the link rule is untouched: a denial on a link that is gone is refused with its own sentence (`denyReachable`).

**The button matrix, before and after.** `hidden` is the App-lock/private-lists/widget-cannot-read-settings state; `denyOk` is the card's own permission.

| hidden | card's `denyOk` | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | true (every card the PC sends today) | Deny **opened the app**; Review opened the app | **Deny denies**; Review opens the app |
| no | true | Deny denied; Review opened the app | Deny denies; Review opens the app |
| yes | false (needs extra approval) | Deny **opened the app**; Review opened the app | **one "Review"** opens the app |
| no | false | no Deny at all; Review opened the app | **one "Deny in app"** opens the app |

**Honest scope of the `false` rows.** `jarvis_gate.notice_for` sends `"deny_ok": True` on every card the PC raises today, so no field card has ever been in the bottom two rows. They are the shape the rule provides for a card that needs a confirm step - the direction the owner's rule names - and the client already honoured `deny_ok` on the lock-screen notification. The change is what the widget does with each shape, not a new server field.

**Proven by.** `ApprovalWidgetRulesTest` (all four hidden x denyOk combinations, plus `denyActsDirectly` on its own), with `DenyNotHeldTest`, `WidgetStatesTest` and `CardWordsContractTest` updated where they pinned the old shape - the last of those used to read the widget's own literals for the Deny-before-Review order, and now asks `ApprovalWidgetRules.buttons` for that order and pins that the drawing code holds no "Deny" literal of its own. On this PC's Android toolchain, `.\gradlew.bat --offline --console=plain :app:testDebugUnitTest` in `jarvis-client` runs **2,721 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped** (252 result files; the four named classes are 4, 6, 14 and 8 tests). **Not proven:** the behaviour on a phone. No APK built from this branch has been installed, and a JVM test cannot tap a launcher. The retest is one CI APK and the owner tapping Deny once with the phone in App lock - the same situation that produced the evidence above.
## 2026-10-28 — A cloud answer is corrected like a local one, and a crisis turn is never sent to a cloud lane

The 2026-10-27 AI-safety audit (`.dsh-scratch/AUDITS-2026-10-27/partner-ai-safety.md`, findings H1 and M1) found that the honesty machinery was local-only. The "nothing was actually done" line, the four newer corrections and the 988/911 help text are all appended inside `jarvis_agent.run_local_turn`; the HUD's cloud relay copied the provider's stream straight out, so every one of them was missing on the one lane where no tool can run and a claim of action is therefore unbackable by construction. Two decisions settle it.

**One function builds the lines, for both lanes.** `jarvis_agent.postscript_lines` is the list; `run_local_turn` appends it, and the cloud relay asks for it through `jarvis_agent.cloud_postscript` with an empty step list. They are the same code, so the two lanes cannot say different things, and `backend/test_cloud_honesty.py` compares the cloud lines with the ones a driven local turn appends for the same words. `jarvis_chatbot_api.CloudAnswer` gained `answer_text()` (the answer as the owner saw it, never the withheld working-out) and a `tail=` parameter on `close()`; the ending events are now held for EVERY streamed reply, not only a blank one, so the lines land after the model's words and before the `finish_reason`/`[DONE]` event every reader finalizes on. There is no new wire field and no new route.

**A crisis turn is not sent to a cloud lane at all.** The audit's other half was that a crisis check could be skipped - the quick path answered first, and the answering turn read only the owner's own typed/voice words while the route header read the raw message, so a distress message pasted, shared, captioning a picture or said with a failed voice print drew the calm panel and got no help line. The router already refuses a crisis turn the cloud lane; that must not be the only thing standing in the way, and on `origin/main` a hand-picked lane bypassed every gate (F-01, fixed separately as `f01-manual-lane-gate.patch`). So the HUD rebinds a crisis turn to the local model itself, rebuilds the payload as a local turn's, and says so in `X-Jarvis-Route` (`cloud_refused: "crisis"`, `lane` naming the model that really answered, `where: "local"`). An owner who picked a cloud lane is not quietly ignored - the route says why it was answered here. The fixed help text is code-owned and does not depend on the provider's mood.

**One crisis rule, three callers.** `jarvis_wellbeing.crisis_in_turn` is now the only place that decides WHICH words are checked: the last message in the conversation, when it is the owner's (a `user` one), whatever its provenance tag. The route header, `jarvis_agent._TurnWatch` and `jarvis_quick.answer_turn` (which returns None on a crisis turn, so the fast path can no longer answer before any check runs) all ask it. Widening it is deliberate and bought a real cost: a pasted article that quotes a first-person crisis phrase now gets the help line too. That is the trade taken - an extra supportive line is a smaller harm than a missing one - and it is written into `jarvis_wellbeing.py`'s own docstring rather than left to be inferred.

**The classifier's three holes** (audit H2, H3, H4) are closed in `jarvis_claims.py`: a second, subjectless pass catches "Reminder set for 7pm.", "Email sent to Alex.", "Your timer is running." and "All set."; "noted" no longer exempts a sentence that names a place a note is written; and `read_web_page`, `propose_plan`, `feature_guide` and `rea_investigate` no longer count as actions. `ACTING_TOOLS` names the other half, and `backend/test_smarter_answers.py` fails when `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` holds a name in neither set - the guard the audit asked for, so the next tool is classified by the person adding it.

**Proven by.** `backend/test_cloud_honesty.py` (49 passed: the patch applies to the published base with `git apply`, compiles and reverses byte for byte; the cloud lines equal the local turn's; the tail lands before the finish event for a streamed and a whole reply; the crisis block, lifted out of the patched base and driven, rebinds the lane and says so), `backend/test_smarter_answers.py` (161 passed, including the passive-confirmation and "noted" cases and the classification guard), `backend/test_wellbeing.py` (the pasted/share/voice-unverified cases, the fast-path refusal, and the one-rule checks), `backend/test_reasoning_fallback.py` (45 passed - an ordinary cloud answer is still byte for byte what it was), and `backend/test_chatbot_api.py` (239 passed). **Not proven here:** the route end to end against a real cloud provider - that needs the owner's PC and a real key, and nothing in this change drives it.
## 2026-10-28 — The Anti-Slop filter is a cardless preference, like the prompt coach

**Gemini's ruling on it (review edition 2, 2026-10-28), recorded in its own words:**

- **2026-10-28 — Anti-Slop filter (`jarvis_antislop.py`) is vendored as a distilled local module, default OFF, cardless in both directions:** Evaluated `miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop` `v3.2.23` (`6732aee`, MIT). To protect the local 9B model's 3,800-token system-prompt budget and obey the no-unpinned-network-installer rule (`#594`), Jarvis does not run `npx antislop-ai` and does not inject the raw 56.3 KB rulebook. Instead, `jarvis_antislop.py` vendors a distilled task-scoped prompt block (`<= 240 tokens` when ON, `0 tokens` when OFF) plus a deterministic local Python post-processor and `after`-mode static auditor (`< 2 ms`). Because it is a local output-style filter that opens no external door and loosens no security gate, turning it ON or OFF requires `0` approval cards in either direction (same class as Prompt Coach, How Jarvis talks, and Write Like Me).

**Decided:** `miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop` (MIT, v3.2.23) is integrated as a **cardless preference in both directions**. Turning it ON raises no approval card and neither does turning it OFF - the same class as Prompt Coach, "How Jarvis talks" and "Write Like Me". It is a filter on the WORDS Jarvis writes: it opens no network door, reads no folder, takes no action, and loosens no gate, so there is nothing for a card to decide. Every change still leaves ONE action receipt with a one-click Undo (`jarvis_receipts.py`), which is this project's pattern for "this changed something, put it back".

**What was taken, and what was not.** The rules are distilled and vendored into `backend/jarvis_antislop.py` (+ its byte-identical twin), not installed: no `npx antislop-ai`, no npm, no network install, no second rulebook read at run time. The 56 KB rulebook is not redistributed - the checkable rules are re-expressed as Python (R-02, R-10, R-13, R-15, R-16, R-25, R-26, R-32 and the `antislop-code` skill) plus a compact prompt block, and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` carries the MIT attribution and says exactly what was taken and what was left out.

**Why it is worth its tokens, measured rather than assumed.** Off, the prompt block is the empty string and no filter object is built - **0 tokens and 0 work**, which `backend/test_antislop.py` proves in both directions. On, the block is at most 1,050 characters (about 240 tokens) and only the rules for the owner's own scopes are sent, with the UI rules paid for only when the question is actually about a screen. What the filter really CHECKS is deterministic Python, not prompt: an em-dash scrub and a code-comment cleanup on the words the model already wrote, and an auditor for an existing page or file. The rules no static check can prove are guided by that small prompt block and are never reported as checked - see (3) below.

**The four decisions inside it that could have gone the other way.** (1) **`during` and `after` are different promises.** `during` filters as Jarvis writes. `after` audits and lists findings first and **rewrites nothing** - an audit is allowed to quote the very em dash it reports, so the scrub is bypassed and a test holds that. (2) **`R-37` beats `R-02`, and the owner can override `R-02` himself.** When "Write Like Me" is on and the owner's own writing samples use em dashes, the ban yields, in the prompt and in the scrub. `jarvis_antislop.voiceprint_uses_em_dash()` is the single place that decides, and it answers False whenever it cannot read the samples - no exemption is ever invented. On top of that automatic rule the owner has a stored `allow_em_dashes` flag (default **false**), so em dashes can be allowed outright while the rest of the copy scope - generic CTAs (R-15) and AI buzzwords (R-16) - keeps working. It is stored rather than read from the samples, because a preference the owner set must not move when their samples do.

(3) **Only what a program really checks is called enforced (Gemini's Q1 ruling).** The rules are split in two, and the audit report says which is which **before** it says anything else: **Class A** is deterministic and checked here - R-02 (with the R-37 exemption and the `allow_em_dashes` override), the R-10/R-13 dose caps, R-15/R-16, R-17/R-36/R-38 through `jarvis_claims.py`, the static half of R-24/R-26, R-25's unrounded WCAG 2.1 contrast, the static half of R-32, and `antislop-code`. **Class B** is **prompt-guided only and never mechanically enforced** - R-03's dynamic overflow and rendered 44x44 tap targets (they need Playwright layout), R-18 (is a testimonial fabricated?), R-20 (the identity test), R-23 (asset confirmation), R-27 (semantic empty/loading/error completeness), R-28 (is an FAQ generic?), R-30 (clone detection), and R-34/R-35 (live theme switching and click-through, which this project's own Playwright suites prove, not this module). The split is data, not prose: `ENFORCEMENT_CLASS_A` / `ENFORCEMENT_CLASS_B` build the header, so a rule can never be described as enforced in one place and guided in another.

(4) **The scrub only ever touches the model's own chat words (Gemini's Q4 ruling).** Its prose and the fenced code blocks inside that answer - never a tool's input or output, a file Jarvis writes, a diff or a patch, or a file already in a repository, and `audit_text_or_ui` stays read-only. Inside fenced code it removes only two shapes that carry no information: a purely decorative separator line with no words on it, and a comment led by one of ten decorative emoji. A headed banner (`# --- Phase 2: Database Migration ---`) is left to the prompt rule and the `after` audit; a shebang, a coding/`type`/`noqa`/`pragma` line, a Rust doc comment and a diff header are never touched at all.

**The ordering that keeps a helpline out of its reach.** `run_local_turn` flushes the scrub **before** `jarvis_claims.py`'s correction lines and **before** `jarvis_wellbeing.py`'s crisis line are appended (there is no `finalize_turn_output` in this backend - the blueprint named one that does not exist here, and the ordering is tested where the lines really are). A helpline number or an honesty-gate sentence is a safety-critical system string; the filter may rewrite the model's words, but it must never rewrite those, and a test proves both the ordering and that a crisis sentence containing an em dash survives it.

**What it deliberately is not.** Not a second settings system: `antislop` is a `BOOL_SETTINGS` row and `antislop_mode` a `CHOICE_SETTINGS` row, so "turn on anti-slop", "set anti-slop mode to after" and the generic "set `<name>` to `<value>`" grammar all reach the same setters the route and the Settings page call. Not a patch: its three routes come from its own `install()`, called by the drop-in folder `plugins/ready/antislop`, which is the repo's own pattern for a feature born as a folder. Not a gate: no `jarvis_gate` call exists in the module or in the new fast-path sentences, and `backend/test_antislop.py` proves zero cards with a spy on the gate.

**Proven by:** `backend/test_antislop.py` (239 passed, 0 failed, including **seven** mutation bite-proofs - the six from the integration blueprint plus one for the Q4 comment guard - each one breaking a throwaway copy of the module and requiring the same check to FAIL, so a check that proves nothing is reported as a failed bite), `backend/test_settings_registry.py` (798 passed), `backend/test_quick_wins.py` (217), `backend/test_feature_guide.py` (1832), `backend/test_ask_to_change.py` (89), `backend/test_settings_rows.py` (21), `backend/test_settings_tool.py` (180), `backend/test_shipped_modules.py` (791), `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` (123), `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` (39), `tools/check_stale_twins.py` (all 284 compared files match), `tools/check_plugins.py` (21), `tools/gen_notices.py --check` (up to date), `tools/check_docs_map.py` (green), `tools/roll_changelog.py --check` (13 fragments OK) and, in a throwaway copy with the Settings half's files applied, `tools/check_feature_controls.py` (142/142 features, 32/32 switches, 52/52 rows, exit 0).

**Not proven, and said rather than hidden:** the desktop Settings card and the phone's settings screen are the other half of this feature and are not in this change, so nothing here was driven by a person on a screen. Two consequences, both measured rather than guessed at.
