(1) `tools/check_feature_controls.py` **cannot be green on this branch alone**, because the contract rows, the `features.json` row and the generated catalogue it reads belong to that half: run here it prints exactly the two lines that half owns - `BOOL_SETTINGS switch missing from the matrix: antislop` and `named choice setting missing from the matrix: antislop_mode` - and it exits 0 only once those files are present (proved in a throwaway copy of this tree with them applied: 142/142 features covered, 32/32 switches, 52/52 rows). (2) The `allow_em_dashes` flag is reachable by `POST /api/antislop` today and by the Settings checkbox once that half draws it; there is no spoken sentence for it yet, and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §159.1 says so. The `after`-mode auditor sees a page's CSS declarations, not a rendered page (no click-through, no focus ring driven with a keyboard), and the report's own Class B header lists every rule it therefore does not check, as NOT CHECKED rather than a pass.

## 2026-10-28 — The Anti-Slop filter is a cardless preference: 0 approval cards in both directions, and 0 prompt tokens when it is off

**What it is.** The ruleset is `miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop` (v3.2.23, MIT), distilled to what fits a local model's prompt budget instead of the raw 56 KB file: no em-dashes in prose, no AI buzzwords, no decorative comment banners in code, no dead buttons, WCAG AA contrast and a visible focus ring. Where it lives: `GET`/`POST /api/antislop` (`docs/JARVIS-API.md` §159), the desktop card at Settings → How Jarvis talks → Anti-Slop filter, the phone's switch and mode under the same heading, and the spoken names in `jarvis_settings_registry.py`.

**Decided (the toggle class).** Turning it ON and turning it OFF are both **cardless**, in the same class as Prompt Coach, How Jarvis talks and Write Like Me, and for the same reason written down here: the filter changes only how an answer is **worded**. It opens no way out of the PC, reads no folder, adds no reach, takes no action and loosens no rule — so there is nothing for a card to protect. It also leaves ONE action receipt with a one-click Undo (`jarvis_receipts.py`, action name `antislop`) — the project's pattern for "this changed something, put it back" — and still no approval card in either direction.

**Decided (not held on a stale link, on the desktop).** The two Rust commands (`src-tauri/src/antislop.rs`) do **not** consult the event stream, which is why the desktop card's controls never grey for the link's state. Rule 4 blocks *acting* when the stream is stale; de-slopping an answer is not an act, and a stale link says nothing about whether an em-dash should stay. The **phone keeps its own hold** (`JarvisRuntime.setAntislop`), because every change the phone sends is held there — the same asymmetry Prompt Coach already has, and the reason is the same in both places: "at once" means no approval card, not "works while the link is down". Both halves say so out loud where the code is, so the day one of them changes, the reason is there to argue with.

**Decided (the phone is a mirror).** The phone gets the master switch and the During/After mode and **not** the three scopes, the Delivery Gate switch or the three Liveliness dials. Recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8. The phone already keeps two-shape settings for How Jarvis talks and Voice; scopes and dials are tuning, not a state to check on the go, and the standing rule says no model catalogue and no deep config editing on the phone. `tools/check_parity.py` classifies `/api/antislop` `ported`, because both apps really call it.

**Decided (what OFF costs, said on screen).** The card carries one line: **"Off: costs 0 prompt tokens. Nothing is added to a prompt and no answer is rewritten."** That line is the promise the toggle class rests on — an inert-off filter cannot cost anything — so it is written where the owner reads it, not only in the module's docstring, and `tests/antislop.mjs` fails if the words leave the copy.

**The counts, and what they mean.** The controls matrix now holds 142 features (was 141) at 42 Switchable/Adjustable, 2 Settings-Only, 15 PC-Only, 71 Command-Only and 12 Always-On. The switch's `bool_settings` entry is recorded as `planned` on purpose, with the reason written into the contract: the desktop control is a **bespoke card**, not one of the 29 `<label class="toggle">` rows `SETTINGS_ROWS` generates, so there is no `desktop_row` to name — exactly the recording "Write like me", the other bespoke card, already carries.

**Deliberately not done.** No new route beyond `/api/antislop` (the audit variant the source ruleset describes is a later slice, not this one). No `npx` and no run-time download. No text change to `CHANGELOG.md` — the entry is a `changelog.d` fragment. No edit to `backend/jarvis_settings_registry.py`, `jarvis_quick.py`, `jarvis_agent.py` or `jarvis_antislop.py`: those were built in a parallel slice on the same day, and this slice writes only the surfaces that read them.

**Proven by.** `jarvis-desktop/tests/antislop-settings.mjs` — 21 checks driving the real page in a headless browser with a stubbed bridge: the card renders OFF, the four ON-only halves are hidden while off, the master switch sends exactly `{change: {enabled}}`, OFF → ON → OFF round-trips through the stubbed PC, each scope/the mode/a dial/the gate sends only its own field, a refusal shows the PC's own sentence and springs the switch back, an older PC says so and never claims "off", an `antislop` bus event re-reads, and an unrelated event does not. `jarvis-desktop/tests/antislop.mjs` — 13 pure checks on the mapping. `src-tauri/src/antislop.rs` — 10 unit tests pinning the POST bodies, run by `cargo test`. `jarvis-client`'s `AntislopTest` (14 tests) runs on the JVM in CI.

**Not proven, and not claimed.** No Android build exists in this container, so `net/Antislop.kt` and `AntislopPlate.kt` are compiled for the first time by CI's `phone-unit-tests` job — nothing here claims they compile. The desktop pixels are Playwright-only: no real Tauri window was opened. And `tools/check_feature_controls.py` cannot be green on this branch alone, because the two registry rows it resolves the typed phrases through are the parallel slice's files; measured against a simulated registry carrying them, the checker exits 0 with 142/142 features covered.

## 2026-10-28 — "Allow em-dashes (—)" is the owner's blanket exemption, off by default, and the card now says which anti-slop rules are really checked

**Decided (the em-dash option).** The Anti-Slop card and the phone plate get one checkbox, **"Allow em-dashes (—)"**, bound to a new `allow_em_dashes` boolean on `GET`/`POST /api/antislop` (`docs/JARVIS-API.md` §159), **off by default** and cardless in both directions like the rest of the filter. It is deliberately NOT the voiceprint rule, and the sentence beside it says so: when the owner's stored writing samples use em-dashes, Write Like Me's own `R-37` precedence already exempts `R-02` whether the box is ticked or not, because the owner's prose is direction rather than slop. The box is the blanket "keep them everywhere" on top of that, for a general chat, a code comment or a page, so ticking it never has to mean "and also forgive my samples". One field per change, in the PC's own spelling, so it cannot reset a scope, the mode, a dial or the gate.

**Decided (say what is enforced, and only that).** The card, the phone plate, the feature list's `limit` line and `JARVIS-API` §159 now state the enforcement split in one sentence: the filter guides generation, then deterministically checks a fixed list in code (em-dashes, buzzwords, comment banners, dead buttons, contrast, focus rings, glass and glow caps), while layout, taste and rendered sizes are guidance only. Live horizontal overflow, 44px tap targets, a real theme switch and whether a quote is genuine need a rendered page or a person, and the Playwright suites are what prove those, where anything does. So no screen and no record claims "every anti-slop rule is mechanically enforced".

**Deliberately not done.** No typed phrase for the em-dash box (it is a Settings checkbox; a phrase would be a second control surface the PC's grammar does not have), and no 30th registry row (it is one field on the existing `antislop` switch). This slice also does not claim the PC already stores the field: `backend/jarvis_antislop.py` is the engine slice's, and until its `allow_em_dashes` lands the PC refuses the key with its own `unknown_setting` sentence and the box springs back - which `jarvis-desktop/tests/antislop-settings.mjs` proves against a stub.
## 2026-10-28 — Jarvis recommends a model or preset change; only the owner's cards download and apply

**The owner's request, in their words:** *"can you give jarvis the ability to
recommend a change to presets (for the local ai models being used) with a one
click check for new models button and it will look on hugging face for newer
potentially better models, give me a card to approve a download and a bench
mark testing locally, then it will recommend changing the presets based on the
local gpus and what model goes where and i can approve or give my opinion and
jarvis can change the preset recommendations then i approve?"*

**Decided.** (1) Three read-only, cardless answers for the desktop: a cached
catalogue check (`POST /api/models/check`), a bounded benchmark of a model
**already installed** (`POST /api/models/benchmark`), and preset changes
computed from measured numbers (`POST /api/presets/recommend`), plus the read
that combines them (`GET /api/models/recommendations`). (2) The owner's note
refines the recommendation through **deterministic rules** - keep / lower the
footprint / raise the candidate pool / quality / recorded only - never through a
model's guess at what they meant, and never by inventing a measurement.
(3) **Nothing downloads and nothing applies.** A download stays the EXISTING
`/api/models/install` card, and a preset change stays the EXISTING
`/api/work/apply` card; this feature adds no install route, no apply route, no
gate action and no tier line. (4) The five routes are **PC-only**, refused 403
from another device before the body is read, because the standing rule keeps a
model catalogue off the phone. (5) The Hugging Face lookup reuses the existing
capability, `jarvis_models.discover()`'s fixed public catalogue URLs - no new
key, no token, and no query term derived from the owner. (6) A preset change is
justified only by numbers this PC measured: tokens/second from Ollama's own
reply timings, video memory from `/api/ps`, context from `/api/show`, card sizes
from `nvidia-smi`. A model with no local benchmark is never compared, and a
candidate with no measured video memory or context is never chosen.

**Deliberately not done.** No timer, watcher or background job: every call is
the owner's click. No "newest" claim: the existing catalogue pass sorts the
Hugging Face GGUF list by trending and discards `lastModified`, so the answer
says "the public trending list" and never "newer than yours". No estimate in a
preset recommendation (only the candidate list's fit is an estimate, and its own
sentence says so). No phone screen and no phone route.

**Proven by:** `backend/test_model_recommendations.py` (121 checks) - the check
endpoint never downloads (source-scanned for every download/apply/gate call),
the benchmark refuses an uninstalled model before measuring and stores nothing
when it cannot measure, recommendations quote only benchmark-store rates and
`nvidia-smi` card sizes, a faster model that would shrink the window is refused,
an opinion changes the suggestion without changing a single measured number,
a candidate carries the licence only when the catalogue reports one and carries
no hash at all, the five routes refuse a phone before reading a body, and the
existing `/api/models/install` and `/api/work/apply` cards are untouched.
**Not proven
here:** the live Hugging Face lookup - this checkout has no network, so every
test injects the catalogue pass; the first real click on the owner's PC is the
field test (and it is a read-only request either way). Also not proven: any
model's quality. This feature compares speed, memory and context window, and
says so.

## 2026-10-28 - Jarvis may recommend models and preset changes, and the owner still approves every change

**The owner's ask, in their words:** "can you give jarvis the ability to recommend a change to presets (for the local ai models being used) with a one click check for new models button and it will look on hugging face for newer potentially better models, give me a card to approve a download and a bench mark testing locally, then it will recommend changing the presets based on the local gpus and what model goes where and i can approve or give my opinion and jarvis can change the preset recommendations then i approve?"

**Decided:** (1) the Brain's Model card gets ONE "Check for new models" button, which asks the PC to look on Hugging Face - it downloads nothing and raises no card. (2) A candidate's Download is the EXISTING carded install (`/api/models/install`, `brain_model`): the owner sees one card and nothing downloads until it is approved. (3) A model already installed can be measured with "Benchmark on this PC" (`/api/models/benchmark`), and the numbers are labelled "measured on this PC" - a newer model is never called better without one. (4) The preset advice (`POST /api/presets/recommend`) shows its proposed rows, their Why and its evidence; Approve changes is the EXISTING carded preset apply (`/api/work/apply`, `apply_focus_preset`), and "Tell Jarvis what you think" (`POST /api/presets/recommend/opinion`) revises the advice before the owner approves it. (5) The surface is the desktop's alone: the standing rule keeps the model catalogue off the phone and the phone's install is a typed name, so a phone version of this screen would be the catalogue - ARCHITECTURE §8 records it, and `tools/check_parity.py` classifies all five routes `deliberate`.

**Deliberately not done.** No uncarded download and no auto-apply, and no second route for either: the advisor only asks questions, which is why `brain_model_recommend` refuses every action that is not one of its four. No automatic check when the Brain opens: **the owner's explicit click on "Check for new models" is the per-use trigger** for the Hugging Face lookup - no timer, no lookup at startup and no silent refresh - and that lookup is read-only and keyless, sending no user data and no query term derived from the owner. A candidate row shows what the catalogue actually reports - its ref, quantization, size and licence - and says "not reported by the catalogue" where a licence is missing rather than inventing one; `jarvis_models.discover()` carries no SHA-256, so no hash is shown at all. No on-disk cache of candidates or measurements: the PC's own `checked_at` dates the list and a benchmark is a fact about one day, so painting either as current after a restart would be a lie of the same kind `models-cache.js` exists to prevent. No new card, no new permission for the phone, and no phone half.

**Proven by:** `jarvis-desktop/tests/model-advisor.mjs`, 31 checks, all passing - the pure reading and every honest state, then the REAL Brain page driven through the test harness against stubbed answers at the bridge: button -> progress -> candidates -> Download on the carded install shape -> benchmark shown as measured -> opinion revises -> Approve on the carded preset shape, plus the lookup-failed, no-advisor, no-candidates and benchmark-unavailable states, each in the PC's own words, the licence line (reported vs "not reported by the catalogue") and the no-hash sentence. The bridge is stubbed rather than `fetch` because the Brain window holds no token and calls no URL (apps security audit M2); the routes behind the four actions are pinned against `src-tauri/src/brain.rs` in the same suite. On the integration branch `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --all-targets` (which type-checks `model_recommend_tests` - the action/route/body table and the waits) and `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --all-targets -- -D warnings` are all clean; **`cargo test` was still NOT RUN here**, so those Rust tests are compiled but unproven. `tools/check_parity.py`, `tools/check_feature_list.py`, `tools/check_command_acl.py` and `tools/check_invoke_grants.py` are clean.

**Not proven:** the real backend routes. The backend half is a parallel branch, so no Hugging Face lookup, benchmark or preset recommendation has been run against a live backend here, and no window was rebuilt and installed - the panel has not been seen in the shipped Tauri shell, only in the harness. A real lookup's candidate shape, and how long a benchmark of an 8B model really takes on this PC, are both unmeasured.
## 2026-10-28 — A failure is never drawn as the answer, and a rollback says only what it checked

**What was decided.** Six places where Jarvis told the owner something that was not true now say what really happened, and the rules behind them are standing rules for every feature after this one (the silent-failure audit of 2026-10-27, `.dsh-scratch/AUDITS-2026-10-27/FAILURES.md`, rows 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 10):

- **A restore names only what was observed.** Applying a focus preset that fails after the model has switched restores the model, the chat lane and the remembered preset; each of the three is now checked, the answer lists what was put back (`restored`) and what was not (`not_restored`), and the sentence contains "were rolled back" only when every attempted restore succeeded. Before this, one `except Exception: pass` and an unread return value could sit under a sentence claiming all three were undone. **The rule:** never claim a step that was not seen to happen; when one cannot be restored, say which and tell the owner to check the PC.
- **Each failure kind keeps its own words.** A connect **timeout** ("Your PC isn't answering. It may be asleep or switched off, or Tailscale or NordVPN Meshnet may be off at one end") is not a **refused** connection ("Jarvis isn't running on your PC"). The page already had both; the Rust shell sent the timeout to the refused sentence, which sent the owner to press Start on a service that may never have stopped.
- **An unread question is not the answer "nothing".** A Today board whose read failed used to reach the page as "no board", which draws exactly like a clear day - no "Due now", no "Next steps", and the said-I'd-do switch reading off, which the page cannot know. Rust now keeps three cases apart (read / this PC has no board / the read failed), and the failed one is drawn as "Jarvis could not read today's board from your PC. That does not mean nothing is due - it means this page could not ask", with a Retry. A PC that simply has no board (an older backend) still says nothing, because nothing failed there.
- **One door to the shell, with a budget.** Every command from these surfaces goes through `invoke-budget.js`, so a command that never settles ends in "it is not known whether it happened" instead of a control that waits for ever. The HUD's preset apply was the named hole: `apply_focus_preset` has had a 1,250 s budget since the 2026-10-16 freeze, and this menu could not reach it. That module is now a SERVED page file (`/invoke-budget.js`), because `hud-presets.js` imports it and the browser HUD's `STATIC_ASSETS` is a closed world - shipped in `backend/static/`, the published base, both `$SHIPPED` lists and the `BESIDE` table, with the live key in `tools/hud-deltas/hud-static-assets.txt`. The remaining direct `core.invoke(` sites (45 files / 96 sites in `src/*.js` plus 11 in `src/*.html`) are counted by `tests/invoke-budget.mjs` and are **not** claimed to be converted.
- **A success word needs a read-back.** Settings' browser-engine card says "Saved." only when a fresh read shows the mode that was asked for, and "Asked your PC. Reopen this page in a moment…" otherwise. This is the same rule `commands.rs`'s `save_file_then_token` already runs on the desktop.
- **A dropped event is written where a release build can read it.** A HUD push that threw, a quickbar event that could not be emitted and a failed broadcast went to `eprintln!`, and a release build (`windows_subsystem = "windows"`) has no console - so the one record of the lost event was the place that does not exist. They go through `logfile::log` now.

**What this does not change.** No route, no approval card, no capability, no loosening and no new network path. `restored`/`not_restored` are additive keys on `/api/work/apply` (JARVIS-API section 145), so the phone and any older reader behave exactly as before. The one new page word ("Asked your PC. Reopen this page in a moment to see which browser it uses.") is a page-only word like "Saved.", not one of the PC's fixed words.

**What is deliberately NOT done.** The HUD's gap detector for a missed event push (the audit's T8 second half) needs a new IPC surface and a capability grant, so a dropped push is logged but the page cannot yet notice it. And the audit's rows outside the desktop+backend lane - the five Android widgets, the phone's `prefs.edit` read-back, the TTS refusal, the swallowed `audio.play()`, the quiet `brain_memory_saved_unseen` count and the swallowed `open_external_url` - are not in this change.

**Proven by.** `backend/test_presets_apply.py` (37 checks, including a restore that raises and one that returns False), `backend/test_presets.py` / `test_presets_cloud.py` / `test_presets_lanes.py` / `test_presets_latency.py` / `test_work.py` / `test_schedule_actions.py` / `test_schedule_contract.py` / `test_schedule_phase2.py` / `test_schedule_taint.py`, the Rust suite on the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` target (with the window probe skipped), and the browser-free node suites `tests/hud-shell.mjs`, `tests/today-board-unread.mjs`, `tests/browser-engine.mjs`, plus the static halves of `tests/invoke-budget.mjs` and `tests/plain-errors.mjs` run on their own. **Not proven here:** the Playwright half of `tests/today.mjs` (the rendered page), and the Android (Kotlin) suites - no Playwright and no Android build in this container; CI runs both.
## 2026-10-28 — The Settings menu gets the two learning switches, and the audit's wrong claims are corrected

**The owner's question, and what it found.** On 2026-10-27 the owner asked for an audit: "make sure all features and functions that are part of jarvis have proper settings in the settings menu ... and can be turned on and off or adjusted otherwise properly". The audit (`.dsh-scratch/MAXOUT-2026-10-28/SETTINGS-AUDIT.md`) checked 141 features, the registry, both apps' Settings pages and the HUD, and found the Settings *menu* complete except for one real feature: `background_learning` and `learn_sensitive_topics` were switches with a route, a typed name and an approval card, but no Settings row on either app - they lived only in Brain -> Memory -> Learning. The rest of the findings were controls in the wrong card, a feature row that sent the owner to a Settings control that does not exist, and a stale gap record the directory was still showing.

**Decided: the learning switches get a real Learning card on both apps, and the Settings window may change them.** The card is drawn from the Brain's OWN `brain_memory_learning`, `brain_memory_learning_sensitive` and `brain_memory_learning_status` commands, so a change in Settings, a change in the Brain and "turn on background learning" are one write path, one card, one rule - not a second idea of learning. The grant is deliberately the narrowest thing that works (a new `learning-settings` set: the switch state and the two switch writes). It does **not** carry `/api/memory/auto`, the "saved unseen" ids, Forget, export or any fact's words, so the Settings window still cannot read a saved fact. ON raises the PC's ONE `learning_enable` / `learning_sensitive_enable` card and changes nothing until a person answers it; OFF is immediate. Each app says the same words the Brain uses, and the phone reuses its own `AutoLearnSwitches` under the background switch.

**Decided: the wrong Settings claims are corrected, not papered over.** (1) Read-aloud's feature row said "Settings, Voice, 'Read aloud'" - a switch that does not exist. It now names the two Voice choices that really decide whether memory-based answers are read aloud ("Answers that use what Jarvis remembers" / "Answers that use sensitive saved facts") and the HUD's "Read-aloud buttons on answers" row, and says plainly that the HUD row adds a speaker and does not turn read-aloud on or off. (2) "Let Jarvis Desktop start and stop Jarvis" is drawn in Starting Jarvis for you again: a bad 2026-10-11 merge had put it inside the Pictures body, which is hidden on a PC without the picture program, so a refusal sentence could send the owner to a card that did not contain the switch. (3) The same merge had also moved "Making pictures" into the unrelated "Startup and logs" card; it is back in its own card, outside the body that can be hidden. The settings tests now prove a row is drawn inside the card its `section` names, which is what none of the old checks did. (4) `SETTINGS_GAPS["history"]` said the desktop Settings page had no chat-history control; it has had the switch and the retention in Security since 2026-10-22, so `chat_history.section` is `security` and the gap table is empty.

**The bug the fix uncovered, and its fix.** Linking `chat_history` to the Security section made "Lock Jarvis, and hide what it remembers" (an Always-On safety rule, which shares that section) find exactly one switch - and it would have turned chat history on. That is the one thing a typed setting path must never do, and `tools/check_feature_controls.py`'s own guard 2 caught it. `jarvis_feature_guide.switches_for()` now refuses to link any switch to a feature in `ALWAYS_ON_IDS` (the same rule `_build_matrix` already applied), and `jarvis_quick._feature_own_controls()` refuses them too, so an Always-On title answers with its version of "that is always on", never with a switch it does not own.

**Deliberately not done, with the reason.** The audit's other findings are left for their own changes: G4 (the "Write like me" block is a `<section class="block">`, not a card, so making it openable by name also means converting it to a card, adding a jump link and a hideable menu id, wiring `data-menu-id`, and recording the phone's honest PC-only refusal); G6 (the interrupt choice is a new named choice setting, a grammar and contract change of its own); G7 (two phone-only rows with no registry section); G8 (the HUD's own Galaxy/rail toggles, which need one honest line rather than a second Settings card); G9 (`big_coder.section`, a one-field change that belongs with G6's settings-registry pass). None of them is a switch that cannot be changed - they are naming, placement and record work.

**Proven by, on this tree.** `python -B tools/gen_settings_cases.py --check` (the four generated files and the page's rows match); `tools/check_feature_controls.py` (141/141 features, 31/31 switches, 34/34 rows, 53/53 sections, 13 enforced); `tools/check_feature_list.py` (9/9); `tools/check_parity.py` (no undecided drift); `tools/check_stale_twins.py`; `backend/test_settings_rows.py` (21), `test_settings_registry.py` (778), `test_feature_guide.py` (1815), `test_feature_controls.py` (16), `test_feature_list.py` (41), `test_menu_visibility.py` (450); `test_base_matches_repo.py` (123) and `test_base_regeneration.py` (39); the desktop tests including a new `learning-settings.mjs`, the new per-row card-placement check and the read-aloud wording check in `settings-catalogue.mjs`, plus the existing settings, menu, feature-directory, security and automatic-learning suites.

**Not proven, and not claimed.** The phone's Learning row has not been compiled or run here (this container has no Android build; CI's `phone-unit-tests` and the client build are its first compiler), and no Rust source changed - the permission set and the settings capability are the only shell-side files, and they are parsed and cross-checked by the node security tests, not compiled. The audit's own limits stand: nothing here proves each switch's write reaches a live backend end to end, and the Pictures-body hiding was proven by reading the code, not by driving the owner's PC.
## 2026-10-28 — The HUD's left column lists every face model

**The owner's request, in their own words:** *"add a jarvis model icon to the left column of the jarvis desktop that has all of the jarvis models (face models)"*.

**What was built.** A `Faces` button (a line-drawn head on the page's own 24-unit grid) joined the HUD left column's toolbar, where Presets and Live already are. It opens one panel listing **all 25 faces from `faces-spec.js` itself** - the same file `faces.html` draws and `spec.rs` compiles, so there is no second list to drift - with the current face marked. Choosing a row runs one new narrow Rust command, `hud_set_face`, which reads the stored appearance document first (so an empty cache cannot wipe the bindings), validates the id against the same spec, and then calls the **same `set_appearance` the Faces window's "Use this face" already uses**: settings store first, then the existing `/api/appearance` route. So `appearance.json` stays the record, the phone wears the chosen face, and a reload keeps it; a failed save moves no mark and says so in the PC's words. No new store, no second list, no route, no approval card, and the command carries only a face id. The toolbar now wraps because a third button did not fit the 212px rail at the two-button width.

**Both apps and the one-sided note.** The picker is deliberately **desktop-only**: the phone already has its own Faces screen and its own choice, the HUD's left column is a desktop surface, and the shared document remains the single record. The reason is written in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 rather than left to be inferred.

**Honest limits.** Nothing was seen on a real desktop: Playwright is not installed here, so the panel's pixels and placement were proved with a fake DOM plus source pins, and `hud.mjs`/`hud-presets.mjs` are CI's first run. `cargo test` is 1030 passed / 3 failed, the same three `%TEMP%` "Access is denied" tests this file already records for this machine; the three new Rust tests pass. **Not proven:** the packaged WebView2 window and the 20 real face pixels.

**Proven by:** `jarvis-desktop/tests/face-models-rail.mjs` (23 checks: markup, row count equal to the spec's own array, no face id or name copied into the page, one current row including fallbacks, the click, the no-op, the failed save, Escape and focus, the browser path, the reload chain and the single narrow capability, three copies byte-identical), plus `hud-current-models`, `hud-shell`, `hud-rail-tools`, `hud-edit`, `hud-layout`, `csp-inline`, `test_hud_static`, the base/twin checkers, `check_parity`, the changelog check and the docs-map check.
## 2026-10-28 — Edit HUD paints a hidden card as a dimmed ghost while editing, so hiding is reversible

**The owner's words, and the defect they found.** "can you field test the edit hud and change everything then revert back to make sure it all works?" The field test written for that question (`jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-edit-fieldtest.mjs`) changed every region, place, size, fold and visibility of every card that offers them, reloaded, and then reverted - and found exactly one thing that would not come back: **a hidden card**. A card's Hide control sent `{type:"setVisible", id, visible:false}` on every press while the app painted it as a toggle (`aria-pressed`, a circle instead of a cross); a hidden card's shell is `display:none` (`.hud-card[hidden]`), so the one toggling path - the `h` key, which needs focus on that card's own handle - could never be reached again. After a reload the only ways back were Undo / Discard changes (same editing session) or Reset to preset, and Reset replaces the arrangement of a layout that is not the base preset, so an owner's **own** saved layout could not be fully restored.

**Decided.** (1) Hide is a real toggle: the control sends `setVisible` with **no** fixed value, through the one reducer (`applyAction`), which is the same call the `h` key already made - one door, both directions, no second mutation path. (2) While Edit HUD is on, a hidden card's shell stays painted (`shell.hidden = !card.visible && !editing`) as a dimmed, dotted ghost: its header, the word "hidden", and its own Show control, with the card's **body** folded away by a page rule (`body[data-hud-edit="on"] .hud-card-hidden .hud-card-body{display:none}`), so the card itself is still hidden and its content is not reachable. The control reads `Show <card>` while the card is hidden, so the words name the action the press takes. (3) Outside edit mode **nothing changed**: `.hud-card[hidden]` still hides the whole shell, so the ordinary HUD looks exactly as it did. (4) No new action type, no new IPC command and no change to `hud_layout.rs`: one saved document, the same validation, the same refusals. Protected cards (`approvals`, `bar_launcher`) are still refused hiding by the reducer, in the same words, and their control is still disabled.

**Alternatives turned down.** (a) A "hidden cards" tray or restore list beside the HUD: a second surface holding the same state, which grows a second way to change it and has to be kept in step with the saved document. (b) Making Hide one-way but honest (an undo toast instead of a toggle): it still leaves an owner's saved layout unrecoverable after a reload, which is the defect. (c) Leaving hidden cards painted **outside** edit mode too: that is the opposite of what hiding means. (d) Having the button compute an explicit `visible: true/false`: two places computing the same next state, and the keyboard path would have to agree with it.

**What it costs, honestly.** While editing, a ghost keeps its grid cell and its full toolbar, so a narrow card's toolbar can spill into a neighbour exactly as a visible card's does - the field test counts those and prints them (`note A/B: 1 edit control(s) ... brain_stats.collapse <- budget`), and it drives card controls by keyboard for that reason (Ruling 27 / WCAG 2.5.7). The ghost's look is a CSS choice (`opacity:.6`, a dotted border, a `hidden` word) with no measurement behind it.

**The three copies.** The page and the editor ship in three places - `jarvis-desktop/src/`, `backend/` (`jarvis_hud.html`, `static/hud-edit.js`) and the published base `jarvis-backend/` - and the fix is carried to all of them, kept byte-identical, so the page the owner's PC is served gets the fix and not only the app's copy.

**Proven by.** `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-edit.mjs` (82 passed, including the new "Hide toggles, and a hidden card can be reached again in Edit HUD" block that pins the toggle call, the ghost's shell rule, the folded body and the "Show" label), `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-edit-fieldtest.mjs` (**22 of 22**, both scenarios - A from the Cockpit preset and B from an owner's own saved layout - run twice with the same result; the previously failing `B (e2)` and `B (f)` now pass), `tests/hud-edit-geometry.mjs`, `tests/hud-layout.mjs` and `tests/hud-settings-layout.mjs`; on the repository side `backend/test_hud_static.py` (42 passed), `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` (123 passed), `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` (39 passed) and `tools/check_stale_twins.py` (exit 0).

**Not proven.** No real WebView2 window was driven: the field test drives Chromium at one viewport with the two IPC commands stubbed, so it proves the page's edit/save/reload logic against the store's contract - not the Rust store, not the owner's DPI, and not a click with a real mouse on the ghost. The ghost's dimmed look is in the screenshots and was not measured; whether it reads clearly to the owner is their call, not a test's.
## 2026-10-28 — The deploy tool may not call a patch done on a guess, and the four 2026-10-27 patches get exact rules

**What was measured, not assumed.** The read-only drift audit of the running backend (`.dsh-scratch/AUDITS-NEXT-2026-10-28/LIVE-DRIFT.md`, section 4.3) ran `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` twice against the owner's live folder, dry run only. It found the tool would have **silently skipped `cloud-escalate.patch`**: its presence rule was "any one distinctive added line is already in the live file", and two lines on that patch's **added** side are unchanged signatures the old file already holds - `_says = _api.CloudAnswer(` and `def _lane_names() -> list:` - so a live HUD with none of the patch's three hunks (the standing cloud switch, the honest lane list, the `auto=`/`fallback=` CloudAnswer) read as `ALREADY_PRESENT`. An `--apply` from that plan would have finished `RESULT: PASS` with the cloud-escalation changes absent. The same run refused `f01-manual-lane-gate`, `reminder-actions` and `update-in-chat` for having no rule - safe, but incomplete.

**Decided: presence is PROVED, never inferred, and an unprovable patch is refused.** A line the patch's own hunks already show in the old text is a re-written line - it is in the file with or without the patch - so it may never decide presence; the probes are the added lines that appear NOWHERE in that patch's pre-image for that file, and a `DELTA_TABLE` entry's explicit probes, all of which must be present. When the tool can prove neither presence nor absence - every line the patch adds is a re-written line - the patch is **REFUSED by name**, never skipped and never inserted on a guess: a second copy of a block is as wrong as a missing one, and either is worse than stopping. The live `_jarvis-state.json` patch list stops being proof of anything: it records what a patcher ran once, not what the bytes hold now, which this PC's hybrid live tree proves. It survives only as a sentence in a refusal, so a human can see it.

**A measured correction to the brief, which named the published base as the reference.** `jarvis-backend/<file>` is a snapshot of the owner's LIVE folder, and that folder already carries the whole patch stack applied - so **132 of the 160 patches in `$PATCHES` have every one of their added lines in it** (measured 2026-10-28: `_PUMP = _ev.Pump(engine=_ENGINE)`, added by `events-pump.patch`, sits at `jarvis-backend/jarvis_hud.py:6307`, and `def _lane_names() -> list:` at 6099). A rule of "absent from the base" would therefore call 132 patches unprovable on ANY live file and refuse the whole deploy. The reference that means what the brief meant is the patch's own pre-image: the `-` and context lines of its hunks. Both lines the audit named are in cloud-escalate's pre-image, which is why the old rule read them as evidence, and both are excluded by the new one.

**The rules, and why each shape.** The four 2026-10-27 patches are carried as their own hunks (`"hunks": True`), because each changes several disjoint regions of one file: `cloud-escalate.patch` (3 hunks) and `f01-manual-lane-gate.patch` (5 hunks) on `jarvis_hud.py`; `reminder-actions.patch` (`schedule_action` in both gate places) and `update-in-chat.patch` (`desktop_update` in the never-a-standing-rule set) on `jarvis_gate.py`. Order matters for one pair and is already the stack's: F-01's hunks 2 and 3 rewrite cloud-escalate's post-image, so cloud-escalate must be applied first, and `$PATCHES` puts it immediately before F-01. Cloud-escalate's region-1 probe is a line of its own comment block, because F-01 rewrites the `owner_said_yes=(` code line below it - a probe there would make a fully deployed pair look like a missing patch on the second run.

**What did not change, and the limits said plainly.** The ref guard stays: the tool still refuses to run from a checkout whose HEAD is not `--ref`, so the procedure is a `git worktree` at `origin/main`, dry run, `apply-patches.ps1` while anything is refused, restart, dry run again until 0/0 - written out in `docs/DEPLOY.md` section 2. A patch with **no** `DELTA_TABLE` entry is still judged by "any one base-absent line is present": that rejects unchanged context, but it is not a byte-exact proof, and a half-applied patch of that kind could still read as present. **The tool was not run against the owner's live folder by this change**, so a dry run there may now name patches the old state-file fallback used to wave through; each is either genuinely absent (the patcher is then the route) or present-but-rewritten (add a rule).

**Proven by.** `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py`, 375 checks, all on temporary folders: the trap pinned on the published base itself (the removed rule calls a file that cannot contain the patch present), cloud-escalate absent refused rather than skipped even when the patch list records it, each rule's staged text **byte-for-byte** what `git apply` makes of the same patch on the published base, a second run reporting `ALREADY_PRESENT`, a shifted live file refused, and a runtime proof that the CLI refuses to start without `--backend-path`. `tools/check_vacuous_checks.py`, `tools/check_no_source_pins.py`, `tools/check_stale_twins.py`, `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` (123 passed), `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` (39 passed) and `tools/check_docs_map.py` are clean. **Not proven:** anything about the owner's live folder's current bytes - that is the next dry run's job, at the desk.
## Decisions written as `decisions.d/` fragments, folded in here in date order

From 2026-10-28, a pull request records a new decision as ONE file under
`decisions.d/` (`decisions.d/README.md` says how) and does not edit this file.
`tools/roll_decisions.py` folds those fragments in below this heading, at the end
of the file and in date order, and removes the fragment files. The roll is
deliberate and is never run by a feature pull request. This heading is that
tool's anchor: do not rename or remove it.

- **2026-10-28 — An approval card shows no time limit; a request whose wait ended is swept:** the owner ruled today, about approval cards: **"if there doesn't need to be a time limit don't have one."** This supersedes the half of the 2026-10-23 ruling (Q1) that kept every routine card on a visible 15-minute countdown. Q1's own record says why a limit existed for the cards it refused to exempt - **"a stale 'yes' on a card that loosens a rule is a time bomb"** - and that record also says its original wording "is not recoverable from the repository", so both halves are quoted here rather than paraphrased. **A first version of this change went too far and review caught it** (Gemini's F3, ruling f): removing #965's read-time sweep left a timed-out request's card in `/api/pending` with a live Approve that was guaranteed to fail with `409 LATE_APPROVAL` after Windows Hello - a "zombie Approve button" that regressed the "4 WAITING ON YOU" cards #965 had just removed. **The shipped synthesis:** (1) no screen draws a countdown and `pending()` sends no `expires_in` for any card - while a request is genuinely waiting, its card shows Approve and Deny and no clock; (2) **#965's read-time sweep is kept**, re-keyed on the moment the request stops waiting, which is written on the row as `waited_until` at the INSERT: once that plus the same 60-second grace has passed, `pending()` marks the routine row `expired` before it builds the list, so no client is handed a card whose Approve can only answer 409. It is a lapse, never a decision, and it is recomputed on the PC at the read; (3) the four ceremonies of the 2026-10-23 ruling (`pair_device`, `unretire_shared_key`, `register_approval_key`, `restore_backup`) carry `waited_until = NULL`, are never swept, and their request waits until its own flow withdraws the card, so they stay answerable as long as the owner needs; (4) the late-approve 409 stays as a race guard - inside the grace a stale page can still tap, and `_wait_open()` refuses it, `still_waiting()` answers the same question read-only, `decide()` refuses the APPROVE, and `jarvis_owner_check.approve_check()` answers 409 with one plain sentence ("That card is not waiting for you any more: the request that asked has finished, so nothing can be approved from it. Nothing was changed - ask Jarvis again if you still want it.") and withdraws the card at that moment, so it leaves rather than lingering. **A DENY always works**, including on a card whose request is gone: refusing is the safe direction and is how the owner clears an old card. **Why a literal "no time limit" was refused:** the thread that waits for an answer is the thread that runs the action. Holding it for ever is a resource leak on a `ThreadingHTTPServer`, it makes "Stop everything" unable to interrupt a wait, and a dozen modules (`jarvis_vault`, `jarvis_voice_enroll`, `jarvis_voices`, `jarvis_speech`) compute their OWN waits from `approval_timeout_seconds` and would give up while the card lived - the exact "approved, nothing ran" pair this project refuses to produce. **Nothing else is relaxed:** no card is ever auto-approved, no control approves more than one card, no client clears anything, nothing runs without a person, the Windows Hello / signed-approval receipt is unchanged, and there is no new public route. **Costs, said plainly:** inside the 60-second grace a card can still be on a screen whose queue was read just before `waited_until` passed, and a tap then answers 409 with the sentence (the race guard, not the routine path); a late Approve is refused rather than honoured, because nothing is left to run it; and a backend restart does not preserve a card whose request died with it. **Reality checked, not assumed:** the connect-account and credential hand-off cards are NOT gate cards - they are host-side in-memory cards with their own short TTL (`jarvis_connect_account.CARD_TTL_S`, `jarvis_secret_handoff`), they never enter `/api/pending`, and no request thread parks on them, so `APPROVAL_NEVER_EXPIRES` cannot and does not cover them; they keep their own TTL and are untouched here. Built in `backend/no-deadline-cards.patch` (applied after `no-expiry-cards.patch`), the shipped `backend/jarvis_owner_check.py` (+ its `jarvis-backend/` twin), and client copy on the desktop bar/widget/HUD and the phone; proven by `backend/test_gate_no_deadline.py` (70 checks: a routine card still pending inside the grace with no `expires_in`, the read sweep taking it after `waited_until + 60` so no live Approve is left, a late approval refused with those words and cleared, a deny still working, the four ceremonies answerable a day later and never swept, a withdrawn card gone, dead-process rows settled at start-up and on the next read, and no duplicate-request swallowing), with `test_pending_expiry_on_read.py` kept as the evidence for #965's sweep in the patch that introduced it.

- **2026-10-28 — Connect an account by talking, with a secure pop-up (supersedes the 2026-10-22 Settings-only rule for the calendar and GitHub):** The owner asked, verbatim: *"if I need to put in a password a notification will pop up ... it should be able to connect all features just through me talking to jarvis"* — and the answer he had been given, *"jarvis cannot connect directly to external calendars ... Would you like instructions on exporting your calendar to ICS?"*, was false about Jarvis, which reads CalDAV and a private iCal link today. Decided: a typed or spoken "connect my calendar" / "set up github" raises ONE card in the desktop HUD that takes the token, the private link, or the CalDAV username and password; the OWNER types them on this PC, a host-only route saves them straight into Windows Credential Manager (and nowhere else — no plaintext fallback of any kind), and Jarvis then runs ONE real test per service and says exactly what it proved. Nothing typed in that card is ever in the chat, the model's context, a tool result, a log line, a file, a database or the clipboard; the model gets no argument for a value and refuses one. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-22 ruling that "Accounts and API keys are never typed or spoken" **for exactly three services** — the private iCal link, CalDAV, and the GitHub token — because the card types the value on the PC, which is the same act Settings performs, not a second one; every other account (email, Notion, Obsidian, the search and chatbot keys, Home Assistant) still gets the Settings-only answer, unchanged. It also fixes a rule 3 breach found by the same audit: the CalDAV username and password and the GitHub token had no Credential Manager entry at all and were read only from plain-text Windows user environment variables. Deliberately NOT done, and still forbidden: a password spoken or typed into the chat; the phone sending a credential (there is no phone card and no phone route); any Google or Microsoft OAuth flow; a public tunnel; a second store. The record is JARVIS-API §162, `journal: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8's connect-account row, and `backend/test_connect_account.py`.

- **2026-10-28 — The Galaxy's look becomes a shared setting, reversing the written per-device rule, because the owner asked for his devices to look like one another:** the owner's words were *"including changing the jarvis face model and galaxy models"*, said one sentence after he asked that the voice be the same on the desktop and the phone - so this is the appearance half of "the same Jarvis wherever I look at it", not a new idea of mine. **What it replaces, in writing:** `galaxy-presets.js`'s own comment said the look was "a DEVICE display choice, in the same place and spirit as the theme ... never sent to the PC and never written to the backend", and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 (2026-10-27) recorded that the eight looks "write ONE `localStorage` key (`jarvis.galaxy.preset`), add no route, no command and no phone surface". That design was honest but it had a gap the owner could see: no device can read another device's `localStorage`, so a look chosen on the PC could never reach the phone, and the phone's Galaxy picture was always the same shape whatever the PC drew. **What it becomes:** `galaxy` is one more key in the `appearance` document the face already uses - same merge (a key that is present replaces, a key that is absent keeps), same server-stamped `updated`, same `appearance` event, no approval card - and the HUD's Look switch writes it through ONE new narrow Rust command (`hud_set_galaxy_look`), proved against `galaxy-presets.js`'s own list inside the existing `hud-faces` set. The server reads the look ids from that module rather than keeping a list of its own, and refuses an id no renderer knows instead of storing a choice that would be in effect nowhere. **The phone draws the look**, which is what makes the shared key mean anything: seven layouts ported from `galaxy-presets.js` into `GalaxyLayouts.kt` and held to the JavaScript's exact numbers by a regenerated contract fixture (`tools/gen_galaxy_picture_cases.py --check` joins CI) plus `GalaxyPictureTest`, and an Appearance-screen picker so a look chosen on the phone is the look the PC draws. **What is deliberately NOT reversed:** the desktop theme, the face's sharpness/frame rate/speed and the face's size on each screen stay per device - they are tastes about one screen and neither app can draw the other's - and the phone still cannot draw the desktop's default `constellation`, because that is the PC's own physics simulation. Rather than substitute silently - the failure `docs/APPEARANCE-SYNC-PROPOSAL.md` §2 calls the worst of the three outcomes, "a phone quietly showing one face while the desktop shows another" - the phone draws its zen ring for that one and the Galaxy plate says in words which look is on screen. **Honest limits of this decision as it lands:** the Brain window's own look switch still writes the device key, so it follows a change on its next load rather than live - a named follow-up, not a silent difference; and the two-way sync is proved by tests (the backend's, the Rust command's, the JVM's and the regenerated fixture), not by driving two real devices, which stays a field-test row.

- **2026-10-28 — The Google Calendar connection is both ways, and the sign-in comes back to loopback only:** the owner was asked "For Google Calendar, which do you want?" (a private iCal link, or real Google OAuth) and chose **"Both at once"** - build both, and let him pick one - which reverses the standing sentence in `jarvis_calendar.py` that "there is no Google/Microsoft OAuth flow here and none is planned". What is built: the private iCal link stays exactly as it is (read-only, `jarvis_calendar.py`, no change to it), and beside it `backend/jarvis_google_calendar.py` adds the Google "installed app" authorization-code flow with a **loopback redirect** - `HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0))`, an ephemeral port, `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback` - so the browser round trip never leaves this PC and there is nothing to forward, which is how rule 2 (never a public tunnel; no ngrok, no Cloudflare Tunnel, no Tailscale Funnel) is kept rather than bent. PKCE (S256) and a random `state` are required, the state is compared with `hmac.compare_digest` on the callback, and a wrong or missing state is refused WITHOUT exchanging the code - a callback that did not come from the tab this flow opened saves nothing. Scopes: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events` alone, the narrowest scope that can list, create, change and delete events; `calendar.readonly` is deliberately not requested. `access_type=offline` and `prompt=consent` so Google hands back a refresh token every time. The refresh token goes into Windows Credential Manager (`Jarvis Backend/Google Calendar refresh token`) through the existing `jarvis_token_store.WindowsStore`, the client secret into `Jarvis Backend/Google Calendar client secret`, and access tokens live in memory only - never a file, a log line, a route answer, a card, a model prompt or the phone, and both tokens are registered with `jarvis_scrub` by value. The client ID is not a secret and sits in `google-calendar.json` beside `accounts.json`; that file refuses any secret-shaped field. Writes: creating, changing or deleting one event raises ONE approval card at tier `ask` showing the exact event, and nothing is sent to Google before the yes; a denied, timed-out or refused card sends nothing; a change or a delete is refused as stale when the last read of the calendar is more than five minutes old or the event was not in that read (rule 4). Reads are card-free. One-time setup is `docs/GOOGLE-CALENDAR-SETUP.md` plus three commands (`client`, `mode google`, `connect`), because the Settings window has no door of its own to the backend and every Settings card in this program is a Rust command in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, which the parallel account-connect work owns. Deliberately NOT done in this slice, and said rather than implied: the Settings row, a model tool, and anything on the phone. Google's own limit is written down rather than hidden: `calendar.events` is a sensitive scope, so a "Testing" app works for the owner alone and Google deletes its refresh token after about 7 days, and publishing it needs Google's verification review.

- **2026-10-28 — One voice, one setting, and it is the one that is heard:** The owner reported, in his own words: *"when i change the jarvis voice in the android app it still stays the same in jarvis live in the android app. it needs to be consistent, including across gemini on desktop and android. if i change voice on desktop jarvis it should change it on android jarvis and so forth."* The cause was a second, hidden decider: `jarvis_speech.tts_voice()` asked the chosen personality first (`jarvis_manner.voice_for_speech`, added with the personality presets on 2026-10-23) and returned the preset's fallback voice and pace **before** it ever read `jarvis_voices.speaker()` — so with a preset chosen (his PC has "Classic British Butler" with the voice lock at its default, ON) both apps' Voices screens, `voices/state.json` and the `voices` event all said one voice while every spoken sentence, Live's included, was made in another. Live was never a second path: the phone's Live reply asks the same `/api/voice/say`. Decided: the built-in voice and the speaking speed are ONE PC-wide setting (`voices/state.json`), every spoken sentence on this PC is made in it (`jarvis_speech.tts_voice()` reads `jarvis_voices` and nothing else), and a chosen personality **applies** its voice INTO that one setting (through `jarvis_voices.set_speaker_name`, the same function the two apps' pickers call) instead of overriding it at speech time — so the screen, the event and the sound are one value whichever app or person changed it last, and a voice changed in either app is heard on both. Turning "switch Jarvis's spoken voice" on now applies the preset's voice straight away rather than waiting for the next personality switch, and the answer names the voice, so nothing changes silently. A temporary chat's personality still changes words only: the voice is PC-wide, and a chat that is not saved must not change the machine. Two small losses, said plainly rather than hidden: a preset's own pace (`voice_speed`, 0.94–1.1) is no longer applied, because a pace on this PC is one of three choices (slower, normal, faster) and a preset's own lands on "normal"; and the phone's Live screen gains one line naming the voice it is speaking in (and saying plainly when the PC has no voice engine and Live is using the phone's own offline voice, which no PC setting can change) — the desktop's Live needs no such line, because Settings → Voice is on the same machine. No new route, no approval card (a voice is cosmetic, like the speed and the manner), no client-side speech-to-text, and nothing recorded.

- **2026-10-28 — "Pair with your PC" goes inside Settings, Devices, not as a Settings row of its own:** The owner reported a Pixel 9 that would not pair and a Settings screen with "nothing for pair/reconnect to the PC". The gap was real, and the smallest honest fix was not a new `item(key = ...)` row: it is a Primary action inside the existing Devices card, drawn in both of that card's branches. Three reasons. First, that card is where the phone already talks about pairing - its own sentence tells the owner to "press Pair a phone in Settings, Devices, on your PC" - and it is the card Settings search already surfaces for the word "pair", so the button lands where someone looking for it is already standing. Second, the card's only pairing-adjacent control today is "Unpair & clear the token", which destroys the very thing the owner was trying to establish; putting the safe action directly above it, in the same card, is the pairing of opposites that was missing, and it keeps the destructive one last. Third, a new row would have moved `SETTINGS_ITEM_INDEX`, the jump list, the search labels and `jarvis_settings_registry.py`'s section table - four hand-kept records that `SettingsJumpTest`, `SettingsSearchTest` and `backend/test_settings_registry.py` hold in step - to say something the Devices card was already the right place to say. Nothing is loosened: the button starts the same re-pair the Platform checks screen already starts (`repairing = true`), it opens the same pairing screen, pairing still needs the PC's own card approved with Windows Hello, the old token is put back if the new pair does not connect, and no token is sent anywhere new - the phone still only ever sends it to the PC it pairs with. The one wording this replaces is the card's claim that a PC it had not reached "does not have a device list yet": `Devices.notShown` now tells "cannot reach your PC right now" apart from "reached a PC too old to serve the list", because the first was being reported as the second on the one card that could have said what to do instead.

- **2026-10-28 — The personality presets are one PC-wide list, chosen on both apps; only the editor stays on the desktop:** the owner asked "make sure the presets for jarvis personality and other presets are consistent too", after the voice fix that same day. Now both apps draw the same `GET /api/manner` `personalities` array (ids, titles, descriptions, order), mark the PC's `personality` and nothing else, and switch with the same one field `{"personality": "<id>"}`; the PC also rings one `manner` event from its one writer, so an open card follows a change made elsewhere. **Still one-sided on purpose:** the four tuning dials, the "My personalities" save/delete form and Hear Sample are the desktop Settings window's, because writing a personality by hand is deep configuration and the dials are where a character is tuned rather than chosen; the phone names that in one line instead of drawing a second, weaker humour control. - **2026-10-28 — A settings search answers with the sections that NAME what was typed, and a fixed overlay must reserve its own room:** Two rules came out of Gemini's `F4` on the phone (2026-10-28), both measured there. **Search:** the phone's Settings box filters in the screen's own draw order and never ranks, so a word found in a section's printed prose was as good as a word on a button - typing "pair" returned VOICE, APPEARANCE, DEVICES, because the first two print "Pair with your desktop first - these settings live on it." while Devices carries the button "Pair with your PC". The rule now: a section's heading, the names of the controls drawn on it and the search index's own synonyms are the words it NAMES; its printed sentences are not, and a mention-only match answers ONLY while no section names what was typed (so "pair" answers Devices alone, and "pair with your desktop" still finds the two sections that print it). This replaces "every field is searched as one bag of words, and the screen's order decides the order of the answers". It does not change the four match tiers, `rankPart`, the shared cross-app fixture, or what a section carries; it makes the phone's answer depend on the words the section uses for a thing rather than on where the card happens to sit. The desktop already sorts matches by rank (`compareMatches`) and the phone's own `FindAnything` already scores its rows; this is the Settings box catching up, by the one mechanism a fixed-order `LazyColumn` can offer. **Room for an overlay:** a control drawn over a scrolling screen takes no room from it, so the screen has to keep the room - and the room must be MEASURED, not typed in. The phone's "Needs your OK" line wraps the PC's own card title, so its height changes with the card; `MainActivity` measures the drawn line and `SettingsScreen` adds that height, the line's 12 dp edge gap and 10 dp of air to its own bottom padding (`BottomReserve`). The rule for the next screen that gains a control: reserve the drawn height plus the gap, never a guessed constant, and reserve nothing when the control is not drawn. The overlap it replaces, on the installed APK: the Unpair button at `[90,2058][990,2202]` and the line's top at `y=2064`.

- **2026-10-28 — Make the sentence work: changing the built-in voice by asking is cardless, and both apps follow:** The owner asked *"also can jarvis change his voice if I asked him to in chat?"* A read-only audit answered yes for the voices the pack already has, but only when the local model chose to call the tool - the natural sentence ("change your voice to Ashby") was not a phrase, and the model has no voice control. The owner chose option A, **"make the natural sentence work"**: "your voice", "his voice" and "Jarvis's voice" are now aliases of the `voice_speaker` named choice, and "use the Clara voice" / "switch to the Ashby voice" is a closed-world phrase that only fires on a voice the pack really offers, so the sentence reaches the setting's own setter with no model behind it. It stays **cardless** and PC-wide for the same reason the speed and the manner are: changing which of the built-in voices speaks is cosmetic, it is one `voices/state.json` write and one `voices` event, and both apps already follow that event - so this adds no route, no tier and no card. It deliberately does NOT reach a recorded voice: adding or switching to one needs a clip and the `custom_voice` card, in the Voices screen, and that feature is untouched. It also does not touch the voice-print gate, which is the separate "is it the owner talking" check. An unknown voice name is refused with the real voice names and changes nothing, and the near misses ("change the volume", "use the passive voice") still fall through to the model. Proved in `backend/test_settings_registry.py` and `backend/test_settings_tool.py`; the contract's `voice_speaker` row moves from planned to enforced with that proof, and the Settings directory's example sentence becomes the natural one.

- **2026-10-28 — The two stale HUD pull requests are recovered by comparing trees, not by merging them, and only what `main` is really missing comes across:** #910 and #914 have both been open since 2026-10-27 and both show as DIRTY against `main`, but most of what they carry already landed through the #924 batch and earlier merges, and those merges were squashed so commit ancestry cannot answer what is missing. A three-dot diff is useless for the same reason - its merge base predates the batch - so the check is the actual trees: every file each branch touches, compared blob-for-blob against `origin/main`, and for each one either identical, newer on `main`, or genuinely absent. That comparison leaves exactly two deltas. **The Galaxy's frame budget** (the resolution rule `nextRenderScale` and the every-other-frame cadence that `#910`'s perf commit is the second half of) is new to `main`: no commit there ever contained the rule, because the branch merged `main` into itself and the rule arrived in that merge's conflict resolution, which is the one kind of content a squash silently drops. **The History panel's chevron** is new in the same sense: `main` rotated the caret for a CLOSED group, and since the glyph is a right-pointing chevron that left an open group reading as collapsed beside its own rows. **What it deliberately does not do, and this is the part worth remembering:** it does not take `HALO_LIMIT` (glow haloes off past 120 names), which is also absent from `main`, because it changes what the picture looks like with no test and no measurement against `main`'s newer per-role node builder - a visual change earns its own evidence rather than riding along. It does not take the branch's instanced-link renderer, because `main` superseded it with a newer tested link-plan cache (`state.plans`, `a38ba8cbd`); it does not take the branch's literal-invoke rework of `hud-history.js`, because `main` solved that `check_invoke_grants` problem its own way (`eb2d3321b`); and it does not take any file whose branch copy is a strict subset of `main`'s, which is every one of the two branches' `jarvis_hud.html`, `hud-galaxy-looks.mjs`, `hud.mjs`, `docs/JARVIS-API.md`, `capabilities/hud.json` and changelog fragments. The rule this leaves behind for the next stale pull request: **compare the trees, keep the newer side per file, and never resolve a squashed merge by trusting ancestry** - and when both sides of one file hold real work, take the smaller half that can be tested on its own, not the whole file.

- **2026-10-29 — An attached file is a READ, it is cardless unless reading files asks, and it never goes to a cloud lane:** the owner chose "file attachment in chat" for both apps at once, with the design's recommended defaults (a 2,500,000-byte raw cap, 12,000 characters of text to the model, nothing kept on the PC). Three rules follow, and they are the feature. **It is a read, not a write and not a grant:** the PC reads one file, in the one turn it arrived with, and adds no folder to "Folders Jarvis may look in" - so the turn counts as having read outside text, a card raised afterwards says "Proposed after Jarvis read: the file you attached", a later web search or note write in that chat still asks, and `jarvis_gate.latch_taint` latches the conversation private. **It is cardless because picking the file IS the decision a card would ask for** - the same precedent pictures set on 2026-09-29 - and the switch that already exists decides the one case a card belongs to: `read_files_readonly`, so a PC whose owner set "Ask me first" for reading files will card the attachment too (name and size only, never the contents). A second switch for the same act would be the duplicate the audit rules call out, so there is none, in either app. **It never goes to a cloud lane:** `jarvis_router.choose(has_file=True)` answers gate "file" before the private check, the budget, the complexity check and the offer, the manual cloud pick comes through that same call and is refused with it, and `_open()` strips the `attachment` field off every relay request on every hop - the gate is the brace and the strip is the belt, because `cloud-one-turn.patch` keeps exactly the newest user turn and that is where a file's words would ride. **And it leaves nothing behind:** no upload folder, no temporary file (the converter reads a stream through its new `-` stdin mode), no history row, no log line, no memory fact and no learner input, because the file's words live only in the request they arrived in and are never written into `content`. Deliberately not built, now or later: an upload endpoint, a resumable or chunked transfer, a document preview, a second image path, and any "attach anything" share target on the phone.

- **2026-10-29 — A waiting card is re-read on a 30-second beat on both apps, a failed read is recovered by the next one, and a phone decision says "phone" (narrows the 2026-10-27 "no second poller" rule):** The owner's report: *"when a decision/approval card has already been addressed (approved or denied) on either the Android app or the desktop program, make sure the Android widgets (and every other surface that shows a card/notification) update to reflect that - no stale card left showing, no dead Approve/Deny on a resolved card."* Decided: every surface still takes its queue from the ONE read (`GET /api/pending`), and that read is now also taken on a clock - once every 30 seconds, and **only** while a card is actually waiting on a CONNECTED link, on the phone (`QueueBeat.due` → `refreshPending`) and on the PC (`stream.rs`'s `queue_beat_due` → `refresh_pending`) - because the `approval` event every surface relied on is a poller diffing ids on the backend's own pump: it publishes only on change and catches its own exceptions, so a failed read, a backend restart or a pump that is not running rings nothing, and the phone had no fallback at all (a decided card stayed on the home screen with a Deny that could only answer "no longer waiting"). The rule is the SAME TWO conditions the phone already used - a card waiting, and a connected link - and `stale` is deliberately NOT one of them: a failed read is exactly what makes a link stale, and the next successful read is the recovery, so a `!stale` gate switches off the only retry that can clear it (the desktop's first version did that, and one transient `/api/pending` failure held Approve until the hourly reconnect while Deny still worked). A successful read on a connected link now clears `stale` from one shared rule (`queue_read_landed`), which is what the `approval` event already did. This NARROWS the 2026-10-27 decision's "no second poller" to what that decision was actually about: a *background* refresh that wakes a phone to fetch a queue nobody is showing, or a poll of an idle PC. This beat starts no service and wakes no widget, reads nothing when the queue is empty, and can neither approve nor deny - it is the same 30-second safety net the HUD page has carried since before that decision (`jarvis_hud.html`'s `setInterval(() => apprPoll(), 30000)`), now the same number on all three surfaces so "how stale can a card be" has one answer, and it is the documented exception to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §6's "from the pump and nowhere else" (two 30 s pending reads run on the PC while the HUD is visible and a card waits, deliberately: either can fail without silencing the other). A 2026-10-30 adversarial review hardened the two silent-failure halves and fixed the bound: the PC's beat cannot move the stream's 70-second silence deadline any more (the deadline is absolute, `last_chunk_at + SILENCE_TIMEOUT`, and only a real chunk moves it, so `"Jarvis went quiet"` still fires on a dead socket), and on the phone a queue response is applied only if no newer read has started (`PendingRefreshOrder`), so a slow pre-decision GET cannot re-add a card the owner just answered; and the honest bound is **30 seconds while the app is running and the link is live, up to 30 minutes for a killed phone's widget, and the next event or reconnect while the desktop's stream is down** (a stale-but-connected link recovers on the next beat). Two consequences decided with it: the approvals widget carries `updatePeriodMillis="1800000"` (the board widget's period since it was written), because a RemoteViews drawn by a killed process is otherwise held by the launcher for ever and a cold redraw must say "Not checked yet" rather than draw a card it cannot vouch for; and the phone sends `"by": "phone"` on BOTH `/api/approve` and `/api/deny` from one constant (`SignedApproval.BY`), closing the open disagreement in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §7 - the route does read `by` and stores it as `decided_by`, so the phone's old `{"id"}`-only body inherited the `"hud"` default and every phone decision was recorded as the browser HUD's. Deliberately NOT done: no new route, no push channel, no service started from a widget draw, no client-side "clear expired" control, and nothing that decides anything by itself. The record is `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3's "A decided card leaves every live surface within 30 seconds; a killed phone's widget is bounded by 30 minutes", `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §3/§7, `backend/test_decided_by_attribution.py`, `QueueBeatTest`, `PendingRefreshOrderTest`, `WidgetStatesTest`, `SignedApprovalTest`, `ApiContractTest` and `stream.rs`'s beat, silence and recovery tests.

- **2026-10-29 — A bigger face, and the hidden Galaxy's space belongs to it:** the owner's own words on installed 0.2.356 were "the Jarvis face models are too small on the HUD" and "when the Galaxy is hidden, the face model should take up that space instead of showing the 'The galaxy is hidden. Your brain map is still here...' description + 'Show the galaxy' button". **What was decided:** the three face-size steps keep their names and their control but move up one rung each - Small 1x, Medium 1.25x, Large 1.5x, where Small is the size Medium used to draw and Medium is what Large drew - and the shells' own bases are unchanged except Studio's, whose 48px "dock face" was the one the owner was looking at and is now 120px. With the picture hidden, Studio's Inspector column is collapsed and its space is the face's (a centred 200px x the device's step); the paragraph that used to fill that space is not drawn at all, and the way back is one small chip in the stage bar plus the existing Galaxy options toggle. **What it replaces:** the 2026-10-28 decision that set the three steps at 0.75/1/1.25 on each layout's own base and left Studio a 48px face - the steps are the same idea, one rung higher, and the per-layout bases still own their own numbers, so nothing about the control, the storage key (`jarvis.face.size`, this device only) or the "the layout reserves the box" rule changes. It also replaces the 2026-10-27 hidden-galaxy place holder, which deliberately filled the empty stage with the words and a button: the owner has now said the opposite, so the sentence stays only for a screen reader and the space goes to the face. **What it deliberately does not do:** it does not add a second face renderer (the Ambient and Cockpit shells show one view at a time, so with the picture hidden THEIR Galaxy view is simply empty with the same chip - the face lives on the Talk view there, and this is the one place the change is Studio-only); it does not touch the phone, which has a read-only Galaxy picture and no hide at all; and it does not change what "hidden" means - the picture, the dots, the legend and the trace still go, and the choice is still per device with no route, no command and no approval card.

- **2026-10-29 — A new HUD card must be reachable from Edit HUD, including for an owner who already saved a layout:** The salvaged HUD slice had deliberately kept the calendar out of the layout registry, with a written reason: `contract/hud-presets.json` mirrors every preset's cards and belongs to another slice, so a registry row no preset carried would list a control Edit HUD could never place. The owner then made it a standing rule: "every easily-accessible feature must be addable to the main screen from Edit HUD". So the card is a real card - `calendar` in `CARD_REGISTRY`, in `MOVABLE_IDS`, in `CARD_DOM`, in all seven built-in presets, and the contract regenerated from the module. The other half is the one that makes the rule true for HIM rather than only for a fresh install: his own Studio layout was saved before this card existed, and a saved layout document is a closed list, so a card it does not name gets no shell and is listed nowhere. `hud-edit.js`'s `withRegistryCards` therefore puts back any movable registry card a saved document is missing, IN MEMORY only - opening the HUD is not an edit, and the first real change he makes saves the document that by then carries the card. It repairs what is missing and nothing else: a card he hid on purpose is still in the document, so it stays hidden. Recorded because it is the general answer, not a calendar detail: any card added later needs a registry row, a preset row, a contract row and this repair, or the owner cannot reach it.

- **2026-10-29 — A connect question is answered from this PC, never with a secret in chat:** The HUD field test of 2026-10-29 caught four answers that were wrong about this PC, and one of them was dangerous: asked "can you connect my calendar and email" and "what about connecting to a gmail account or google calendar?", Jarvis said connecting Google Calendar "requires a refresh token ... tokens are managed in your browser's signed-in account; I cannot retrieve them from here ... generate an OAuth token, then share the resulting code with me". The first sentence got the private-iCal card with the email half silently dropped; the second matched no fast path and reached the 8B model, which invented the rest. The rule now is the project's own rule 3, applied to these words: **a token, an auth code or a password is never asked for in a chat, and the two-way Google setup is not a secret exchange at all** - it is the one-time Google Cloud setup plus three commands on this PC (`py -3 jarvis_google_calendar.py client <client-id>`, `mode google`, `connect`), documented in `docs/GOOGLE-CALENDAR-SETUP.md`, with the sign-in returning to a loopback address on this PC. So a sentence that names a **Google calendar/account or email** is answered deterministically by `accounts_connect` (a read-only intent, no card, no connection) and names the four real paths: Google read/write (the CLI steps), the private iCal link on the secure connect card, GitHub on the same kind of card, and email as not built yet with its IMAP details typed in Settings, Accounts. It deliberately does not raise the iCal card for those sentences - one card cannot answer a question that names two accounts - while a plain "connect my calendar", "set up a calendar bridge for me" and "external calendars like google or outlook" keep the card they have had since 2026-10-28.
