Three more were fixed the same way, from the PC's own state: "change your voice to Ashby" says Ashby and Clara are the two voices made for Jarvis and not made on this PC, in the Voices screen's own `BLENDS_TO_MAKE` sentence, instead of dumping the built-in voice ids - the settings grammar's existing `settings_choice_bad` answer, not a second intent of its own (a blend the pack really offers still goes through the same cardless setter); "what voice are you using" reads `jarvis_voices.speaker_view()`, the same read the Voices screen makes; "how do I pair my phone" names Settings, Devices and "Pair a phone" on this PC and "Pair with your PC" on the phone, both buttons' own words. Two stale sentences went with them: the "Not connected yet" calendar answer no longer names a Google sign-in row that Settings does not have and keeps the `py -3 jarvis_google_calendar.py mode ical` step that chooses the read-only way, and the Appearance card no longer says the HUD always stays dark - the HUD follows the theme, Daylight included. Proved in `backend/test_hud_fieldtest_answers.py`, with `backend/test_calendar_answer.py`, `backend/test_connect_account.py` and `backend/test_google_calendar.py` updated for the sentences that changed hands. It touches no HUD file and no phone code: the HUD and the Kotlin app are another session's files.

- **2026-10-29 — The phone's calendar draws only what the PC actually sent, and the widget keeps its place:** the owner's calendar decision of 2026-10-29 (a full Jarvis Calendar, local only, on by default and disableable; design brief `.dsh-scratch/JARVIS-CALENDAR-DESIGN-2026-10-29/REPORT.md`) reaches the phone as a `CALENDAR` screen, a Settings switch and a home-screen widget, and three things were decided on the Android side to keep it honest. **First, the read window is stated, not implied.** `GET /api/calendar?days=N` only ever answers from the PC's today forward (1-90 days), so a day before today, or a month past the end of what was sent, has not been read at all; the phone now asks for the full 90 days and says "Not read: your PC sent 3 November to 2 February, and nothing outside that is known" instead of drawing an ordinary empty day, and an unread day's number is drawn in the quiet colour. Saying "Nothing on this day" over a day nobody asked about would be inventing a fact, which is the one thing these screens must not do. **Second, the Repeat choices are the PC's own four** - none, daily, weekly, monthly - because `jarvis_local_calendar.RECURRENCES` refuses anything else with a 400: a fifth word ("Yearly" was in the first draft) is a control that looks like it worked and did not. **Third, the widget's own two rules.** It never disappears and never shows a blank square: switched off, it keeps its place and says "Jarvis Calendar is off · tap to turn it on", opening Settings at the calendar's row (the owner's decision D5); under App lock or "Hide memory lists and chat history" it draws one sentence and no title at all, not even a count, because the home screen is public; and on a stale link it says "Not up to date" rather than drawing yesterday's list as today's. Its date line comes from the PC's own window rather than the phone's clock, so just after midnight - before the launcher's half-hourly tick - the date and the events under it agree instead of disagreeing. The tap opens the calendar screen itself, by action, not the app's Home. Deliberately NOT in this slice, and said rather than implied: a week view (the brief's phone design is a month grid over a day list, and a second grid was not in it), reminders that ring (the owner's D3 stores `remind_minutes` and rings nothing, so the box says "Saved with the event. Nothing rings yet"), recurrence beyond the PC's four words, and any desktop or backend file - the HUD card, the four routes and the registry rows are the other slices'.

- **2026-10-29 — Jarvis's own calendar is on by default, and one local event at a time needs no card:** The owner asked for "a full fledged easy to use calendar built into Jarvis ... disabled but on by default", local-only and shown beside Google Calendar and iCal, never synced out. Two decisions are recorded here. **First, adding, changing or deleting ONE local calendar event is cardless**, and it is the "One job on the schedule" row of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s cardless table extended, not a new class of exemption: one event per request, no list form, no delete-all and no bulk anything, the audit line carries ids and outcomes only and never the title, place or note, and rule 4's stale-link hold still blocks acting while the event stream is stale wherever the write is drawn. The reasoning is the same as the schedule's - it writes one row on the owner's own PC, changes nothing outside it, and stopping or undoing only makes things quieter - and the write still rides the server's existing origin and token checks, with no new permission model. **Second, the calendar is ON when no settings file says otherwise**, because the owner asked for on by default; OFF hides every surface, refuses writes in words and KEEPS every event, and a damaged settings file is OFF with the reason said rather than a silent on. **The store is wall clock, never an epoch:** `date` and `time` are the record and the epoch is computed on read, so a 09:00 event stays 09:00 across a daylight-saving change; that is the same rule `jarvis_schedule`'s own docstring states for a daily 07:00. What this deliberately does not do: no Google or iCal merge, no invitations, no sharing, no reminder that rings (the field is stored for later), no per-occurrence edit of a repeating event, and no screen in either app yet - S1 is the store, the four routes, the switch and the records, and the HUD card, phone plate and widget build against the contract in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §164.

- **2026-10-29 — The main screen holds one shared catalogue of feature cards:** The owner's requirement, in their own words: "for features that I would like EASILY accessible in jarvis desk jarvis Android app, make sure I can add them to the main screen through the edit jarvis hud on desktop and make an equivalent edit android hud for the android app." **The contract decided here.** (1) ONE catalogue of feature cards, keyed by the feature's own id in `features/features.json`, so a card can never name a feature that does not exist; 24 cards today, each with which apps draw it, its default, its size and its smallest size. (2) ONE shared choice - a `{version, cards:[{key,on,order}]}` document - that both apps read, so the owner's arrangement is the same on the PC and the phone rather than two separate layouts. (3) Two screens that draw it, each in its own geometry. **What this slice builds:** the catalogue, the one reducer (`applyHomeAction`), the Edit HUD panel, and the main-screen strip - desktop only, with the choice kept in the HUD window's own store. **What it deliberately does not do:** the catalogue contains NO safety surface (approvals, Stop everything, app lock, What asks first, the stale link), so ruling 25's "a layout may never hide the one surface a pending approval must reach" is a property of the data instead of a check somebody could forget. **Why no new permission tier:** a card changes nothing about what Jarvis does - it is a door to a screen that already exists - it raises no approval card, it cannot hide a safety surface, and the document is bounded by the catalogue. It is the same class as `theme` and `hud_layout`, which are saved with no backend call, no pairing token and no approval card. **Still open:** moving the document into the PC's settings store and publishing it at `GET`/`POST /api/home-cards` so the phone reads the same choice, and the phone's own equivalent Edit Android HUD screen; `docs/HUD-MAIN-SCREEN-CARDS-2026-10-29.md` section 7 is that work order.

- **2026-10-30 — Jarvis builds sideloadable Android apps from a fixed template, and every command is a card:** The owner asked *"can jarvis build android apps? that i can sideload into my phone? if not add them"*. Decided: yes, in the narrowest way that ends with an app on the phone. A model writes only a page and a few validated values; the Gradle files, the manifest and the Kotlin activity are a FIXED template in `backend/jarvis_android_builder.py`, so the model cannot add a permission, a dependency or a network address, and the generated app declares **no permission at all** - no internet, no files, no route back into Jarvis. Every COMMAND is its own risky card, because a git worktree is not a sandbox for a program (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11): `app_build_android` runs exactly `<task copy>\gradlew.bat assembleDebug`, and `app_install_android` runs exactly `adb install -r <the apk inside that copy>` by full path - no `adb shell`, no uninstall, no serial, no free-form argument. Both are tier `ask`, both say "no undo", both ask for Windows Hello on the PC and the screen lock on the phone, and a denial never becomes a standing rule. **A first build fetches dependencies from the internet and the card says so, naming the three hosts**: about 130 MB of Gradle (checked against its SHA-256 before it runs) plus the Android Gradle plugin from Google's Maven; it is a download, so nothing of the owner's is sent, and a build that exits 0 without an APK is a failure, not a success. **The debug key only** - there is no release signing here - and **sideload only, never the Play Store** (rule 5). The routes are PC only because the SDK and the phone's cable are on this PC, and the two cards reach both apps; there is no app screen for either. Deliberately NOT done: a per-app icon (it needs a binary resource-table edit), any second command, any release signing, any Capacitor/npm route, and any network capability in the generated app. Record: JARVIS-API section 166, `docs/APP-BUILDER-DESIGN.md` milestones C/F/G, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8, `backend/test_android_builder.py`, and the scratch research note `.dsh-scratch/ANDROID-APP-BUILDER-2026-10-30.md`.

- **2026-10-30 — The settled picture-in-picture design is built on the phone, and only for the phone:** the owner chose to build it next, from the design whose questions he had already answered on 2026-10-11 (`docs/PIP-DESIGN.md` §9): its own Settings row "Picture-in-picture" (`pip-mode`, Off / The face and the answer / The conversation / Jarvis Live) next to "Floating Jarvis" with both allowed on at once; a dimmed face and the owner's own sentence "Hidden while Jarvis is locked." whenever "Hide memory lists and chat history" or App lock hides content; a running Live session takes the window over by itself and gives it back when Live ends; and Expand is the only action, because a PiP window never approves anything and never becomes a second Settings surface. Built as written, in the phone app only: Android's picture-in-picture is an OS window over other apps, and the desktop's nearest equivalent is the floating face over other windows - its own window, not an OS-managed miniature of the activity - so no desktop half is missing and `tools/check_parity.py` has nothing to classify. Choices made inside the settled design, recorded rather than hidden: (a) the window is handed CHAT TEXT and the fixed words only - never an approval card, its title, body, plan, recipients, search words or file names, and never the pairing token or a key - so the forbidden-words test proves the pipeline cannot carry one, which is §4.3/§4.5/§5 made structural; (b) hidden content outranks a running Live session, so privacy wins the truth table before §2.4's automatic swap; (c) the state word reuses Home's own short words (Listening / Thinking / Waiting for you / Not connected); (d) auto-enter is off the moment the setting is Off, and the below-Android-12 fallback is written but cannot run on this app's `minSdk` 33. NOT yet driven on a real phone: whether the window appears, what Android's own chrome does to it, the face's frame budget inside it, and whether Expand returns the app are the §7 field steps, still owed.

- **2026-10-30 — The phone keeps the shared debug signing key while it is sideloaded only, and that boundary is accepted on purpose:** Gemini's Q4 ruling on the 2026-10-30 12-hour review put the choice plainly - rotate the shared debug signing key now, or keep it and write down what is being accepted. **Keep it now.** The app is signed with one shared debug key that lives only in the `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64` repository secret (`keystore/README.md`), it is sideloaded onto the owner's own phone and is never listed on Play (rule 5 in `CLAUDE.md`), and its only update path is the in-app check and download from this repository's own `client-latest` release over https, with the APK's certificate checked against `UpdateCheck.SIGNER_SHA256` before Android's installer is offered anything (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`). This is a recorded boundary, not a claim that one shared debug key is a good release key. **Rotating it is not a one-line change:** Android refuses a build signed with a different certificate over an installed app (`INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE`), so the only way through is `adb uninstall com.jarvis.client`, which deletes the app's data - the pairing token and the device id it carries (`TokenStore`, Keystore alias `jarvis_token_key`), the fingerprint/PIN approval key (`ApprovalKey`, alias `jarvis_approval_key_v1`), the three home-screen widget slots' saved choices (`home_widget_*` in the `jarvis_client` preferences), the captured-notifications key, and every local preference - and then the phone has to be paired again with the token from the PC. That is the re-pair ceremony, and it is why the 2026-10-18 decision ("Android signing-key rotation: later, after the current feature work") still stands instead of being quietly dropped. **The boundary must be revisited when any of these becomes true:** the APK is distributed publicly or handed to anyone other than the owner; this repository is made public with its release assets; or the key or the `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64` secret leaks - a leaked key is not made harmless by the certificate pin, because an APK signed with the same key carries the same pin. **The rotation path is now one command, and it never fires by itself:** `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\rotate-android-signing-key.ps1 -Rotate` makes a new keystore OUTSIDE the repository (default `%USERPROFILE%\.jarvis\keys`), refuses to run without that flag, refuses to overwrite an existing key, reads the alias and password from `jarvis-client/app/build.gradle.kts` instead of carrying them (so no password is written into the repository or printed), prints the new certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint and the exact remaining steps, and changes nothing else - no secret, no CI, no phone, no publish. `docs/DEPLOY.md` section 5 is the same ceremony in writing, with what the uninstall deletes and what only the owner's phone can prove.

- **2026-10-30 — An attached file is read on this PC only, and that is enforced rather than promised:** an attachment's words are private local-only content, and four rules now hold it there. **The owner's own permission decides whether it is read:** the read is put through `jarvis_gate.check("read_files_readonly", …)` - the SAME row `file_read` and "Folders Jarvis may look in" use, the one the owner sees as "Ask me first" for reading files - BEFORE a byte is decoded; its card (only when that row says ask) shows the file's name and size and never its contents, `never` refuses with no card, and a gate that cannot answer refuses rather than reading (no second permission model, no new switch). **It never goes to a cloud lane:** `jarvis_router.choose(has_file=True)` answers gate "file" before the budget, the complexity check, the offer and the manual pick, and `_open()` strips the `attachment` field from every message on every relay hop, so even a request that ignored the gate cannot carry a byte of it out. **It is never stored in history or a backup in plaintext:** `jarvis_chat_log.strip_attachment_fields` takes the field off a copy of the request before the history module reads any message, so the encrypted row holds only the owner's own words - no byte, no base64, not even the file's name - and `jarvis_backup.py` leaves a settings file that somehow held a body out of the `.jbak` and names it in `excluded_settings` rather than carrying it silently. **The latch is the conversation's, not the PC's:** the turn marks the conversation that carried the file private through `jarvis_chat_log.note_outside` (the mark a picture's words set), NOT the process-wide `jarvis_gate.latch_taint`, so one attachment keeps that chat local without keeping every other conversation off the cloud lane. Proven by `backend/test_attached_file.py` (the gate is asked before the bytes; a file turn with a cloud lane enabled is local and the outbound payload holds no attachment and no earlier turn; the conversation is marked private), `backend/test_chat_log.py` (the stored row, decrypted, is the owner's words only) and `backend/test_backup.py` (the archived history row and every archive member are scanned) - docs/JARVIS-API.md section 163 is the contract. This refines the 2026-10-29 "an attached file is a READ" entry with how the promise is enforced after the 2026-10-30 review.

- **2026-10-30 — An answer the app does not understand is refused, never drawn as the owner's real day:** The calendar's read had the shape of a fail-open that this project keeps finding: `readCalendar` in the HUD page tested `available !== false`, so every object it did not recognise - the single-event answer `{"ok": true, "event": {...}}` that `?id=` returns, a bare event, an empty body - came out as an AVAILABLE calendar with no events, and the card drew "Nothing in the next 7 days". An empty day is the most reassuring possible lie about the owner's own calendar, and it is unknowable from an answer nobody parsed. So the rule, recorded here because it is general: a client draws a feature's state only from a shape it POSITIVELY recognises. The page now requires a real boolean `available` and, when it is true, an `events` array; anything else becomes `available: false` with its own sentence and draws nothing, and the sheet says the same thing rather than inventing an empty week. The two write handlers had the same bug one step further on - `reply.ok === false` read an answer with no `ok` at all as a SUCCESS and said "Event added." over a write that may never have happened - so they now require `ok: true`. The Settings command applies the same rule in Rust: an answer that does not carry `on` as a real boolean is an error, never "off" and never "on". The same session added the desktop Settings switch for the calendar, and it is deliberately NOT held on a stale link and raises no card either way: it is a preference on this PC that opens no way out of it, the same class as the Anti-Slop filter's switches, and turning it off only narrows what Jarvis draws - every event stays.

- **2026-10-30 — Put the timer on every card with a limited time:** The owner's ruling, verbatim: **"if there is a card with a limited time of any kind, be sure to put the timer on it."** It came from the same day twice over: his app-builder card ran out while he was reading it, and no screen had counted it down. Decided: a routine card whose REQUEST is still waiting carries the seconds it has left, and every screen counts them down - `backend/show-card-timer.patch`, applied after `no-deadline-cards.patch`, sends `expires_in` (whole seconds left until the row's own `waited_until`, never 0 and never negative, rounded up) and nothing at all for a ceremony card (pairing, an approval key, a restore) or for a request that has already ended; the 60-second grace is not counted down, because no request can act on the card in it, so a clock there would promise what the gate refuses. **What it supersedes, exactly:** only the DISPLAY half of the 2026-10-28 ruling ("if there doesn't need to be a time limit don't have one"), i.e. the sentence "no screen draws a countdown" and the removal of `expires_in` from the read. The CARD's life is unchanged and is still that ruling's: no card carries a deadline of its own, no card is refused because a countdown reached zero, nothing auto-approves, a Deny always works, and the read-time sweep, `still_waiting()`, `decide()`'s late-approval refusal and the 409 with its one plain sentence stay exactly as they were - the timer and the refusal now point at the same moment, which is the point. The desktop words it twice from one place (`countdownWords` in `card-words.js`, and the HUD page's `apprClockWords` held to it by `tests/expiry-parity.mjs`); the phone's own instrument readout ("EXPIRES IN 00:43" / "EXPIRING SOON" in the last minute, with the thin bar) lights up again and its last-minute rule is one pure function (`countdownReadout`) so a JVM test holds it. Not verified on a device or in a live deploy: the phone's Kotlin is compiled by CI only (`phone-unit-tests`), and the owner's gate takes the patch through `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` plus a backend restart, or through `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` once it has a `show-card-timer.patch` delta rule - until then the live app draws the card with no timer, exactly as it does today.

- **2026-10-30 — The deployed context stays 16,384, now measured:** the owner chose "raise deployed context 4,096 → 8K/16K with a measured Modelfile change" from the 2026-10-30 competitiveness audit, and the first thing the measurement found was that the premise was out of date. `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=16384` is already set for the owner's Windows user; both Ollama servers on this PC report `context_length: 16384`; the runner's own command line carries `-c 16384`; and the live chat's model is `qwen3.5:9b` (`%USERPROFILE%\.openjarvis\model-state.json`, and the last recorded turn on 2026-10-29 18:21 ran it at 100% GPU and 39.01 tokens/s). So nothing in the 8K-16K range was left to raise and no live setting was touched. Measured on the owner's PC that night, at request-level `num_ctx` 4,096 / 8,192 / 16,384 with the model alone on the RTX 2060 12 GB: it loaded every time at 100% GPU with 37/37 layers, reporting 5.54 / 5.62 / 5.80 GB, leaving 4,055 / 3,983 / 3,815 MiB free, decoding at 38-43 tokens/s with prompt reading at about 1,200 tokens/s. 16,384 costs 240 MiB more than 4,096 because `qwen3.5:9b` caches only its 8 full-attention layers (the other 24 are recurrent and cache nothing). **What 4,096 actually did is on the record too:** a ~5,019-token prompt reached the runner as 2,050 tokens - half the window - and a marker at its start was gone while the one at its end survived, whereas 16,384 read all 15,409 tokens of a 15,000-token prompt and saw both; and the 1,024-token answer allowance still comes out of the same window (981 tokens of a requested 1,024 from a 15,403-token prompt at 16,384, 984 from 3,112 at 4,096, both stopping at exactly the window edge with `truncated = 1`). **Decided: keep 16,384, change no live setting, and record the limit rather than chase it.** 32,768 and 65,536 were not measured and are not recommended here, although the cache arithmetic suggests they might fit. The repository changed only where it can: `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md` states the measured 16,384 and names `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` in Setup, `backend/jarvis-primary.Modelfile`'s comments stop claiming 4,096, `docs/MEASURED-2026-10-30-CONTEXT.md` carries the numbers, the exact procedure and the undo, and `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` records the figure. No Modelfile parameter changed (it already carried `num_ctx 16384`), no model was created, pulled or removed, no service was restarted, and the live lane on 11436 was never probed.

- **2026-10-30 — The floating face gets a size choice, opens on the cursor's screen, and is clamped fully on-screen; the size lives in the tray, not a new Settings row:** the owner asked, *"can you improve the PC version as well? do research if necessary for picture-in-picture mode on desktop"*. Decided, after reading the existing desktop picture-in-picture window and researching Tauri 2's and Windows' always-on-top/floating behaviour: the face gains four remembered sizes (160/200/240/300 logical px, default 200) stepped by two tray rows under More… ("Floating face: bigger/smaller"), it opens centred on the monitor **under the cursor** instead of always on the primary display, and a saved position is clamped **fully** inside the monitor it overlaps most (nearest monitor when that one is gone) so a monitor change cannot leave it half off-screen. The size choice deliberately does **not** become a Settings toggle: every toggle in Settings is generated from `backend/jarvis_settings_registry.py` and mirrored in both apps' contract fixtures, so a new row would be a cross-app contract change for a desktop-only cosmetic window — the tray is where the face's own on/off row already lives, and this keeps the change to one crate, two menu rows, no new command, permission, route or approval card. This does not change the window's standing promises: always-on-top by default, never takes the keyboard, no visible text box or button, clicks pass through everything except the animal (click-through remains a separate, unchanged switch), and nothing is decided or approved from it. The phone's own "Floating Jarvis" bubble is a different control and is unchanged; no parity entry is needed because the surface is already desktop-only by design (ARCHITECTURE §8). Deliberately left out of this slice, named so the next pass can pick them up: opacity/"solid" variants of the transparent window (would change the window's transparency promise and likely need a compositor-level effect), snap-to-edge (a drag-end decision that needs a window-move listener and a preference), and double-click-to-hide (the window has no command grant of its own by design; hiding stays on the tray, the hotkey and Settings, which are already reachable).

- **2026-10-30 — Chats can be archived from the HUD/Brain and the phone, and delete keeps its confirm:** The owner asked on 2026-10-29 that chats can be archived and deleted, with a confirm step. Delete already existed, so this adds archiving as a **reversible local flag**, not a deletion: the PC's own encrypted history file gains a plain `archived_at` column (NULL while the chat is in the list), `POST /api/history/archive {"id": "<conversation id>", "archived": true|false}` sets or clears it, `GET /api/history?archived=1` lists the archived chats while the ordinary list shows only the ones still out, and every conversation row carries `archived: true|false`. It deliberately raises **no approval card and needs no confirm step**, unlike Delete, because it reveals nothing and sends nothing: no chat word is opened, sealed or rewritten, nothing leaves the PC, and Unarchive puts the chat back exactly where it was. It is the same class of change as a pin or a chat tag, and both apps read the one flag back from the PC rather than keeping a list of their own, so archiving on the phone and archiving on the PC cannot disagree. A fork made from an archived chat is not itself archived: it is a new chat the owner just made.

- **2026-10-30 — Jobs start with no permissions and a grant is answered one job at a time:** Long Fuse's two new routes (`POST /api/jobs`, `POST /api/jobs/answer`, jobs-routes.patch; JARVIS-API §169) follow the owner's existing 2026-10-15 "finish what I already started" rule rather than widening it. Creating a job freezes exactly the capabilities the request names - and the desktop's Work pane names **none**, so a job started there runs with an empty frozen set and parks on its first need. Answering a parked job decides ONE grant for ONE job: it is spent by its next use, a second tap is refused, and a No stops that job at once (it does not sit saying "waiting for you" until the next heartbeat) and writes no rule anywhere - the next job needing the same action parks and asks again. There is no list form and no "allow all". Both routes live beside `/api/jobs/cancel` behind the same origin and token checks, are granted to the desktop in the one `brain-act` set, and are unreachable through the Brain's read allow-list.

- **2026-10-30 — Notification styles: a closed look for the phone's notifications, built by talking to Jarvis:** The owner asked, verbatim: *"does jarvis android have custom animated notifications? if not can you build this feature into it? research on girhub repos or more to find out how to add it? i want them customizable and buildable by just chatting to jarvis"*. Decided: the phone's approval-card and reminder/timer notifications may be drawn in a **style the owner describes in their own words**, built the same way "Widgets you describe" is (JARVIS-API §86): the local model turns the words into **JSON on a CLOSED MENU** and nothing else, plain code on the PC checks it, the phone shows a **preview**, and the style is applied only when the owner taps **Add** — so asking never applies anything, and there is **no approval card**, because a style shows nothing new, adds no button and grants no capability. The menu is `name`, `theme` (six colour NAMES — never a colour value), `figure` (six single characters), `motion` (`none`, `pulse`, `flip`, `spinner`), `speed` (three buckets) and `kinds` (`approval`, `reminder`); the phone owns what each name draws. The animation is deliberately one **Android performs itself** inside the notification — a `ViewFlipper` over two frames and an indeterminate `ProgressBar`, both on `RemoteViews`' allow-list — so it keeps running when the app's process is dead, costs no wakeups, and is never a stream of `notify()` frames (which would need the process alive and meet the platform's enqueue cap). The privacy floor is structural: the spec has nowhere to put an email, a fact, a file or a token; the layout receives only the title and body the notifier already had, already redacted; and while the phone is locked, or App lock or "Hide memory lists and chat history" is on, the styled layout is **not used at all** — the notification is exactly what it was before this feature existed. An approval card still offers **Deny only**, still opens the Inbox, and is still never approvable from a notification. Deliberately NOT done, and named rather than hidden: the owner's real face in a notification (those are GL/Compose drawings, and `RemoteViews` refuses every View class it does not know — it would need pre-rendered PNG frames, a later slice); a style-level sound setting (sound belongs to the notification channel, and the approval routing already chooses the channel); styling the ringing alarm, Live, the chatbot line, the hand-off, the watch line, the wake word or the link's own ongoing notification (an animation there is noise); Android 16's `ProgressStyle` live-progress notifications (a different, ongoing-journey feature); any overlay window or in-app arrival animation (a different feature, and a second surface to secure); and any **desktop** styling — a Windows toast is drawn from Windows' own template, so there is no layout to style (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8). The record is JARVIS-API §167, `backend/test_notification_styles.py`, `jarvis-client/.../NotificationStyleTest.kt`, and the research note `.dsh-scratch/NOTIFICATION-STYLES-2026-10-30-RESEARCH.md`.

- **2026-10-30 — A parking estimate may send a point, and one place name the owner said — never the calendar:** `jarvis_parking.py` talks to three public services, so the boundary is written down rather than assumed. Overpass and Seattle's ArcGIS layer receive a latitude, a longitude and a radius and nothing else; Nominatim (the one lookup that necessarily carries words) receives only the place name the owner himself typed or said - never the calendar event's own LOCATION line, never its title, never a chat message, never a note or a saved fact. The calendar bridge deliberately does **not** geocode by itself: it quotes the venue back locally with the padded window and offers the exact sentence to say, because a calendar entry is private even when the venue in it is public. Every request refuses a redirect rather than following one to a host nobody chose, and while Lockdown is on `jarvis_quick._run_parking` answers in one plain sentence and sends nothing at all. The 24-hour local cache is a plain SQLite file beside the module, deliberately not backed up - its geocode keys do hold the place names the owner looked up - because restoring yesterday's prices would only put an old answer in front of today's question. This replaces an implicit "it is probably fine" with a rule the suite can check, and it is the reason there is no `find_parking` model tool: the six-slot Live budget on the 8 GB card is worth more than a tool that must stay switched off, and `jarvis_quick.py`'s grammar answers the same sentence for zero model tokens.

- **2026-10-30 — The phone approves the same cards the PC checks with Windows Hello, with the phone's own fingerprint:** The owner's ruling, verbatim: *"if there is anything that needs approval for Jarvis on desktop with the Windows Hello PIN as well, make the Android app require a fingerprint to approve the same card - but I can approve the same level of card on Android as well."* Decided: the cards that need the owner's own check are the **same set** on both apps - `jarvis_owner_check.is_risky`'s (not classified, leaves the PC, cannot be undone, or was rushed), one rule written three times and tested against the PC's own answers through `tools/gen_risky_approval_cases.py` - and the check is the same level on each: Windows Hello (PIN, fingerprint or face) on the PC, Android's `BiometricPrompt` (a strong fingerprint, or the phone's PIN, the same check App lock uses) on the phone, with nothing sent when it is cancelled, fails or is not set up. Every one of those cards can be answered on the phone, with a fresh signature over the card when signed approvals are on (JARVIS-API §91), so "the same level" is about the check and never about a card the phone may not answer: the only cards with no Approve there are the PC's own ceremonies (`PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`), which is a decision about where a thing can happen. **It supersedes** the reading that a risky card is a PC's card - that the phone either could not approve heavy cards at all, or could only do so as a lesser, unchecked yes: the phone's own local check was never the weaker half, and the card now says so in words ("Approve asks for your fingerprint or PIN.") instead of "Fingerprint follows". It grants no new way to approve: no new route, no auto-approval, no bulk, no swipe, and no change to the desktop's own path or to what the gate allows. Three limits are on the record rather than hidden: the phone's check is the app's and cannot be verified by the PC for a device still on the old shared key (§90.5), an action with no written words is refused on the PC before any prompt and the phone cannot repeat that refusal because the row carries no field for it, and the real `BiometricPrompt` on a real phone is NOT-TESTABLE at this desk - the phone's own JVM suite compiled and ran on this PC (2,960 tests, 0 failures, six of them the rule above), and only a device can prove the system dialog itself.

- **2026-10-30 — The phone's History gets one filter row behind one Filters button, and More keeps five doors:** the owner sent screenshots of the latest Android app and said *"these both screenshots need further simplification, too many options"*, and when offered choices he picked *"Tuck the rare ones behind one Filters button."* Decided: History keeps one visible filter row (his tags as chips, scrolling sideways) with a Filters button at its end, and everything rare - the conversation kinds, the Archived view, the full tag list with Untagged, the Tags editor and "Forget a time frame…" - moves into ONE sheet behind that button, still combining exactly as they did and still read again the moment a choice is made. The More menu drops to at most five content rows (New chat, Photo, Attach a file, Modes, Quick note) plus Close: Think, Coach this and Incognito move one tap deeper behind a single Modes row, each with its old words, gates and action; Earlier chats is removed rather than duplicated because it opened History and History is the list (Home's status line already opens it in one tap); Pinned messages moves into History's own header as one compact "Pinned" action (the same PinnedScreen, not a copy); and Jarvis Presets leaves More for Home's existing one-tap "Presets →" door. This SUPERSEDES the 2026-10-27 arrangement that put the chats and pins first in More (the record there: "the chat's own three doors open here, first") - the capability is unchanged, the door moved. The conditional Notifications row stays a direct More row on purpose: it is the only door to attaching captured notifications, and behind another sheet it would be three taps instead of two. The desktop app is deliberately NOT changed - these screens are the phone's own History and More, so this is a phone-only simplification, not a half-shipped feature. Nothing new can act and no new route, card, switch or stores a word: every control calls the same callback and the same read as before.

- **2026-10-30 — The phone may type its own town, and the "do it on the PC" limitation goes rather than being explained away:** the owner asked to be able to put his town in "through the android app ... and not have it just limited to the desktop", with a screenshot of Appearance telling him to type it on the PC. That sentence was not an accident: the 2026-09-28 decision said "a town the owner types once on the PC (the phone gets it from the PC)", and the backend enforced it with `jarvis_owner_check.from_this_pc`, answering 403 to any other device so that a stolen token could not move where Jarvis thinks the owner lives. **Widened:** `POST /api/sky {"place": ...}` now accepts a town from either app (`request_place()` no longer consults `from_this_pc`; the parameter stays in the route's signature because the words may one day differ), `view()` says `can_set_place: true` to both apps, and the PC's own words invite the phone (`PLACE_DETAIL`/`PLACE_PHONE`/`PLACE_NONE`) instead of sending it to Settings. **Why this is safe enough to widen:** typing a town sends words only to the owner's own PC over the pairing link; the PC answers from the town list it already carries (`jarvis_sky_places.py`, offline, no geocoding service), keeps only the position rounded to 0.1 degree, and the name is never logged, audited or offered to the model. It adds no route, no egress and no card: the risk the old 403 addressed is a stolen token, and a stolen token can already move the town by asking the PC through the same pairing link when the phone is the thing stolen. **What it replaces, and what it deliberately does not do:** the phone's field waits for a live link (typing a town ADDS something, rule 4), while "Forget my town" stays at once; moving the town while Open-Meteo is on still switches Open-Meteo off, because its ONE card named the old position, and that is kept rather than eased; the desktop's own field and words are unchanged; and no other "type it on the PC" limitation is silently turned on by this entry - each one earns its own decision. Gemini's later ruling that the phone should send `X-Jarvis-Client: phone` rather than `hud` is a separate change and is not part of this one.

- **2026-10-30 — The reseal tool may write the installer's record, but only the rows this repository can prove:** Gemini's Q3 ruling chose `(b')` - put a drifted live install back on `backend/rebuilt/*` plus `$SHIPPED` directly - and that means one tool has to touch `_jarvis-state.json`, which until now only `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` wrote. The decision, recorded because it is a new writer for the thing the whole preflight trusts: **`tools/reseal_live_install.py` owns a record row only when the file it names is one this repository ships**, because then the new hash is `sha256` of a blob in the commit being deployed - a fact, not a guess - and every other key the installer wrote (`written`, `patches`, `patchList`, every row it did not touch) is kept byte for byte, with a `resealed` key added so the record says which tool wrote which rows, for which commit. **A row this repository cannot prove is never rewritten.** The five patched base files (`jarvis_hud.py`, `jarvis_gate.py`, `jarvis_extract.py`, `jarvis_models.py`, `jarvis_skills.py`) are produced by the patch stack, no copy in this repository is their bytes, and writing today's hash there would bless whatever a hand edit or a half-applied patch left - exactly the silence `apply-patches.ps1`'s drift check exists to break. Those rows are printed with both hashes and the run exits 1. `--rebaseline-unprovable` is the explicit way to record them anyway: it is the patcher's own rule for a run with no usable record ("take the current files as the baseline, hashes only", the owner's answer of 2026-10-09), it is off by default, and every row it touches is printed. Two smaller calls ride with it: the tool refuses to run from a checkout at another commit only where it must (every byte comes from `--ref`, so unlike the deploy it needs no worktree guard, and it is run from the branch that carries it until merged), and it reads no `jarvis-backend/` copy of a patched file - that folder is an older snapshot of the same live folder, so copying it would move the file backwards. What this deliberately does not do: repair a patch, run the patcher, restart Jarvis, probe a route, or claim the preflight reaches 0 FAIL on its own - the patch rows move only when the patcher runs.

- **2026-10-30 — An unclassified action is approvable with maximum friction, and CI still demands its row:** Gemini's Q2 ruling, after the app builder's build card could not be approved on the owner's own PC even while he was pressing Approve. The rule, in the owner's own terms: **if Jarvis has not written down what an action can do, it is given the worst case the gate has - it cannot be undone and it can leave this PC - it always asks you first, its card says so in one plain line, and you can still say yes, with Windows Hello on the PC or your phone's own lock.** Nothing auto-approves, nothing approves in bulk, no swipe decides it, and no app or settings switch may loosen it; a yes recorded without that human check is refused by the gate. On the CI side the rule is the opposite direction and stays strict: an action the shipped settings file lets run with nobody asked, and that has no explicit risk row, is a failure that names the action. This replaces the old fail-closed behaviour at runtime, where a card for an unknown action was physically unapprovable ("Jarvis has no written words for this action yet"): that was safe on paper and bricked a real feature on the owner's desk. It does not replace the 2026-10-26 rule that a prompt may only ask about something Jarvis can name - a CLASSIFIED action with no written words is still refused - and it does not give rows to the nineteen ask-tier actions that still have none; their cards keep the warning line instead of a proper sentence until somebody does that work per action.

- **2026-10-30 — A widget's arrangement is one of four fixed layouts, and that list can only grow in a new app build:** The owner asked whether Jarvis could build him custom Android widgets (2026-10-30). The content half already exists ("widgets you describe", §86, 2026-09-28); the look half is limited by Android, not by Jarvis. So a described widget now carries `layout`, one of `stack` (the default, and what every widget made before this date gets), `big`, `list` or `compact`; the PC's own AI model picks it from the owner's words, plain code checks it, and both the desktop widget window and the phone's home-screen widgets draw it by one rule shared through `tools/gen_widget_cases.py`'s generated `widget-cases.json`. The decision worth recording is the LIMIT: Android fixes a widget's layout when the APK is built - the provider is manifest XML and the drawing is `RemoteViews` over the app's own resources - so no route, setting or model instruction can add a fifth arrangement, and "Jarvis, make it look however I describe" is not a feature that can be half-promised. What can change is this list, in an app build; a value off the list is refused by the PC and drawn as `stack` by the apps, so a newer PC's word never blanks a widget. It deliberately does NOT touch the palette, fonts, images, grids or per-widget accent and transparency: those are the separate queued owner decision recorded in this file ("per-widget transparency, accent, high contrast and a live preview"), and half-building them here would have made that queue's own line untrue. Nothing new is approved: same blocks, same sources, the same five Quick Settings tile actions, the same App-lock hiding and the same stale-link gate, and no new route.

- **2026-10-30 — The phone asks the launcher to put a Jarvis widget on the home screen, and never claims it did:** The owner asked, verbatim: *"i want them customizable and buildable by just chatting to jarvis, including the custom widgets by chatting with jarvis"*, and in the field-test instruction: *"jarvos can build a custom wodget through the android app i can add immediately to my android screen"*. Until this slice the app only printed the touch-and-hold route in its hint text, so "immediately" was still three manual steps in a launcher picker. Decided: a home-screen slot that has a saved widget offers **Put it on my home screen**, and the phone calls Android's request-pin API (API 26+, `AppWidgetManager.requestPinAppWidget`) for that slot's own board receiver. The API answers whether the **request was sent**, not whether a widget was placed, so the app's words are three and the asked one never reads as done: that widget is already on the home screen; the home screen was **asked** (a launcher may still show its own confirm, or refuse); or this launcher cannot add widgets on request, in which case the touch-and-hold route is given in words. It adds no route, sends nothing to the PC, raises no card, and changes nothing about which saved widget a slot shows - that stays the slot picker. The three slots, the picker's count and the three receiver names are held equal in one list (`JarvisWidgets.PIN_RECEIVERS`) by `JarvisWidgetsTest`, so a slot can never be offered without a receiver again. Not verified on a device: no phone or emulator at this desk - what is proven is that the app compiles, `assembleDebug` succeeds, and the JVM tests pin every sentence and every receiver; the pin is driven in the field test after deploy and stays NOT-TESTABLE until then.

- **2026-10-31 — The architect's rulings after the six-PR wave (live gate repair, catalogue, chat answers, route contract, preflight baseline):** Gemini's review (`gemini_rulings_after_wave_2026_10_31.md`, answered against `origin/main = 8f7e165d5`) is recorded as one decision. **(a) Live patch lineage, approved, with no general in-place adopt mode:** the 2-hunk `DEF-021-gate-delta` repair (`3e9b8068… → 39a0c407…`) plus `reseal_live_install.py --apply --rebaseline-unprovable` is approved; instead of a patch-stack rewritter, `tools/repair_live_backend_gaps.py`'s `UNKNOWN_RISK` entry is to be folded so it accepts BOTH the 5-hunk #1008 gate and the pre-#1008 gate and brings either one to the 6-hunk #1023 post-image `39a0c407…`, while new features keep the drop-in `install()` plugin pattern so the base files rarely need new patches. **(b) Deletion semantics:** deleting an explicit `[autonomy.tiers]` line returns that action to the tool's built-in default tier (the #1023 behaviour); no hidden tombstone is written, because a config file must not lie to the owner. **(c) Catalogue:** the two new catalogue rows and their Tutorials lessons (36 → 38) are approved, and the "Protected from Jarvis" row's `covers` must carry BOTH `protection` (the settings-registry section) and `settings.protection` (the menu id). **(d) Deterministic feature answers, approved with one guard:** verbatim catalogue quoting (with "Everything Jarvis can do" named at the end) replaces model hallucination; common owner synonyms must map to catalogue rows (`obsidian`/`vault` → notes, `schedule`/`events`/`appointments` → calendar, `block`/`exclude`/`permissions` → protection, `send file`/`download file` → files), and the hard "not one of my features on this PC" sentence is emitted only for a known-unsupported topic or zero catalogue overlap, otherwise with a pointer to "Everything Jarvis can do". **(e) Route-field contract, approved as the long-term shape:** Python classifies the owner's words into a structured route field (`jarvis_open.py`) and the desktop executes it through its existing safe window-navigation commands (`Settings`, `Brain`, `Brain:History`, `Brain:Tutorials`, `Calendar`) - the PR #1028 shape, kept. **(f) Preflight baseline:** `35 pass / 4 fail / 3 warn (5 skipped)` is the authoritative live baseline - the four patch rows stay PARTIAL on the live lineage (`appearance 216/334`, `show-card-timer 10/60`, `cloud-honesty 3/80`, `attached-file 0/30`), while the three base-file hash rows and `unknown-risk-approvable.patch` must PASS; the deploy runbook records this with one sentence saying why those four stay PARTIAL. **(g) Field-test record:** DEF-026 stays in the defect register (and its twin) only, cross-referenced from the desktop calendar matrix row - the matrix tracks features and surfaces, not individual bugs - and matrix row 141 (chat feature Q&A) must read **FAIL (0/4 accurate on 0.2.376; fixed by PR #1030, re-drive owed)**, never a PASS, until the #1030 deploy's live re-drive flips it to PASS at 4/4. **(h) Sequence and owner time:** DEF-023 stays closed (pass 10 already proved it on 0.2.3326, including force-stop + fresh start); merge order is #1029 → #1026 → #1027 → #1028 → #1030 → #1021, then finish #1025's rebase and checks, then ONE combined live deploy with desktop ≥ 0.2.377 and phone ≥ 0.2.3327 and re-drive the machine-testable halves (#1028 "open the second brain", #1030's four chat feature questions, #1027's locked desktop calendar banner, #1021's Today board read); defect priority is DEF-022 → DEF-020 → DEF-017/018/019; and the owner's one short sitting is a Show + fingerprint pass (Mind → Notes save card, History archive/unarchive, The Galaxy), one Protected from Jarvis Add + Remove card (plus one #1025 send-file-to-phone card once it lands), an on-device check that DEF-025 and DEF-026 no longer show the event title before both are closed, and optionally a refresh of the Downloads backup.

- **2026-10-31 — Feature-list claims are checked against files, symbols, routes and real gate actions:** every row in `features/features.json` is prose, so `tools/check_feature_list.py` now verifies its evidence: a path it names must exist, a `module.symbol` must be defined in that module, an `/api/...` route must be carried by `docs/JARVIS-API.md` (or the plugin's own design note/README/module for plugin routes), and a row may never cite a line number. A row that says its feature raises an approval card must carry `gate` naming the action the card is written under, and that action's `[autonomy.tiers]` value must be `ask` - an invented action or an `auto`/`never` one fails. 56 rows now carry gate metadata; the six that cannot yet (the per-fact memory cards, the quiz link and the approvals mechanism itself) are a self-emptying `CARD_GATE_GAP` work list, not a silent pass. The checker's own suite proves a fabricated file, route, symbol, action and wrong tier are each caught. The Gemini round-2 ruling (6) extended it: each row's primary `lesson_id` must exist in `jarvis_tutorials.py`, and every `settings.*` token in `covers` must be a real settings/menu id in one app's registry; both are checked with the same synthetic-row tests that prove a fabricated entry FAILS.

- **2026-10-31 — Creating a brand-new note is card-free; editing an existing note keeps its one card (owner's rule change):** The owner asked Jarvis to "make a new note into my notes without needing an approval card", and hit the old rule when asking "can you write a note?" - the chat wrongly said it could not write without approval. Creating a brand-new note is additive: it cannot overwrite, delete or change anything already there, so it now needs NO approval card - and only for a DIRECT owner write: provenance `typed` or `voice` with `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`, never after outside text, never from a background job, never from another client. The card-free payload is capped at 64 KB; a collision is refused case-insensitively on Windows with `O_EXCL`; the vault sandbox, Protected-from-Jarvis and hidden/`.obsidian`/symlink/junction/`..` refusals are unchanged and tested. Everything that matters still applies: the path must be inside the configured Obsidian vault, a name that already exists is refused instead of overwritten (and the write itself is `O_EXCL`), the undo receipt is recorded BEFORE the file exists so one Undo removes exactly the new file, the bytes are read back, and the protected/hidden/reserved refusals are unchanged. Every change to an EXISTING note keeps its ONE approval card (append, insert, format, replace, customize, rename, move, template save), and deleting a note is still not built. The chat gains "write a note for me about ...", "write me a note with ...", "can you write a note?" (answers yes and how to ask, and writes nothing), "make a new note called X with ..." and "create a note called X and put ... in it"; the owner's words become the body, a title is drawn from them when none is named, and the answer is the module's own "Created ... You can undo it." Hidden lists still create the note card-free, but the reply echoes no title or file name - it says a note was created and nothing more. The follow-up question from the same field test is answered deterministically too: "what folder is it in?", "where did that note go?", "which folder are my notes in?", "where is my vault?" and "where do you save my notes?" now say the configured vault location and, when this process just filed a note, the exact file it wrote (an in-process last-filed record, no new persistent state); with no last note they still give the vault location honestly. They never say the folder name is unavailable and never offer to search the PC's files, hidden lists say the vault location only, and these read-only answers are in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS` so no "Nothing was actually done" footnote appears for them.

- **2026-10-31 — Obsidian customization, wave 3:** The owner asked to really enhance the customizability of notes in Jarvis. Wave 3 adds deterministic surgical edits on top of wave 2: more formatting (strike, inline code), line/checklist conversions, heading rename and new sections, one frontmatter property set/remove, one wikilink, and plain-Markdown templates that can be created, saved and listed. The exactness rule is the owner's: ONE exact match or a plain refusal naming the count - never a guess, never a regex surprise, never a bulk edit. Every write keeps ONE approval card, the File Guardian copy, one Undo, and no note is ever deleted; deleting lines/notes, moving lines between sections and reciprocal links stay unbuilt and are said so plainly.

- **2026-10-31 — A real notes editor for the whole Obsidian vault, in both apps:** The owner was asked whether to build a read-only notes view and answered *"how about option 1 with actual editing?"*, then chose **"The whole vault, both apps"**. Decided: both apps get a Notes surface in the Brain (search the vault, open a note, edit, save), limited to `.md` and `.txt` files inside the configured Obsidian vault. **Every save raises ONE approval card** — the existing gate card, Approve or Deny, never an app-side approval; the File Guardian copies the old bytes before any write; a save whose starting sha256 no longer matches is refused with `conflict` and the current hash rather than overwriting someone else's edit; and **create, delete and rename are deliberately not in this slice**. The phone reaches the same four PC routes and never approves anything itself; its plate sits behind the existing lists' Show gate, with no new bypass. The backend half is a drop-in module (`backend/jarvis_notes_edit.py`, `edit_vault_note` at tier `ask`, four `/api/notes/*` routes) and the two app halves call it; the work is implemented and proved locally on branches and is **not deployed to the live PC** — the live apps do not show it until a deploy pass runs.

- **2026-10-31 — Rename and move notes with link preservation:** The owner's next flexibility item is changing a note's path without breaking the vault. Rename and move now plan, read-only, every link that named the note - `[[old]]`, `[[old|alias]]`, `[[old#section]]`, embeds `![[old]]` and relative Markdown links - show the old path, the new path, the exact counts and (when lists are visible) up to the first three affected note filenames on ONE ordinary `edit_vault_note` card, and after approval change only those link targets. Fenced code blocks and inline code are never rewritten. The File Guardian copies the source and every note whose bytes change, ONE batch Undo restores every byte and path, a missing folder is refused unless `create_folder` is explicit, and protected/hidden/symlink paths, collisions, `..` paths and notes changed while the card waited all write nothing. Deleting notes, moving outside the vault, renaming or moving folders, renaming onto an existing name and cloud sync stay unbuilt; the chat says so plainly. The module keeps one card and one undo, adds no second permission model, and both routes are available to both apps (their screens are owed with the same controls).

- **2026-10-31 — Obsidian surgical edits, wave 2:** The owner asked whether Jarvis can add something to a specific PART of a note, before an anchor, or in bold. Wave 2 builds insert-under-heading, insert before/after a literal anchor, bold/italic wrap and unwrap, and exact replace. The owner's exactness rule governs: ONE exact match or a plain refusal naming the count; never a guess, never a regex surprise, never a bulk edit. Every write is ONE approval card with the exact before/after preview, the File Guardian copy first, and one Undo; deletions are not built.

- **2026-10-31 — Flexibility with the Obsidian vault, wave 1:** The owner asked for a lot of flexibility with Jarvis and their Obsidian notes. Wave 1 builds create one note, append to any existing note, and add/remove one tag, all single-file writes with ONE approval card, a File Guardian copy first where there are old bytes, an undo receipt (a created note's undo removes exactly that file), and the sha256 the change started from. Rename, move, delete and multi-note/batch changes deliberately stay out until wave 2, when the link repairs a rename needs are built; themes, CSS and templates stay Obsidian's own. No note text goes to a model, a card or a log, and the hidden-lists/Show rules are unchanged.

- **2026-10-31 — Pick-a-set mode for the Obsidian organizer:** the owner approved "organize just these notes" (the default stays the whole vault). The organizer's plan route accepts an explicit selection of vault-relative note paths or bare unique names and computes tags only for those notes: no note moves, no Map-of-Content or Vault Home is created (those are whole-vault artefacts), and no other note is read for content. The selection is validated in the module's own words - empty, absolute, traversal, outside, hidden/protected, link, unknown and ambiguous selections are refused and change nothing - and while the app's hidden-lists mode is on the reply and the card carry counts, never note titles. The writer is the existing ONE-card whole-batch route: applying a scoped plan writes only the selected notes (plus nothing else), never deletes, and one Undo restores exactly that batch; a denial writes nothing. Chat says "organize just my Welcome note" / "organize these notes: Welcome, Alpha" for the read-only plan and "apply the plan" for the one card, and the whole-vault mode is unchanged.

- **2026-10-31 — "Protected from Jarvis", a list Jarvis may not touch:** The owner asked for a list of file folders, files and programs "that i can manually add to (or ask jarvis to exclude in chat and get a card) that blocks jarvis from having any access (read or write) or the ability to make certain files or folders or programs read only". Decided: ONE store on the PC (`protected-items.json`), kinds folder/file/program, two modes - blocked (no read, no write, no action) and readonly ("see it, never act" for programs); adding by hand on the PC is immediate because it only TIGHTENS what Jarvis may reach, every removal raises ONE card because it LOOSENS, and a chat add raises ONE card before the store changes. Enforcement is one central check called at every named door (documents, file tools, notes, attachments, File Guardian restore, open, UI control, screen/OCR, schedule, pictures), with the gaps this version cannot close written down plainly in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §170.5 rather than left silent. Both apps read the list; the phone's Remove asks the PC for the same card, and the phone cannot add from Settings because it has no PC file picker - that one route is the desktop's alone on purpose (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8). Implemented and proved in this repository, not deployed to the owner's live PC by this change.

- **2026-10-31 — Jarvis knows which app the owner is talking from:** The owner's requirement: "Jarvis must know whether the owner is talking from the Android app or the desktop program, and tailor its answers/features accordingly — and this must work by default (no setup)." Measured before this change: the phone still sent only the legacy `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`, so the PC could not tell the two apps apart and no answer named the app. Decided: both clients add one additive header, `X-Jarvis-Surface: phone` / `desktop`, beside the unchanged client header (which the origin and cloud-escalation rules still read); the shipped origin gate reads it once per request; the deterministic quick answers, the feature guide's own `surface`/`where` fields and one model system sentence use it; no setting, no opt-in, no first-run step; a missing header is `unknown` and behaves exactly as before; the header is not authentication, never logged, and adds no route or card. Implemented and proved in this repository (backend `test_surface.py`, phone `SurfaceHeaderTest`, Rust `surface_header_tests`), docs/JARVIS-API.md section 173.

- **2026-10-31 — In-app tool switches stay tiered, not indiscriminate (architect's ruling):** The owner asked for in-app switches instead of editing `[tools].enabled`; Gemini ruled the expansion must be tiered. Tier A, in-app now: calendar_read (kept from the earlier four), notes_search, append_obsidian_daily, create_joplin_note, append_logseq_journal, set_timer, set_reminder, todo_add, todo_done, coming_up, protect_from_jarvis, github_search, send_file_to_phone. Tier B, `Connected accounts & home` (included because the owner clicked for maximum flexibility): email_check, send_email, draft_email, tidy_inbox, home_read, home_control, my_spending, retirement_whatif. Tier C stays TOML-only and is never exposed in-app: shell_exec, run_data_script, control_computer, control_phone, browser_control, read_web_page, connect_account, rea_investigate - raw shell/computer/browser control stays a deliberate settings-file choice and REA also needs its own `[rea] enabled = true`. Not offered in-app by this slice: calculator, memory_search, file_read, web_search, my_files, propose_plan, change_setting, feature_guide. The vault organizer's own one-card switch rides in the same UI section as its own row; it is not a `[tools].enabled` toggle. Every switch is ONE PC-only card plus Windows Hello, one tool at a time; OFF is instant from either app; the phone is read-only; per-use action cards are unchanged; the card says each use still asks; send_file_to_phone stays off by default because its deterministic chat request is the normal door; unknown tools and Tier C/unlisted tools answer 403 with the plain reason.

- **2026-11-01 — An approved step survives a stream that died with it, instead of being dropped:** The owner's report was "approved card, then Jarvis forgets my question": the tap is consumed by `jarvis_gate.decide()`, the app says "Approved. Carrying on." because the gate really said yes, and the turn then finds `out.gone` - the phone closed its stream while the card waited - so it refuses to run the approved tool (nobody is there to read the result) and unwinds. He re-sends, and nothing on the PC remembers the yes, so the new turn answers from scratch without the search he approved. Measured on his own run of 2026-11-01, 15:44-15:47 (`.dsh-scratch/APPROVAL-CONTINUITY-2026-11-01/EVIDENCE.md`): `route turns=7`, `gate.asked`, `gate.approved by=phone`, `agent.chain web_search ran=true ok=true`, then `route turns=7` again 91 ms later and `SPEED rounds=1 tokens=17 tools=False` - the working card turns in the same session read `rounds=2, ~6000 prompt tokens` instead. Decided: keep that one approved step for that one conversation, in memory only, and run it once at the start of the next turn for the same conversation, through the same `prepare()`/`gate`/`execute()` contract, with its result in the transcript the model answers from - so the answer is the one the tap was for. Chosen over "make the card turn never lose its stream" (the client-side fix the evidence could not pin down, and which would leave any other cause of a dead stream losing the same yes) and over "re-raise the card" (a second card for an approval already given, which the owner would reasonably read as a bug). The permission model is deliberately unchanged: the record is written only from the `out.gone` branch that `allowed` and `_a_person_said_yes()` already passed, `owed_record()` tests `_a_person_said_yes()` again for itself, one card still means one action, nothing is auto-approved, and the carried step raises no second card because it already has its yes. Bounded so it cannot become a queue or a replay loop: keyed by the card's own id (`_OWED_DONE`, so a client that re-sends twice still runs it once), dropped after `OWED_TTL_SECONDS` (ten minutes), never carried across conversations, never written to disk, and never written for a denied, timed-out or never-answered card. **Re-authorised at replay time, because a yes is a decision of the moment and not a standing permission:** `owed_may_run()` re-makes the gate's CURRENT decision before anything is appended - a Stop everything pressed after the approval OR WHILE ITS CARD WAITED (the record carries the turn's own earlier stop mark, so the dead stream cannot become a way round the product's existing "a stop wins over the approval" rule), a crisis turn in the same conversation after it (ordered by a counter, not by a millisecond monotonic clock that can put both in the same tick), the tool no longer in the turn's allowed or offered set, or its action now at tier "never" all DROP the step (`agent.owed_dropped`, reason recorded) and the answer says so in code's own words, and none of them raises a second card: nothing the gate would now refuse is ever run, and nothing is asked again. A picture-lane turn and a turn whose model cannot use tools run no tool, so they leave the step owed rather than spending it; a replay that raises after its tool-call message was appended puts a result beside it, never a tool call with no answer. A carried step that fails says so in code's own words and claims nothing; both the record and the replay are in the audit log (`agent.owed`, `agent.owed_ran`, `agent.owed_dropped`) with names and ids only. Delivered as the whole `jarvis_agent.py` (a module this repository ships whole, in `$SHIPPED`, targeting no patch) in `backend/` and `jarvis-backend/`, and proved headless by `backend/test_approval_continuity.py`: 109 checks green, including the reported seam driven end to end (a dead-stream `web_search` card whose search runs once on the next turn with its result in the first round of the answering turn, and a second re-sent turn that runs nothing) and the replay-time policy drops; red without the replay-time re-check (92 passed, 0 skipped, 17 failed with only `owed_may_run()` disabled in the same tree - 16 policy checks plus the base-copy check), and red without the fix itself (the earlier run: 6 failing checks with the record and replay halves switched off in the same tree; the same suite against HEAD's own two agent files in a separate worktree is 2 passed, 0 skipped, 17 failed).

- **2026-11-01 — A calendar moment is built from its local components, never from midnight plus absolute minutes:** The desktop HUD's calendar computed an event's moment as local midnight plus the clock time in absolute milliseconds, which is right on ordinary days and wrong by an hour on both daylight-saving change days (a 23- or 25-hour local day); on 2026-11-01 an event at 12:14 read "past" five minutes after it began. Decided: a moment is always asked from the PC as its own local date and clock time (`new Date(year, month, day, hours, minutes)`), so the time the owner reads is the time the event happens, every day; the same shape the PC's own calendar store already uses, and the phone never had the bug because it keeps local date strings and no instant arithmetic. The rule is pinned by five fixed-date cases in `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-calendar.mjs` (both transition directions, the all-day arm and the midnight rollover) - fixed dates, because CI runs in UTC where the old arithmetic could never fail, so the value is that the bug can no longer hide on a Pacific PC. Stated limit: proved by the page's own helpers under Node, not yet by watching the installed window cross a change day.

- **2026-11-01 — A conversation-scoped web-search approval, granted with ONE card, is allowed; nothing else widens:** The owner asked, in their own words, *"if I ask jarvis and say you have full approval to search the web for anything during this conversation. give jarvis the approval to search the web for the entire conversation until I say it doesn't have authorization to do that. make sure a card comes up that I have to approve before this happens"*, and then *"and if I ask anything further like book a flight for me online then it will have to have another card to approve further action beyond just searching the web."* Decided: a standing permission is allowed only in this one shape - ONE action (`search_the_web`), ONE conversation (keyed on the request's own `conversation_id`), granted only by a person answering a card, revocable instantly with no card, capped at 8 hours, held in memory only so a restart ends it, outranked by Lockdown, and logged on every use with the grant's id. The alternative - letting the grant follow the words ("full approval to do anything") - was rejected because a model's reading of an open-ended sentence is not a permission: the grant's scope is fixed by the ACTION, and every other action keeps its own card. The other alternative, a setting that survives restarts, was rejected for the same reason: "until I say it doesn't have authorization" is a promise about a conversation, not a preference to keep. Refusing to grant at all when the request carries no conversation id is deliberate: a grant that cannot be limited to one chat is not what was asked for. Two new model tools (`approve_web_search_for_conversation`, `stop_web_search_approval`), two new gate actions (`grant_web_search_conversation` at tier `ask`, `revoke_web_search_grant` at tier `auto` - a card to STOP what the owner just asked to stop would be wrong), one new patch (`backend/web-search-grant.patch`, three additive hunks in `jarvis_gate.py`), and the store, the tools and the one place a grant is read in the shipped `jarvis_agent.py`. Proved by `backend/test_web_search_grant.py` (95 checks across all nine cases, driven through the real turn loop, the real `jarvis_search` planning and the real `jarvis_gate` audit writers, with the patch rehearsed forwards and backwards byte for byte), with `tools/check_patch_original_text.py` pinning the three hunks and 14 lines of the owner's own text that the patch has to read.

- **2026-11-01 — Four tools with no gate action are mapped onto actions that already exist, in a new patch applied last, and the published base carries the same lines:** `send_file_to_phone`, `protect_from_jarvis`, `connect_account` and `rea_investigate` are in `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` and had no entry in `jarvis_gate._TOOL_ACTIONS`, so `action_for_tool()` answered `unclassified_tool` for all four - fail-safe (`unknown_action_tier` is "ask" as shipped) and wrong anyway, because the card was never the one the tool raises and `jarvis_reach` reported each as unclassified. **The decision is the mapping: no new action name, no new tier and no new card wording.** `send_file_to_phone` maps to itself (`jarvis_send_file.ACTION` and `jarvis_agent.SEND_FILE_ACTION` both name it, and `send_file_to_phone = "ask"` already ships). `protect_from_jarvis` maps to `protect_item` (`PROTECT_ACTION` / `ACTION_PROTECT`), whose removal half `unprotect_item` is its own route and not a model tool. `connect_account` maps to `change_own_config` on the `change_setting` row's own recorded reasoning: `_one_call` intercepts it before the gate, so the entry only states the conservative answer for the Reach page - the connect card is a host-side card with its own TTL and never enters `/api/pending`. `rea_investigate` maps to `run_shell_on_host`, because `jarvis_rea.py` starts a local MCP program and `jarvis_protection.py` names it beside `shell_exec` and `run_data_script`; that action's worst-case risk row is the one the gate already uses for a spawned program. One side effect is recorded rather than hidden: anything resolving to `run_shell_on_host` also runs `_SHELL_NEVER` over its arguments, so a REA query containing `git push` would escalate to a stricter card - the direction the gate permits. **The alternatives refused:** inventing four new action names (a new tier row and new card words for each, and a Reach page that would need four new plain sentences); mapping REA to `read_files_readonly` (tier "auto", which would tell the owner a tool that always asks does not ask); adding the `_RISK` rows the two modules' own docstrings ask for (a separate change with its own wording to get right - the gate still forces these four to "ask", which is what their tier lines already say). **Where it lives:** a NEW patch appended after every patch whose context it could move, and immediately before `unknown-risk-approvable.patch` - that patch's own guard (`backend/test_gate_unknown_risk.py`) requires it to stay the last patch that writes `jarvis_gate.py`, and the two do not interact because its eight rows are at the top of `_RISK` while these four lines are at the end of `_TOOL_ACTIONS` - never a line added to `gate-entries.patch`, because later patches' hunks were written against that patch's exact output (`readpage.patch` anchors on the `tidy_inbox` line and the `# plan.patch:` comment it writes); the new patch's own context is `gate-entries.patch`'s last line, so the stack walk invents no pre-image and `_stack.py`'s `jarvis_gate.py` RATCHET stays at 55. `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py`, the published base that is meant to be the state after the patches (`b908d7368`), carries the same four lines, so a clone and the owner's next deploy agree. **And CI gets a check that can see the next one:** `backend/test_gate_tool_actions.py` rebuilds the table an install gets from the base plus every patch's added lines, needs no `import jarvis_gate`, asserts each of the four comes from BOTH halves and that every action is a tier word or a real `[autonomy.tiers]` key, and bites on the pre-fix tree by reporting exactly those four. Measured against a copy of the installed backend: `test_agent.py` 311 passed / 4 failed before, 315 passed / 0 failed after; `test_runtime_identity.py` 13 / 0.

- **2026-11-01 — A backend suite that pins prompt bytes pins its own config folder:** `backend/test_agent.py` and `backend/test_runtime_identity.py` assert the exact request a local turn sends, and two lines of that request are read from this PC's saved state at request time - the Cloud preset line `jarvis_agent.with_cloud_state_note()` adds when `cloud-choice.json` names a provider, and the `run_data_script` sandbox tool that `sandbox.json`'s switch offers on top of whatever enabled set a test passed. The suites were therefore green in CI and red at the owner's desk on the same commit: measured 2026-11-01 at `c1b5c5236`, `test_agent` was 304 passed / 11 failed on the live folder against 311 passed / 4 failed on an empty one, and `test_runtime_identity` was 12 passed / 1 failed against 13 passed / 0 failed. Decided: a suite whose assertions depend on defaults makes its own empty temporary config folder and sets `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` to it **before the first product module is imported** - several modules (`jarvis_framework`, `jarvis_presets`, `jarvis_sandbox_exec`) resolve the folder themselves, so setting it after an import can arrive too late - and restores the previous value with `atexit`, the pattern `test_schedule.py` and `test_manner.py` already carry. Pinned by the suites themselves: pointed at a folder holding the owner's own `cloud-choice.json` and `sandbox.json`, both now report what they report on the live folder (311/4 and 13/0), so the caller's environment can no longer change the result. The rule deliberately does not extend to `JARVIS_BACKEND`: a run against a real install must keep testing that install's copy (`_where.require_shipped` says so), and the 4 remaining `test_agent` failures are that install's `jarvis_gate.py` missing `_TOOL_ACTIONS` entries for `send_file_to_phone`, `protect_from_jarvis`, `connect_account` and `rea_investigate` - a separate gap, left visible rather than skipped, and not fixed here.

- **2026-11-01 — Jarvis Live is shown the same tools as typed chat, and its tool limit is a floor rather than a cut:** The owner asked that Jarvis Live be able to "reasonably do anything that jarvis can do through chat". A Live turn already used the same chat route, agent, gate and cards; what narrowed it was the tool list the model was shown - `[live] tool_limit` capped it at 6 names and the cap also cut the diet's full-list fallback, so words the tool diet did not recognise were shown 32 tools typed and 6 spoken (26 hidden, notes, timers, reminders, email, settings and account connection among them), and a Live conversation carried three fewer forward (min(9, 6) = 6, against typed chat's 9). That was written down on 2026-10-18 as a speed slice, with the note that it "changes what is shown, never what is allowed" - true, and it is why this was a reachability problem rather than a permission one: the gate would still accept a call to any allowed tool, but the model was never told the hidden tools' names or arguments, so a spoken request would not reach them in practice. Decided: a Live turn is shown exactly what a typed turn is shown for the same words. `jarvis_live.LIVE_TOOL_FLOOR` equals typed chat's own diet size (8) and `[live] tool_limit` may raise it, never lower it; the full-list fallback is not trimmed; the carried list uses typed chat's cap.
