What is deliberately kept is the rest of the speed slice - the `[live]` model, its single lane and the 16K window - and the deliberate Live rules: cards stay the same gate cards decided by tapping only, Live still pauses while a card raised since it started waits, a spoken yes is never heard, and the phone still does no speech-to-text. The switched-off persistent-stream path now sends `provenance: "voice"` with `live: true`, the two marks both apps already send, so a streamed Live turn is recognisably spoken instead of looking like an untagged typed turn. Proved by `backend/test_live_parity.py` (tool-list equality over six kinds of question, the floor, the carried list, a whole Live turn reaching the tool path and raising its one card with nothing run first, the fast path's identical PC-state answer, and the kept rules) and by updated assertions in `backend/test_live.py` and `backend/test_agent.py` that had pinned the old cap; no real model, phone or Live session was driven, so that remains NOT-TESTABLE until an owner test.

- **2026-11-01 — A Jarvis Live session is verified once, and an answer it can say is said:** The owner's request, "once I actively verify my voice in a single jarvis live session, jarvis shouldn't need to re verify my voice", replaces the 2026-10-18 refinement in which one successful check bought a 120-second window or 16 short clips and then asked again. **What is cached, and for how long:** in the `Live` engine's own memory, three things and no audio - the clock time of the one successful strict check, the strictness it passed at ("very_strict" or "balanced"), and the identity of the enrolled print it passed against (its label, file size and write time - the print itself is never read). It lasts from that check until the session ends, and it is reset by `_trust_start` on every start, by `_trust_end`, by a failed or erroring check (`abort_trust`) and by a changed print (`_trust_print_changed`). Nothing is written to disk, no new secret is created, and a page reload or backend restart starts unverified. **Why that is not a weakening of the check:** the check was done, once, in this session, by the owner's own voice, at the owner's own setting - this caches a result rather than skipping the check itself. Nothing else moves: the first clip must still be a full sentence, the >= 2.0 s spot check still runs silently on every full sentence (which is what refuses a voice that is not the owner's and what a private answer needs before it may be read aloud), a failed check still voids the session at once, no approval, no lock and no permission rule is touched, and no answer becomes readable that a setting keeps on screen. The one trade is said plainly and is the same 1.5 s trade the 2026-10-18 decision took: a 1.5-2.0 s clip in a verified session runs without a speaker model, so a voice in the room that is not the owner's is treated as the owner for those clips, and their answers now keep the read-aloud flags the session's check earned (before this change those flags were lost, which is why Live said "It's on your screen" about an answer that used what Jarvis remembers, read aloud by default). **The alternative that was NOT taken:** skipping the spot check too, so that no speaker model ran for the rest of the session. That would have let any voice command Jarvis for up to two hours, and it would have lost the real check a private or remembered-fact answer needs before it may be spoken - it is the owner's call, not this change's, and it is not in this pull request.

- **2026-11-01 — "One moment." can be turned off by asking, and the PC keeps that answer:** The owner asked: *"id like the ability to tell jarvis in jarvis live to adjust any settings, includimg no longer saying one moment while it comprehends or calculates something"*. Decided: "Say \"One moment\" if I'm kept waiting" leaves `jarvis_settings_registry.NOT_BY_ASKING` and becomes the real switch `one_moment`, changed by talking (typed or spoken, and through the `change_setting` tool) with no approval card - one cosmetic sentence in Jarvis's own voice, acting on nothing, and switching it off only takes something away (the same rule `jarvis_voice_flow.py` already states for its three `[voice]` switches). The PC keeps the owner's answer itself in `voice-flow.json` in the settings folder and reports it as `flow.moment.enabled`, the value BOTH apps already gate the clip on, so the sentence changes what the owner actually hears on the desktop bar and the phone with no client change. `[voice] one_moment_enabled = false` in the framework file stays the hard hand-edited switch and wins: asking for the clip back while that says false answers that it is still off instead of pretending. A damaged answer file reads as ON - the state before the file existed - so it can never silently change what the owner hears. The desktop Settings row and the phone's own switch keep their existing meaning (may THIS device play it) and do not yet show the PC-wide answer; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records that gap and why closing it needs a route no client calls yet.

- **2026-11-01 — Jarvis may open the owner's own listed apps on the phone and start a media search in them, and the list is the permission:** The owner asked for Jarvis Live to open certain apps on their Android phone when asked, and to do things like "open YouTube Music and play The Weeknd". Decided: this is execution, not a new surface - the existing `control_phone` tool and `jarvis_android_control.py` gain `open_app`, `play` and the read-only `list_apps`, and the phone stays the hands while the PC stays the brain and the gate. The permission is a `[phone_apps]` table in `jarvis-framework.toml` (friendly name to package) that ships EMPTY; an app that is not in it cannot be opened, played or searched for, an empty list refuses everything with one plain sentence, and anything under `com.jarvis.` is refused so no tap can reach Jarvis's own Approve button. Chosen over a phone-side AccessibilityService allow-list (the separate app-control slice) because this needs no new Android permission, no new route and no second authority: `list_apps` answers from the same settings file, so the phone can never widen what the PC allows. `play` means "open the app on that app's own search address" and is offered only for apps whose address is documented (YouTube Music today); everything else can be opened and not searched, and the refusal says so. `open_app` and `play` are also exempt from the Jarvis-in-front guard, because both name the package in the command itself and a `com.jarvis.` package is refused before a command exists - the guard protects against a tap inside Jarvis's own app, and it would otherwise refuse this request every time it is asked FROM the phone, which is where Live is. One card per plan at the unchanged `ask` tier, every literal command printed, and the tool stays opt-in (`control_phone` is not in the shipped `[tools].enabled`); a list-only call or a refusal raises no card because there is nothing to approve. Recorded with the honest limit that opening a media app backgrounds a Live session on that phone, and that the intent's behaviour on the real device is verified on hardware, not in this repository.

- **2026-11-01 — A small read-only approval is approved by the card alone, and the fingerprint is a setting:** The owner's own request: *"for small approvals like asking jarvis to search the web (for things like weather or the news or anything small) i would like to only have to approve the card, not necessarily use my fingerprint on top of approving the card. make this setting adjustable in settings or through chatting to jarvis."* Decided: the approval check gets a third value, `small` (`small` / `risky` / `every`), and **it ships as the default** because that is what the owner asked for. A card is small only when its action is on an explicit read-only list AND the gate's own risk row for it says it changes nothing, is classified, and was not rushed - so nothing unclassified, irreversible, rushed, or that writes, spends, sends, deletes or changes an account, a credential, a device, the network, an app or a permission ever qualifies, and the list is named action by action in `jarvis_owner_check.SMALL_ACTIONS` and `SecurityRules.SMALL_ACTIONS`. What it changes: on the PC the backend no longer shows its Windows Hello prompt for such a card approved from this PC (it was asking because `is_risky` calls anything outbound risky, and a web search is outbound); on the phone such a card is approved by the card alone and is not signed (`SecurityRules.approveTakesSignedPath`), which is safe only because the same rule exempts it from the device signature at `approve_check`; and "Every approval" still asks every time, on every card the rule does not exempt. **How to turn it back:** on the phone, Settings, Lock and fingerprint settings, "Fingerprint for approvals" - choose **Risky only** (today's rule, the small ones included) or **Every approval**; on the PC, say or type "check the small approvals too" (the `small_approvals` setting, through the existing `change_setting` tool) to put the check back on the small cards, and "leave the small approvals alone" for the default again - the loosening direction is this PC only, never a phone, because it is this PC's own check. Chosen over a per-card exception list or a guess from the card's words because the gate already carries a risk row for every action and the project's rule is that a security rule is read from the metadata, not inferred from prose. **What it costs, said plainly:** the phone's copy and the PC's copy are two settings with the same name and the same default, as every security setting in this project already is (the phone's lock is the phone's); changing one does not change the other, and the desktop's Settings card says which is which. Held by `tools/gen_risky_approval_cases.py` (the shared rows, now with `small`), `SmallApprovalContractTest`, `SecurityRulesTest`, and the new checks in `backend/test_owner_check.py` and `backend/test_settings_registry.py`.

- **2026-11-01 — A typed "was this answer right?" is answered by the app, not the model:** The owner's field test of 2026-11-01 typed that sentence into the desktop HUD and into the phone, and both sent it to the PC as an ordinary question; the model answered conversationally while the answer menu the sentence is really asking for stayed shut. Decided: each client recognises that short list of whole-sentence asks itself, opens the most recent finished answer's own menu (the caret menu the owner asked for on 2026-10-27), and sends nothing - no chat turn, no history entry, no request; when there is no finished answer on screen the app says so in its own voice and still sends nothing. Chosen over a backend quick answer because the menu is a client surface the PC cannot open, and because the phrase names that menu. The same pass gives the phone's answer menu the read-only date+time line the desktop HUD already shows, and gives "where am I talking from?" a deterministic backend lane reading `X-Jarvis-Surface` (an honest unknown sentence when a request carries no label). A miss is deliberately harmless: anything not on the list keeps its old path. Proved by `backend/test_surface_origin.py`, `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-answer-route.mjs`, the phone's JVM tests, and the seven required CI checks; the live rows are recorded in the deploy #6 field test, where only a row actually driven is a PASS.

- **2026-11-02 — Approve, Deny and Review in Jarvis on an Android approval notification:** The owner asked, 2026-11-02: *"make sure i can approve jarvis cards through an android notification with a deny or approve button or tap too see more button if the summary that's short enough to fit into an android notification isn't long enough."* Decided, under Gemini's binding five-point envelope, that the phone's approval notification carries two actions and one redacted public version. **(1)** Deny may run from the lock screen - refusing without reading is the safe direction and was already allowed. **(2)** Every approve action is built with `setAuthenticationRequired(true)`, so Android withholds its `PendingIntent` until the device is unlocked; no Kotlin check is the wall. **(3)** Only a card that `SecurityRules.isSmall` exempts (the owner's 2026-11-01 request) and that the owner's setting does not ask about may submit directly; that route goes through the app's non-exported `EventService`, which waits for a live link, re-reads the live card, re-checks `isSmall` and the phone's privacy state, and then calls the existing `JarvisRuntime.decide`. Every write, config, send-file, phone-app or otherwise non-small card's Approve opens Jarvis on the focused card and runs the same `approveItem`/`BiometricPrompt` the card's own button runs, forcing the check even where the card alone would not have asked. **(4)** When the text the notification shows (title and body together) is over 240 characters, Approve is replaced by **Review in Jarvis** and Deny stays; the same applies to a PC-only card and to a proposal that needs one of several plans chosen, neither of which the phone may approve. **(5)** The notification stays `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE`, its public version says exactly **"Jarvis: 1 approval waiting"** with no title, summary or action name, its `sync()` cancels a notification when `/api/pending` no longer carries that id, and no secret is added. A redacted notification - App lock on (the default), hidden memory lists, or a phone with no secure lock - offers Review in Jarvis and Deny, never Approve: approving words the notification did not show is the same blind approval point 4 forbids, and the redaction itself is the owner's existing 2026-09-30 privacy rule (`SecurityRules.notificationsLocked`), not weakened here. App lock off is what shows the card's safe `notice` words in the shade and therefore what makes Approve appear. The policy lives in `service/ApprovalNotificationPolicy.kt` so the JVM tests hold it without a phone; the two routes both end at the existing `/api/approve`, so there is no backend change, no new route and no second permission path, and `notice.approve_ok` is still not read. This supersedes the 2026-09-26-era rule recorded in `ApprovalNotifier.kt` that an approval was never approvable from a notification. It deliberately does not build: a desktop/Windows notification for approvals, any bulk approve, any approve on a locked phone, any approve of a card the owner cannot see, or an approve that skips the fingerprint for a write. Evidence: `ApprovalNotificationPolicyTest` (19 checks) and the updated `AppProjectsTest`, `NotificationStyleTest`, `MainActivityLaunchTest` and `ApprovalDecisionTest` in the required `phone-unit-tests` job; the phone itself is NOT-TESTABLE at this desk.

- **2026-11-02 — The Coding preset gets a pooled both-card lane, and heavy mode may evict the other two models:** The owner asked for the Coding focus preset to be usable and accepted that measuring it may evict the Live/Fast models and slow Live while it runs. The preset's model is 14.8 GB and fits neither single-card lane, so its lane is ONE Ollama on port 11450 with no card pin, started by the apply and stopped by the next apply that is not heavy: the two lane models are paused while it runs and put back afterwards, proved from `/api/ps`, and the card says so before the first unload. The apply keeps ONE `switch_model` card and records the model chat uses without a second card, because `jarvis_models.switch_to` probes at the single-card lane address and would try to load 14 GB on a 12 GB card. The measured zero-spill context on this PC on 2026-11-02 is 16,384, not the 28,672 the 2026-10-18 measurement used (28,672 / 24,576 / 20,480 all spilled 204-212 MiB), so the preset asks for 16,384 and the lane refuses rather than loading a model that spills. `jarvis_big_coder.NUM_CTX` (that mode's own rung) was not changed.

- **2026-11-02 — The reminder area's goals are the existing goals, with a progress log added to them:** The owner asked, 2026-11-02: *"add a goals section in the reminder area and a way for me to record progress there along with talking to jarvis."* `jarvis_goals.py` already keeps the owner's goals, their plans and a weekly check-in (the 2026-09-27 "Goals with one card per step" feature, JARVIS-API §59), and both apps already show them, so the progress log, the `paused` state, done/remove and the four model tools were added to that module and its `/api/goals` routes rather than built as a second "goals" feature. Decided: one store and one route set, because two goals features would be exactly the duplicate CLAUDE.md's fit rule forbids and the owner would have two places holding goals that could disagree. Recording progress is a personal-data write, so it follows the closest analogue exactly rather than inventing a gate: it is cardless like ticking off a to-do item or accepting a goal, the four tools resolve under the existing `_TOOL_ACTIONS` `"todo_add": "auto"` line (no new action, tier, patch or card wording - the same pattern `feature_guide` uses with `skill_list`), and the page that promises every action, `jarvis_asks_first`'s `fixed:goals` row, was extended to say so. The progress log is append-only: no function updates or deletes one line, the only delete is the owner's own Remove of a whole goal (which takes its log), and no model tool can remove or forget anything - so "talking to Jarvis" can add but never throw away what the owner wrote. In a turn shaped by outside text the three write tools are refused (a page or an email cannot invent a goal), while `goals_list` is allowed there and its result is marked as outside text like `coming_up`'s. `create(start=True)` makes a goal open at once with no weekly check-in, which is what the reminder area's Add uses; the §59 draft/accept path is untouched. Two new columns are added to an existing `goals.db` by a guarded `ALTER TABLE` on open, and progress lives in a second table in the same file, not a second file. Evidence: `backend/test_goals_progress.py` (90 checks: origin/token refusals with the store unchanged, list/add/progress/done/pause/resume/remove, append-only, the four tools and the shaped-turn refusal) and `backend/test_goals.py` (142 checks, unchanged); `backend/test_pictures.py` holds the new §182, and `backend/test_gate_tool_actions.py` proves the tools resolve under the existing cardless action with no patch added.

- **2026-11-02 — Habit and mood data are excluded from learning entirely, not merely card-gated:** The second of the life-coach owner decisions (`.dsh-scratch/LIFE-COACH-RESEARCH-2026-11-02/OWNER-DECISIONS.md`, D2). Habit names, the words typed on a tick, mood values and mood words **never become learned facts at all**; the rejected weaker option was the project's existing sensitive-category rule, where a candidate fact is proposed and waits for the owner's yes, which `jarvis_sensitive.py` already applies to health and money. The reason a card is not enough is written in `jarvis_intake.mood_rule`'s own docstring: a card can arrive in the review queue "possibly minutes after a hard moment", which turns a private tap into a question about it. So the exclusion is by construction rather than by permission: `backend/jarvis_habits.py` and `backend/jarvis_mood.py` import no learner and name no fact store, no learner module imports or names either one, and neither holds SQL against the facts table - proven in both directions by `backend/test_learning_exclusion.py`, which also proves that writing a habit and a mood creates `habits.db`/`mood.db` and **no fact store at all**, and that a sentinel written into each lives in that one file and in no other SQLite file in the folder. This is deliberately stronger than the existing rule and does not replace it: `jarvis_intake`'s mood rule ("Moods ... is not a fact. Do not propose it.") stays exactly where it is, so the model is still told not to propose a mood in ordinary chat, and this decision covers the two stores. Neither module imports `jarvis_sensitive` or `jarvis_gate`, so the mechanism cannot be mistaken for a card-gated one later; a test pins both absences. What this does **not** claim: that a model cannot write a fact about the owner in ordinary chat from his own words - that is the existing learning path with its existing rules, and it is not what is being excluded here.

- **2026-11-02 — The skills menu installs only through the existing scanner and ONE card, imports only from this PC, and keeps a skill's scripts inert:** the owner chose scope B of the Hermes-skills research (`.dsh-scratch/OWNER-QUEUE-2026-11-02/HERMES-SKILLS-RESEARCH.md`): a PC skills menu that installs from a folder or a `.zip`, turns a skill off and on, edits it, and imports what is already in `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\skills` - and **no marketplace and no network install**, so there is nothing to browse and nothing to download. Four rulings are recorded with it. **(1) The install card is the existing one, given one more line.** `jarvis_skills.install()` vets first and then raises ONE `modify_own_code` card; the menu passes the card a sentence (`note=`) saying what is being imported and that a bundled `scripts/` folder is kept inert. `backend/skill-install-note.patch` is additive: with no note the card's words are unchanged. **(2) `install()` now re-checks the gate's TIER, as `refine()` already did.** `jarvis_gate.check` returns `allowed=True` on `notify` and `auto` - nobody asked - so a config that listed `modify_own_code` that way would have installed a skill with no person in the loop. A skill is instructions the agent follows, so the card has to be a real card; `notify`/`auto` install nothing and say why. **(3) Turning a skill off is immediate and deletes nothing; turning it on is a card.** Off MOVES the folder to `skills-off\` and takes its row out of `.index.json`, which is the list `cards()` hands the model - so the skill stops being offered and `load()` cannot find it either - and it does not raise a card, like every other switch that takes an ability away. On is the same scanner and the same ONE card as installing it, because it re-adds instructions the model will follow; a skill that changed while it was off is re-scanned and refused if it now fails. **(4) One request is one card, and import is one card per skill - the owner's brief said "one card" for the import and this deliberately reads it as one per folder.** A single card that installs several skills at once is bulk approval, which `CLAUDE.md` forbids outright, so the Hermes scan is a READ-ONLY list (it copies and installs nothing and raises no card) and each folder the owner picks is installed by its own request and its own card. Hermes-only metadata (`platforms`, `metadata.hermes.*`, `required_environment_variables`) is kept and does nothing here, and a skill's `scripts/` never runs - both said plainly on the card and in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §178. The phone keeps exactly what it had (the list and Remove); install, turn-on and edit are the PC's alone and `tools/check_parity.py` records why (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8).

- **2026-11-02 — Jarvis Live records through a car's hands-free microphone in call mode:** The owner reported, 2026-11-02: *"when I am using jarvis live in my car and my phone is connected to Bluetooth it acts like it is in a call but jarvis cannot hear me. the mic doesn't seem to be working properly at all. I have a 2017 Chevrolet bolt."* A car's Bluetooth is a hands-free device (HFP/SCO) whose microphone only exists in a call, so Live now records on `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` with the phone in `MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` and the car as the communication device while such a device is connected, and restores the previous audio mode and device in a `finally`. The decision is pure (`LiveAudioRoute`) and unit-tested on the JVM for no Bluetooth, A2DP only, hands-free Bluetooth, a wired headset, a device unplugged mid-session and restoration after stop; the voice-print gate is untouched (a complete clip is still checked, nothing streams) and there is no route change. What the app cannot prove: that a 2017 Chevrolet Bolt hands its microphone over in that configuration. Only the owner's own car can confirm it.

- **2026-11-02 — How long Jarvis Live waits before it turns off is the owner's setting, changeable by asking and in Settings:** The owner asked: *"also id likee to he able to tell jarvis to change the setting that turns off jarvos live by extending how long ot takestoo turn off when it doesntt hear anything"*. Decided: the silent window that ends an idle Live session stops being `jarvis_live.py`'s constant `QUIET_S = 90` (whose own comment said the owner's call was pending) and becomes `[live].quiet_s` in the owner's settings file, with ONE row owning it - `jarvis_limits.LIMITS`' `live_idle_seconds` - and one reader, `jarvis_live.quiet_seconds()`, used by the engine's tick and by the status both apps draw. The default is 90 seconds, exactly today's behaviour, so nothing changes on a PC that never touches it. The range is 30 seconds to 10 minutes, and it is bounded for two real reasons: below 30 seconds Live would end in the pause between two thoughts (the voice check alone needs a 2-second clip), and above 10 minutes an open microphone has been forgotten, which is the very risk that window exists to bound; the engine clamps a hand-edited value to the range as well as the route. It is changeable BOTH by asking Jarvis (chat or Live: "make Jarvis Live wait three minutes" changes it and is answered with the new value and the range in plain words; a length outside the range is refused in words that name the range and nothing is written) AND in Settings on the desktop ("Limits and frequency") and the phone (Limits), which draw the same row and therefore the same label, words and range - the spoken sentence goes through `jarvis_settings_registry.set_live_idle` -> `jarvis_limits.change`, the exact function `POST /api/limits/settings` calls, so it adds no writer and no range check of its own. No approval card in either direction: Live must already be running (the owner started it, the microphone was already open), the number only decides when an idle session ends, it never starts Live, reads, sends or stores anything, and the same session's time limit already extends instantly by saying "give me twenty more minutes" - asking a card to keep listening longer would be stricter than the control beside it. `GET /api/limits` gained one additive field, `step` (how far one tap of the -/+ moves a row; 30 on this row so three minutes is three taps from the default, 1 elsewhere), which both apps read and an older screen may ignore.

- **2026-11-02 — A Live session started by voice is verified by the clip that started it:** The owner asked for one voice verification at the beginning of a Live session. #1069 (2026-11-01) made ONE successful check cover the whole session, but the check that starts Live by voice was discarded: "Hey Jarvis, let's talk" is only answered after that clip passed the owner check, yet the session began unverified, so the first 1.5-2.0 s Live clip was answered "Say a full sentence so I can re-check your voice" - the owner verifying twice at the beginning of one session. The passed check is now carried into the session with the strictness and print it earned, through the existing `jarvis_live.note_verified`. It is the same kind of check the session's first full sentence would be: `_live_start` never runs before the owner check, and a clip too short to be a command never reaches it. **What an attacker who starts Live as the owner could do, and why this does not widen it:** to start Live by voice they must already pass the owner check - the very check the session would otherwise ask for - so nobody is admitted who could not already admit themselves by saying a full sentence one clip later. For the rest of that session a 1.5-2.0 s clip is treated as the owner without a speaker model (the trade #1069 recorded), a >= 2.0 s clip is still silently checked, a failed or erroring check still ends the session's verification at once, a re-enrolled print still voids it, every start and every end still clears it, approvals are still taps and never by voice, and a private, sensitive or screen answer still follows its own setting. A start whose check was not a real one (broad mode, where every voice is let in) records nothing, so that session still earns its check on a full sentence. **The alternative not taken:** keeping today's second full sentence after a voice start - it is the double verification the owner reported, and it buys no check that was not already passed.

- **2026-11-02 — One memory switch that trusts Jarvis's rewording, and nothing else:** The owner was asked to choose from the memory-card research (`.dsh-scratch/MEMORY-CARD-RESEARCH-2026-11-02/`) and chose **option C** - *one named switch, off by default*, "Save facts even when Jarvis had to reword them", plus the three free repairs, and the bulk Discard held back until the repairs have been measured. Decided, and enforced in code and tests: the switch's ON is ONE approval card (`learning_paraphrase_enable`, tier `ask`) and its OFF is immediate, exactly like "Learn automatically"; it relaxes **only** the "not in your own words" family (`jarvis_auto_learn.check_grounded`, with `check_meaning` and `check_tense`), and it may **never** relax the sensitive gate or the always-asks floor (passwords, PINs, account and ID numbers, birthdays, phone numbers, email addresses), a fact from pasted text or a tool's reading or any provenance but the owner's own live typed or strictly-verified voice turn, a fact that would change a stored one, a fact the owner asked to forget, an instruction in the fact, the topic controls, the switches, or the per-pass ceiling of five. Why that shape: a standing setting for one named, enumerated kind of thing is legal under `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §2 only when it is off by default, turned on with one card, off immediately, narrow, and cannot be answered by anything else - and this one is a Settings switch on both apps, never a button on a card. The cost is said in the card's own words before it is turned on: a wrong paraphrase can then be stored and recalled, so every fact it saves is marked "Jarvis's own words", listed in both apps, and forgotten with one tap. Alongside it, three repairs with no policy change: the other "Remember" shapes ("remember that …", "remember this: …", "please remember: …", "remember, …") are accepted like the literal colon; length alone no longer makes a typed message "pasted text"; and a sensitive-topic check that could not run now reads as a fault and is counted. The safe default is unchanged (automatic learning on for the owner's own words, every other path a card, sensitive off, background learning on, topics learn-and-use), and the bulk Discard stays unbuilt until this has been measured.

- **2026-11-02 — The mood log is built, and it reverses the 2026-09-26 decline for the owner's own log and nothing else:** Asked as one of four clickable answers in the life-coach set (`.dsh-scratch/LIFE-COACH-RESEARCH-2026-11-02/OWNER-DECISIONS.md`), the owner chose the third option for a mood log: **"1-5 tap + optional words + a history chart"** - he explicitly chose the chart, so the old rule "no mood log, score or chart" (`docs/CUTTING-EDGE-2026-09-26-round4-wellbeing.md:314`, "a health-like record nobody asked for") is superseded **for his own log, by his own request**, and not as a general reopening: there is still no unprompted "how are you feeling today?", no sentiment or emotion model, no diagnostic questionnaire, and no advice. What is built is deliberately small and local - `backend/jarvis_mood.py` with `GET`/`POST /api/mood` (JARVIS-API §180.2), `mood.db` beside goals.db, one row per day holding a whole number 1-5 and up to 200 characters of the owner's own words, a second entry replacing the first, and an upsert that computes no average, no trend and no verdict. The chart is a display concern and no app draws it yet: neither app has a screen for the log today, and the Mood section on the Reminders screen (his placement choice, D3) is the next lane. Logging raises no card in either direction, which is the same class as ticking a to-do. This entry records the decision and its limit; the learning boundary that goes with it is `2026-11-02-habit-mood-never-learned.md`, and the words that are allowed to talk about any of it are still the Reflective Coach's own (never diagnose, prescribe or advise on medicine, never a therapist, no therapy record, harm goes to a real person).

- **2026-11-02 — The phone's app allow-list is managed by ONE approval card per app, added or removed, from chat or from the PC's Settings:** The owner asked, in their own words: "any apps that i ask if to open or do something with. i would need to approve a card with the apps i would like it to manipulate first and i can remove or add any android app to that list any time with an approval card... or by going to the settings and changing it there too." Decided: the `[phone_apps]` table that PR #1067 made the whole permission for opening an app on the phone is now managed, because it ships EMPTY and a permission that can only be filled by hand-editing `jarvis-framework.toml` is a permission that cannot be used. Two doors, ONE permission model: a new model tool `phone_apps` (`list` / `add` / `remove`) in chat and Live on both apps, and `GET`/`POST /api/phone/apps` for the settings screens. Every add and every removal raises ONE card that names both the friendly name and the exact package id, nothing is written until a person approves it, a rejection changes nothing, and there is no bulk path - one app per call, refused by the route before a card and refused by the tool's schema. The gate mapping needed no new gate action and no new `backend/*.patch` hunk: the tool resolves through the existing `change_setting` key to `change_own_config`, the same action the other settings changes use, at the `ask` tier it already has; the tool's own name is deliberately NOT a gate key, so the mapping is load-bearing rather than decorative, and `backend/test_phone_app_allowlist.py` proves it and fails pre-fix. The line is written through the same config layer the other settings use - one line of the owner's own text, the whole file re-parsed and compared, an atomic replace, then a framework reload - and an applied add or remove writes one audit line naming the app and the package. `phone_apps` ships ON in `[tools].enabled`, chosen over making it opt-in: a tool that is the only way to fill a list that ships empty cannot itself be behind a hand edit of the same file, and what it can reach is that ONE table, card-first; `control_phone` - which actually opens apps - stays opt-in, `ask`, and one card per plan. THE SURFACE DECISION, with its record reference: add and remove are the PC's Settings and either app's chat; the PHONE's Settings is a READ-ONLY list plus "ask Jarvis to add an app", not an editor, because typing a friendly name AND a package id is deep config editing, which the standing rule keeps off the phone, and the phone is the one device that cannot look a package up - the owner's "or by going to the settings and changing it there too" is answered by the PC's Settings and by the same card from the phone's chat. The phone is not a second authority: the same card approves the same line whichever surface asked. Recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §176.

- **2026-11-02 — Appearance is Settings-only on the phone, and Reminders takes its Home-row place:** The owner's request, verbatim: *"also, move appearance to only in settings for the android app and replace the appearance button with a reminders button instead"* (said 2026-11-01, built in the 2026-11-02 branch). Decided: the phone's Home row is Brain, Inbox, Live, Reminders, Settings, Help - the Appearance button is REMOVED, and a Reminders button in the same `NavItem` shape takes its slot, opening Brain → Coming up (`brain.work.coming-up`, the plate that already reads "Reminders, alarms, timers and repeating jobs") through the app's existing one-time section jump (`pendingSection` + `pendingSectionScreen`), so nothing new is read, no route is added and no second navigation system exists. Nothing is deleted from Appearance: its screen and its own Settings row are untouched, `settings.appearance-card` is still the switch that hides that row, and "open appearance" by voice or chat still lands on it. The menu id `entry.appearance` is KEPT - ids are never reused or renamed, and the phone still has Appearance - but it is no longer a home-surface toggle: `backend/jarvis_menus.py` now says `hide=False` with the reason written down, because a switch over a button that no longer exists would turn nothing off, and a dead switch is worse than no switch. So "Show or hide menus" stops offering it, hiding it is refused rather than stored, its derived spoken name "appearance button on home" goes with the button, and `MenuPlaces.INSIDE` keeps the id listed (with where it went) so the phone's map of menus with no place of their own stays complete and Find anything lists exactly one Appearance place, the Settings row. The phone's planned-but-unwired Home layout model (`net/HudLayout.kt`, A1: no screen reads `MenuPrefs.hudLayout` yet) drops its Appearance card and its references in the Default and Brain & Learning presets, so a preset or a pasted document cannot put the removed button back. Desktop: unchanged, and no §8 parity gap - the PC has no such row, its Appearance is already a Settings card and Coming up already lives in its Brain, which `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 now records beside the HUD's own Reminders tab. Proven by `HomeNavRowTest` (the row's six destinations in order, no Appearance item, the Coming up landing, Appearance's Settings route, the refused hide, Find's one Appearance row, the drawn bell), `HudLayoutTest`, `MenuVisibilityTest`, `FindAnythingTest`, `ComingUpReachabilityTest`, `backend/test_menu_visibility.py` (467 checks) and the regenerated `menu-cases.json`/`MenuCatalog.kt`/`menu-catalog.js`; no device was driven, so the button on glass is CI's emulator smoke, not a PASS here.

- **2026-11-02 — The phone gets its own editable HUD, and the desktop's seven widescreen presets stay desktop-only:** The owner's instruction of 2026-11-01, "add building the real editor to the queue", is acted on by building the Android `A1`-`A4` slice into shipped code rather than leaving it a model nothing drew. **What decided it:** `HudLayout.kt` and `MenuPrefs` already existed on `main` with four ordered sections (`top_strip` / `hero` / `body` / `composer`), five read-only built-in arrangements, one `apply` reducer, a `normalize` for untrusted documents and a versioned JSON document - and a `git grep` for `hudLayout|applyLayout` under `ui/` returned nothing, so the owner could not reach any of it. **What the phone gets:** Home draws the saved layout (with the existing hide rules applied on top, so a hidden menu still empties its card), and an "Edit HUD" screen moves cards by drag, by click-only buttons and by TalkBack custom actions that all call the one reducer; the five built-ins stay read-only and a copy is what the owner edits; a pasted layout goes through the same safe reader a stored one does; `Done` is the single write. It is a display preference - the same class as the theme - so it raises no approval card, opens no route, sends nothing to the PC and needs no pairing. **Why the desktop is deliberately untouched:** the desktop's HUD is a 1280x820 widescreen cockpit whose named regions (`header`, `left_rail`, `stage_top`, `stage_main`, `right_rail`) and card ids exist only there, and its seven built-in presets are desktop data mirrored in `contract/hud-presets.json` for its own Rust and tests. The phone's four sections are not those five regions and its card ids are the phone's own `MenuCatalog` menus, so the two layouts are different questions rather than two halves of one choice - the phone never reads `contract/hud-presets.json`, and `tools/check_parity.py` has nothing to classify. **What this does not do:** it adds no shared route (the PC has no `/api/home-cards`, and the phone's choice is not readable from the PC - `docs/HUD-MAIN-SCREEN-CARDS-2026-10-29.md` section 7 is still the design for that), no adding or removing of the *cards the catalogue offers* beyond putting a layout-missing card back, and no real-device drag: the phone's own touch and pen drag is NOT-TESTABLE at this desk and CI's Gradle build is the compiler.

- **2026-11-02 — The phone's generated feature directory is checked against the PC contract, not against counts typed into its test:** The Settings "All features and abilities" list is generated from `contract/feature-controls.json`, and the test that pins its shape counted rows per label with numbers typed by hand (42/2/15/71/12). Those numbers were last corrected on 2026-10-28; six days later the contract held 168 features and the checked-in directory still held 142, and every assertion passed because the test agreed with the stale artifact rather than with the source. Decided: the test READS the contract (its `feature_count` and `label_counts`) and compares the generated rows against it, so regeneration drift fails the test; the typed counts are gone. This is the same rule the repo already applies to twins and to generated fixtures - a generated file is proven against the file it is generated from, not against a number a person remembered to update - and it is why the miss surfaced only when a separate lane regenerated the directory for an unrelated wording fix. Two consequences are recorded deliberately rather than hidden: (a) the regenerated prose quotes the PC's own words, and two rows now name `/api/receipts` and `/api/notion/preview`, which the phone cannot call - `tools/check_parity.py` gained `PHONE_TEXT_ONLY`, a text-only exemption that applies to that one generated file and is void if its GENERATED header ever disappears, so a hand-written file naming routes is still a caller; (b) the directory itself is regenerated by its own tool in this change; no desktop file changed and no owner-visible surface was switched on or off.

- **2026-11-02 — The phone's Photo row is gone in favour of one Attach a file row that also takes a photo, and Quick note must open where it is pressed:** The owner's words, 2026-11-02: *"in the screenshot remove the photo option because ATTach a file on my Android phone will bring up the option to add a photo"* and *"the quick note button doesn't do anything and I don't even know what it was for in the first place"*. Decided: the phone has ONE row for sending something with a question, "Attach a file", and it opens the system picker filtered for the eight documents the PC already reads plus an image type wildcard while the PC's Pictures feature works - so the picker itself is where a photo is chosen, which is what the owner said his Android file picker already does. A picked image is routed by the pure `AttachFile.goesToPicture(name, mime)` to the existing picture path (`ChatPicture` and `PictureEncoder`: vision, and secrets covered with black boxes before any model sees it) and is NEVER read down the document path; a name whose extension is one of the eight documents wins over a provider's image type, so a mislabelled PDF cannot be swallowed. The Photo row's gate is kept: with `HomeState.pictureOffered` false the picker offers no images, and an image that still arrives is refused with `AttachFile.photoNeedsPictures` in plain words rather than read as a document. The More menu is four rows (New chat, Attach a file, Modes, Quick note) plus Close, and the `MoreMenuWords.PHOTO` constant is removed with the row. Quick note is a real feature - it files the owner's own words into Logseq, Joplin or Obsidian through `POST /api/notes/capture` (`backend/note-capture.patch`) - and the reason it looked dead is that its plate was a `LazyColumn` item inside `ConversationList`: full screen composes no conversation list at all, and in the chat the item sat at the very end where it could open below the fold. Decided: it is a `Dialog` sheet drawn once above both layouts, next to the More menu, with the same words and the same Close, and its dead closed-state `Quiet("Quick note…")` branch is removed with the parameter that kept it alive. Nothing in the backend changes - no route, no approval behaviour, no capability - and the desktop keeps its own photo and note surfaces, so this is a phone-only UI change, not a half-shipped feature. Stated limits: compiled and unit-tested only, no device built or driven from this branch, so the box's fit at 360dp, the keyboard's Send key and the sheet on screen are NOT field-tested (BLOCKED, never a pass).

- **2026-11-02 — Resetting the phone app must never change the PC's chosen voice, and the PC must always be able to say which voice the owner chose:** The owner's words, 2026-11-02: *"when I reset the jarvis Android app it changes the voice to the default. it doesn't seem to remember what I changed it to. fix it"*. Decided: the phone's one app-level reset ("Unpair & clear the token", `POST /api/devices/remove`) may clear what the phone owns - its pairing, its Keystore token, its saved address and resume point - and must never change a setting on the PC; the voice Jarvis speaks in, its speed and any animal's voice are the owner's PC-wide settings in `voices/state.json` (`jarvis_voices`), and the reset route writes the device registry only, which is now pinned by a test that compares the file byte for byte around a real reset. A re-paired or reinstalled phone gets the stored choice back the moment it connects - the PC reports `speaker.choice` (the voice that SPEAKS) plus `speaker.saved` (the owner's own choice), because with only `choice` a fallback or a fresh install made the pack default look like the choice the owner made, which is what "it doesn't remember what I changed it to" was. And a `voices/state.json` that exists but cannot be read is REFUSED rather than merged onto defaults: one changed key must never rewrite the owner's whole voice, the same rule `jarvis_manner` already follows for its own file (data-integrity audit F3, 2026-10-28). Stated limits: the exact click that wrote the default on the owner's PC is not identified from the audit log (it proves the route and the moment, not the finger), and no real phone was reset and re-paired or built from this branch, so the field row stays BLOCKED, never a pass.

- **2026-11-02 — In picture-in-picture, "hey Jarvis" is one single voice input and never starts Live:** The owner asked, 2026-11-01 ~21:47 PT, with a screenshot of the small window on his home screen: *"whenever jarvis is in picture-in-picture mode like in this screenshot I would like to be able to say hey jarvis to be able to say something to jarvis and have jarvis process what I said. if it's not in live mode don't have a turn on live mode but comprehend it as a single input."* Decided: a "hey Jarvis" heard while the picture-in-picture window is up is ONE clip on the existing `source=wake_word` route and ONE ordinary turn - it never starts, resumes or moves Jarvis Live, it never brings the activity out of the window, and the answer is spoken by the same runtime path as outside the window, so no new route, permission, dependency, backend change or phone-side speech-to-text is added and no second listener is built. The already-existing half was verified rather than assumed: the microphone foreground service pauses only for the talk button and for Live on this phone, so the window - a paused activity - never stopped it, and nothing on that path starts an activity. The one thing missing was that the window said nothing, because a wake turn has no `CAPTURING` phase (the service records before the desktop is asked); so the window now draws the existing state word - Listening / Thinking / Speaking - only while a turn is actually running (`PipWords.working`, from the voice phase plus `WakeWordService.state`), in the two modes that have no words of their own, never in the hidden window and never over Live's own status line. That keeps the owner's 2026-10-31 revision intact: the resting window is the face alone. NOT verified on a phone: that the word reads at window size and that the answer is heard while another app is in front - `docs/PIP-DESIGN.md` §7 step 14 is that step, and it is not a pass.

- **2026-11-02 — Plugins are listed and switched by chat, one card per change, and OFF is immediate:** The owner decided: "Jarvis may list plugins and turn them on/off by chat, one card per change." Decided: two model tools in `backend/jarvis_agent.py` are the door to the drop-in plugin folder `jarvis_plugins.py` already loads - `plugin_list` (read-only: every folder, whether it is on, and why it is off) and `plugin_switch` (ONE named plugin, `on` or `off`). TURNING ONE ON IS CARDED, because a plugin is program code that runs inside the backend at start-up: it goes through the EXISTING gate under `modify_own_code` (the action `jarvis_skills.write_skill` already raises for the same kind of act, already at tier `ask`), reached through the published `skill_manage` `_TOOL_ACTIONS` key, so no gate action, tier line, risk row, card wording or `jarvis_gate.py` patch is invented. TURNING ONE OFF IS IMMEDIATE AND CARDLESS, the project's own on/off rule: stopping only narrows what runs. The tool is also in `NEEDS_A_PERSON`, so a settings file that ever loosened `modify_own_code` still cannot switch a plugin on with nobody asked; a denied or timed-out card changes nothing. NO SECOND MECHANISM AND NO DELETE: the write is the loader's own `disabled` marker file (created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`, removed only after the folder and its `plugin.json` are still there) - the same marker `discover()` already reads - and no folder is created, moved, renamed or deleted; a plugin switched off by `"enabled": false` in its own `plugin.json` is reported and refused, because that is a hand edit on the PC, not a chat toggle. THE RUNTIME TRUTH IS SAID, NOT PRETENDED: the loader runs once at HUD start-up, so neither direction is live in the running process; every answer says the change lands the next time Jarvis starts and that Jarvis cannot restart itself, and nothing here restarts anything. NO NEW ROUTE AND NO NEW SCREEN: both tools are model tools, so either app's chat reaches them, but neither app draws a plugin list or a switch (a phone screen would be deep config editing, and a desktop section would be a second door beside the one the owner asked for) - `tools/check_parity.py` is unchanged and clean, and the surface decision is recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8. Both tools ship ON in `[tools].enabled`, because a feature reachable only by hand-editing that same list would not be reachable by chat; both are listed in `jarvis_reach.TOOL_NAMES`, sit in the `settings` short-list group and carry tool-diet hints, and the feature is on both apps' Features pages (`plugin-switch`). Proved by `backend/test_plugin_switch.py` and the every-tool suites, and recorded in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §181.

- **2026-11-02 — The phone's mic press does not check the voice print:** The owner asked: *"also, when i do the mic press to make a short verbal message to jarvis, dont have it confirm my voice through the voice id"*. A `source=push_to_talk` clip from `mic=phone` - the phone's own talk button, and nothing else - now skips `jarvis_voice.verify()`, and the 2-second "say a little more" refusal goes with it, because that minimum exists only to give the speaker model enough audio; a short message is transcribed and answered. The press on his own paired phone is the act, the way typing a message is, so whose voice it is no longer decides that one surface - stated plainly because it is the honest cost. What the check also bought is NOT granted: a private, memory or sensitive answer is not read aloud (the reply says `strictness: ""` and `mode: "quick_message"`, so `_really_checked()` is false), automatic learning refuses the turn (GUARDS L8 needs `very_strict` in mode `owner`), and `screen_aloud` is unchanged because that rule never rested on the check. It cannot open Jarvis Live either: "let's talk" from that press is an ordinary message, so the ways into a session stay a passed check (the desktop's button, "Hey Jarvis, let's talk") or the app's own Start control - "NO LIVE WITHOUT A REAL VOICE CHECK" is not loosened. Every other surface still checks every clip: Jarvis Live (its own start gate and its per-clip check are untouched), the phone's "hey Jarvis", the desktop's talk button (`mic=desktop`), and any clip that names no microphone. The button's readiness gate (`listening.push_to_talk`: a trained print, the voice-ID model and speech-to-text) is unchanged too - this removes the per-clip confirmation, not the enrolment. The desktop's own quickbar microphone was deliberately NOT changed, because the request names the phone's press. No route, setting or permission was added. Proved in `backend/test_quick_mic.py`, with the unchanged halves in `backend/test_voice_mic.py`, `backend/test_live.py` and `backend/test_voice_strict.py`; the reasoning in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 ("One-sided on purpose") and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §5.

- **2026-11-02 — Reminders may ask a question with three of the owner's buttons, and answering is a cardless log:** The owner asked for reminders he can shape himself - *"tell Jarvis exactly how I want the reminder to appear and what interactive elements there are"* - and then, asked how much flexibility, *"as much flexibility or options as I want"*. Decided and built in one lane: a reminder's action gains a fifth kind, `ask`, carrying his own question, up to three buttons in his own words (each doing exactly one of record / done / snooze N), and per-reminder recording destinations (its own history, today's Obsidian note, a goal's progress, a habit tick). Three ceilings are deliberate and were not negotiable: three buttons, because Android draws three notification actions; no button that runs a command, a script or a webhook; and no approval card for an answer, because an answer is a log line, cardless like ticking a to-do, and the phone takes one only while unlocked since it writes a personal record. The schedule grammar grew every N days, every N weeks, several times in a day, a first occurrence and an optional end date, all on the existing rule object so a plain rule is byte for byte what it was. The one thing REFUSED, with its reason in the UI and the docs, is a button that opens a saved file or a page: the desktop's single opener opens a reminder's own action and takes the job id only, so a per-button target needs a second opener in Rust, which is a security surface this lane does not own. Two seams were left deliberately unfinished and say so out loud rather than pretending: goal progress (PR #1105's log) and habit ticks (the life-coach lane) each answer "not set up on this PC yet" and keep the answer.

- **2026-11-02 — Make the existing No-Nonsense Critic a real skeptic instead of adding an eleventh preset:** The owner asked for a personality that questions his assumptions - especially his own - to counter AI agreeableness, read the research report that measured the options, and chose **A + C**: rewrite `devils_advocate`'s `prompt_block` in `contract/personalities.json`, and carry the same behaviours in its per-turn `post_history_hint`. The rejected option was a new eleventh "Skeptic" preset, and the reasons are recorded because they still bind: "ten" is asserted in more than six places (the contract's `preset_count`, `tools/gen_personalities.py:90`, `check_personalities.py`, `test_manner.py`, both apps' fixtures), "skeptic" is **already** an alias of `devils_advocate` and aliases must be unique (`gen_personalities.py:158-159`), so a second preset would have to take away the one word he wanted to be able to say - and two presets that red-team the same thinking is the duplicate-of-an-existing-feature the audit rules out. What was decided, in the owner's words and the measured constraints: (1) the block treats his claim as a question, not a fact, and says "especially mine" - the wording the research found measured to work (Dubois et al., *Ask don't tell*, AISI, 2026) - and it holds its ground when he only repeats himself, separates what it verified from what it assumed, and never folds to be agreeable; (2) it **keeps** "Do not manufacture objections." (the antidote to contrarian theatre) and the kindness guard "without cruelty", and gains the valve "If I say drop it, drop it."; (3) the budget is the project's measured hard cap - the assembled block must stay at or under 750 characters (`backend/jarvis_manner.py:1023`, gated by `tools/check_personalities.py:186-190` for both a preset's own dials and the longest word on every dial) - so this was a rewrite paid for by cuts, not an append: the "You are Jarvis as a no-nonsense critic and red-team partner" name repetition, "Find where the plan breaks", "briefly" and "the one change that most improves the odds" are gone, and the persona tag's `name="No-Nonsense Critic"` plus the base system prompt's "You are Jarvis" still carry the identity. The old "Label guesses" half is replaced by the sharper "Separate verified from assumed", and "never claim an action not taken" is deliberately not repeated in this preset because `jarvis_profiles.JARVIS_SYSTEM` already sends "Never claim an action was taken that was not" to every model word for word, so nothing project-wide is lost - that same base prompt also keeps "Honest before agreeable ... Do not change a correct answer just because they push back", which the preset now sharpens rather than duplicates. Measured after the change: `prompt_block` 323 characters, assembled 738 with the preset's own dials and 747 with the longest word on every dial (was 722 / 730 - the critic remains the widest preset in the set, now with 3 characters to spare), and the hint is 215 characters (was 96, cap 220, `gen_personalities.py:124`). The id, title, description, aliases, dials, voice blend, voice speed and greeting are untouched, no card is added or removed (a personality switch raises none either way), and no new route, permission or egress exists. Proven: both generated copies and the SHA pin rewritten by `tools/gen_personalities.py --check`; `check_personalities.py` 47 passed; `backend/test_manner.py` 624 passed, 0 failed (clean config folder); `test_quick_wins.py` 233, `test_base_matches_repo.py` 135, `test_base_regeneration.py` 39, `check_stale_twins.py` all match. **Not proven, and not claimed:** that the local 8B model actually resists sycophancy better - no model-quality measurement exists for any of the ten presets, and the research report says the same; this change makes the instruction present and measurable, not the behaviour proven.
