- **2026-11-02 — To-do day carry-over: BOTH modes, full daily rollover by
  default, and `created_date` is immutable:** The owner's answer, 2026-11-02
  ~00:41 PT, to the measured gap in the to-do list: *"To-do carry-over: build
  BOTH, with full daily rollover (option B) as the DEFAULT, changeable by asking
  Jarvis or in Settings."* He asked the question himself the same night - *is
  Jarvis smart enough that next day "what's on my to-do list today" brings up
  yesterday's unfinished items while saying they are from yesterday?* - and the
  measurement against `origin/main` said: yes, they carried over, but nothing
  said they were yesterday's, and the Today board's `rollover_cards` had never
  been built. Gemini's ruling 8 fixed the design: an **immutable `created_date`**
  (YYYY-MM-DD, the PC's local day) written once when an item is created and
  never rewritten - not at midnight, not by an edit, not by the mode switch -
  because a rollover that re-stamped items with "today" would erase the age it
  is meant to show; **dynamic tags measured from it** (1 day = "from
  yesterday", 2-6 days = "from <Weekday> (<N>d ago)", 7+ = "from <MMM D>"), so
  a 3-day-old item never says "from yesterday"; **full daily rollover as the
  default**; **a day-labelled mode as the alternative, switched in Settings on
  either app or by asking Jarvis**, lossless in both directions because no item
  moves; and a **migration** backfilling `created_date` from each row's
  `created`, or today for a legacy row with no usable stamp. This is NOT the
  already-documented `rollover_cards` plan for the Today board and does not
  build it: that needs a per-day completion record for a card, while this is the
  scheduler's to-do list, whose items carry their own day. Everything ends at
  ONE PC method (`jarvis_schedule.set_todo_mode_here`), so a tap and a sentence
  cannot disagree; no approval card either way, because it changes how the
  owner's own list is drawn and touches no row. Both apps draw it: the desktop's
  Brain "Coming up" card and its Settings card, and the phone's "Coming up"
  plate and its control under Limits (JARVIS-API §179). The same night's second
  half - the phone's UI text removals - is a separate decision, not this one.

- **2026-11-02 — The conversation web-search grant ASK rides with web search and is not a Settings switch, and an approval may never be claimed from the owner's words:** The field test of 2026-11-02 asked for the grant in two natural sentences and got NO card, with the model answering "Understood. Search is approved for this conversation." The cause was design, not wording: the two tools shipped as "Safety and sharing" switches that were off, so the model was never offered the grant tool and no card could be raised. Decided: the ask and its instant stop are not switches at all - `jarvis_agent.GRANT_ASK_TOOLS` is offered whenever `web_search` is offered, and switching web search off in Settings takes both with it. Offering the ask grants nothing: the store is still written only after a person answers the card, the action is still tier `ask` and in `NEEDS_A_PERSON`, the scope is still one conversation and `search_the_web` only, the stop is still instant with no card, and nothing is written to disk. The alternative - leaving them as switches and asking the owner to switch them on first - was rejected because it is what made the feature dead on the owner's own PC while telling him it had worked. The second decision is the honesty half: an approval is real only when a real state read says so. The rules block now says an approval is not the model's to give or assume and may not be claimed unless a tool result in that conversation said one is in force; while a grant is live the prompt carries `_grant_prompt_line`'s line read from `web_search_grant` (the same function the search consults), and an answer that claims an approval the store does not hold is corrected in plain words (`_grant_claim_line`, through `postscript_lines`, for both the local and the cloud lane). A wrong correction after a true sentence is worse than a missed one, so an honest denial and a conditional are never touched. No new gate action, tier or `_RISK` row; no bulk or automatic approval; the conversation id is still never written down.

- **2026-11-03 — A bare pasted link is read behind one card, the page is remembered for 15 minutes so a follow-up needs no second card, and a typed "yes" only points at a card while one is really waiting:** Three rules, each measured before it was decided, and what each replaces. **(a) A pasted link is a request.** Gemini's ruling Q2 supersedes the read-a-link slice's own gate of earlier the same day ("a link with no read verb is never read"): a message that is ONLY an `http(s)` address, or an address plus a question about it, now reaches the same read-a-link path and raises the SAME ONE card per URL under the reader's own action (`read_web_page` / `youtube_captions_read`), with the canonical address the card showed on the FIRST LINE of the answer so both apps make it tappable with no rendering change. Nothing is fetched before a person answers, a decline fetches nothing, and a link inside a statement ("here is a link ...") or a browser command ("open <url> in my browser") keeps its own path - the card is the only guard, and a card per paste is the accepted cost of not letting an 8B model guess at an address nothing opened. **(b) One page is kept per conversation, in memory, for 900 seconds.** A follow-up that refers to the page just read ("what does it say about the limescale filter?") is answered from the words already on this PC with NO second card and NO second fetch, quoting around what it finds and saying plainly when the kept characters do not mention it. It is a word-find, never reasoning, and it says so when it finds nothing; the text lives in `jarvis_quick.py`'s own process, capped at one page per chat and eight chats, cleared by a restart, replaced by a new page in the same chat, and never stored on a private turn. This is why no card is needed for the follow-up while a fresh fetch still needs one: nothing new leaves the PC. `jarvis_readpage.py`'s own promise that it writes nothing and keeps nothing is untouched - the kept text never reaches that module and never reaches disk. **(c) A typed decision word answers only while a card is waiting.** The 2026-10-11 behaviour ("approve", "deny", "yes", "no" as the whole message says where the approval window is) was unconditional, so a bare "yes" or "no" in ordinary conversation got the canned "approvals are decided on the card itself" sentence with nothing pending - measured on all four of "yes", "Yes", "yes please" and "no". The intent is now returned only after this PC's own approvals table (`jarvis_gate.pending()`) says a card is really waiting, and otherwise the sentence is left to the model; it still can never approve anything, and a gate that is absent or unreadable counts as nothing waiting, so a broken approvals read can never replace a healthy answer. Deliberately NOT in this change: the "Where this came from" source row for a page read (it needs `read_web_page` in `jarvis_sources.KNOWN_TOOLS` and a seam in `jarvis_hud.py`), and the nine cardless settings-receipt families of ruling Q1 (they need value readers in `jarvis_settings_registry.py`), both of which stay open for their own pull request.

- **2026-11-03 — Accounts self-knowledge ships backend-first, on its own route, under its own names:** The owner asked Jarvis to explain "what accounts are actively connected to jarvis, what permissions and abilities jarvis has for those accounts, whats changeable, how to disconnect the account, and how to connect new accounts". Built as one read-only `GET /api/accounts` (`jarvis_accounts.OVERVIEW_PATH`) over twelve account families, with every ability resolved live from the permission table (`jarvis_framework.action_tier`) and the gate's own risk words (`jarvis_gate.risk_for`) - never a copied tier, never a socket, never a value, entry NAMES only - plus `disconnect()` / `removability()` in `jarvis_connect_account.py` that delete exactly one service's own Credential Manager entries. Two decisions are recorded here because a later slice must respect them. **First, the names:** `jarvis_accounts.py` already shipped `view()` and `handle_get()` as the shipped `GET /api/accounts/addresses` answer (`backend/accounts.patch`), so the new surface is `accounts_view()` / `handle_accounts_get()` and the addresses answer stays byte-untouched - appending same-named functions would have shadowed a shipped route and silently changed what the desktop's Settings > Accounts reads (found by two independent workers before it shipped). **Second, the split:** the chat sentence, `/api/self`, the desktop and phone Accounts plates, and the API/parity documentation are a coordinated follow-up, not part of this change; `disconnect()` and `removability()` exist but no route and no card calls them until the Remove-button slice. The honest limits ride in the rows themselves: "connected" only when a verifier actually ran in that call, "I can't know when" for the connect time, and four gate actions that have `[autonomy.tiers]` lines but no `jarvis_gate._RISK` row carry `classified: False` and the gate's own unclassified warning rather than an invented tier.

- **2026-11-03 — Cloud escalation on an ordinary turn, and the blank cloud answer:** the 2026-11-03 field test (`.dsh-scratch/F6-2026-11-03/DEEPSEEK-FIELD-TEST/`) measured two defects. First, `jarvis_hud.py`'s Project Mode gate zeroed the cloud lanes unless an active project was also Shareable, so an ordinary turn could never escalate (`gate: "unavailable"`, "no cloud lane was offered") even with the DeepSeek key saved and the Cloud preset chosen. The owner's decision, in his words *"an ordinary turn with no active project MAY escalate when every router gate passes and the standing switch is on"*: the gate now zeroes the lanes only for an ACTIVE project that is not Shareable - that privacy promise is unchanged - and an ordinary turn keeps them, with `jarvis_router.choose()`'s own gates (private, tainted, picture, no-lane, complexity, budget) and the PC's standing escalation switch deciding exactly as before. Second, DeepSeek's thinking mode bills its hidden reasoning INSIDE `max_tokens`: at the relay's 2048 default it returned `finish_reason: "length"` with `content: ""` and all 2048 tokens on `reasoning_tokens`. The owner's decision *"make it usable or fall back honestly"*: a lane this PC measured as reasoning-inside (`Preset.thinking_inside`, one field, DeepSeek from the 2026-10-14 and 2026-11-03 tests) is sent the cap `money_check()` priced PLUS `REASONING_ROOM`, and a reply that still has no usable answer is answered on THIS PC under ONE honest line ("The cloud model used its whole answer budget thinking and sent nothing back; here is the local answer:") - the working-out is never shown, on a clicked turn or an automatic one. This replaces the 2026-10-14 "show the working-out on a clicked turn" rule; nothing about the privacy gates, the money limit, the crisis rule or the standing switch's own card changed.

- **2026-11-03 — Desktop navigation rides the per-answer route field, a chat window is a HUD page with its own conversation, and one Update press moves both halves:** decided while building the F6 desktop slice. (1) Navigation is the EXISTING `X-Jarvis-Route` path extended with `open_area`/`open_anchor` - one table in `hud_nav.rs` maps an area id to the HUD view/tab, the History sidebar, the Presets menu, Settings at a card, the Brain at a place, Faces, the feature list or a new chat window, and the injected chrome performs the page switch. There is deliberately no `ui.navigate` stream listener: the backend kept navigation on the route field (the F6 research correction, RESEARCH.md F3/F5) and publishes no such event, so a listener would be a doorbell into an empty room. If a navigation frame is ever added it must be label-filtered and its client handler must ship with the publisher, never a broadcast - Tauri event payloads are outside the ACL. (2) An extra chat window is the SAME vendored HUD page with its own conversation id, not a reduced surface: the capability's `windows` now carries `chat-*`, the eight labels are a fixed `&'static str` set so `lock.rs`'s capture sweep and hide loop and `window_memory.rs`'s tracked list can include them without widening their types, and the same conversation in two windows is a focus of the existing window, never a second copy on one transcript. The HUD page is a byte-identical twin of the backend's copy, so its controls are injected by the shell bootstrap rather than forked into it. (3) The Settings Update press runs `update_both` (backend first, desktop second) for the owner's "both are always updated at the same time"; the desktop-only `install_update` survives ONLY for a PC whose backend half cannot run, and that path says in words that the backend was not updated and where to finish it. A read-back handshake compares this executable's version with `GET /api/self`'s `version.app_version` and may say "IN SYNC" only when both sides name the same version; a different numbering scheme is reported as incomparable rather than guessed at. `/api/self` and `/api/conversations` were added to `hud_proxy.rs`'s fixed read allowlist because the HUD page cannot read any route that is not on it.

- **2026-11-03 — The GitHub tools get their own read action at `ask`, never `auto`, and `github_read` is left alone:** The owner's decision was "Read + actions" - Jarvis may read his GitHub (repositories, open pull requests, issues, CI status, one file) and may comment, open an issue and re-run a workflow, each action behind its own card, and it may never merge, push, commit, delete or close. The tempting shape was to reuse `github_read`, which already exists and whose risk row already says "reads public GitHub data". It was refused for a measured reason: `github_read` is the action a "tell me when" GitHub watch makes on a timer, its line in the shipped settings is `auto`, and `jarvis_tellme.py` REFUSES to run a GitHub watch unless it stays `auto` - a look every ten minutes cannot raise a card every ten minutes. Reusing it would either run these new reads at `auto` (the owner's token leaving this PC with nobody asked, on a read the model chose the moment of) or force that line to `ask` and break every GitHub watch. So the on-demand reads are their own action, `github_inspect`, at `ask`: one card per read. Three things were weighed and two rejected. **`auto`** was rejected outright - "it is only a read" is not a reason to spend a credential with nobody looking, and the same call was already made for `github_search` when it was found resolving to `web_research` at `auto`. **A one-per-conversation grant**, the shape the owner chose for web search on 2026-11-01, was rejected here: a web search sends words the owner just asked about, while a GitHub read carries his personal access token and can reach private repositories, and a standing grant would let every later call in that chat spend the credential without a person looking at what was asked. It is the more conservative of the two, and it is also the one that needs no new standing-permission store. **`ask` per read** is what shipped. All six tools are ALSO in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`, so the setting says how much Jarvis asks and that set says a read like this is never done with nobody asked - the same belt `github_search` already wears. The three actions are `ask` for the obvious reason and cannot be anything else: a comment and an issue are posted in the owner's name and Jarvis cannot edit or withdraw either, and a re-run can deploy or notify if that workflow does. `github_rerun_workflow`'s risk row is `reversible = "no"` for that reason, even though it changes nothing in the repository. Nothing here is reachable until the owner saves a token ("connect GitHub") and adds the six names to `[tools].enabled`, exactly like `github_search`.

- **2026-11-03 — Fact-by-fact learning, a patient sensitive check, and a recheck for the reworded cards:** Gemini's rulings Q1-Q3 on the memory review, built as Slice 1 of the owner's "all of them starting with one" choice. What was decided: (1) per-fact attribution replaces the pass-wide rule - a fact is learned from the clean turns that hold its words, and the words must fit one clean turn or two consecutive clean turns with no tainted turn between them (a union of separate clean turns could be assembled by a tool output in the middle; that is closed), and in a pass where any turn is not learnable from, the reworded switch cannot bypass the grounding check; (2) a sensitive-topic check that could not run is asked once more after a 1.5 s pause with a 30 s deadline - a clean second answer saves, a second failure is still a card and still counted as the fault it is; (3) the pending cards whose only reason was "not in your own words" save by themselves when the reworded switch turns on, and on every later pass, at most five per call. What it deliberately does not do: it changes no check on a turn that itself read outside text (that turn still cards the facts that need its words), adds no switch and no store, stores no conversation turns to make old cards recheckable (so the other two old card reasons stay cards for the owner's yes, said plainly in the API doc), and touches neither the memory store's plaintext-at-rest ruling nor the per-turn recall budget.

- **2026-11-03 — The Memory tab's pending cards come first, and stay first:** The owner's own request, verbatim: "when i click on the memory cards waiting notification, these pending memory cards should be at the top of the list, not towards the bottom." "Waiting for you" (the pending memory proposals, `#memory-waiting-card` / `#memory-proposals` in `jarvis-desktop/src/brain.html`, painted by `renderProposals()` in `brain.js`) now sits first inside the Memory view's `.panes`, above the Learning card and every saved-memory list, and `showView("memory")` scrolls the view back to it on every arrival. The measurement behind it: the HUD's "N memory cards waiting for you" notice (`jarvis_hud.html`, `#init-memory`, and the Memory-tab list under `#memory-door`) is the way in, its Review button calls the existing `open_fix_place {place:"brain"}`, and the Brain's landing view is already Memory - so the queue's position in the page, not the click, was what made the cards "towards the bottom". What this deliberately does NOT do: it adds no place to `open_fix_place` or `BRAIN_PLACES`, carries no scroll hint from the HUD page (that page is vendored byte-for-byte into `backend/` and `jarvis-backend/`, and this change touches neither), changes nothing a card does or how the queue works, and moves no focus - the scroll is the page's alone, so the rail's tab keeps focus and the heading order is read once. Recorded so a later tidy-up of the Memory tab does not quietly put the queue back under the saved lists.

- **2026-11-03 — The page-reading tool stays unswitchable, and the chat read-a-link path raises one card per link:** Decided on 2026-11-03: `read_web_page` is NOT made switchable from inside either app. It stays in `jarvis_asks_first.TIER_C` and out of `TOOLS_SWITCHABLE`, so `request_tool_enable` keeps answering `403` with `TOOLS_TOML_ONLY_NOTE` for it; its tier stays `ask` (`jarvis-framework.toml`'s `read_web_page = "ask"`), and it stays in `HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`, so nothing in an app can loosen it either. The settings file's `[tools].enabled` line remains the only way to offer the tool to the model, by hand on the PC - which is what `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §115 and `backend/jarvis_reach.py`'s own row already say, and what `backend/test_reach.py` pins. What the owner asked for is built the other way: "read this link" / "read this YouTube video and tell me about it" in either app's chat reaches `jarvis_youtube`'s caption reader or `jarvis_readpage`'s page reader directly - the modules that already exist - and raises ONE `youtube_captions_read` or `read_web_page` card per link, through the readers' own gate calls. A second link is a second card, never a standing permission; a declined, timed-out or unraisable card fetches nothing and says so in the reader's own words. No new route, no new model tool, no new gate action and no tier line are added, which is why this needs no patch and no plugin-catalogue regeneration. The reasoning: both readers already run behind a one-link card and the owner's sentence names that one link, so an in-app switch would widen what the model may reach for no gain, while the hand edit stays the documented, deliberate way in. The chat path therefore does not depend on that switch at all, and the older sentence that taught the hand edit is not made false by this slice - it is still the only way, and it is still true.

- **2026-11-03 — "Personalize Jarvis" is the setup quiz's own name, upgraded in place:** The setup questionnaire is now 25 questions in seven sections, in the SAME Settings card (`setup-questionnaire`) rather than a second window: a section tab row and a step-through view are less plumbing than a new Tauri window, and the card id stays what OpenPlace and both apps reach. The noun is "Personalize Jarvis" (aliases "customization quiz", "setup quiz", "retake setup quiz") so it cannot be confused with `jarvis_quiz.py`'s Quiz Decks. `setup.json` gains a schema version, `completed_version`, `runs`, `dismissed_at` and `in_progress`, and `apply()` now MERGES its answers into the saved ones: a partial retake used to replace them, so every question it did not ask lost its answer. A partial retake still marks the question set complete (`completed_version = QUIZ_VERSION`) because the owner has seen the new questions by then. Applying remains the desktop's own step (`POST /api/setup/apply` is PC-only and card-driven); `POST /api/setup/progress` is cardless and desktop-only, records where the owner is and stages draft answers, calls no setter and never applies, and the chat `setup_quiz` tool can explain and stage but has no way to apply.

- **2026-11-03 — The phone's F6 slice reuses the closed paths rather than adding a second navigation or clearing mechanism:** Two rules, from the F6 research and the wave lead's course correction, and what they replaced. **Navigation** rides the answer's `X-Jarvis-Route` field and the existing `ChatSession.openSettings` one-time request into `OpenPlace`, whose table is extended to name whole screens ("chat", "live", "history", "approvals", "inbox"), the Brain's plates ("memory", "models", "goals", ...), the shared menu ids from `backend/jarvis_menus.py`, and - in words - the real places this build has no screen for yet (Habits, Mood, Plugins are backend-only today). It deliberately does NOT add an SSE `ui.navigate` event kind (a new kind is a two-client, allowlist and `tools/check_event_names.py` change; an empty-room doorbell is a known defect here), Navigation Compose, a deep link, or a new `Screen` entry - the back stack is saved by enum name, so new screens may only be appended, and none was needed. The field's spelling is read in the four reasonable forms (`open_settings`, `open_place`, `open_area`, `open_screen`) because the PC side is being built in the same wave and its name is not pinned yet; a PC that keeps sending `open_settings` needs no change. **Clearing** a conversation is two-phase and per item: one request carries one exact conversation id, the PC raises ONE approval card naming that conversation, saying it cannot be undone and that the facts it taught are KEPT (the same `DELETE_STAYS` sentence the desktop and the phone's confirm use), and nothing is deleted until the owner answers. A waiting answer (202 / `waiting` / `asking`) is never read as "deleted"; the row stays, the queue is re-read so the card can be answered on the phone, and the list re-reads when that card leaves the queue. There is no bulk clear, no card-in-one-card, no cardless delete, and the model cannot clear anything without the owner's card. The desktop's own clear keeps its existing per-item confirm; the two apps still cannot drift on the kept-facts sentence because it is one constant.

- **2026-11-03 — The Coding preset runs at 32,768 tokens, with one measured spill allowance:** The owner chose the full measured rung: 32,768 tokens loads at 16,513.7 MiB with 323.5 MiB in system RAM, cold load is the same as before (36.0 s against 37.0 s at 16,384), and decode is inside the model's own run-to-run noise (80.36 against 79.88 tok/s median on three short prompts). The whole ladder was measured on this PC through the same shipped path (20,480: 203.5 MiB spill; 24,576: 207.5; 28,672: 211.5; 32,768: 323.5), and 16,384 keeps its record as the largest rung with zero spill. So `jarvis_model_lanes.POOLED_CTX` becomes 32,768, and the pooled start passes `POOLED_SPILL_ALLOWANCE` (352 MiB - that measurement plus about 9%, and nothing larger is accepted) to a new `allow_spill` argument on `jarvis_big_coder.load_coder`. That argument is one number for one window: its default is `None`, which keeps the exact zero-spill rule every other caller gets, the big-coder mode's own 28,672-token load and its zero-spill check are untouched, and a load that spills past the cap is still refused with both the actual spill and the allowance named. The measurement configured the window, it did not fill it, so a 15-minute real coding session after deployment is the next test; it was not run here.

- **2026-11-03 — Multi-part reminders are ONE row with two optional columns, not child jobs:** Gemini's Q8/Q9 ruling, and the owner's ask. `schedule.db`'s `jobs` gains nullable `steps` and `step_state` JSON - the same shape the sixteen columns before them took, so an old file opens and a code rollback stays safe. One row, not a parent with children, because every existing path (snooze, the repeat card, `next_due`, both apps' rows) already walks one row, and parent/child would have needed cascade rules in all of them. A part may be TIMED (`offset_min`, or an `at` clock time on the occurrence's own day) or UNTIMED (`offset_min: null`, surfaced when the part before it is answered), and both live in one schema. A part's buttons and destination are the existing action block, validated by the existing `_clean_action`/`_clean_record`, capped at three by Android's own notification ceiling. `due` stays the one cursor: it means "the next moment this row has something to say", so the loop that already fires a reminder fires part 2 and part 3 with no second scheduler, and the part's `fired` mark is written in the same UPDATE so a restart cannot notify one twice. A part more than 12 hours missed while the PC was asleep is marked missed and counted instead of notified - a part is a distinct action rather than a repeat occurrence, so the 2026-09-26 "once, late" rule does not literally apply, but unbounded catch-up is how a feature becomes a nuisance. Creating a routine in chat is cardless, like every one-off reminder since 2026-09-25, and leaves one `jarvis_receipts` entry so Undo survives a restart; pressing Undo raises the ordinary `undo_action` card, because undo is a mutating action and creation is not. Only a part that runs a task raises the existing `schedule_action` card, and its dedupe pair carries the part's index so a second `run-task` part is its own card. Editing an existing reminder's question, buttons or parts is now cardless through the same `edit` verb, which closes the gap JARVIS-API section 21.14 had documented since 2026-11-02. The phone answers parts and never creates or edits one - the standing one-sided rule in ARCHITECTURE section 8, because a part's destination can be this PC's Obsidian vault or a goal/habit id.

- **2026-11-03 — A scheduled task may run any job in the owner's own words, and one that would ask its own card is refused rather than scheduled as two:** The owner's decision of 2026-11-02 was that a scheduled task may record the job in his own words, and that at fire time Jarvis starts it and raises ONE card naming exactly what it will do, with no shell, command or script kind. This slice builds that: a reminder's `run-task` action may carry `job` (the owner's phrase, at most 240 characters) instead of only the closed `briefing`/`backup` names, resolved through the same `jarvis_quick.match` parse half chat uses when the reminder is saved and again when it fires, and run through `jarvis_quick.run` - the same chat path, so there is no executor, no command line and no second interpreter. The batch audit of 2026-11-03 found the one place the first cut broke the promise: a phrase resolving to an intent that raises its OWN approval card (`forget_range`, `update_start`, a setting change that asks, a repeating briefing, "read this link", and the rest read off `jarvis_quick.run`'s dispatch) produced a second card after the scheduler's `schedule_action` card. The PR had disclosed that as a deviation; the owner's promise is kept instead. Such a phrase is refused when the reminder is saved, in one plain sentence that says it needs the owner's approval each time, that it therefore cannot be scheduled as one card, and which action the words matched - nothing is silently dropped, no other intent is substituted, and no reminder is written. A stored row that nevertheless resolves to a carded intent at fire time (an older build, or an upgrade that changed the grammar) is refused there too: no second card, nothing runs, the audit says `needs_approval`, and the row's own view says it did not run and why. Every intent `jarvis_quick.py` can construct was classified carded or cardless against its runner; anything the map does not name is refused conservatively in its own sentence rather than assumed cardless, so a future intent cannot slip a second card through unclassified. Both apps' Reminders screens still send only the closed `task` name, and that one-sided gap is recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 as a deliberate follow-up rather than built here.

- **2026-11-03 — Jarvis knows its own settings, abilities and places, and clears a conversation only through ONE card, one exact item at a time:** the owner's directive of 2026-11-03 - *"open any menu or setting area on request, pull up any old conversation, have multiple conversation windows open at once, clear any memory or conversation on request, and know every setting/function/ability it has"*, plus *"refresh its function and capabilities awareness"* - is built as ONE read-only self portrait and a small set of named asks, not as a new permission. The inventory is IMPORTED, not retyped: `jarvis_self_portrait.places()` joins `jarvis_settings_registry.SECTIONS` and `jarvis_menus.MENUS` (already generated into both apps and test-held to their real ids) and a test fails if any real row is missing or any id is invented; settings are the registry's own switch/choice/number tables with values read through the one public reader; abilities are the feature list's own rows; `/api/self` carries fixed registry data and live state only and never a token, key, secret, memory or chat word, owner path or model-written sentence, with an unreadable value saying "unknown". Navigation is NOT a new event kind: the model's answer header is sent before the turn runs, so a model tool cannot set it, and chat navigation stays on the existing per-request `X-Jarvis-Route` field both apps already read, with `resolve_place()` as the exact-alias door for the deterministic path (a settings sub-row opens its parent card; words that name no place fall through, never jump to a dead id). Conversation ids already existed per request, so the conversation routes are aliases onto the one History store rather than a second list. **Destructive clears keep the existing rule, one action and one decision:** clearing a conversation is irreversible, so it is two-phase and per item - exactly one id, ONE `conversation_clear` approval card naming that chat by title and message count, that it cannot be undone, that the learned facts are KEPT and that older backup copies age out, with no bulk form, no cardless form and nothing deleted until a person approves; **the model is deliberately NOT offered a clear tool at all** (Gemini ruling 1, 2026-11-03): an LLM must never have an autonomous way to wipe the transcript, so clearing stays the REST route, an app UI action or the fast path, and this file's tool set carries only the read-only `self_portrait`, `conversation_find` and `conversation_open`; memory forgetting is not duplicated (it keeps its existing Forget and Forget-a-time-frame flows, never touched by a chat delete). The same rule covers versions, the owner's second ask of the day ("when i click update on the jarvis hud i want it linked to the back end"): `version.app_version` is the one shared version string and `version.deploy` is what the installer RECORDED for the live modules, so the HUD can compare both halves and report a mismatch instead of claiming they moved together. Refreshing its own awareness is a re-read that changes nothing and restarts nothing. The storage self-scan stays a separate module, wired defensively so neither half depends on the other landing first. Nothing here adds a bulk clear, a new way to approve, an auto-clear, a public route, or a second mutation path for any setting.

- **2026-11-03 — A settings change is receipted only when it really happened, and a chat's "undo" names the receipt the setting's own module wrote:** Q1b closes DEF-031 (nine cardless families that told the owner to "say undo" and wrote nothing to take back) and records the three rules the fix runs on. FIRST, a receipt exists only for a change that REALLY happened: a change that only waits on its card writes none, a sentence that changes nothing writes none, and a value that genuinely cannot be read is changed without a receipt rather than with a guessed "before" - so the wake-word switch is read through `jarvis_speech.wake_state()` before the setter, because a two-state switch is only "the other state" when it really moved (measured: "turn on the wake word" while it was already on wrote a receipt whose undo called `set_wake_enabled(False)`, which is instant and cardless, so "undo" silently switched the microphone OFF; reproduced on the Q1b tree and fixed there). SECOND, when a setting's own module records the receipt (the Anti-Slop filter records one per write: its switch, its mode and each scope), the chat's undo pointer names the id that module RETURNED for that exact change - `jarvis_antislop` already put it on its return value and `jarvis_settings_registry.Outcome` now carries it (`receipt_id`, filled by `_say`) - and never "the newest row in the database", because two rows can share a clock tick and another chat or either Settings screen can write one inside the same change; an empty id writes no pointer and no extra receipt, which degrades to the plain "there is nothing here for me to take back" rather than to a guess. THIRD, that bridge's scope is exactly the three Anti-Slop settings reached through `_run_settings_bool`, `_run_settings_choice` and `_run_settings_antislop_scope`; it does NOT cover "make sure the anti-slop filter is on" (`_run_feature_change_apply`, which takes no `conversation`), and it does not cover the model-facing `change_setting` tool, filed open as DEF-034. The receipts store also follows the environment first now (`jarvis_receipts._config_dir()` reads `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR`/`JARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` before the framework constant, which is resolved once at import), because a suite that pointed the environment at a temporary folder afterwards was writing real rows into the owner's own `receipts.db`; the load-bearing assumption is written down rather than assumed - the shipped launcher exports those variables before start, so on the owner's PC the two answers agree and no existing undo history moves. The evidence is executable, not read: `backend/test_settings_receipts.py` is 98 checks, 0 failed, 15 registered test functions, one per family plus the no-op and concurrent-write cases, each driven through the real `jarvis_quick.match()`/`run()`.

- **2026-11-03 — The owner's standby hours free the graphics cards, and the next question wakes them:** asked "jarvis should have the ability to offload the gpus during standby hours: can i set standby hours for you?" and offered the behaviours, the owner chose "Unload the GPUs in my hours" - in the hours he sets, Jarvis unloads the model from the cards, the next question wakes it (a few seconds slower), and the hours are a real setting changed with one card. **What it replaced:** a `[power]` section that described a power the program did not have. `jarvis_power.current()` returned a hard-coded `"quiet"` whenever the clock was inside the window - so the hours could never free a card, whatever `schedule_mode` said - and called `should_standby()` never, so `idle_mode` did nothing either; the settings file itself annotated both keys `# not read`. It also replaced "quiet hours are the only thing a window can be": the window now drops to whatever `schedule_mode` says, `"quiet"` or `"standby"`. **Why a second way to set a window is not a duplicate:** the job-shaped way already exists and is untouched (`jarvis_standby_schedule.py`, kind `standby`, a row in Coming up, no card). This is the settings-shaped way, which is what the owner asked for - four rows on the screen both apps already draw, read from the one table in `jarvis_limits.LIMITS` with no client change, defaulting to today's behaviour (off, quiet, 23:00-07:00). Both end in `jarvis_power_switch.set_mode("standby")`, the one function here that unloads, so there is one unload path rather than two. **Why it waits for a card when the standby schedule does not:** `jarvis_power`'s own docstring draws the line - changing the MODE is free, changing the RULES that put Jarvis under on their own is a config change and waits - and the owner's 2026-09-26 decision that a standby *job* needs no card is about a job he creates and deletes, not about the rules in his settings file. All four rows therefore carry `always_asks` and go to `change_own_config` in either direction, including a time change, because moving the window decides when a card is freed even though it loosens nothing. **And the limits it keeps:** nothing is unloaded while a task, a turn, a Live conversation or a waiting card is using the model (each is a real signal in this codebase, checked in the code rather than only in a document, and again after the card); the mode is still computed from the clock on every call with no background thread flipping a variable; and an explicit choice by the owner or by the standby schedule is never overruled by the window until the clock's answer next changes, which is what his settings file already promised. Not measured on a real card: the suite drives a fake `jarvis_models` and a fake Ollama, so no window has been run against the owner's own Ollama and the first-question delay is the existing standby path's measured 5-15 s rather than a new measurement.

- **2026-11-03 — Storage self-cleanup only ever touches Jarvis's own files:** The owner asked for a storage self-scan that can "clear any temporary files up safely", and when offered categories he chose that Jarvis may clear only the temporary files it made itself - Python cache, its own logs, old deploy snapshots and its own prefixed `%TEMP%` leftovers - behind one approval card naming every path. Build caches (node_modules, target, build, out, dist, .gradle) are reported as *regenerable, slow to rebuild* and are never cleared by Jarvis itself; the owner clears those by hand if he wants the space. Anything outside the live program folder, the repository and `%TEMP%` - the memory/chat/receipt stores in `~/.openjarvis`, the owner's own folders, Downloads, the backup folder - needs the owner's separate approval and is refused by the module rather than ever being planned. Logs and old deploy snapshots are moved into a quarantine folder, never deleted.

- **2026-11-03 — The tray's update row is absent unless an update exists, and its press installs the update rather than opening Settings:** The owner, 2026-11-03: *"when i right click the tray icon for jarvis I want a menu option that appears if there is an update to jarvis"*, with the no-update state being the row **absent, not greyed out**. Presence is one pure function, `tray.rs`'s `update_row(Option<&str>) -> Option<String>`: `None` is "no row", `Some` is the text, naming the version when the check gave one (`Update Jarvis to 0.2.411`) and otherwise `Update Jarvis`. Availability is the **existing** check's own result, read from `update::UpdateState` through `update::available_version` - the same answer the Settings Updates card paints - so there is no second network path and the two surfaces cannot name different versions. The row is parented into the "More…" submenu by `Submenu::append` and taken out with `Submenu::remove` (it is that submenu's last row, so no index is needed); Tauri 2.12's `MenuItem` has no `set_visible`, so the menu is where absence has to live, and the same `MenuItem` handle is kept so it can still be re-labelled. Pressing it runs `update::install_from_tray`, which calls the same `install_update` the Settings Install button calls - never a second updater, never a setting or timer, and never anything automatic - after turning the row into "Updating Jarvis to <version>…" and disabling it so a second press cannot start a second download; a toast carries the `INSTALL_CLOSES_AND_RESTARTS` sentence. On Windows a successful install ends the process and the next launch starts with no row; a failure re-reads the state with `check_for_update` and rebuilds the row from the answer, so a stale "Updating…" or a version the endpoint no longer offers cannot linger. **This supersedes the 2026-10-27 decision that the row "still never checks, downloads or installs"**; the Settings Updates card, its notes and its Check button are unchanged, and the tray press is still one explicit press by the owner. **No App-lock gate**, decided by reading `lock.rs` rather than assuming it: `may_open`/`Covered` answers "may this covered *window* be shown now", and its unlock path ends in `open_now(which)` - it would open Settings after Windows Hello, which is not what this row does. The existing update commands themselves (`install_update`, `update_both`) never ask App lock, and the tray's other machine-changing rows (Quit Jarvis, Stop everything, start/stop the backend) are likewise not gated; what this row does is install a signature-verified official release on an explicit press, and it reveals nothing (a public version number). If the owner ever wants it gated while away, the one-line shape already exists in `lock::app_locked`, the same test `live::start` refuses on.

- **2026-11-03 — Jarvis only asks for your voice on a locked phone, and that is one setting:** The owner's ask, in their own words: *"my voice should only need to be confirmed if i say hi jarvis when the phone is locked … when i start jarvis live on my unlocked phone i dont want it to need to confirm my voice. make this a setting i can change"*. **This SUPERSEDES the 2026-11-01 decision "a Jarvis Live session is verified once, and an answer it can say is said" (`decisions.d/2026-11-01-live-session-verified-once.md`) and the 2026-11-02 decision that followed it (`2026-11-02-live-voice-start-verifies-the-session.md`), but only for the PHONE and only for the trigger:** under those two decisions the first full sentence of every Live session was checked and the result then covered the session, so a session the owner began by pressing Live on a phone he had just unlocked still ran the speaker model on its first clip - exactly what he asked to stop. That check is not cached differently now, it is **removed for that trigger**: the unlock of the phone is the act that proves who is holding it, in the same way the 2026-11-02 decision already treated the phone's mic press as the act. Everything the old decisions protected still holds where it mattered: the **desktop is unchanged** (a PC has no "locked phone", so it keeps the 2026-11-01 rule, its spot check and its read-aloud flags); a **voice-started** session still carries the check in, because "Hey Jarvis, let's talk" is only answered after that clip passed the owner check (2026-11-02, untouched); a phone session that does not say whether it was locked - every app older than this change - keeps the check, so nothing about an old phone changes; approvals are still taps and never voice; and a session that was not checked carries no strictness, so **nothing that needs a real check is read aloud on it** - the rule grants nothing, it only stops asking. **One rule, one place:** `backend/jarvis_live.py`'s `voice_check_needed(trigger, device, locked, setting_on)` answers (a) the mic press never checks, (b) "hi Jarvis" on a LOCKED phone checks (the only check left), (c) Live started from an UNLOCKED phone does not check; the phone's copy is `jarvis-client`'s `voice/VoiceCheckRule.kt`, held to the Python table row for row by its JVM test, and the phone's only power is to SAY whether its own screen was locked - one new `"locked"` field on the existing `POST /api/voice/live` start body, never a new route and never a client-side skip. **The one setting** (`voice_check_locked`, ON by default = the rule above) changes the EXEMPTION, not a check: ON is the owner's own rule - an UNLOCKED phone's Live start, and (once the patch wave can carry the lock state) an UNLOCKED phone's "hi Jarvis", skip the check - and because ON is the looser direction it raises ONE `change_own_config` approval card, while `OFF` is at once and gives the OLD, FULL checks back with the phone's "I am unlocked" then IGNORED - OFF is never "no checks", because withdrawing an exemption must not quietly weaken a gate. It is read and written through the SAME existing Live route (`{"do":"voice_check"}`, no value = read), so no route was added for it. Its `section` in `backend/jarvis_settings_registry.py` is deliberately `None` - the third switch with that reason - because the "voice" Settings card belongs to the "Say Hey Jarvis" feature and `jarvis_feature_guide.switches_for()` would otherwise teach "turn on Say Hey Jarvis" to change this switch (`tools/check_feature_controls.py` caught exactly that). **Chosen over two alternatives:** keeping the check and caching it per session (the 2026-11-01 rule, which is the asking the owner reported), and skipping the check only for the first clip (which would then re-check mid-session against nothing the owner could predict). **The honest gap, recorded rather than hidden:** the desktop has no switch for it yet - the phone's Settings, Voice card draws it, the spoken phrases work on both apps, and `contract/feature-controls.json` carries the desktop row as `planned` / `setup-ui` - and the UNLOCKED WAKE WORD's exemption is not applied yet - `backend/jarvis_speech.py`'s `hear()` decides that check and has no `locked` input until the patch wave carries one, so a wake clip is still checked on an unlocked phone: MORE checks than the rule asks, never fewer, and DEF-033 records it (the rule itself already lives in `jarvis_live`'s one function, so that later hook needs no second copy).

- **2026-11-04 — Four `dsh-superagent` patterns are adopted for watchers, and a watcher must run in `observe` before it may interrupt:** the owner forwarded the 2026-11-04 spec (Part II sections 2.2-2.4 and 2.6B) after reviewing `deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype` (MIT), and chose to port its four mechanisms natively rather than embed any of its code: **Pattern 1**, an `accept_mode` with three states - `off`, `observe` and `active` - where `observe` is the default for a NEW proactive rule and runs the whole pipeline while writing a structured would-accept decision row instead of interrupting; **Pattern 2**, per-thread trigger batching so one pull request at one commit is one thread and the seven checks finishing minutes apart produce ONE message, with terminal fail-fast and terminal all-green settle and a receipt keyed `(pr_number, head_sha, terminal_verdict)`; **Pattern 3**, a pure deterministic `gate()` followed by an optional `assess()` that a filtered or informational event can never reach; and **Pattern 5B**, effects and outbox receipts with a deterministic `(kind, key)` written to disk before delivery and re-hydrated on startup. The decision, in the owner's terms: a watcher earns its voice rather than being given one, and a restart must never lose a question it was holding. Two boundaries are recorded with the decision because they are the parts a later reader would otherwise widen: `audit` and `python-advisories` are INFORMATIONAL - they are red on `main` while merges land - so they can never be the reason for a notification, and `observe` may only be promoted to `active` by the owner's own edit of `[watch] pr_checks_mode` in his settings file, never by a route and never automatically (an unreadable value reads as `observe`, never as `active`). The outbox is at-least-once by design and the limit is stated in the module: a crash between the send and the settle repeats one notice, and it can never do the opposite. Rehydration re-announces a parked card; it approves nothing, and `decide_grant()` remains the only thing that decides a grant. Nothing in this slice adds an approval path, a push, a merge or a new standing permission, and the watcher is off until a job names a pull request.

- **2026-11-04 — Adopt `waits_for_person` attention-first sorting in the Work pane (pattern 4):** ported from `dsh-superagent`'s `waits_for_person` predicate (Part II pattern 4 of the owner-forwarded `GEMINI-RULINGS-1253-AND-SUPERAGENT-SPEC-2026-11-04`), because a Work pane that lists every background job equally makes healthy work look like work the owner must look at. The list under the Start form is now two sections decided by ONE predicate in ONE shared place per platform (desktop `jarvis-desktop/src/attention.js`; phone `com.jarvis.client.net.JobAttention`): **"Needs you"** holds every job whose approval, an answer, a retry or an unacknowledged failure a person has to look at, drawn first and expanded with the job's own action, and when it is empty it is **not created at all** - no heading, no empty box, no reserved gap, so it takes zero pixels; **"Quiet / healthy"** is ONE collapsed line that opens on a click or tap to the same rows. The contract is `state in ("waiting_approval", "blocked", "needs_input") or (state == "failed" and not dismissed_by_owner)`, and the PC's own optional per-job `waits_for_person` boolean WINS when a payload carries one, with this derivation as the fallback. That fallback is not a stub: no backend in this repository sends the field yet (PR #1148 does not add it), so an older PC must look right rather than broken, and the field is where a later backend can take the decision over. It replaced the single flat list that drew every job the same way, and it deliberately keeps everything else: the order is stable (the read's own order on both sides, so a row never jumps between two reads of the same answer), there is no polling (the existing refresh path rebuilds it), there is no new action and no new approval - a quiet job keeps its Cancel and a parked one keeps exactly its one "Allow once"/"No" pair - and folding the quiet bar only changes a local flag. Its truth table and the zero-pixel empty state are pinned in `jarvis-desktop/tests/attention-first.mjs` (with Playwright DOM checks) and `AttentionFirstTest.kt`.

- **2026-11-04 — Call recording is armed by the owner's own keyword on the phone, and the phone records its MICROPHONE because Android blocks the call's own stream:** The owner asked for Jarvis to record a call when he says "record call", with the PC transcribing it, dating it, identifying the speakers and storing it as a new Obsidian note named with the date and time. Three parts of that decide the shape and none of them is a taste: (1) the call rings on the phone and Android does not let a normal app capture the call's own audio - `VOICE_CALL` is privileged, and a sideloaded app never holds it - so the recording is the phone's microphone with the call on **speaker**, `UNPROCESSED` where the platform opens it and `MIC` where it does not, and **never `VOICE_COMMUNICATION`**, whose echo canceller removes exactly the far end the feature exists to keep; the service asks Android to put the call on speaker and, when it refuses, the notification says "Turn the call on speaker so Jarvis can hear both sides" rather than claiming both sides were captured. (2) The phone never turns speech into words and never writes to the vault: it posts PCM16LE mono 16 kHz to the owner's own PC in 64 KiB pieces, with the date the call began and a `consent_notice: "on"` flag, and the PC transcribes, dates, works out who was speaking and names the note. (3) The recording is safe before it is sent: every piece is written to this app's own files directory first and uploaded after, a failed chunk is retried with the SAME sequence number - and a 409 that names the number the PC wants (`expected`) means the pieces below it are already there, so the phone records those as sent and sends the real next one rather than retrying the same number for ever (the 2026-11-05 privacy audit's D3) - and a recording the PC has not taken is kept and offered again, with its own notification saying so, and can be deleted from the phone by the owner behind a confirmation that says it cannot be undone (D7). A persistent notification runs for the whole call with the elapsed clock, Stop, and the one-line reminder "Recording - tell the other person", and it is redacted on a locked phone by the same rule every other Jarvis notice uses. The microphone is arbitrated by ONE point (`voice/MicOwner.kt`, held in `MicNow`): while call recording is armed or recording, Jarvis Live, "hey Jarvis" and the talk button **pause** their recorders and resume when it is released - paused rather than stopped because Android 14+ refuses to start a microphone foreground service from the background, so a stopped Live could not come back until the app was in front, and "paused and restored" would quietly become "off until the owner notices". The armed state is visible in one line ("Call recording armed" / "Recording call 00:04:12") in Settings, Voice, which is also the one place to arm, stop and re-send. A recording under a second is the one thing deleted, and it says so; a low battery, an unplugged headset, a refused microphone and the app shutting down all end the recording the same way - close the microphone first, then finish the upload. The routes are `POST /api/call/recording/start`, `/chunk` and `/finish` (the frozen contract of 2026-11-04), classified `phone-only` in `tools/check_parity.py`, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 carries the one-sided reasoning: the PC has no microphone in that call and must not, the phone has no transcriber and cannot see the vault, so each half does the only half it can. **A real call was NOT placed from this session** - the owner's own Pixel 9 is the one real-call field test, after this PR and the PC half land.

- **2026-11-04 — A phone call can be recorded by saying "record call", and what happens after it is all local:** the owner's request, in their own words: *"add the ability of jarvis to record a call if I tell it a keyword 'record call' where it will record all the audio, transcribe it, put a date and identify the speakers in the transcription, and store all of it in a new obsidian note labeled with the date and time"*, the call being taken through the Android Jarvis app. **Six decisions in one, each with its reason:** (1) **the keyword is the whole message** - the eight sentences ("record call", "record this call", "record the call", "start recording the call", "start call recording", "stop recording", "stop the call recording", "stop call recording") are matched whole-message only, after the repo's own tidier, and are answered by `jarvis_quick.py` with the additive `X-Jarvis-Route` field `call_record: {"action": "arm"|"stop"}` that the phone acts on; a longer sentence ("record call now") is the model's. (2) **Android cannot capture the call stream, so the phone records on the speaker path** - `VOICE_CALL` is privileged (his primary phone is a Google Pixel 9), so the phone records through its microphone with the call on speaker and uploads 16 kHz mono s16le PCM in order; the far end is heard through the speaker and the words are less clear than a system recorder would give, which the card, the docs and the note all say, and importing a file from the phone's own call recorder is a later addition that is not built. (3) **transcription and speaker labelling are local, and reuse what is already here** - `jarvis_media_read.read_media()` (the existing sherpa-onnx model, English only, in 9-minute parts because its own ceiling is 10 minutes) and `jarvis_voice`'s enrolled print + the embedder it was made with (`EcapaEmbedder`, or `StrongEmbedder` when the print says `strong`) + `cosine`, then clustering at 0.55 up to six; with no speaker model or no trained print every line says "Speaker" and the note records why, because a guessed name on other people's words is worse than no name. (4) **a NEW Obsidian note named for the date and time** - `Calls/YYYY-MM-DD HHMM - Call.md`, created through `jarvis_notes_edit.handle_create()` (its own `edit_vault_note` card, File Guardian copy and undo receipt; the transcript is `after_outside_text` provenance because a call's words are other people's), with `date`, `started_at`, `duration`, `source` ("phone call, speaker recording"), `speakers`, `audio` and `[HH:MM:SS] You: ...` lines in the time of day they were said; if the vault is missing or invalid the transcript is still written beside the audio and that path is returned, so a recording is never lost. (5) **a consent reminder, three times, and one gate** - the phone's own recording notification, the card, and the note's frontmatter plus a visible line in its body: "Recorded locally; tell the other person"; `finish` refuses unless the phone sends `consent_notice: "on"`. (6) **off by default until the owner turns it on** - `[call_recording] enabled = false` in the shipped settings file, a hand edit with no in-app switch (the same shape `github_search` and `shell_exec` use), and starting is ONE `record_call` approval card shipped at tier `ask` because it starts capturing other people's speech - the owner-initiated note actions ship `auto`, and this one deliberately does not. **Chosen over three alternatives:** starting the recording with no card at all (it would capture other people's speech with nothing asked), a PC-only start (impossible - the phone holds the microphone), and a cloud or on-phone transcription (against the local-only rule, and the phone must not do speech-to-text). **Recorded rather than hidden:** this fix gives `jarvis_gate.py` a `_RISK` row for `record_call` (`("yes", "local", ...)`, 2026-11-05), so the card says what the action really is - a recording made on this PC, deletable here, that never leaves it - instead of the generic "able to leave this PC" warning whose second half was wrong. The phone's recorder is its own pull request written against JARVIS-API §186, and neither lane drove a real call on the owner's Pixel 9 - the speaker path and the quality of its words are NOT-TESTABLE until his field test. Deleting one recording is a PC-only route behind its own `delete_call_recording` card, and recordings are kept until the owner deletes them: nothing expires on a timer and the 400-recording cap refuses a new start rather than deleting anything (`docs/CALL-RECORDING.md` section 7). English only, ten-second segments, and no import of a phone-recorder file. No real phone recording, transcription, speaker model, vault write or approval card was driven by this lane - those rows are NOT-TESTABLE, never passed. The whole story is `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md`, the wire contract `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §186, and the architecture `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §14.

- **2026-11-04 — Jarvis discusses any of its tools from a code-verified dossier, deterministic answer plus bounded model context, and no new tool or route:** The owner asked on 2026-11-04 to be able to hold full detailed discussions about any of Jarvis's tools and how they change what it can really do. The record is the two-way answer, and what it deliberately is not. A new shipped module, `jarvis_tool_profiles.py`, holds one hand-written page per name in the real `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` dict (51) and per capability family (11), each carrying what the thing is in beginner words, what it lets the owner do, what it refuses, what it pairs with, how to switch it on, and the repository files that prove every claim; its own suite re-derives the load-bearing claims from the modules rather than trusting the prose. Chat reaches it two ways. A deterministic fast path answers a sentence that names a tool **as a tool** - the word "tool", or the tool's own code name typed with its underscore - and sits after the plug-in block and before the feature guide, registered in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS` so a private chat hands it to the model instead. The model gets the same page as a system note of at most 1,200 characters plus one fixed line, subtracted from the room, present **only when a tool is actually named** so every ordinary prompt keeps the bytes it had, and kept alive across a follow-up by looking back at most two earlier user messages. Three things are refused and this is the binding part: **no new model tool** (five mandatory registrations, and it would ship switched off in the owner's own settings file, to buy a round trip for facts that fit in 400 prompt tokens), **no new HTTP route** (a third copy of what `/api/reach` and `/api/self` already serve; `GET /api/self/tools` is named for the day a Tools page exists, and not built), and **no new authority** - the dossiers decide nothing, read no live state and raise no card, the same fixed-data rule the self portrait states. The vocabulary split is the part that had to be proved rather than assumed: 42 of the catalogue's 175 feature titles open with words that also name a tool, and one feature alias is the exact phrase "plugin list", so the tool layer is addressed by its own marker and the feature layer keeps every one of its answers - `test_feature_answers.py` and `test_feature_guide.py` are the proof, not a preference.

- **2026-11-04 — Clearing old chats by date: keep the pinned ones, erase the facts they taught, ask twice and check a fingerprint:** The owner's decision, in his own words after Jarvis wrongly said it had no such action: *"it should be able to clear conversations it does NOT have pinned when asked to clear ones of a certain date, INCLUDING FACTS ... it must give a card with all the details, with a DOUBLE CONFIRMATION of yes, and require a Windows PIN or fingerprint (phone: fingerprint; Windows desktop: Windows Hello PIN/biometric) before deleting."* What that settles, and what it deliberately differs from: (1) **pinned chats are the boundary** - a chat the owner pinned is never deleted by a date purge unless the preview was explicitly asked to include pinned chats, which is never the default; a chat pinned after the card is skipped at execution time and counted; (2) **facts go with their chats, by provenance** - the facts cleared are exactly those whose own record names one of the deleted conversations, and their words are ERASED, where 2026-09-28's "Forget a time frame" retires them and keeps their words; a fact that records no chat, or another chat, is untouched; (3) **two separate yeses, plus a platform check** - the first yes only restates the exact counts, the second needs an HMAC-SHA256 ticket valid for 90 seconds and usable once, signed with `~/.openjarvis/purge-auth.key` by the desktop app after Windows Hello, or with the existing pairing token by the phone after its fingerprint; (4) **it cannot be undone**, and the card says so plainly; the ten-minute Undo belongs to Forget a time frame, which this does not replace. The trust model is local-only and is written down rather than implied: the backend proves the caller holds an owner-level secret and both yeses, it cannot prove a human was at the prompt, because it cannot see Windows Hello or a fingerprint reader - the app asks, and then signs. That is the same trust level the pairing token already has.

- **2026-11-04 — Chat reaches "Protected from Jarvis" through the feature's own doors, with three tool actions and fixed phrasings, not a second mechanism:** The owner asked for folder-level restrictions settable by plain chat on the PC and the phone, after an answer failed to reflect a capability the backend already had. Decided: EXTEND `jarvis_protection.py` rather than build anything parallel. The model tool `protect_from_jarvis` gains `action` = `add` | `remove` | `list` (default `add`, so every existing caller and card is unchanged); add and remove keep their ONE ordinary card with the shipped `"ask"` tier (`protect_item` / `unprotect_item`, no new action name and no new tier), and `list` answers with NO card because there is nothing to approve - the same sentinel shape `_PhoneAppsListed` already uses for the phone's app list. `jarvis_quick.py`'s fixed phrasings call the feature's own functions - `handle_propose`, `handle_remove`, `handle_get`/`status_for` - so the PC's fixed path and the model path are one door, not two: the store is written only after the card's verdict and removing still always asks. A sentence naming a PATH acts on it; a sentence that only describes a folder ("the folder with my medical scans") names no path, so the answer ASKS for the whole path and quotes the sentence to repeat - it never guesses at a target (protecting the wrong folder is itself a failure) and never falls back to a generic "I cannot", and because it is deterministic it works on a default install, where `protect_from_jarvis` is not in the shipped `[tools].enabled` at all. **Alternatives refused:** a new model tool for removal (it would need a new `_TOOL_ACTIONS` row and a new gate patch, and the tool name is not the permission - the action is); a second protection list or a second mode (the feature's whole point is one list every door asks); making the fast path answer with the rule and point at Settings (that is the wrong answer the owner reported, and its offered-test was comparing gate ACTION names against TOOL names, so it could never say yes); and a phone-only route (both apps chat through the same `/api/chat`, so the phone needs no client change and no new parity exception). The `_TOOL_HINTS` gap is part of the decision rather than a side fix: a hint table that does not carry the owner's own vocabulary HIDES the tool from the model, which is how a real capability gets answered generically - so the owner's words (restrict / restriction / folder-level / unrestrict / stop Jarvis / let Jarvis ... again / what is restricted / is Jarvis blocked) are pinned by the new suite, and "restrict the folder ... from Jarvis" went from `matched 2, protect hidden` to `matched 3, protect shown`. The eleven enforcement points are unchanged and still ask the module; nothing is loosened, and no auto-approval was added. Proved by `backend/test_folder_restrictions.py` (99 checks, 0 failed) driving every owner phrasing through the real fast path and REAL route with a recording fake gate, plus the existing protection, chat-honesty, agent and tool-text suites green.

- **2026-11-04 — Both apps draw the second yes, and a kept chat's title is as private as a deleted one:** The apps lane's half of the owner's "double confirmation of yes" is drawn from the PC's own status, never invented: `confirm` non-null means the card was approved and the checked items are held, and only then does either app offer "Yes, forget them", carrying the held id and a literal `true` that each app BUILDS from two checked values (the desktop's Rust `confirm_body`, the phone's `ForgetRange.confirmBody`) rather than passing a body through, so a `"yes": "true"` cannot be sent by either client. Both steps that change something - "Forget these" and the second yes - are held on a stale link and refused while the private lists are hidden, because both act on a list a person read, and the second is the one that deletes. Every 400/409 is shown in the PC's own words and the status is read again after it; a refusal is never swallowed, and it is never wiped by the list re-read that follows (the re-read that a 409 asks for used to erase the very sentence asking for it - fixed in the same change). Two rules about the words: the pinned chats' three sentences are the PC's own constants (`PINNED_ONE`, `PINNED_MANY`, `PINNED_WHY`), mirrored into each app's `EXTRA` map and pinned to `backend/jarvis_forget_range.py` by tests, because the contract's generated `words` map is compared key for key in both apps and adding to it is a backend-generator change, not an app one; and the one sentence the PC has no use for - "2 min left to say yes", shaped like the existing `undo_left` - lives only in those `EXTRA` maps, said the same in both apps. Finally, `pinned_kept` carries chat TITLES, so it is redacted exactly like `chats`: the desktop's Rust `redact()` empties it and the phone's `ForgetRange.redact` blanks its titles out of what the plate holds, because hiding a list while still naming the chats it is keeping would leak the one thing hiding it is for.

- **2026-11-04 — "Forget a time frame" is extended, never duplicated:** The
  owner chose "Extend the existing one (Recommended)" over a stricter
  irreversible sibling purge, and set the contract: clear the conversations
  "that i dont have pinned" from "a certain date, including facts", with a
  card carrying "all the details", a "double confirmation of yes", and a
  Windows PIN or fingerprint on the PC or phone. So pinned chats are kept and
  named in the preview, the card and the status; a measured estimate answers

- **2026-11-04 — A spoken yes answers an approval card in hands-free mode, and the phone may send a text message with `SEND_SMS`:** the owner's request of 2026-11-04 settles two questions this project had already written down, and both are recorded here rather than left to be inferred from the code. **(a) A voice yes counts, in hands-free mode, for every card raised for a task he asked Jarvis to do.** This is his own security decision. It does not weaken `CLAUDE.md`'s "the app never auto-approves anything": every card is still raised by the PC, still pending until the owner's answer arrives, and the answer is still the owner's - what changes is the channel it arrives on. The authority stays on the PC, which is why the phone only ever uploads a clip: the client still never does speech-to-text, and the PC transcribes it, checks it against the owner's voice print and decides, so a `not_you` answer approves nothing. Voice does NOT begin to answer cards outside this mode, and the old rule stands elsewhere: `CardVoice` still only says where a card is. **(b) Jarvis may WRITE a text message for him, which needs `SEND_SMS` and `READ_CONTACTS`.** `docs/UI-CUTTING-EDGE-2026-10-09.md` §16.7 A3 had settled "you say send" as *hand it to my SMS app* - `Intent.ACTION_SENDTO` with an `sms_body` and **no `SEND_SMS`** - precisely because the owner presses Send in the other app. He has now asked for hands-free texting, where he does not press anything, so that route cannot do it; the later word is his, and it replaces A3 for this feature only. What the permission is bounded by, so a later reader does not have to re-derive it: the app asks for `SEND_SMS` at runtime when hands-free is switched on (never at launch), sends exactly ONE message per `phone_command`, only after the name resolved to exactly one number in the phone's own address book, never reports "sent" without Android's own `RESULT_OK`, and never becomes the default SMS app - Tier C1 of the same section, still refused. `READ_CONTACTS` is for the name only: no contact, number or message is stored, and none is sent to the PC. **(c) The phone half is one-sided on purpose:** the mouth, the ears and the SMS hand are the phone's; the decision is the PC's (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, and the four routes are `phone-only` in `tools/check_parity.py` until the desktop's own half of the same contract lands).

- **2026-11-04 — A voice yes counts for every card, in hands-free mode: the owner's answer, and what it supersedes:** Asked on a clickable card about the one conflict this feature could not settle itself, the owner answered **"A voice yes counts for every card"** (2026-11-04). That is a deliberate reversal, for one mode, of the sentence the 2026-09 security review put in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: *"Never approve-by-voice: the voice check cannot tell a recording from the owner, so a spoken 'yes' answers nothing."* The old sentence is not edited or deleted - it stays in that file, marked SUPERSEDED FOR HANDS-FREE MODE ONLY, with the owner's words and this fragment as the record. **What the new rule is, exactly:** while the owner has turned hands-free mode on, ONE spoken answer may decide ONE waiting card, including a card whose risk row would otherwise demand Windows Hello on the PC or the phone's own lock and signature, and including the cards `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS` keeps to the PC. **What it is not, and why it is narrower than the old sentence feared:** the mode is OFF by default in both shipped settings files; turning it ON is ONE ask-tier card (`handsfree_enable`, itself a risky approval), and turning it OFF is instant and cardless; the clip is turned into words ON THIS PC (`jarvis_speech._transcribe`) and a client never does speech-to-text; the owner's voice print is checked BEFORE any words are made (`jarvis_voice.verify`), because the voice module's own rule is that a stranger's speech is never turned into words - the brief for this feature said "transcribe, then verify", and that order was refused rather than followed; with no print enrolled a spoken yes is refused outright, so the decision's premise (a check that can run) is never assumed; the answer must be one word from a closed list, inside 60 seconds of the card being read out, for a card that is still waiting; one read-out gets one decision and a second answer is refused; an unclear answer is asked once more and then treated as a DENY; and every confirm calls the SAME `jarvis_gate.decide()` a tap calls, after the same in-memory stamp a Windows Hello approval leaves, from ONE function (`jarvis_handsfree.approve_one`) reachable only through that route, only with the mode on, and only after the voice check passed. **Nothing outside that branch changes:** `jarvis_owner_check.approve_check` gained no hands-free exception and neither gate module imports the new one, so outside hands-free mode a risky approval still needs Windows Hello or the phone's own lock, and a spoken "yes" still answers nothing - `backend/test_handsfree.py` proves both halves. The owner's words are the authority here, not this fragment's reasoning; what the fragment adds is the list of guard rails the implementation owes that authority, so a later reader cannot mistake "a voice yes counts" for "any voice, any words, any time".

- **2026-11-04 — A patch-stack repair is targeted and reviewed, never a whole-stack rerun:** the owner's direction of 2026-11-04, after the deploy/partner session measured that `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` REFUSES on this install and writes nothing (`.dsh-scratch/PATCH-RUN-2026-11-04/REHEARSAL-REPORT.md`: exit 1, 46 patches refused, 43 with `-FixLineEndings`, 77 "already on your backend and cannot be taken off and put back on", and 0 of 3,288 files changed by SHA-256 - so it can neither repair the backend nor damage it, and it costs zero downtime), and that exactly THREE newer partial rows are missing on the live build (`ollama-direct.patch` 38/52, `cloud-say-yes.patch` 21/36, `update-in-chat.patch` 1/2, on `jarvis_hud.py`/`jarvis_gate.py`) while the four long-standing FAIL rows (`appearance`, `show-card-timer`, `cloud-honesty`, `attached-file`) are accepted as they are. Decided: repair those three rows and nothing else, as a reviewed change with a rehearsal on a COPY of the deployed tree against the DEPLOYED ref's patch text (`8a4a8e76f`, not the branch's HEAD, or the row count comes out false-green - at the older text these three read 38/38 and 31/31 and 1/1), and never re-run the stack. **What was actually wrong, proved against the text:** the three patches are NOT stale and their hunks are right in stack order - `e7a461ba9` (2026-11-03 13:09) added the 2026-11-03 field test's fixes to them and the owner's live files were last written at 11:49 the same morning, so the live install simply predates the commit while the patcher that would have carried it refuses. Re-aiming those hunks at the live text (the obvious first idea) was rejected on measurement: `ollama-direct.patch`'s hunk 4 is already applied here but a LATER patch (`presets.patch`, `active_ollama_url()`) rewrote four of its message lines, `cloud-say-yes.patch`'s single hunk rewrites a block whose every line a later revision changed, and `update-in-chat.patch`'s hunk pre-image ends at the set's `})`, which the DEPLOYED `desktop_update` line now sits in front of - so edited hunks would apply on this PC and stop applying on a fresh install, which is the opposite of a repair. **Decided shape:** carry the three missing pieces as three exact OLD -> NEW region pairs in `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py`'s `DELTA_TABLE`, with their block bytes under `tools/hud-deltas/` and the NEW side taken from the patch's own post-image at the deployed ref, because that is the tool that actually deploys this PC and because its own rule already says "Adding a new HUD patch is one small entry, not new code". The skip it fixes is the tool's own documented failure (DEF-018): two of the three had no table entry, so the fallback rule saw their older lines in the live file and reported `already present: 221, to insert: none` while three rows were short; the third's probes were lines the old version carried. **Rehearsed, not assumed:** on a `robocopy` copy of the live folder, `selftest.patch_states` went 207 rows / 7 bad -> 207 rows / 4 bad with `ollama-direct` 52/52, `cloud-say-yes` 36/36, `update-in-chat` 2/2 and the four accepted rows byte-identically unchanged (216/334, 10/60, 3/80, 0/30); the deploy's dry run stages exactly those three, `--apply` ends `RESULT: PASS`, and a second dry run stages nothing. Nothing live was written: the fix reaches the owner's PC on the next `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py --apply`, and the one visible side effect is disclosed rather than hidden - that write turns `jarvis_gate.py`'s 3,153 CRLF endings into LF, which is what `-FixLineEndings` already asks for.

- **2026-11-04 — "Personalize Jarvis" is finished only when every question has an answer:** This reverses the 2026-11-03 sentence *"A partial retake still marks the question set complete (`completed_version = QUIZ_VERSION`) because the owner has seen the new questions by then"*.
