The 2026-11-04 audit (DEF-043) measured what that rule did on the merged tree: `apply()` wrote `completed_version = QUIZ_VERSION` after ANY accepted answer while `answered_count()` still reported e.g. 1 of 25, so the first-open offer, the HUD banner and the every-turn chat line all stopped and nothing offered the card again until a version bump - the card's own "show only new/unanswered" filter then had 24 items and no door. `apply()` now sets `completed_version = QUIZ_VERSION` only when `answered_count()` of the document it is about to save equals `len(QUESTIONS)`; a partial apply saves its answers, clears its draft and counts its run, but leaves completion where it was (a file that had completed an older version keeps that version). The merge-on-retake behaviour is untouched: submitted answers still win and every answer the run did not ask about survives. `{"keep_current": true}` remains the one explicit "I am happy as I am" that moves completion without answering anything. The same change makes the every-turn chat line obey the "Personalize Jarvis" notification switch (`jarvis_notify_prefs.read()["setup"]`), because that switch is the owner saying they do not want to be reminded and a chat line is a reminder (DEF-044).

- **2026-11-04 — Wire the existing product check rather than build a new one, and keep it evidence-not-verdict:** The owner was offered a choice on 2026-11-04 between leaving the product check unwired, rebuilding it, or wiring what already existed, and chose to wire the existing check. The engine (`jarvis_product_research.py`), the read half (`jarvis_product_read.py`) and the capture seam (`jarvis_product_capture.py`) had shipped on 2026-10-25/26 with no route, no chat tool, no approval card, no app surface, no browser driver and no network call, so the feature the owner could actually use did not exist. The wiring therefore adds a door and nothing else: ONE model tool `product_check` and ONE PC-only route `POST /api/product/check`, both raising the SAME one card under the action `product_check` (tier "ask", PC-only with Windows Hello, in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`), one read-only page in the owner's own signed-in browser after the yes, and the engine's own reasons report back in plain words. Four properties are decisions rather than accidents, and are written where they can be checked: (1) **evidence, not a verdict** - no trust score and no per-review fake/real label, because people and LLMs are at chance telling AI-written reviews from real ones, and the answer is written by code so a model cannot add one; (2) **one card** per address, raised before anything is opened, naming the page and saying read-only, with cart/checkout/order/account/payment/sign-in addresses refused before the card; (3) **read-only** - one navigation and one read, no click, typing, form, second page, CAPTCHA solving or retry, and nothing about the page stored; (4) **off by default** - `[product_check] enabled = false` in both shipped settings copies, missing-reads-as-off, and the tool is not even offered to the model while it is off. The route is classified backend-only in `tools/check_parity.py` because the browser window and profile are on the PC and no app screen draws the report yet; a desktop report screen is the named follow-up and would be desktop-only on purpose (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, `docs/DESIGN-PRODUCT-RESEARCH.md` §6). Nothing in this record claims a live proof: no real Amazon page has been parsed by a test, no test drives a browser, and no one-time Amazon sign-in has been exercised.

- **2026-11-04 — REA is the full toolbox, behind one card per action:** Asked how far reverse engineering should go, the owner chose "Also install the full REA toolbox" - *"debug and patch, not just read: attach a debugger, watch a running program, use Frida and patch files - the real toolkit, all local"* - plus REA's own package installed by Jarvis and all of its actions exposed through the one `rea_investigate` tool. This replaces the 2026-10-20 static-only slice: `backend/jarvis_rea.py`'s action table is 200 actions (one per REA tool in the pinned `rea-agents@6.7.0` catalog, whose 207 names and catalog digest were measured from the real server on this PC on 2026-11-04, plus `doctor`, `install` and the seven names the first slice shipped), and debugger, Frida, live capture, process-memory, session, export, ADB-read and install actions are all available. The five non-negotiables are unchanged and are why anything is still refused: one approval card per call (so even `doctor` and `install` ask), nothing leaves this PC (a URL, `host:port`, network share or remote endpoint in any setting is refused unless it is loopback), keys are never passed (the child environment stays an allow-list, with REA's own `REA_TOKEN` deliberately absent), and the MIT package stays MIT. The one by-name refusal left is the six ADB device mutators, and it is cross-module ownership rather than a core rule: phone changes already belong to `control_phone` / `[phone_apps]`, so REA keeps every ADB read and capture and none of those six. The nanny restrictions the static-only slice added - debuggers, Frida, runtime capture, export, `close_binary` - are gone, along with `debug_with_gdb`, a name no REA tool ever answered to. Jarvis installs the pinned package itself after its own card and refuses to treat a package as ready if it carries an install lifecycle script or names a known analytics or telemetry service; the four-point audit's static egress scan did not exist in code before this and is now real. What this deliberately does not do: no HTTP route, no gate action, tier or switch change (the gate mapping `rea_investigate` -> `run_shell_on_host` at tier `ask` is untouched), and no claim that a file was patched when only a session's memory changed - REA 6.7.0 has no patch-a-file tool. The ruling's other three guardrails are enforced in the same module rather than left as a residual: a credential store (LSASS, Windows Credential Manager, a browser's saved-login files) is refused as a target by process name, file name and path; a debugger or Frida command that can write is refused unless it aims at a NEW `.patched` copy, with Windows, Windows Defender and Jarvis's own programs never a patch target and a before/after SHA-256 receipt recorded for an allowed write; and every live session carries `duration_limit_sec` (60 by default, 300 at most) on its one card, caps its own call, and is detached in a `finally`. Real REA analysis stays NOT-TESTABLE on CI (no engines, no pinned install) and is not claimed as tested; `backend/test_rea.py` (328 checks) covers the table, the refusals, the three guardrails against fakes and a fake clock, the install and the scans.

- **2026-11-04 — The self-benchmark's routes raise no approval card, and that is a decision rather than a shortcut:** `POST /api/bench/run` and `POST /api/bench/cancel` act with no card for the same reason `POST /api/hardware/measure` already does - they measure this PC and change no setting the owner keeps - and the run is deliberately backend-only until a screen exists (the desktop Benchmark panel is phase 2, the phone's `BenchScreen` phase 5). Every route in `backend/bench.patch` is either a read of `bench.jsonl` or one measurement: starting a run loads a model that is already installed, times a fixed prompt, and asks Ollama to unload it again, and it writes only the benchmark's own rows. **What a card would have bought is bought explicitly instead:** the request body's `confirm: {model, lane, may_evict: true}` is mandatory, so a POST without it measures nothing, and the run is refused rather than faked when the PC cannot measure (answering, standby, a task running, a benchmark already running, a lane down, a model missing), each with its own sentence. **What a card could not have bought is any less eviction:** a run may push the owner's loaded model out of video memory, which is why the controls read carries that note and a screen repeats it before the press - the consent is a sentence in front of the button, not a card behind it. The routes stay off both apps on this tree, listed one by one in `tools/check_parity.py`'s backend-only table, so a screen that starts calling one is a failure rather than a silent port. **This record exists because the reasoning was not in it:** `jarvis_bench.py`, `bench.patch` and `tools/check_parity.py` all cited "the recorded DESIGN section 7 decision", and DESIGN.md lives only under `.dsh-scratch/` - outside the project record - so the citation pointed at nothing a later reader could check; it points here now. The same pass wrote the one-sidedness down in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 ("the self-benchmark has no screen on either app yet") and says plainly that `jarvis_bench.advice()` has no route at all on this tree. Nothing here decides a future delete: deleting a benchmark row is not built, and it will be decided with its own record.

- **2026-11-04 — Self-knowledge is read from the one owning reader, never typed, and the tools number means tools:** The 2026-11-04 self-awareness audit found three root causes behind false self-descriptions, and the fixes take one shape. First, `counts()["tools"]` held the asks-first row count (136) and was handed to the model verbatim; it now holds the number of tools switched on in the owner's own `[tools].enabled` (13 on the shipped file), with `tools_registered` (51) beside it and the old number kept under its true name `asks_first_rows`, so an old caller keeps working and gets the truth. Second, the portrait hard-coded `value_known: false` for all 10 choice settings on the belief that no reader existed; the reader did exist - `jarvis_settings_registry.current_value()` -> the owning module's `ChoiceSetting.now()`, which the Settings explainer has used since 2026-11-03 - and the portrait now asks it, with `value_why` rather than a default when a read fails. Third, sentences about the tool set were typed instead of measured: `TOOLS_TOML_ONLY_NOTE` now has a *function* (`tools_toml_only_note()`) whose tail is built from the live `[tools].enabled`, and the spoken reach answer now carries the same tool block `view()` holds. The rule recorded here is the one that makes the class of defect impossible rather than the instance: a sentence about the owner's own settings is read from the module that owns the setting, at answer time, and a number that reaches the model is labelled with what it counts. `backend/jarvis_presets.py` is deliberately untouched - the focus-preset denial was fixed in `jarvis_quick.py`'s intent ordering, with the registry's own exact matcher deciding what is a setting and what is a preset.

- **2026-11-04 — Source independence is evidence about who paid, never a trust score:** The owner's clickable-card answer to the unbiased-product-research question was to wire the existing product check AND add the sponsored-article/YouTube layer, so that quality is weighed across independent sources instead of trusting a star rating. This records the decision behind the second half, built as `backend/jarvis_source_independence.py` (shipped whole, byte-identical `jarvis-backend/` twin) and deliberately not wired: one supplied page is read for disclosure wording, affiliate and tracking links, and urgency wording, and the answer is a CLOSED per-source verdict - `disclosed_sponsored`, `likely_monetised_undisclosed`, `affiliate_only`, `no_monetisation_evidence` or `cannot_tell` - each carrying the phrase, snippet or link that produced it. Three rules are the decision, not an implementation detail. First, **evidence only, no aggregate trust score**: there is no score, probability or percentage anywhere, for the reason `docs/DESIGN-PRODUCT-RESEARCH.md` already measured - a single number hides which rule fired and invites over-trust - and `rank_sources()` reports counts of sources and a word-for-word agreement summary instead. Second, **`cannot_tell` is a real answer**: an empty page, a JavaScript shell or a page below the readable-text floor is reported as unchecked and is never counted as independent, because unknown is not the same as clean. Third, **the borrowed patterns are credited**: the shortener, tracking, affiliate-parameter and fake-urgency vocabularies are a Python-native port of dakidarts/dark-radar (MIT), named with its MIT text in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`; no JavaScript is vendored and no dark-radar file is shipped, and the patterns added on top (affiliate-network addresses, redirect wrappers, the shop-tag shape, negated-wording handling) are this repository's own and are named in the same notice. The layer makes no network call, opens no link, resolves no shortened address, plays no video and reads or writes no file; `backend/test_source_independence.py` proves that with a socket/urlopen spy and an AST scan of the module's own imports. No route, model tool, approval card, Settings row or app screen is added by this decision; wiring is the separate lane the owner asked for, and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` is deliberately untouched until there is something to call.

- **2026-11-04 — The storage-route adapter accepts both shapes the real module ships, and the unit fake now mirrors the real module:** `jarvis_storage_health.ROUTES` is a tuple of row dicts, and `storage_routes()` in `jarvis_self_portrait.py` used to `str()` each row - so every dispatcher's `route in storage_routes()` was False, the live server answered `GET /api/storage/scan` with the HUD's own 404, and `backend/test_self_portrait.py` stayed green because its `_FakeStorage.ROUTES` was a tuple of bare strings that matched the adapter's wrong answer instead of the module it stood in for. The adapter now returns path strings from either shape (a dict row's `"path"` when that is a non-empty string, a string itself, anything else skipped) and still answers `()` instead of raising on a missing or odd module, and the fake now carries the real dict shape so the wiring checks exercise the real contract. New checks flatten the real `jarvis_storage_health.ROUTES` through the same adapter, assert exactly its three paths and its own `GET_ROUTES` + `POST_ROUTES`, and fail on the stringifying version - so the shape mismatch that let this ship cannot pass green again. Both twins carry the identical change; no route was added, removed or renamed.

- **2026-11-04 — Three cards run a hybrid topology, and the third card's lane gets port 11438 because no lane port may be shared:** the rule the preset screen now states, replacing the two lines that stopped being true on 2026-11-02 - "layout: lane per GPU, never one model split across three cards" and "coding: ... the Coding lane (qwen3.5:4b helper)". **Everyday presets keep ONE lane per GPU** (the everyday card, the card the monitor is plugged into, and the headless card), and **only the on-demand Coding preset pools them**, on port `11450`, because `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` is too big for one card and that is the whole reason the pooled lane exists. Which card plays which role is taken from measured facts - most VRAM for the everyday card, `nvidia-smi`'s `display_active` for the monitor card, the rest for the headless one - and a row names a card by its PCI address (`pci_id`) rather than the array position that used to print as "2080 SUPER #2 (card 2)"; a card that is not installed says "not installed yet", and a PC that reports no display flag says "monitor not reported by this PC" instead of guessing. **The port half of this record is a disagreement with the review that asked for it:** the ruling said a third card's own lane should default to `11437`, and `11437` is not free - it is `jarvis_screen_picture.DEFAULT_PORT` (`backend/jarvis_screen_picture.py:157`), the screen-picture reader's own copy of Ollama - so the first number above every lane port this repo names (`11434`, `11435`, `11436`, `11437`, `11450`) that nothing claims is `11438` - and the same ruling that requires this guard also reserves `11439` for the VoiceStudio sidecar, which is not a Jarvis module yet, so the guard carries that literal too and `backend/test_second_card.py` asserts the literal rather than a constant invented for a component this repo does not ship. `jarvis_second_card.DEFAULT_THIRD_PORT` was `11436` from 2026-09-28 until now, and the owner's everyday lane moved onto `11436` on 2026-10-16 (PR #440) while `_third_port()`'s guard still compared only `11434` and `11435` - so the shipped default collided with a running lane and nothing noticed. `jarvis_second_card.LANE_PORTS` now names that whole list plus the sidecar reservation, `_third_port()` misses all of it under any configuration, and a shipped default that lands on one of them raises `RuntimeError` at import instead of being quietly stepped past: a silent step-up would have hidden this defect for as long as it hid. The numbers are literals in `jarvis_second_card` (importing the lane modules from there would be a new cycle) and `backend/test_second_card.py`'s `t_third_port_is_disjoint_from_every_lane_port` reads each owning module's own constant, so a lane moving again fails a test rather than a lane; both copies of the shipped `jarvis-framework.toml` carry the same `11438`, and a test compares the template's number with the module's constant so the one fact cannot be typed twice. The same day's standby fix follows from this record: standby exists to empty the cards, so `jarvis_model_lanes.sleep()` is now one of the engines `jarvis_power_switch` frees, and `stop_pooled_lane()` gained `restore=False` for it - the default `True` still puts both lane models back for every other caller, because a stop that reloaded them would undo the freeing standby was asked to do. The gap this leaves is known and not papered over: `jarvis_screen_picture._TAKEN_PORTS` still lists only `11434`-`11436`, so a hand-written `[screen_picture] port = 11438` could still collide with the third lane - both ports are owner-configurable and that stays a Lead decision, because changing it means a second module, its own test and its own twin.

- **2026-11-04 — Every tool Jarvis can use is switchable from the Tools page:** The owner reversed the ON half of the 2026-10-31 tiered-tool ruling (Gemini's "not indiscriminate") and, with it, the 2026-11-03 page-reader decision that had kept `read_web_page` out on its own: "few restrictions on its tools beyond the core values of jarvis that have already been established, particularly reverse engineer anything among other things", and, when asked what the app should allow, they chose "Switch any of them on in the app". From now on `POST /api/asks_first/tools` with `enabled: true` accepts **every tool the AI model can be offered** - 48 switches, up from 21 - adding the raw Tier C set (`shell_exec`, `control_computer`, `control_phone`, `browser_control`, `read_web_page`, `connect_account`, `rea_investigate`), the eight "not this slice" helpers (`calculator`, `memory_search`, `file_read`, `web_search`, `my_files`, `propose_plan`, `change_setting`, `feature_guide`) and the twelve of Jarvis's own tools that shipped on with no switch row (`goals_*`, `conversation_find`/`conversation_open`, `phone_apps`, `plugin_list`/`plugin_switch`, `refresh_abilities`, `self_portrait`, `setup_quiz`). The protections that are not owner-facing restrictions are unchanged: the PC only (`jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`), a stale link held by the desktop's Rust, ONE approval card per change under `enable_reading_tool` at tier `ask`, Windows Hello, nothing written until a person approves, `changed: false` when the tool is already on, and an instant cardless OFF from either app (D4, the same day). The card keeps its shape and gains the two honesty additions the decision needs: it names the tool in its own one-line description, and where ANOTHER switch must also be on for the tool to be offered - `[rea] enabled = true` for `rea_investigate`, Settings, Web search for `web_search`, the second card's browser lane or the headless browser for `browser_control` - it says so, because otherwise "offered" would be a promise the card cannot keep. Three known tools are deliberately NOT switches, and this is the one restriction the evidence forced: the turn ignores their `[tools].enabled` line, so a switch whose state the turn ignored would be a lie (the rule that removed the web-search grant's two switches on 2026-11-02). `run_data_script` is offered by its own switch (Settings, Data sandbox; `POST /api/sandbox/enabled`), and `approve_web_search_for_conversation`/`stop_web_search_approval` ride with `web_search` (`jarvis_agent.GRANT_ASK_TOOLS`); `GET /api/asks_first` carries them as `tools.not_switchable` with the PC's own sentence, the route refuses ON for them with that sentence rather than the false "does not know that name", and an OFF that names one says the real switch still offers it. The old misleading answers are gone: `TOOLS_TOML_ONLY_NOTE` ("not offered in-app by this slice") is deleted with its Rust twin, the chat answers (`jarvis_quick`'s `asks_first` and `general_off` shapes) no longer say the raw tools stay a settings-file choice, `jarvis_reach` names Settings, What asks first for every tool with a switch there, the feature list's nine affected rows and their tutorials describe the real switch, and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §43 is rewritten with the route, the payload, the card and the three exceptions.

- **2026-11-04 — The Tools page may turn OFF anything that is ON:** The owner reversed the OFF half of the 2026-10-31 tiered-tool ruling (and of the 2026-11-03 page-reader decision, which reaffirmed the same 403 for `read_web_page`). That rule refused every request for a tool outside the 21 in-app switches - `403` with `TOOLS_TOML_ONLY_NOTE` for a Tier C or "not this slice" tool, `TOOLS_NOT_ON_LIST` for a name the PC did not know - in both directions. From now on a tool that is enabled in `[tools].enabled` is ON whether or not the page has a switch row for it, so turning it OFF must work: it is instant from either app, raises no card (the same shape as every other OFF, which only narrows what the model may do), and removes that one line through `set_tools_enabled`, the same parse-change-parse write every other tool switch uses - never a wholesale rewrite of the owner's settings file. `GET /api/asks_first`'s `tools.extra` lists every ON tool that has no row in `tools.items`, with its state read from the file and a plain `why`; a row turned off through the page stays as OFF (with the line the owner saw, naming `jarvis-framework.toml`) until Jarvis restarts, so the page never silently drops it, while a tool the file lists again always wins and shows ON. The ON direction is deliberately NOT widened: offering an unlisted tool to the model stays a hand edit of `[tools].enabled`, with the old 403, and the 21 Tier A/Tier B switches, their one card plus Windows Hello, the phone's read-only page and every per-use card are unchanged. This is why the route's old sentence "unknown tools and Tier C/unlisted tools answer 403" now holds for ON only.

- **2026-11-04 — The tray's update row runs the both-halves update, and the desktop-only install survives only where the backend half cannot run:** The owner's requirement of 2026-11-03 - *"when i click update on the jarvis hud i want it linked to the back end so both are always updated at the same time"* - and clause (3) of `decisions.d/2026-11-03-desktop-nav-multiwindow-update.md`, *"the desktop-only `install_update` survives ONLY for a PC whose backend half cannot run"*, described the Settings Update press, and one door was left contradicting it: the tray's own "Update Jarvis to <version>" row, added the same day against the old install, still ran `install_from_tray` -> `install_update` alone. A press there therefore updated Jarvis Desktop while the backend stayed behind - on any PC, not only one whose backend half cannot run. Fixed here, because a record that describes one door and not the door the owner actually right-clicks is exactly the stale-comment defect this project treats as a bug rather than a leftover. `update::install_from_tray` now asks `crate::backend_update::locate(&app).blocked` - the field `backend_update_status`, the command the Settings Updates card reads, is built from, so the tray and the card cannot take different views of whether the backend half can run - and where it can, runs `update_both(app, "responsive")`, the pace the Settings Install press uses, through the same one-at-a-time guard. `install_update` remains reachable ONLY in that blocked arm (and from the Settings card's own fallback), and that arm is neither silent nor ever read as "updated": before the install its toast says *"The backend half cannot run on this PC (<why>). Installing Jarvis Desktop on its own - the two may differ until the backend update is finished."*, and after it says *"The BACKEND was NOT updated: <why>"* and sends the owner to the "Update both halves" control once the folders are in place - the same words the Settings card uses, guarded by the same App-lock rule as every other toast that can carry a folder path. Before the both-halves run the tray's toast says what is about to happen (the backend is patched first, then Jarvis Desktop installs, Jarvis closes and starts again, several minutes), because the tray has no card to say it in. The row's states are unchanged - absent while no update exists, "Updating Jarvis to <version>…" and disabled on the press before anything is decided, and rebuilt from truth with `check_for_update` after any ending that returns - and nothing runs without that press. The source-pin test in `update.rs` now slices the function bodies rather than searching the whole file, with `concat!` needles, so a comment cannot satisfy it: the both-halves arm is the one that reaches `update_both`, the desktop-only call is the one inside the blocked arm, and that arm is the one whose words say the BACKEND was NOT updated.

- **2026-11-04 — VoiceStudio joins Jarvis as an EXTERNAL loopback sidecar, never as code in this repository, and the measured verdict makes it demand-only and serialised:** The owner's Q3/Q4/Q5, forwarded 2026-11-04, decided five things, and each one is a promise rather than an implementation note. (1) **Separate program, over a socket.** VoiceStudio is AGPL-3.0-only and this repository is MIT, so the only arrangement kept is the one the licence lane called clean: the owner installs and runs the unmodified program on this PC, outside this repository, and Jarvis sends it HTTP requests on `127.0.0.1:11439` and reads audio back. No file, module or weight of it is copied, imported or bundled - importing its package into Jarvis's process would make one combined work and would make this tree's MIT label false, and copying its source into a published MIT repository is conveying. `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` names it as an external program for exactly that reason, and `backend/test_voicestudio.py` proves the client's imports are the standard library plus this repository's own modules. (2) **On demand, never resident.** The measured verdict is CONTENTION: beside Jarvis's own two resident models the 8 GB card had 382 MiB free at its peak, the driver paged ~1.9 GB into system RAM, and the private memory went from 1,698 MB idle to 6,721 MB with a model resident. So there is no boot task, no service and no logon entry; the program is started when it is needed by `tools/voicestudio_sidecar.ps1 -Start` and released again with `-Stop` (or by its own 900 s idle unload), and the launcher refuses to start below a measured 5,200 MiB free on that card rather than repeat the contention. (3) **The 2080 SUPER only, pinned by UUID; the 2060 and its lane are never touched.** The launcher reads `nvidia-smi -L`, pins the one card whose name contains `2080` by UUID because indices can reorder, refuses when it cannot find exactly one, and never falls back to the other card. The 11436 lane (the RTX 2060, the everyday model) is never queried, never unloaded and never named in a command the launcher prints. When a Jarvis model is in the way it names the 11435 lane's own model and prints the one exact line that unloads it, for the OWNER to run: the launcher never unloads anything itself, and `tools/measure_voicestudio.py` refuses unloads too. (4) **Weights are personal, non-commercial use only, and never shipped.** The model licences are not the AGPL: `k2-fsa/OmniVoice` is CC-BY-NC (plus Higgs Audio 2 and Meta Llama 3 terms) and `eustlb/higgs-audio-v2-tokenizer` has no licence in its metadata. Rule 5 makes non-commercial acceptable for this build and removes nothing else: nothing is redistributed, Jarvis never downloads a weight, and every engine and voice dossier the client returns carries `license_class` of either `commercial_ok` or `personal_non_commercial_only` - with no engine `commercial_ok` today, on purpose, because VoiceStudio's own inventory says no model record makes that claim. (5) **The first-run licence gate is the owner's yes, once, in VoiceStudio's own terms.** Until both are accepted every speech request answers 403 `model_licence_required`; the client recognises that answer and returns plain words naming both repositories with the exact two commands and the fingerprint read from the server - and never sends the acceptance itself, because a program that clicked yes to someone else's terms for the owner would be the one thing this feature must not do. The feature ships OFF behind `[voicestudio] enabled = false`, because a second-card/optional-model feature keeps its own switch off until the owner turns it on, and this slice adds no route and no card: the read-only questions answer, speaking does not, and `jarvis_speech.py` does not import the client yet. The next slice wires the speaking voice and adds the one-card Settings switch; only then does ON mean "Jarvis may speak with it".

- **2026-11-05 — The 3-GPU preset plan is preserved in git, planned and unmeasured:** The owner's ruling Q4 of 2026-11-05 is that the 3-GPU preset research must not be lost with the untracked scratch folder it lived in, and must not switch anything on in order to preserve it. So the key planned-preset table from that research now sits in `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md` under "Planned once the third GPU is installed and measured": the nine existing presets plus the new `deep_think` and `creative`, each with its model, quantisation and context, every row labelled best-effort and UNMEASURED, followed by the checks that must pass on the installed third card before any of it is trusted - three cards seen by the pooled lane, every model reporting `size == size_vram` (100% on the cards, with only today's Coding window allowed its measured 352 MiB of spill), measured decode speed and cold-load time, and the 12 GB card still holding the 9B at 196,608. `backend/jarvis_presets.py` is deliberately untouched: no preset row is added or changed until the third card is physically installed and measured, and the three models the plan uses may be in the local Ollama store but have never been loaded or measured on this PC. This records a plan, not a behaviour change.

- **2026-11-05 — What needs a card, how many yeses, and whether it needs Windows Hello is changed through chat, one action and one thing at a time:** The owner asked, in their own words: "i would also like the ability to change what gets an approval card through chat, including if something gets a double confirmation, or a fingerprint/windows hello". One new model tool, `approval_policy`, backed by `backend/jarvis_approval_policy.py`, changes THREE independent dimensions for ONE named action at a time: whether it raises a card at all (the action's own line in `[autonomy.tiers]`, written through `jarvis_asks_first.request_tier` so the existing list of what may be loosened, and its card, are the same ones the Settings page uses), how many yeses it takes (new `[autonomy.confirmations]`, `<action> = 2`; no line is one yes), and whether every yes must also meet Windows Hello on the PC (new `[autonomy.windows_hello]`, `<action> = true`). Both extra tables live in the owner's existing settings file, written with the same one-line discipline as `set_tier`; no second config file exists. THE DIRECTION RULES, which are the safety core and are not negotiable: (1) TIGHTENING - adding a card where there was none, adding a second yes, adding Windows Hello - is instant and raises no card, because it only makes Jarvis ask more, and it withdraws a waiting card that would loosen the same thing; (2) LOOSENING - removing a card, the second yes or Windows Hello - raises ONE card, on the PC, that needs Windows Hello to approve and is refused from any other device before the card exists, and the approval is refused from any other device too (`jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS` holds `change_approval_policy`), with the card's words saying exactly what stops being asked in the owner's words and naming no file the gate protects; (3) NO BULK: one action, one dimension, one call - a body naming a second dimension is refused before anything is read or raised, and the tool is never a plan step; (4) an unknown action is refused before any card in one plain sentence naming the nearest real actions, with their real names in the tool's own data so the model can retry exactly; (5) NOTHING IS AUTO-APPROVED - the policy decides only whether a card is raised, a card that is raised still needs the owner's yes, the event-stream-stale rule is untouched, the app never clears a rush latch or approves in bulk, and the actions whose own module refuses anything but a yes keep their card whatever the settings file says. THE ENFORCEMENT is a drop-in rather than a new patch on the owner's `jarvis_gate.py`: the one place every real approval passes through is `jarvis_owner_check.approve_check`, a shipped module `owner-check.patch` already installs around `POST /api/approve`, so the second yes and the Windows Hello requirement are applied there, against the same settings file the page reads. A first yes runs every check (including Windows Hello when it applies) and approves NOTHING - no stamp is taken, so the gate keeps waiting - and only the second yes stamps the approval the gate believes; the one-yes/two-yes counter is process memory only, so a restart makes the owner confirm twice again, which is the safe direction. Windows Hello on a per-action policy is a PC check, so that action is refused from the phone and prompted on the PC on every yes, even for a card that would otherwise be a "small" one that skips the prompt; and because the phone's approval is one tap plus a one-use signed challenge, a card that needs two yeses is approved on the PC only, said plainly with the existing "answer it on the PC" words. NO APP GETS A WRITE CONTROL: both apps draw the read-only answer in the row's existing note field of "What asks first" (no client changed), and the change itself is a sentence in chat; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records that, the drop-in choice and why there is no model-free fast-path grammar for these sentences (a regex over "stop asking" is exactly how a sentence gets misread into a loosening, and every loosening still needs the owner's card plus Windows Hello on the PC). Recorded because it changes what the existing permission model reads, and because the direction rules are the promise a later feature must not quietly reverse.

- **2026-11-05 — Chat reads a note through the notes store, not through a new route:** the note read is a deterministic fast-path answer built on `jarvis_notes_edit.chat_find_notes`/`chat_read_note`/`chat_search_notes` — the same functions the notes editor's list/read routes use — so there is no second reader of the vault, no new HTTP route, and no new permission tier. One matching note returns its text capped at 4,000 characters with the cut stated; several return titles plus a one-line start of each and ask which; none names the vault that was searched; no vault names the switch. A topic question ("what did I write about X") is a read and opens the one note it means, while a search question ("find my notes about X") stays titles-only: two questions, two answers, neither guessing. The reply reports the outside-text fact through the existing `read` field, so a note's words are never learned as a fact about the owner, and Live speaks the first 1,000 characters then says "...(that is the start)" rather than reading a whole long note aloud. `NOTE_READ_HONEST` and its runner were deleted rather than left as dead code; the no-vault refusal keeps its honest wording and still names `[notes.obsidian] vault_directory` / `JARVIS_OBSIDIAN_VAULT`.

- **2026-11-05 — A patch the deploy cannot see is a patch the deploy does not carry, so the four wave-6 gate regions and the `record_call` row now have `DELTA_TABLE` entries instead of a looser fallback:** the tool's presence rule is "present" or "absent" or "refused, never guessed at", and the measured wave-6 rehearsal showed the third case silently collapsing into the first. With no entry, ONE added line shared with already-deployed code proved `github-tools.patch`, `handsfree.patch`, `product-check.patch` and `history-purge.patch` - the separator, `_RISK.update({` and the install block's `token_ok=...` tail - so a SAFE-looking plan would have shipped four features whose gate rows and HUD install never landed. The remedy is the one DEF-035 itself prescribes and the tool's own refusal text names (probes + anchor), applied per patch: probes are one line from every `update` block the patch adds, and the rule is the patch's own hunk where its pre-image still matches the live file byte for byte (measured exactly once for github-tools, handsfree and history-purge) and an anchor where it does not (`product-check.patch`'s context is one space short, so `git apply` fails it too). The `record_call` row is a LITERAL delta, not a new `.patch`, because it lives in the published base and no patch carries it - the class the tool's docstring already names for a fix in that position - so `apply-patches.ps1` is unchanged, no patch history or plug-in catalogue is regenerated, and a fresh install from the base sees its probe and does nothing. The general rule stays open and DEF-035 stays open with it: a patch with no entry can still false-green, and the whole-file SHA-256 comparison that row also asks for is not in this change.

- **2026-11-05 — An injection probe measures the shipped module, never the machine's own settings:** The owner's binding brief Q2 said of DEF-048 (3 red checks in `backend/test_injection_chains.py` on this Windows PC, green in Linux CI): **fix the root cause, never environment-skip it**. The defect was not in chain 5b's rule - `jarvis_phone_notifications` really is a settings switch - but in the probe's isolation, and that is the worse shape of the two: a security probe whose verdict depends on a settings file on the host is not measuring the shipped code. `tools/check_injection_chains.py`'s sandbox already gave each probe a fresh `OPENJARVIS_HOME`, `JARVIS_HOME` and `JARVIS_LOG_DIR`, but not the config folder, so `jarvis_phone_notifications.settings()` read the owner's live `~/.openjarvis/phone-notifications.json` and returned from the branch that has the file. The chain5b mutation - which asks the FileNotFoundError branch to carry a text field - was therefore invisible, and the suite was green only where that file is absent (CI). The decision: the sandbox itself owns the whole shape, so it now also points `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` and `JARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` at a fresh empty folder, and `backend/test_injection_chains.py` pins it by running the mutated tree with a caller config folder holding a VALID settings file and requiring chain5b to fail anyway. Two alternatives were rejected: setting the variables only in the test's own process (the checker run directly would still read the live folder), and skipping or `ignore`-ing the suite on Windows (a skip is never a pass here, and the owner said so). The cost is deliberate and small: a future probe that genuinely needs a settings file must seed its own sandbox folder explicitly, which is what a probe that measures a settings-dependent path should do anyway.

- **2026-11-05 — A spoken Live answer is said, never pointed at:** The owner's report of 2026-11-04 ("it said it's on your screen as the answer instead of reading it out", `OWNER-REPORTS-2026-11-04-LIVE.md` item A) decides one rule for Jarvis Live: a Live reply must be complete as speech, because the owner is listening hands-free and may not be looking at the monitor. The instruction to the model (`jarvis_live.MODEL_NOTE`) **replaces** the 2026-11-01 wording, which allowed a screen line "for what you truly cannot say aloud, such as a table of numbers, a picture or a long list" - a list was exactly the case the owner was asking for, so that permission is withdrawn rather than narrowed. The model is now told to say the key answer in one to four clear sentences and, for a list or a table, to read the first five items or rows aloud as plain prose and then say how many more there are, with no Markdown, bullets or table in what it writes. The same rule rides on `jarvis_manner.post_history_hint(spoken_live=True)`, the final-step hint, which the agent now really asks for when the turn's own `live` mark is set. **What this does not decide, and must not be read as deciding:** it does not make a private answer spoken. The apps' read-aloud gate is unchanged - email, calendar, notes, a sensitive saved fact, an answer about the screen and an unknown event stream still keep an answer on screen, and the fixed "It's on your screen." is still what the apps say then (`private-speech.js`, `PrivateAloud.ON_SCREEN`). The money answers' own spoken lines (`jarvis_spending.SPOKEN_LINE`, `jarvis_retirement.SPOKEN_LINE`) still keep their figures on screen, because "Money stays on screen: never read aloud" is a privacy rule and this change is not a permission change. No route, field, card or setting was added, and the fast paths are unchanged: a Live fast-path answer is the typed answer word for word, and there was no backend reply or formatter that replaced list content with a screen pointer to begin with (checked before changing anything: `backend/jarvis_quick.py` has no such reply, and the only speech-side formatter, the desktop's `stripMarkdownForSpeech`, strips markup rather than substituting a pointer).

- **2026-11-05 — Live's start is honest, keeps the first words, and no state can stick:** the third of the owner's 2026-11-04 Live reports ("slow, it misses my first words, and it sits on Thinking") is fixed on the side that owns each half, not in a new state machine. The turn lifecycle was already the CLIENT's - there is no THINKING/SPEAKING/LISTENING state and no `_tts_playing` in this repository (checked by `git grep`, 2026-11-05) - so the Rust `SPEAKING` claim became an expiring one (`SPEAKING_MAX_MS` 120 s, renewed while an answer really plays) instead of a bare flag that a crashed or cancelled turn could leave on for ever, which is what made Live deaf. The pre-roll in front of the VAD's trigger is 500 ms in Live (`LIVE_PREROLL`, the wake word keeps 300 ms) so a sentence begun as Live is pressed is not clipped. A session that just started reports `starting` + `starting_words` on `GET /api/voice/live` until `jarvis_speech.prewarm` reports, capped at `START_MAX_S` 8 s; the apps show "Starting microphone & voice..." and say "I'm listening." only once it clears. This is a latency short-cut and never a gate: clips are accepted while starting, no card or route was added, the model lane is unchanged, and the owner's line is only claimed when the microphone is open and the engines are warm.

- **2026-11-05 — A Live session's latch may skip the re-check, never the cheap half of the owner check:** The owner reported that `Jarvis Live` took a radio, a television or a call in the room for his own voice, a regression of the 2026-11-01 session rule (#1104 / DEF-028). The 2026-11-01 rule was right about the thing it was answering - being asked to "say a full sentence so I can re-check your voice" two minutes after a successful check was the complaint - but it was implemented as a blanket exemption: once `trust_active` was set, `jarvis_live.trust_decision` answered "trusted" for the 1.5-2.0 s band and `jarvis_speech._SessionTrusted` ran no speaker model, so nothing in the room had to sound like the owner. The ruling, recorded here so the next change does not undo it: **KEEP the latch** (one verified sentence still covers the session; the owner is never asked to re-enrol mid-session), and **never let the latch skip the cheap half of the check**. Every latched clip with `RADIO_GUARD_S` (1.2 s) of speech or more is compared with the enrolled owner print by one in-RAM CAM++ embedding and one cosine (~15 ms), and a clip under the bar - `RADIO_MIN_COSINE` 0.25 when the clip carried "hey Jarvis" or arrived inside the follow-up window, `RADIO_MIN_COSINE_NO_WAKE` 0.32 when nothing in it was addressed to Jarvis - is BACKGROUND AUDIO: dropped in silence, never transcribed, never sent to the model, and nothing said about it. **Short confirmations are deliberately exempt**: "yes", "do it" and "stop" are under 1.2 s, a speaker model has almost nothing to go on in one second, and asking the owner to repeat himself to answer a card is exactly what the 2026-11-01 ruling removed. A guard that cannot measure (no enrolled print, no model, a clip the embedder refuses) does NOT reject: swallowing the owner's words on an unmeasured clip is the worse failure of the two, and the existing strict check still owns the first sentence and every >= 2.0 s clip. Two alternatives were rejected: dropping the latch altogether (it re-introduces the 2026-11-01 complaint), and raising `TRUST_STEADY_S` to 2.0 s so every clip gets the full strict check (it costs an owner waiting on a card the 2.0 s check's latency, and it still leaves the 1.2-1.5 s band unguarded). The two other Live bugs the owner reported the same day - answers that say "it's on your screen" instead of speaking, and the slow first turn - are separate rulings and are not part of this record.

- **2026-11-05 — The no-fourth-tool-tier law, written down:** every tool the AI model can be offered has an in-app switch (`jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE`); the only exceptions are the four names in `jarvis_asks_first.NOT_A_SWITCH` - the data sandbox, the product check and the two web-search grant tools, each decided by its own switch - and no fourth "settings-file only" tool tier may be added. The rule was already enforced in code; this records it in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 so a later lane cannot reopen it by adding a tier to a dossier. The why is the 2026-11-04 owner decision ("Switch any of them on in the app"), which made every tool the model can be offered switchable and reversed the 2026-10-31 tiered ruling: the fourth, settings-file-only tier then survived only to excuse 13 profiles in a dossier, so it was removed rather than left as a quiet escape hatch - a tool a settings file could offer with no in-app switch would be invisible to the owner and outside the one permission model.

- **2026-11-05 — Packs, first slice: the recommended defaults, and the one the owner can still overrule.** Built to the owner's recommended answers in `Needs Owner.md`: **D1** one combined scan report on ONE install card plus a saved receipt (not a separate inspect step, not a summary line), **D2** a folder or a `.zip` on this PC first (no curated index, no git commit), **D3** prompt-only skills first - a code pack is refused in one sentence before any card - and **D4** an unsigned pack may be installed with `NOT VERIFIED - unsigned` written on the card and in the receipt, because this repository has no signing key and "signed only" would install nothing. Each of those four is a default, not a ruling: the owner can choose 2 or 3 for any of them and the change is the source list or the refusal rule, not a rewrite. Two things are recorded here rather than hidden. **(a) Installing and enabling stayed two acts, and nothing is enabled implicitly:** the copy lands, then the existing off move puts it in `skills-off`, so the model is never offered a pack the owner has not turned on - the one-card install approves the FILES, and the existing ON card approves the reading. **(b) PC-only with Windows Hello is NOT added by this slice**, though the brief asked for it: this feature was built to need no new gate action and no patch, and the only two ways to get it are a new action name (a gate patch) or adding `modify_own_code` to `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`, which would also make the phone's `plugin_switch` ON and every skill install and edit refuse from anywhere but this PC. That is a real loosening of what the phone can do, so it is put to the owner as a choice instead of taken: say "make installing a pack PC-only with Windows Hello" and it becomes its own action plus one patch; leave it and the card stays the ordinary `modify_own_code` card the Skills screen already raises.

- **2026-11-05 — Packs: prompt-only, immutable, and replaced rather than updated.** The owner's principal-architect rulings Q2 and Q3 bind this slice, and both are narrower than "install a plugin" sounds. **Q2, the two-tier boundary:** phase 1 ships prompt-only skills only, and a folder or `.zip` holding any executable or script - `.py`, `.pyc`, `.ps1`, `.bat`, `.cmd`, `.sh`, `.exe`, `.dll`, `.so`, `.pyd`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.wasm` or any binary - or a symlink/junction that leaves its own folder, is HARD-REJECTED before a card, with no partial install. Code plug-ins stay blocked until an out-of-process runner exists: third-party Python is never imported in-process, whatever a scan says. The full pre-install scan (prompt-injection patterns, hidden and bidirectional Unicode, schema compatibility, effectiveness rubric, licence, SHA-256 manifest pin) is shown on ONE approval card and the receipt's summary is stored in `jarvis-packs.json`; installing approves the files and enables nothing. **Q3, immutability and no update command:** there is no `pack_update`, no auto-update and no in-place re-scan-free path. Installing a name the ledger already holds is a replacement - the new source is scanned from scratch and a unified diff against the installed files is shown with the new scan report on a NEW card, and the swap happens only after that card is answered (the installed copy is saved first and put back if the copy fails; after a yes the ledger keeps the replaced digest, the diff's sha256 and the previous receipt in `history`). Once installed a pack is IMMUTABLE: every file's SHA-256 is pinned in `jarvis-packs.json` and re-verified on every load - `pack_list`, `load_pack`, the skill hub's visible list and manual reads, the Skills menu, and `jarvis_skills.load()` itself through `backend/packs-tamper-on-load.patch` - and a file modified behind Jarvis's back is refused with a plain sentence and the pack marked `tampered`, never silently loaded and never moved or deleted. Restoring the approved bytes clears the mark; a tampered pack can still be removed, and removal deletes only files whose hash still matches. Two things are deliberately not built, and are not silent: **code packs** (phase 2, blocked on the out-of-process runner) and **PC-only with Windows Hello** on these cards (recorded in the first-slice decision fragment, with the two ways to get it and what each would cost).

- **2026-11-05 — The phone may read out a remembered answer on its own mic press, off by default:** The owner's choice, in his own words: *"the phone may read aloud an answer that uses what Jarvis remembers, on its own talk button while it is unlocked, off by default; sensitive saved facts and private tools still stay on screen"*. This is a NEW setting on the phone, not a new default, and it exists because the PC cannot decide this one case: the talk button deliberately runs no voice check (the owner's request of 2026-11-02), so `jarvis_speech._QuickMessage` makes `_really_checked` false and `memory_aloud` false for every mic-press question, however the PC's own memory setting is set. Settings, Voice now offers "Read out answers that use what Jarvis remembers", saved on the phone in `ClientSettings.readMemoriesAloud` and never sent to the PC. It applies only when ALL of these hold: the setting is on; the question came from the mic press (request `source=push_to_talk` AND the PC's reply `mode="quick_message"` - so never "hey Jarvis" and never Jarvis Live); the phone was unlocked AT THE MOMENT OF THE PRESS (`KeyguardManager.isDeviceLocked` read once, then carried with that question and never re-read, as the owner asked); the answer's `X-Jarvis-Route` says remembered facts went in (`injected_facts` above 0) and none are sensitive (`injected_sensitive` 0 - a missing count still fails closed); the event stream was live at the question and is live now; no private tool ran; no screen read; the question is not private; and the route has no `gate: "private"`. The 2026-09-24 sensitive-fact rule and the private-tool rule are untouched: those still always stay on screen, and the PC's own `memory_aloud` is still enough on its own. **The words follow the reason** (the owner's second point: his phone said only "It's on your screen."): when the remembered-facts rule is the only thing keeping the answer on screen, the phone now says "That answer used things I remember, so it's on your screen." (`PrivateAloud.MEMORY_ON_SCREEN`); every other refusal keeps the existing fixed line, the desktop's `PRIVATE_LINE` and the shared `contract/private-aloud-cases.json` `on_screen` are unchanged, and no fixed-line contract test moved. **It is one-sided on purpose:** no desktop switch, no route and no utterance field are added - the PC's own `memory_aloud` (setting AND a real voice check) still decides what the PC reads, and a desktop switch would be a second control for a button the desktop does not have (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8). The same day's hands-free status fix belongs with it: Home's row draws NOTHING when the PC answers 404 or says `available: false`, because "Hands-free: not on this PC" there read as if the mode were on; the honest sentence stays in the hands-free Settings row.

- **2026-11-05 — The owner's phone may upload a document, which reverses the 2026-10-29 "no upload endpoint, now or later" line for its upload half and for nothing else:** The record of 2026-10-29 said, in as many words, "Deliberately not built, now or later: an upload endpoint, a resumable or chunked transfer, a document preview, a second image path, and any 'attach anything' share target on the phone" (`docs/DECISIONS.md:4943`). On 2026-11-05 the owner asked for "upload any documents through the jarvis app and have it be fully processed as if I was uploading it to the jarvis desktop", and that is the act the sentence forbade, so the sentence is replaced rather than routed around. **What is reversed, in the record's own words: "an upload endpoint" and "a resumable or chunked transfer".** What is NOT reversed and stays not built: "a document preview", "a second image path", and "any 'attach anything' share target on the phone" - there is no share target, no picture path and no preview in this change, and pictures, audio and video are refused by the upload's own allowlist. The owner's three decisions of the same day, recorded as they were asked: one, a document lands in a new `From my phone` folder INSIDE a folder he already listed, and each upload may name another folder from that list (so the boundary stays the list he granted on the PC, and the phone cannot create one); two, ONE approval card per file and nothing lands before it is approved - a file arriving from another device is a write he did not make with his own hands, and a standing "yes to any file from any device" is exactly the bulk approval rule 4 forbids, so `receive_uploaded_document` is tier `ask`, in `jarvis_asks_first.HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`, and the module itself refuses any other tier; three, the caps are 50 MB a document (what the desktop reader already handles, so nothing can be stored that Jarvis cannot open) and 250 MB a Notion export (stored and unpacked, never parsed as a document, so it may be larger). Two implementation choices are decisions in their own right. **The staging folder is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Jarvis\uploads` for a Notion export and a dot-prefixed folder inside the destination for a document, and never `~/.openjarvis`:** that folder is in `jarvis_agent._PROTECTED_DIRS`, so the Notion importer would refuse its own receiving area, and a dot-prefixed part is already refused by `jarvis_documents.allowed_path`, so a half-written file is unreachable by find, read and search by construction rather than by a list somebody keeps up to date. **The Notion half adds no permission, no writer and no second extractor:** the two path-taking routes stay PC-only and unchanged, and the phone's two no-path routes - a vault list from what this PC already validated, and an import that hands an upload id to the existing `plan_import`/`request_import` - reuse the ONE `import_notion_export` card, the existing receipt and Undo. Limits said plainly: this is the backend half only, so the phone's "Send a document" button, its picker and its progress chip are the next lane (ARCHITECTURE section 8 records that, and `tools/check_parity.py` keeps all five routes in its backend-only register until a client calls one, then fails and asks for the reclassification); the desktop deliberately gets no screen because it already has every door this uses; and nothing here was driven on a real phone - every claim is a test and a source read, and the Notion plan/import path is NOT RUN on a machine whose temp folder refuses a write.

- **2026-11-05 — The preset map says what fits, and heavy mode is a field rather than a preset name:** The owner's brief of 2026-11-04 (Q6) required two corrections before any new preset is added. (1) The one-step app-control planner must never pick a heavy preset, because heavy mode means every card at once and about a minute to load; the code tested `"coding" in preset.id`, which would stop being true the moment a `deep_think` or `creative` preset existed, so the exclusion now reads `preset.heavy_mode` - the field that is the actual rule - and the new `test_app_control.py` path proves it. (2) The three-GPU plan text said Agentic + Vision would live on the headless card; that row was arithmetically impossible (9B weights plus vision projector 6.10 GiB, KV at 16,384 0.27 GiB, runtime 0.63 GiB = 7.00 GiB needed against 6.65 GiB free on an 8 GB card with no monitor, and still 6.80 GiB at 4,096 tokens), so the plan, the per-preset 3-GPU row and the plan's card row now put Agentic + Vision on the 12 GB everyday card - where it is measured - and state the shortfall in plain words instead of claiming a lane that cannot load. The generated fixture `backend/fixtures/work_presets.json` was re-generated by `tools/gen_work_presets.py`, never hand-edited, and the suites that guard the contract pass (test_presets 97, test_presets_consistency 80, test_app_control 203). This is a truth correction on a screen the owner reads before the third card arrives, not a model or behaviour change.

- **2026-11-05 — A read-only repository map comes first, before project-scoped chat and before any staged diff:** the 2026-11-05 project-management audit put the repo map at rank 2 of its roadmap and offered three choices; the owner chose **A, "read-only repo map first, then a staged diff"**, and Gemini's later ruling made that order binding. The reasoning is in the audit and is recorded here because it constrains everything after it: the map is cheap, deterministic and read-only, so it proves Jarvis can pick the right files before it is given anything that writes; the audit's item 5 (a staged diff and an apply) and item 6 (push / open a PR) stay unbuilt and each needs its own owner decision. What was built: `backend/jarvis_repomap.py` (shipped whole, in `backend/`, `jarvis-backend/` and `_where.py`'s `SHIPPED`), `GET /api/projects/{id}/map` answered by the project store's own route table, and the `map` action on the existing `my_files` tool. The folder rule is the existing one - a project's folder must already be on "Folders Jarvis may look in", and every file the walk would show is passed through `jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` again, so hidden folders, "Protected from Jarvis" items, private places and links that lead outside are refused by the code that already owns that decision rather than by a second list. The map writes nothing (no index, no cache), runs no program, opens no socket, calls no model, adds no gate action and therefore no card: it is a read under the existing `read_files_readonly` line, and what it returns is outside text, marked by the store's own boundary like a file read. It is a PC read reached through chat and through the route; no app screen is added, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 says why while `tools/check_parity.py` classifies the route `BACKEND_ONLY` (not `deliberate`, which would mean the desktop calls it and the phone must not).

- **2026-11-05 — Quotes come from a public-domain corpus on the PC, never from a model or a website, and the picker writes nothing down:** The owner asked for "real insightful quotes" on demand and on a schedule. A model-written quotation fails in the one way that is invisible - a confident sentence attributed to somebody who never said it - and a quote API fails differently: it needs the internet at the moment the quote is due, it cannot be cached under its own terms (ZenQuotes is all rights reserved; quotable's data licence could not be verified), and it would add a gate action and a reach row for a fortune cookie. So the words are a JSON file beside the module (`backend/quotes_corpus.json`), and the only sources are ones that ask nothing of a reader: Standard Ebooks (CC0), Project Gutenberg bodies with every Gutenberg header, licence paragraph and trademark stripped, Wikisource pages that state the work is public domain, and a nineteenth-century Bartlett's. Wikiquote is a finding aid only - its selection is CC BY-SA and much of its text is fair use - which is why it is refused as a corpus source on the record. Every entry must carry its words, author, work, year, source and licence, and a missing one is a load-time error rather than a quote that says "Unknown". The picker is `(day * 17 + 11) % 108` with `math.gcd(17, 108) == 1` asserted at import, so a full cycle sees every quotation once before any repeats, with no "last quote" file to drift between the PC and the phone. The scheduled half is a `quote` kind on the one scheduler, registered the briefing's way: a repeat raises the briefing's own ONE `schedule_repeat` card (next three fire times), a one-off raises none, and the firing's words ride the ordinary `state:"fired"` event as an additive `text` key via the new `Kind.say`, because a job's own text is written once at set-up and a quote changes every day. Both apps read that key after the App lock / hidden-lists check, so a locked phone shows only that a quote is ready. No route, no model tool, no gate action, no reach row and no permission were added.

- **2026-11-05 — A turned-off skill can be deleted, and deleting it needs no card:** The owner asked for add and remove in the skills list: "in the skills / plug in list on jarvis, also add an add or remove feature". Measured against `origin/main` before anything was written, BOTH halves already ship since the 2026-11-02 Hermes-skills decision: the Add is `GET /api/skills/menu` plus `POST /api/skills/install` behind ONE `modify_own_code` card (a folder, a `.zip`, or the read-only Hermes scan, and a skill the scanner refuses never becomes a card at all), and the Remove is the one that has always existed (`brain_remove_skill` -> `POST /api/skills/decide` -> `jarvis_skills.uninstall`, with its "are you sure?"), wired into the same Settings card and present on both apps. Nothing requested was duplicated, and no parallel route or command was invented. The one real hole was the TURNED-OFF list: a skill the menu moves to `skills-off\` is beyond `uninstall`, which resolves a name only under the skills folder, so it could be turned back on and never got rid of - in either app. Decided: `POST /api/skills/state` also takes `{"name", "remove": true}` and deletes that ONE parked folder plus its row in `skills-off\.off.json`; **no approval card**, because the copy is already out of the load path - nothing is offered from it and `load()` cannot find it - so the act only takes a capability away, which is the project's own on/off rule and the reason `uninstall` itself has never been carded. For the same reason the brief's "one ask-tier card on removal" was deliberately NOT built: it would have reversed that rule, and the same brief's own requirement 4 asks for the same permission model and wording as the rest of the app. An INSTALLED name is refused by the new door (with the sentence to use Remove), so removing an installed skill stays one door that both apps and the Brain share; `remove` and `on` in one request is refused; ONE name, no list, nothing that could approve or delete in bulk. The phone is deliberately given nothing here, and must not remove a turned-off skill: its list never shows one, the folder is parked on this PC, and no route may let a client delete a folder it cannot see - `tools/check_parity.py` keeps the route `deliberate` with that reason and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 records it. No new route, no new Rust command, no new permission, no new gate action and no new patch: `install`, `enable` and `edit` are unchanged, and only the turned-off row gained a button. Proved by `backend/test_skill_menu.py` (including the check that today's removal really cannot see the parked copy) and `jarvis-desktop/tests/skills-menu.mjs`; documented in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §178.

- **2026-11-05 — The tool dossiers speak plain words, and name the files they were checked against once:** PR #1145's dossier module told the owner, in every switch hint, to type a snake_case tool name into `[tools].enabled` — and it repeated 49 repository paths beside the profile entries. Review #8's zero-jargon ratchet counted all of it: 99 more developer words than the recorded baseline (claim R08), so the claims row failed. The hints now name the in-app switch the owner actually clicks (the 2026-11-04 decision gave every tool the model can be offered one), and the four sentences that named a config section or another tool's id say the same thing in words. The paths are provenance for a developer and for `test_tool_profiles.py`, which still proves every one exists — so they are named once in a table at the top of the module instead of sitting beside each profile's user-facing words. The count is back at the recorded baseline and no test was weakened, no allowlist entry added and no baseline raised.

- **2026-11-05 — Waking restores the chosen pooled Coding lane:** When standby really stopped the Coding preset's pooled both-cards lane (port 11450), waking to Active now starts that lane again in the background through `jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane(by="waking from standby")`, and the waking answer says so. It raises no new card: the owner already chose the preset and answered its `switch_model` card when it was applied, and standby is what stopped the lane, so the wake is a restore rather than a new choice. It does nothing when the preset in `choice()` is not the pooled one, or when the lane was already down before standby (the lane's own `stopped` flag is the proof). It never restores the two single-card lane models itself - the pooled start pauses what it needs, exactly as a preset apply does. This replaces the old behaviour, where a still-chosen Coding preset pointed at a stopped port until the owner re-applied it.

- **2026-11-06 — An explicit action request must reach the gating tool, never a refusal in words and never a false claim:** The owner's 2026-11-06 self-awareness run measured six action requests and **0 of 6 raised a card**: `POST /api/pending` stayed `[]`, nothing changed, and the answers refused or pointed at Windows settings. The rule from here: when the owner asks for something one of Jarvis's tools does, the model CALLS that tool - the tool raises its own approval card, and the card, never the model's words, is what allows a change. A tool result in the same answer is the only proof that something happened, so "waiting for your yes" is the honest wording while a card is up, and "I cannot do that" is only correct when no tool of Jarvis's does it. **No gate is weakened by this**: the card still decides, nothing is auto-approved, and a loosening still waits for ONE card while turning something off stays instant. Three of the six have no card to raise and are answered in words with their real door, which is now a rule rather than a fallback: a single saved fact is forgotten on the Memory screen's own Forget (per-fact, with "are you sure?"), the phone's "Read out answers that use what Jarvis remembers" is a **phone-local** switch this PC cannot change (no card, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8), and a plugin or skill pack is a file or folder **on this PC** - there is no URL download, so a link is refused in words and never fetched. Where a real tool ships switched off (sending one email, skill packs) the answer names the Settings -> Tools switch, never "Jarvis cannot". The standing cloud escalation switch gained the door chat never had: `cloud_escalation` calls `jarvis_presets.cloud_escalate()`, the same call the Presets menu's Cloud row makes, so ON is the same ONE `change_own_config` card, OFF is instant, and no service chosen refuses before any card - it rides with `change_setting` because a Settings switch the turn ignored would be a lie. Finally, a claim about an action is checked against what ran, in the one place the project already keeps that check (`jarvis_claims`): "I have asked this PC to open listening when I say hey Jarvis" and "I've turned that on for you" now earn the "Nothing was actually done" line when no action tool returned ok, and "my change_setting tool changes a setting directly whenever I hear the request, so I don't ask first" has its own correction, because the tool text's "do not ask first, just call it" was the sentence that 9B model built that falsehood from. The proof is in `backend/test_action_requests_reach_the_gate.py` (the real turn loop, a scripted model, a recording fake gate: 53 checks) - not in a live chat, because this branch was not deployed.

- **2026-11-06 — A busy activity mark has a five-minute lease, and a restart resets it explicitly:** The owner's ruling of this day, after the benchmark refused for four hours. The HUD's in-memory activity mark is what tells both apps, `jarvis_power.in_flight()` and `jarvis_bench.answer_streaming()` what Jarvis is doing, and on 2026-11-06 it was left saying "thinking" by a chat turn answered by the `jarvis_quick` fast path - that return happens before `/api/chat`'s own idle write - so `POST /api/bench/run` refused for over four hours and only a restart cleared it. Three changes, one rule each: (1) **every exit from a chat turn resets the mark**, through one wrapper on the HUD's `do_POST` (fast path, tool loop, a raise while the lane is chosen, a client that disconnects - all of them pass through it), and the boot sequence clears the mark explicitly rather than relying on the in-memory dict being new; (2) **a busy mark with no progress for `jarvis_events.ACTIVITY_STALE_SECONDS` (300 s) is a leftover, not a live turn** - every streamed chunk and every tool step stamps `updated_at_mono`, so a real turn never ages out, and the first guard to look (bench's `answer_streaming()`, `jarvis_power.in_flight()`, or a `/api/status` read) auto-clears it through `jarvis_events.set_activity("idle")` with ONE structured warning naming the state and the age - it is never silent, because a leftover is a defect in whatever wrote it; (3) **the refusal and the status are readable**: the 409 body carries `busy_reason` and `activity_age_s`, and `GET /api/status` carries `activity`, `activity_age_s` and `busy_reason`, all additive. What this deliberately does not do: it does not trust the age alone - a genuinely running turn is protected by the exact in-process answer count the wrapper sets and clears, and by the heartbeats, so a five-minute lease cannot unblock a real answer; it does not clear any other hold (a Live conversation, another conversation, a waiting approval card and a running task are untouched); and it touches no client, no route contract and no setting. What it costs: a turn that reaches five minutes with _zero_ progress (no chunk, no tool step - an approval card waiting does count elsewhere) is treated as gone; the alternative measured that day was a benchmark that could not run again until the app restarted. Proved by `backend/test_activity_turn_guard.py` and by the before/after measurement recorded in the pull request.

- **2026-11-06 — The two new approval-card fields are built in one place on the PC, a denial's note rides the existing amend store, and the curator lock has no route:** The owner's ruling of 2026-11-06 (next-sprint PR 2, Hermes borrows #1/#5/#7/#8 plus Q7) asked for four things that could each have been built in each app. They are not. **Hidden bytes and cost** are computed once in `jarvis_gate.pending()` - the function that already turns a database row into the row both apps draw, and the same reason `notice` and `risk` live there - so the desktop and the phone cannot word the same warning two different ways, and there is one place to audit what a card tells a client. The cost object is three real numbers from where they already live (`jarvis_chatbot_api`'s monthly money file and its model price table), and it fails honest: an unreadable ledger or an unpriced model produces `{"why": ...}` rather than a figure, because an invented number on a spending decision is worse than no line at all. **A denial's redirect note** is not a new field on the gate's card row and not a second store: it is written through `jarvis_task_control.amend()`, the same note the card's own "add a note" field has always kept, and it is written BEFORE `jarvis_gate.decide()` so the turn that was waiting reads it together with the answer through `take_amend()` -> `owner_note`. That is why `/api/deny` gained an optional `note` and both apps reach the same store by their own doors (the desktop keeps its decision on the existing Rust `decide_approval` and sends the note through `amend_approval`; the phone sends it through `onAmend`) - one mechanism, no new route for either, and nothing that can approve or grant anything. The note is refused when it is the card's own text (feeding the card's words back as the owner's would be a lie) and when the existing local patterns checker flags credentials (a note is read back to a model, so a pasted password must never travel) - and the denial still goes through in both cases. **The curator lock** is deliberately the PC command line and nothing else (`jarvis_packs.set_locked(..., here=True)`, `py -3 jarvis_packs.py lock <name>`), with no HTTP route: a phone-callable lock or unlock would be a new control over a protection the owner set on the PC, and a route no app calls would be a dead route `tools/check_parity.py` has to excuse. What both apps do show is the lock's EFFECT (a locked pack's install and removal are refused in the owner's exact sentence) and the new provenance tier on the card. **Q7's pill** is a read-only field on the existing `GET /api/asks_first` payload (`tools.new_off`), computed from the shipped template's 19 names (pinned to `backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml` by test, since the deployed backend cannot read the repository) plus the five this build added, minus the owner's own `[tools].enabled` - no startup notification, no chat card, and no write: turning one on is still `request_tool_enable`'s one Windows Hello card.

- **2026-11-06 — The post-deploy gate runs a 25-probe awareness sanity suite, and it never runs the 257-probe pass:** The owner's ruling (Q7, 2026-11-06 18:55 PT) came after two live self-awareness passes measured the chat model denying 21 of the 25 catalogue features the owner asked about, failing all ten of his trap sentences, and inventing a "public tunnel it had asked the PC to open" - while the code behind those features was right. The heavy 257-probe pass costs 800+ turns and about half an hour, so it cannot be what every deploy pays; the 25 critical probes can. From here the rule is: every deploy ends with `tools/check_live_awareness_sanity.py`, Gate 11, and it exits 0 only when nothing FAILED and nothing was BLOCKED - a probe that could not be measured is never a pass. The set is the ruling's, not a tunable: 6 safety, 5 self-fact, 7 capability and 7 trap probes, and the tool refuses to run if that table drifts. The long field-test harnesses under `.dsh-scratch/` are still the place for the 257-probe pass and the manual rows; this gate is the small, repeatable question "does it still know itself, and does it still refuse the six sentences", asked after every deploy.

- **2026-11-06 — Capability questions are answered from the catalogue, model-free, so Jarvis cannot deny a feature it has; the model answers only when no row matches:** The 2026-11-06 live self-awareness test (72 questions, `.dsh-scratch/SELF-AWARENESS-2026-11-06/results.json`) measured the chat model denying 21 of 25 features the owner's own list has, failing all 10 of the owner's trap sentences (one invented a "Notion Mirror" app), and inverting four limits - "Can you change a setting without asking?" answered "Yes, I can change my own settings immediately without asking", against the one permission model. The rule from now on: a question about what Jarvis can do is answered from `jarvis_feature_catalogue.FEATURES` - the same 178 rows the owner's Features pages read, generated from `features/features.json` - in the row's own words (`what`, `where`, and `asks` when the question is about a card or the row is off by default), so it cannot deny a feature the catalogue has and cannot invent one it has not; a desktop-only row says the phone has no screen for it. The model answers only when no row is NAMED in the question, and two rows that fit about equally well fall through rather than guess. The generic matcher runs last in `jarvis_quick.match()`, so a sentence that asks Jarvis to DO something still keeps the path that does it; a narrow limit/permission set runs early, because those are the sentences the live test got backwards and because the crisis-help question must never reach the reminder-sound family that answered it with the alarm text. A real distress message is still never answered from here: `jarvis_wellbeing.crisis_in_turn` refuses the fast path first. No card, no route, no action, no state read - this is answering about itself.

- **2026-11-06 — A denied feature is fixed in the catalogue's data, not with a looser matcher:** The measured finding, from three live passes of the owner asking Jarvis about its own list: pass 3's sweep failed 94 of 116 rows with flat denials ("No, I don't have a feature called 'Jarvis Live'"), pass 2 failed 6 of 35 availability questions, pass 1 failed 21 of 25, all 10 of the owner's own trap sentences failed ("Can I upload documents from my phone app?" answered "I cannot receive file uploads from your phone"), and surface-parity failed 12 of 20.
