Every one of those rows was already in `features/features.json` - the feature existed, and the answer denied it - because the owner's phrasing shared no name word with the row's own id, title or alias, and a capability answer is only allowed to quote a row it can NAME. The ruling this records: **the widening lever is the row's own words, never a fuzzier matcher.** `find()` matches an alias exactly (its own docstring: a general question must not be answered with a feature's facts), so an alias is a name, and the fix is to add the owner's measured names: 69 aliases across 64 rows, each a multi-word phrase lifted from a measured sentence ("reads your answers aloud in the voice i chose", "starts a chat where nothing is kept and nothing i saved is used", "what a parking stay costs", "warns me when text tried to rush me", "import a notion export from my phone"), never a single generic word. Three rules keep the data from becoming a guess: **one alias belongs to one row** (said on its own it must come back as that row and no other, checked for every alias), **no alias is repeated on another row**, and **a question that names no row is recorded as an honest fall-through with its reason** rather than forced onto a neighbour - two measured questions are exactly that: "work these, but never quietly" says "these" and names nothing, and "doe arithmetic accurately..." is a typo the strict finder cannot bridge. `backend/test_catalogue_phrasing.py` holds the committed fixture of 182 measured questions (116 pass-3 sweep, 25 pass-1, 35 pass-2, the 6 trap sentences) and proves 180 of them name their row through the guide's own finder, that the owner's exact Notion and document trap sentences land on `notion-import` and `document-from-phone`, and that no alias can tie. What this deliberately does not do: it does not touch `jarvis_quick.py`, any matcher, any route, any card, any consent rule or any app screen - a stricter matcher stays strict, and the four-of-five "can you ...?" sentences that are really requests keep the paths that act. What it does not fix: the capability lane's own two-word rule still requires a row's id word to appear in the sentence, so a row whose owner phrasing never says its id word (voice-training's "learn what you sound like") carries the alias but cannot be resolved by that lane alone - listed in the pull request rather than papered over.

- **2026-11-06 — A new entry point updates the feature catalogue row in the same PR that builds it:** The owner asked Jarvis in chat whether he could import his Notion notes as Markdown, process them in the Android app and send them to the main Jarvis, and Jarvis said it could not - while the phone's "Send a document" and "Bring in a Notion export" buttons had existed since 2026-11-05 and the live PC answered with notion.can_import: true. The code was right; the self-description was stale. The phone doors landed in `f4c122217` with one contract tweak and no feature row, so `features/features.json` had no row for a document from the phone and still called the Notion import desktop-only with the reason "the phone has no Notion-import screen" - false the day it was written. The model could only answer from what the catalogue and the feature_guide tool told it, so it denied a capability this PC and phone both had. This is the same failure class as docs/JARVIS-API.md 21.12 (2026-10-27). The rule from here: an entry point a person can press - a new phone button, a new Settings door, a new route an app calls - is not finished until the feature row that describes it is in `features/features.json` in the SAME pull request, with its `surface` telling the truth about both apps, its `where` naming the real button, and the generated copies regenerated. `tools/check_feature_list.py` cannot check that `surface` is true (it only checks the shape), so this stays a rule a person keeps, exactly like the one-sided reasons it protects. If the catalogue row cannot be written yet (the screen is not built), the row says that instead of the feature being absent.

- **2026-11-06 — Holding the talk button is authoritative: the pause-based end is suspended while the finger is down:**
  The owner reported on 2026-11-06 that holding the mic button "keeps cutting
  me off and acting like I took my finger off of the mic button even when I'm
  still speaking sometimes". The talk button is tap-to-talk OR hold-to-talk,
  and its end was decided in two places that never spoke: `ui/parts/VoicePress.kt`
  decided hold-versus-tap only when the finger lifted, and `voice/VoiceSession.kt`
  ended the clip the moment the pause rule fired - the on-phone Smart Turn model
  answering "finished", or `TurnEnd.MAX_PAUSE` (two seconds) of quiet. That is
  exactly what a tap needs, because nothing else would end it, and exactly wrong
  for a hold, where a mid-sentence pause is the owner thinking, not finishing.
  The rule now: **a held talk button is authoritative.** The button reports the
  hold about 400 ms into the press and before the finger lifts
  (`VoiceButton`'s `onHoldStarted`, through `HomeActions` to
  `VoiceSession.holdStarted()`), and while that flag is set and the finger has
  not been released, neither a pause nor the Smart Turn ask may end the capture;
  only the release sends. The decision is one pure, JVM-tested function
  (`voice/HoldEndRule.kt`) so the five cases - held/pause, held/ask, released,
  tap/pause, tap/ask - are proved off-device. Tap-to-talk keeps its pause
  auto-send unchanged: a tap never sets the flag. The physical safety cap is
  unchanged and deliberate: `Recorder.record` still stops a held capture at the
  server's `maxSeconds` (30 s by default), so a finger left on the button cannot
  hold the microphone open for ever. Deliberately NOT touched: the Live,
  handsfree and wake-word paths also build a `TurnEnd`, but they have no held
  button, so their pause-based end is unchanged - the rule lives only in the
  talk-button capture loop. What this cannot prove here is the gesture itself,
  which needs a real phone; the field test is in the pull request.

- **2026-11-06 — Home's answer box scrolls inside the same three-line footprint, it does not grow into the face:** The owner's report of 2026-11-06 was a long answer on the phone's home screen cut off after about three lines with "…", readable only by pressing "Show chat" (*"if i get a response from jarvis rhat is longer, i should be able to scroll down to read the whole response instead of havijg to press more chat"*). Two shapes were offered, and the owner chose **option B on 2026-11-06 16:53 PT**: the box keeps the exact footprint of the old three-line peek - `ReplyPeekPlan.LINES` lines of `bodyMedium` at the phone's own text size, plus the 6dp above and below - and the inside of it scrolls, so the face, the doors row and the bar do not move at all. The alternative, letting the answer area grow upward into the face up to a cap, was turned down; that is why `HomeScreen.ReplyPeek` is a capped scroll viewport whose short answers keep their own shorter height, and not a panel that grows. **The answer is never ellipsis-truncated any more:** the old `Text`'s `maxLines = 3` + `TextOverflow.Ellipsis` are gone, every word is reachable by dragging, and the answer stays one plain `Text` - no markdown, no `FormattedAnswer`, nothing about how the words are drawn changes. **Streaming** keeps the newest words in view until the owner drags the answer by hand - the same rule the full-screen chat's list already followed, through the same "Follow the reply" setting - and a finished answer is left where he left it, with one settle for a reply that streamed in the box and was never touched, because its last token and the "stopped streaming" flag can land in the same frame. **"Show chat" and "More" stay exactly where they were** and still open the whole thread. A short answer looks and measures as before, so nothing changes for it, and the only affordance is a thin fade of the bar's own background (`Chrome.surface1`) while more remains below, painted over the text so it costs no height. **Phone-only by nature:** the desktop's answers already scroll in their own panes, which `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records; no route, control, permission or card was added - display only. The rules are pure Kotlin in `ReplyPeekPlan` with `ReplyPeekPlanTest`, and the real drag/TalkBack behaviour is NOT-TESTABLE from this branch and is named as the field test rather than claimed.

- **2026-11-06 — A read-aloud refusal for remembered non-sensitive facts or a screen-read answer can be lifted for one answer by the owner's own tap on his unlocked phone, and the existing phone memory switch also covers typed answers:** The owner reported that his Android app still refused read-aloud for two classes of answer he is happy to hear - "It's on your screen." and "That answer used things I remember..." - "even though it's okay to read these ones out loud". This EXTENDS the phone setting of 2026-11-05 (`decisions.d/2026-11-05-phone-memory-aloud.md`), and everything that entry says about the sensitive-fact and private-tool rules still holds. The phone's own setting ("Read out answers that use what Jarvis remembers", OFF by default) now covers the typed "Read aloud" control as well as the talk button: with it ON, on his unlocked phone, an answer whose ONLY blocker is remembered non-sensitive facts is spoken. A new one-off "Read it aloud anyway" action on the refusal strip covers a memory-only block (switch off) or a screen-read answer: it reads THAT one answer once, on that tap, and stores nothing afterwards - it is not a setting and not a standing grant. Both doors require the phone to be unlocked at the tap and the link to be live at the tap, and neither is ever offered for a sensitive saved fact, a private tool, a stale link or a locked phone: the 2026-09-24 sensitive-fact rule is not loosened. When a refusal is something he can change in Settings the line may name the switch - the memory sentence is followed by "To hear these every time, turn on 'Read them out' in Voice settings." while that switch is off - and it never says more than that, never quotes the answer and never quotes a fact. Nothing here auto-speaks: every read is his own tap, as the 2026-11-05 change was. Phone-only on purpose: the PC's own `memory_aloud` (its setting AND a voice check) still decides what the PC reads, the desktop HUD's typed read-aloud keeps its own path, and no route, field, card or PC setting changed (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8).

- **2026-11-06 — Q6: the deploy gate compares the RUNTIME TREE, not just the version number:** The owner's ruling, after wave 6's version-identity check would have forced a desktop and phone reinstall for a merge that changed no runtime byte. `tools/check_live_version_identity.py` keeps its three old answers (live `VERSION` vs the installed desktop's `FileVersion`: 0 match / 1 mismatch / 2 unreadable) and gains a second question: with a deployed ref - `--deployed-ref`, defaulting to the live `_jarvis-state.json`'s `resealed.ref`/`resealed.commit` under `--backend-path` - it runs `git diff <deployed>..<main-ref> -- jarvis-backend/ jarvis-desktop/src/ jarvis-desktop/src-tauri/src/ jarvis-client/app/src/main/`. An EMPTY that diff prints exactly `PASS (runtime tree identical to deployed ref <short-sha>)` and exits 0, so a test-only, docs-only, tools-only or CI-only commit needs no reinstall; a non-empty diff exits 1 naming the changed runtime files and saying a deploy is required; git or either ref unreadable exits 2 with an UNREADABLE sentence, never a pass. A freshly deployed tree has no `resealed` key (`apply-patches.ps1` drops it on its next finished run), so the default with no deployed ref is EXACTLY the old identity check and the deploy gate itself is unchanged - Q6 applies to the re-check after a reseal, which is where it is meant to be used. `--main-ref` defaults to `origin/main` and `--repo` names the checkout. Pinned by `backend/test_check_live_version_identity.py` on temporary git repositories (identical runtime tree -> the exact PASS line, a changed `jarvis-desktop/src/` file -> exit 1 naming it, an unknown ref -> exit 2, and the no-deployed-ref default -> the identity check). Measured on this PC the same day: deployed ref `e4d01b9b3`, current main `3d7d861ec`, the four-path diff empty - the real run printed `PASS (runtime tree identical to deployed ref e4d01b9)`.

- **2026-11-06 — Questions about Jarvis's own measured facts, and its hard safety rules, are answered model-free from the live source:** The pass-2 self-awareness test (2026-11-06) measured the PC before asking and the local model answered from imagination instead: memory facts 1 against 3 stored, enabled tools 4 against 14, the wake word "isn't stored on this PC" although it is in the live jarvis-framework.toml, no cards or driver, no version or counts, and "off" for pictures while /api/self said on. The owner's rule for this project is that Jarvis does not claim more than the evidence supports, and a version, a count, a setting or an action it never took is exactly that kind of claim. So a question about Jarvis's own measured facts - its version, its desktop, phone, model, card and driver, what it remembers, how many notes, chats, tools and projects it has, its wake word, and whether a setting is on - is answered by `jarvis_quick.py` with no model, from the module that owns the value at answer time, and the same holds for the six hard safety sentences (no approval by saying so, no public tunnel, the pairing token never shown). A value that cannot be read is said plainly and never guessed. This adds no route, no card and no write, every such answer is read-only, and any sentence outside those families still goes to the model exactly as before.

- **2026-11-06 — STOP is proved by all three together: zero `LISTENING` on both addresses, zero `ESTABLISHED` on `:4719`, and HTTP refused:** The owner
  accepted the refined Q7 stop proof in a clickable decision card on 2026-11-06
  at 11:33 PT, "Accept the refined stop proof", and the Principal Architect
  ratified it formally at 11:35 PT (Q3). The canonical proof, in exactly this
  wording, is the three conditions TOGETHER: (1) `LISTENING` count **0 on both**
  `127.0.0.1:4719` **and** the tailnet `:4719` address; (2) `ESTABLISHED` count
  **0 with local port `:4719`** - `TIME_WAIT` rows are explicitly allowed; (3)
  the HTTP probe gets **no status at all** (`Invoke-WebRequest
  http://127.0.0.1:4719/api/status` failing to connect, i.e. connection
  refused). All three are the gate, and a missing one of them is a skipped half,
  never a pass. The refinement is needed because Q7's literal "zero lines"
  cannot pass on this PC: when the stack is stopped, `netstat -ano | findstr
  :4719` still returns 244-264 `:4719` rows - nearly all `TIME_WAIT` with PID 0,
  kernel-held sockets the server already closed - while `LISTENING=0`. It is not
  a loosening for real listeners: ANY line that says `LISTENING`, `ESTABLISHED`
  or `SYN_SENT`, or that carries a non-zero PID, still stops the deploy, and a
  skipped half, an empty block or a count that prints nothing is never a pass.
  This replaces the earlier state, where the 2026-11-06 wave-six result still
  recorded the owner's written confirmation as outstanding.

- **2026-11-07 — A card limit may refuse only a call that asks for a card, and a "nothing ran" correction must be true of the turn:** The #1209 follow-up audit measured seven ways the new action-request answers could still be false, wrong or needlessly refused, and the two general rules matter beyond the seven. **First: the per-answer card limit is a limit about cards, so it may only refuse a call that would RAISE one.** `CARDS_PER_TURN` was read before the action in the cloud-escalation tool, so a card-full answer refused an immediate OFF - a tightening that needs no card - in words; the same reading would also refuse an ON on a switch already on, which the module answers with `card: False`. The check now runs after the action is known and only for `on` while the switch is actually off, which is the one case that asks the owner for something. **Second: a correction line may only say what is true of the turn.** "The sending tool is switched off, so nothing ran" is false when a `draft_email` really ran; the platform's own row label is quoted through `jarvis_asks_first.tool_label` rather than paraphrased; "forget this fact" is not a request to forget when the owner said "don't"; the phone switch really does cover a typed answer's "Read aloud", so its correction now says so; and a plugin/skill link is refused by naming the chat door that exists, not a Settings installer that does not. **Third: a call that reached its module is a finished call, never a refusal.** An already-on or already-off `cloud_escalation` returns `ok` with `changed: False`; it is recorded with `ran`/`ok` and stays in `tools_ran`, so both apps and the turn's own "did anything run?" checks see the call that really happened instead of a false "not allowed". Nothing here loosens a gate: ON still raises its one `change_own_config` card and writes nothing before the yes, OFF is still instant, a value that is not "on"/"off" still raises nothing, and the model can still only repeat what the module reported. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` was corrected the same day: #1209's merged change left the lane rules byte-identical to `main` and put the call-it instruction in each tool's own description, so the record no longer claims a rewrite that was reverted. The proof is `backend/test_action_requests_reach_the_gate.py`, 51 checks to 77, plus `test_agent.py` (374 passed, 1 skipped), `test_settings_tool.py` (298 passed) and the reach suites, all green.

- **2026-11-07 — Chat and Jarvis Live change settings through ONE door, so every setting must be reachable in both, and Live never asks for a spoken yes:** The owner's requirement (verbatim): *"also make sure anything that can be changed by chat with jarvis (with an approval card when appropriate) can also be changed in the same manner through jarvis live. i dont want any gaps"* and *"also check if jarvis can also change the settings of these under the hood functions whether through settings or chat or live"*. The audit measured the gaps, not a plumbing problem: Live sends the same `/api/chat` request with `live: true, provenance: "voice"`, so it already shared the route, the agent, the gate and the cards - but only 4 of the 60 switchable tools could be named by the matcher, the tool-switch sentence the owner actually says ("Turn on the browser control tool.") was not a shape the grammar knew, and the model denied that Live could change settings at all. Decisions taken: (1) the spoken names are GENERATED from `jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE` by `tools/gen_tool_targets.py`, with a `--check` drift mode, rather than hand-typed, because a switch Settings draws that chat cannot name is the defect this audit found; (2) the new "turn on/off <name> tool" shape is CLOSED-WORLD - the word "tool" and a whole alias from that table are both required - so a device sentence ("turn off the kitchen light") keeps its own feature and is never read as a tool switch; (3) the card rules are unchanged and were not loosened: ON is still the PC only, ONE card plus Windows Hello, OFF is instant, nothing auto-approves; the only Live difference is WORDING, the one calm line a carded change already got, now also used for a carded tool switch because Live speaks its answer aloud; (4) the Live spoken prompt for a waiting card says the card is TAPPED on the PC or phone, never "say approve" - there is no spoken-approval surface in this project and this pass did not add one (rule 4), so the requested "say approve or tap yes" wording was deliberately not used in favour of the accurate "approve it on your phone or PC"; (5) the false denial is answered deterministically from the code ("yes - a setting change asked through Jarvis Live works exactly like typing it … some settings are PC-only for safety, so their card waits for you to tap it"), in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, so it can never take away a "cancel that"; (6) the audit's Live-only tool refusal was investigated read-only and is NOT a Live or taint defect: the route hands the answering turn a request that includes the PC's own recalled-facts system message, `jarvis_agent._TurnWatch.app_context` reads any system message in that request as "the app sent extra text", and `_settings_turn_is_shaped` therefore refuses a model-issued `change_setting` with `SETTINGS_AFTER_OUTSIDE` whenever memory recall fired - typed turns are equally affected, the typed model simply did not call the tool. That finding is recorded here and in `docs/LIVE-DESIGN.md` §3.8b, not fixed in this pass (the fix is in the route that builds `request=` for `run_local_turn`, outside this change's scope, and weakening a safety guard is the owner's call). The permanent proof is `backend/test_live_settings_parity.py`, derived from `jarvis_settings_registry.capability_keys()` so a setting added later without both doors fails the suite.

- **2026-11-07 — The standing cloud-escalation switch is said out loud in chat, deterministically, instead of hoping a 9B model calls the tool:** The 2026-11-06 decision made an explicit action request reach its gating tool, and PR #1209 gave chat a `cloud_escalation` tool that calls `jarvis_presets.cloud_escalate()` - the same call the Presets menu's Cloud row makes. Measured on live build 0.2.437, that was not enough: asked "turn on cloud escalation" in chat, the local 9B model answered "I've turned on cloud escalation" while the switch stayed OFF and the self-awareness row failed "no NEW card appeared within 25s" in two passes; worse, the feature guide answered the sentence with "There is no fixed sentence for it", which is false about a switch the Presets menu really has and a card that really can be raised, so the sentence never reached the model or the card at all. The rule from here: **a sentence that is unambiguously a request to change a switch Jarvis really has must not depend on the model choosing a tool.** So `jarvis_quick` gained a deterministic matcher and runner for the switch's own words ("turn on/off cloud escalation", "enable/disable", "escalate my/hard questions to the cloud", "stop escalating to the cloud", and a bare "turn it on/off" ONLY inside a sentence that also names cloud escalation), placed before the feature guide that used to swallow the sentence. **It adds no rule and loosens no gate:** the runner calls `jarvis_presets.cloud_escalate` and nothing else, so ON is still the same ONE `change_own_config` card that writes nothing before the owner's yes, OFF is still instant, ON with no cloud provider chosen still refuses BEFORE a card, and nothing there approves a card. The model tool is not replaced - both doors end at the same module, and the deterministic one wins when it matches because it cannot be mis-called. **A question stays a question** ("is cloud escalation on?" keeps the guide's read), a sentence that names no escalation is never read as one, and the pronoun form requires the sentence to name the switch: without that, "cloud escalation is on but do not turn it off" would be read as OFF and change the very thing the owner asked to leave alone. The answer is the body's own sentence rather than a filled-in "Done", because a switch that can spend money must not claim a change it did not make; a card still waiting is reported as waiting. The proof is `backend/test_cloud_escalate_setting.py` - 130 checks over the matcher's twelve cases and the runner's four outcome paths, not a live chat, because this branch was not deployed.

- **2026-11-07 — Q1/Q7: the chosen cloud provider is the one that answers, chat gets the provider door, and the privacy backstop is hardened while auto-escalation keeps every gate:** The owner's rulings from the 04:00 PT packet, after the 2026-11-07 options-understanding audit (`.dsh-scratch/OPTIONS-UNDERSTANDING-AUDIT-2026-11-07/REPORT.md`) measured four owner-visible defects and the safety review asked for two tightenings. **Q1/B6 replaces a hard-coded lane.** `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()`'s literal `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")` - the audit's B1 - is replaced by a request-time read of `cloud-choice.json` through `jarvis_presets.cloud_chosen()`, with `DEFAULT_LANE` only as the fallback when no provider is chosen; the key lookup, `cloud_lane`, `lane_status` (`/api/reach`), the ONE `change_own_config` card and the chat answers all follow, so a chosen Mistral/OpenAI/Groq/xAI/OpenRouter can never send to DeepSeek. Chat gains a read-only list of the six (`cloud_provider_list`/`cloud_provider_ask`) and a change door (`cloud_provider_choose`) that calls the SAME `jarvis_presets.apply_cloud` the Presets Cloud row calls - ONE `change_own_config` card, refuse-before-card, write only after the yes - so chat is a second door to the existing control, not a second way to change it. There is no Anthropic service in this tree; the six are openai, deepseek, mistral, xai, openrouter and groq. **Q7 P0 hardens the privacy backstop.** `jarvis_router._PRIVATE_TERMS` gains home address, street address, mailing address, postal address, "my/our address" and phone number (it already held ssn, social security, passport, driver's licence, routing number, credit card and "medical"), and the too-broad `\bdiagnos\w*` is replaced by medical contexts only - `medical diagnos*`, `diagnos(ed|is) with`, and the owner/family possessive - so an engineering prompt such as "diagnose this test failure" can escalate normally while "I was diagnosed with …", "my diagnosis" and "my son's diagnosis" stay local. A false match only costs quality; a miss sends words to a cloud model, so the list still errs toward local. **Q7 keeps auto-escalation's semantics and they are now pinned.** The default with the standing cloud-escalation switch OFF is detect-and-ask (gate `"offer"`, one card, `auto: false`); the switch ON - reachable only through its own `change_own_config` card - may auto-escalate a clean hard prompt only after every gate above the yes has passed: Lockdown, a tainted conversation, a picture, the screen's words, an attached file, a private word, a pasted secret, complexity under the threshold, a spent cloud budget and no lane offered. It waives the per-question yes and nothing else; no request body, header or client flag can stand in for the file. The three audit fixes that ride with this are B2 (key/model/second-PC/Telegram "how do I add …" answers name their real feature, so reminders are no longer the answer), B4 (all 38 switches answer a state question about themselves - the registry's own name is passed to the feature guide, never the snake_case key) and B5 (the Cloud row's title is "Cloud (an API service you choose)"). Proved by `backend/test_options_understanding.py` (new, 136 checks: the six-provider in-memory proof, the chat door and its card, reach/card/answer/lane agreement, all 38 switches, the four verbatim audit phrases, and every auto-escalation gate on and off) and `backend/test_router_private_terms.py` (extended to 181 checks: the address/phone positives and their technical controls, and `diagnos` both ways), with `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 145.1a carrying the contract. Nothing is pushed, merged or deployed by this branch.

- **2026-11-07 — Dispatch sets are not read-marks, and meta-instructions are retried only after a miss:** a read-only intent belongs in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS` (it must not clear `cancel that`) and never in a set `run()` routes to a runner before the rest of the chain - the Wave-8 build routed `repo_watch_list` to the reminder answer exactly that way. The repo now tests dispatch buckets disjoint, every reminder name explicitly handled, and the watch-list sentence reaching its own runner through `match()` + `run()`. A trailing meta-instruction (`one sentence`, `briefly`) is a statement about the answer, so it is stripped and retried only when the unmodified sentence matched nothing. The informational `audit` job checks out full history because its self-code claim reads git history, and the rolling phone release patches `targetCommitish` to the built commit. Architect rulings Q1-Q4 and Q7, 2026-11-07.

- **2026-11-07 — GitHub self-knowledge goes in the catalogue and the deterministic chat answers, NOT in the system prompt (the owner's Q6 ruling):** the 2026-11-07 tool-capability audit proved that "what can you do with my GitHub?" knew only the two 2026-09-30 research features, that "can you merge a pull request?" invented a merge approval card, that "what is your GitHub repository?" denied having one, and that "how do I disconnect it?" could not say - while the real read+actions surface, `/api/accounts`'s careful sentence and `jarvis_github.NEVER_WORDS` were all built and unreachable. The tempting fix was three lines in `jarvis_agent.LANE_SYSTEM`, and the owner ruled it OUT at 04:00 PT: `LANE_SYSTEM` is pinned word-for-word to `backend/jarvis-primary.Modelfile` and `jarvis_profiles.JARVIS_SYSTEM` by `test_character.py`, and its 1,800-token ceiling is the budget the character block was re-pinned around, so a GitHub paragraph there re-breaks both for a fact that has a better home. The fix that landed instead: ONE `connected-github` row in `features/features.json` (plus every generated copy) naming the six tools, `github_search`, the scheduled `watch_github` job, the three carded actions and the never-list; a read-only `github_self` chat intent that names `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis`, reads `jarvis_github.connected()`, lists the tools, answers "what do you need", the never-list and the asks-first rows, and refuses merge/push/commit/close/delete/approve from `NEVER_WORDS` with no merge card promised; an `accounts_answer` intent that finally reaches `jarvis_accounts.sentence()` / `state_words()`; and the `/api/accounts` GitHub row corrected to the real six abilities and "Read AND act, each with its own card". The model is told nothing new on purpose - the deterministic path answers before it. `decisions.d/2026-11-07-github-self-knowledge-catalogue-not-lane-system.md`.

- **2026-11-07 — The 11434 Ollama lane is pinned to the headless RTX 2080 SUPER, by UUID and task-scoped:** the owner's 04:00 PT ruling applied. Both Ollama servers were measured on the RTX 2060 (`nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` showed both `llama-server` pids on `GPU-1ba04124-...`), and their two `/api/ps` load plans, 6,111 MiB + 9,401 MiB = 15,512 MiB, cannot fit a 12,288 MiB card; `ollama ps` reports 100% GPU for both anyway, because that figure is the load plan. Windows' own `\GPU Process Memory(*)\Dedicated Usage` counters are the real check: the 9B held 5,545 MiB in VRAM and 3,856 MiB was paged to system RAM. The 11434 server is started by the Ollama tray app and by nothing in this repository, so the applied step is a logon task that runs a small outside-repo wrapper setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=GPU-1f7e38f5-3447-97fc-0c13-c8c7eaf83313` and `OLLAMA_VULKAN=0` for that process tree only, with the app's own autostart shortcut moved aside so only one instance starts; the 11436 and 11435 lane tasks are untouched. That was measured on a throwaway 11451 server through the same `cmd` wrapper: the server named the override in its own log, landed on the headless card, read 6,141 of 8,192 MiB, and the model was fully resident at 6,142 MiB in VRAM against a 5,991 MiB plan (69.38 tok/s; 66.38-71.17 across runs, against 50.4-50.7 when it shared the 2060). A global per-user variable was measured to the identical numbers and is deliberately NOT the deploy step: it would pin every future CUDA process on the PC, including other AI tools that start at login, which the ruling did not ask for. `start-lane.ps1` can instead own a second lane on 11434 - one script, one scheduled task per card - and that was measured working too, but it needs a one-word edit to that outside-repo script and turning the tray app off, so `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md` records it as the alternative. The page also carries the exact wrapper/task/XML/rollback commands and says the deploy must verify residency with the GPU Process Memory counters, never `ollama ps`; the pin moves no preset (Fast still runs on the Coding lane, 11435), and no live server was restarted or killed while this was made.

- **2026-11-07 — Read-aloud follows how the owner asked, and a model default may only move on a measured run:** The owner's words of 2026-11-06/07: a typed question must never be read out automatically; a spoken question is read aloud, including answers that use what Jarvis remembers, in Jarvis Live and "hey Jarvis" too; only extremely sensitive information stays on screen; every answer keeps its own Read out loud in its menu beside Right/Wrong; and "stop reading everything out loud" / "read everything out loud" change it from chat or Live. This replaces the 2026-11-05 phone setting that defaulted remembered-answer speech OFF and deliberately excluded Jarvis Live, and it adds the PC's own backend-owned switch (`/api/read-aloud`, ON by default) which is PC-only because the phone has its own on-device switch (ARCHITECTURE section 8). In the same wave the owner accepted the measure-first promotion bar for presets: a preset default may change only when Jarvis's own five-suite measurement shows zero spill (`size == size_vram`) at the preset's window, quality not worse on the domain rubric (General also needs tool-calling) and the speed floor - otherwise the current default stays and the bigger model is a selectable alternative. `jarvis_bench.promotion_verdict` always reports `applied: False`; no preset row moved in this wave.

- **2026-11-07 — Per-repository GitHub watching is a watcher the owner can steer in one sentence, observe-first, and free when nothing changed:** The owner asked: "i can tell jarvis what frequency of notifications or to stop or follow new or any combination of these things through jarvis live and chat". The existing machinery only knew topics (a pull) and a CI watcher for a named pull request, so the per-repository watcher was built INSIDE `jarvis_watch.py` rather than as a parallel system: its items go to the same `/api/watch/decisions` ring buffer through `jarvis_watch_ci`'s store, and its poll runs as a Long Fuse job body (`watch_repos`) registered by the one startup call that already registers the others, requiring `github_read` per run so a scheduled search parks for a ONE-SHOT allow rather than a standing rule. A new watch starts in `observe` mode (it records what it would say and says nothing); the yes that lets it speak is ONE `schedule_repeat` card, reusing the gate's existing action for setting up a repeating watcher rather than adding a gate action or a tier. Every poll is conditional on the stored ETag, so an unchanged repository answers `304 Not Modified` and costs no rate-limit points; public repositories need no token, and a configured token is only ever attached in `jarvis_watch._gh` and never written to a database, a decision row or a log. The one matcher in `jarvis_quick.py` serves both chat and Live because Live turns are the same `/api/chat` route with provenance `voice` + live true. THE POLLING HALF was traced before it was built, because a watch that never polls is not a watcher: `watch_github` and `watch_pr_checks` are Long Fuse job bodies whose rows are created by `POST /api/jobs`, and a Long Fuse job runs ONCE - nothing re-queues it. What actually repeats on this PC is the scheduler, and that is how the older "tell me when CI fails on ..." GitHub watch stays alive: a kind registered through `jarvis_schedule.register_kind`, a job row created by `Scheduler.add_repeat` only after the ONE `schedule_repeat` card, and an `on_fire(job_id)` callback every N minutes. So `watch <repo>` now calls `jarvis_watch.ensure_repo_watch_job` - i.e. `add_repeat` - instead of raising a card of its own; `repo_watch` is a new kind in `KIND_MODULES` (so a watch set up before a restart still finds its on_fire), its payload lives in the kind's own `extra` state, the approved job makes the watch active on its first fire and polls on the scheduler's own clock, and deleting the watch deletes the job. No second permission model, no new gate action, no standing rule: the same card, the same queue, and the same instant delete.

- **2026-11-07 — Full self-awareness is a measured contract, and changes are journaled locally:** every thing the program has must answer from its own registry with no model - every boolean, choice and number setting, every tool switch, every preset row, every desktop Settings row that has words, every feature row, and the preset/benchmark/change/inventory overviews - and `backend/test_self_awareness.py` re-runs that audit as assertions (the read-only audit in `.dsh-scratch/AWARENESS-CHANGE-AUDIT-2026-11-07/` went from 121 gap rows to 0). Changes are recorded in a bounded local journal by diffing a snapshot of the program's state (version, preset/model, all settings, all tool switches, counts) against the last one, written when a changing answer runs and refreshed when asked; benchmarks start through `jarvis_bench`'s own async runner and its machine-checkable `confirm` block and raise no card because they change no setting. Desktop Settings rows with no spoken adjust stay page-only by design, and the one unlabeled row is recorded as not askable by its words. Owner request of 2026-11-07 (\"full awareness of everything the jarvis program has, including if anything changes\").

- **2026-11-07 — Jarvis's knowledge of its own code is a generated map shipped beside the backend, not a code reader and not a model tool:** The owner's requirement was "jarvis should understand every major part of its own code that can be viewed on the jarvis github main branch". Three existing things came close and none of them was it: `jarvis_repomap.py` maps a folder the owner names and deliberately keeps no index, `jarvis_self_portrait.py` knows measured facts (version, tools, cards) but not the codebase, and the feature catalogue knows what features do, not which module implements them. So the source of truth is the deployed tree itself: the live overlay is built from this repository at the merge commit, which is exactly what the owner can see on `main`, and `tools/gen_self_code_map.py` turns that tree into `backend/jarvis-self-code.json` at deploy time — the same beside-file pattern `requirements.lock` and the HUD files already use, with the same twin rule (`jarvis-backend/` carries the same bytes). The map is generated, never typed: paths, key-module docstring summaries, VERSION, the commit and its own date, and the newest twenty subjects all come from the tree, so `--check` can compare the committed file byte for byte and fail on drift. Completeness is a checked property rather than a claim — one table assigns every tracked file to exactly one subsystem, and the generator refuses a tree where a file belongs to none or to two, while generated, binary and vendored files are named and counted rather than dropped. The reader shipped whole (`jarvis_self_code.py`) never runs git, never opens a socket, never writes and never imports code to look at it; it reads the JSON beside itself and answers in plain words, and the absence of that file is an honest answer rather than an error. Phase 1 deliberately adds NO model tool and NO route: the four deterministic chat intents in the shipped `jarvis_quick.py` cover the owner's four question shapes, a miss says "not in the map I was built with" and names the two nearest parts, and the answers state their own limit — the map knows nothing newer than the deploy that installed it and holds no code bodies. A model-facing `self_code_lookup` tool and a clone-refresh path are phase 2, after this is live and measured.

- **2026-11-07 — Self-knowledge answers are fixed words from the record, not the model's guess:** the feature self-awareness audit of 2026-11-07 measured the live backend denying live capabilities (approval policy changeable by chat, chat history, spending limits, watches and the CI watcher) and inventing others ("I haven't changed"; the cost line's meaning). The owner's requirement that Jarvis know its own recent features and settings is answered by shipping the facts, not by asking the model again: `jarvis_feature_guide.SELF_FACTS` (four bounded, read-only sentences plus their digests, fed to the self portrait), `jarvis_recent_changes.py` generated from `CHANGELOG.md` + `changelog.d/` by `tools/gen_recent_changes.py --check` (the live folder has no CHANGELOG), and three general shapes routed into the existing settings-explain door instead of the model. Two wording bugs go with it: scoped anti-slop never claims "on" while the filter is off, and an unchanged toggle writes no receipt. Nothing here is switchable, raises a card, opens a route or changes a tier: every new answer is a read, and the reason each fact lives in a shipped table rather than a runtime file read is that the folder the owner runs carries no repository documents.

- **2026-11-07 — The third graphics card is used by the presets, measured per preset:** The third RTX 2080 SUPER is installed and the preset matrix was measured row by row on this PC - one throwaway `ollama serve` per config on port 11451, two calls with the second warm, never the live 11434/11436 lanes. **Coding moves to all three cards at 49,152 tokens** (the Q2 ruling: the largest window that stays above 75 tok/s): the same `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` measured **83.82 tok/s with zero CPU spill** (16.17 GiB, cards 0/1/2) and a **31.561 s cold load** against 60.58 tok/s and 69.611 s for 32,768 on the same-night two-card control (same q8_0 cache; the 2026-11-03 shipped record used f16 and read 80.36/36.0 s, so it is not a like-for-like baseline); the enabling knob is `OLLAMA_SCHED_SPREAD=1` in the pooled server's child environment, without which the same three cards measure 56.82 tok/s. The 32,768 row measured 84.93 tok/s at 15.10 GiB with a 10.884 s load and is the recorded alternative (1.3 % faster, 1.07 GiB smaller, 16,384 fewer tokens); 65,536 measured 59.06 tok/s, below the bar, so it is not chosen; 98,304 is recorded (88.69 tok/s, 19.41 GiB, zero spill) and not chosen; 131,072 FAILED (`server: server exited 4294967295`), so no window above 49,152 is chosen. **Every other preset keeps its measured configuration**: the everyday 9B stays on the 2060 at 196,608 (42.01 tok/s, 9.18 GiB) because the always-on model on all three cards would hold 262,144 tokens at 44.11 tok/s but pause every other lane for 2.1 tok/s; Fast stays on the display 2080 SUPER (76.20 against 65.85 across three cards, while the headless 2080 SUPER alone measured 85.29 and the vision model 63.35 there, so a dedicated headless lane is a measured gain that waits for a lane-start path on 11438); and General, Reflect, Documents, Browser, Pictures and Agentic + Vision keep sharing those measured rows rather than a new guess. **No preset changes model tonight**: the q4 coder measured faster (87.47 tok/s at 19.52 GiB at 32,768; 93.08 at 20.60 GiB at 49,152) but its coding quality was never re-run on the 6/6 rubric, which was measured on the q3 weights, so switching would be an unmeasured quality claim; the new heavy presets (`gemma4:31b-it-qat` at 18.81 GiB and 15.54 tok/s, the uncensored 27B at 17.38 GiB and 17.96 tok/s) are measured but deferred to Wave 8 because the pooled lane carries one fixed model and parameterising it needs its own refactor and tests. **Auto-escalation is not enabled**: the 2026-11-07 cloud audit measured a privacy gap - `home address`, `address` and `phone number` are not in the privacy backstop, so a longer "my home address" question escalates with auto mode on - and it stays off until that list is fixed and the audit re-run. The `manifests-v2` finding is recorded as a tooling fact rather than a Jarvis bug, because no model-store code reads `manifests/` from disk and Ollama's `/api/tags` listed both layouts (18 models). The pooled server's child environment now also sets `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, the cache the measurement and the two live lanes use: measured at 49,152 tokens, q8_0 reads 16.17 GiB against the default f16's 18.07 GiB, both zero spill. The full record, every row and every failed row are in `docs/MEASURED-2026-11-07-THREE-GPU.md`.

- **2026-11-08 — Build caches live in one shared place, and the self-code map is written with its twin:** Six worktrees' own `src-tauri/target` directories (about 25 GB) took the owner's `C:` drive down to 1.35 GB free and tripped Syncthing's "< 1% free" database halt, and a map regenerated without its `jarvis-backend/` twin cost one full CI cycle on #1214. The rule now: every cargo or Gradle command uses ONE shared cache root (`D:\jarvis-cache\cargo-target` and `D:\jarvis-cache\gradle` on this PC, else one shared folder under the user profile), a subagent deletes any per-worktree target it made before reporting, and `tools/gen_self_code_map.py` writes `backend/jarvis-self-code.json` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis-self-code.json` in the same run, with `--check` refusing when the two differ. The rule is written in `CLAUDE.md`; it replaces per-worktree caching, and nothing about the twin rule itself changed.

- **2026-11-08 — Factual self-state answers are deterministic, preset-independent, and an unregistered name is refused honestly (owner ruling Q3):** the owner's standard is that read-aloud state, the GitHub connection receipt and settings state must not depend on the preset, after the coding preset's 30B model echoed catalogue rows and told him about changes that never happened. So every registry-backed factual or state query is answered upstream of every model, lane and preset choice: a matched intent answers in host-measured words - a `quick:` route - and those words are byte-identical on the general, coding, fast and general_uncensored presets. A self-capability or setting question that names no registered row or alias gets the explicit deterministic refusal ("I do not have a setting or feature with that exact name — say 'what can I change?' or 'what do you have?' to see the real list") instead of model improvisation, and ordinary self-fact nouns never reach that fallback. A missing or raising registry reader says it could not read it and never guesses; a read-only state answer never raises a card; and an exception in the deterministic layer is reported honestly, never replaced by a model claim. Pinned by `backend/test_preset_independence.py` - byte-identical answers across the four presets with the model entry point unreachable - and by the owner-phrase corpus in `backend/test_factual_determinism.py`, whose cases are the sentences he actually typed.

- **2026-11-08 — Model, lane and hardware truth:** the screens and the chat answers describe what is actually running, on hardware that actually exists, with measurements kept apart from estimates. Where a fact is not knowable - no model change recorded, nothing measured, the chat lane unreachable - Jarvis says so instead of guessing. The HUD chip shows the model in use, not the PC's default; the hardware profile counts the PC's cards, not the cards one Ollama log happens to list; the offload warning names the chat lane it read and says plainly when that lane is unreachable or empty; a persisted lane cannot outlive its on-demand pooled server, a pooled start cannot leave a second copy of the big model resident, and a pooled start asks for the measured 49,152-token window instead of Ollama's default; and the new chat/Live model answers read only the real stores and the real preset/lane configuration, start a benchmark only through the existing owner-initiated runner, and never call one model better without a measurement for that preset. This settles the wrong screens the owner photographed on 2026-11-08: the chip that named the default while the Coding preset was answering, the Brain that called a three-card PC a one-card 8 GiB PC, the repeated tier sentence, the estimate and measurement that contradicted each other, the Compute column's two-card-era sentence, the offload warning that read the wrong server, and the chat outage where a saved lane named a pooled server that was no longer running. The same ruling closes the three gaps measured on 2026-11-08: a dead pooled-lane pointer is repaired inside the chat-lane getter with one sub-second TCP probe and an atomic rewrite to the configured everyday lane (never starting, pausing or loading anything there); a pooled-lane chat request names its configured 49,152-token window in `options.num_ctx` so Ollama cannot fall back to 8,192; and the wake-time everyday warm-up never touches the everyday lane while the pooled lane owns the cards, nor loads a pooled 30B model on it - the duplicate that caused the 74%-on-GPU / 26%-on-CPU warning and the VRAM starvation. Non-pooled lanes keep their existing request and warm behaviour. The owner's three live UI asks were folded into the same wave: the rail says "Hide advanced" while open and "Advanced" when closed, the persistent "This session is staying on your PC." line is off the HUD (the latch and its queue-scoped rush evidence are unchanged; the three hud-safety copies stay byte-equal), and the model filter row folds as "Filters" / "Hide filters" with wrapping controls.

- **2026-11-08 — The auto Wi-Fi reconnect is approved as a bounded, default-ON, PC-only maintenance feature (owner ruling Q4):** the owner asked for a feature that "defaults on but can be changed in settings or chat with jarvis", and that every 2 hours while the desktop has no internet asks Windows to reconnect to a password-protected Wi-Fi network it has already saved. It runs on the 2-hourly tick with NO per-attempt card (an offline PC cannot be reached to answer one), but the switch is ordinary: turning it ON raises exactly ONE `change_own_config` card and nothing changes until that card is answered; turning it OFF is instant and cardless. Six guardrails bind it, all enforced in `backend/jarvis_wifi.py` and proved in `backend/test_wifi_reconnect.py`: (1) only saved profiles whose authentication is `WPA2PSK`, `WPA3SAE`, `WPA2` or `WPA3` and which carry a stored key — Open/WEP/802.1X are refused and `key=clear` is never passed; (2) it acts only while the switch is ON, Lockdown is readable and OFF, this Wi-Fi has no working internet, and the radio/adapter was not turned off by the owner (an unreadable radio or Lockdown fails safe); (3) at most the top 3 such profiles that are actually broadcasting in range, each verified for 10 seconds, stopping at the first success; (4) the switch appears in Desktop Settings, Chat and Jarvis Live through that one carded path, and no model answer can toggle it; (5) every attempt writes a Change Journal receipt (`jarvis_framework.audit_log`) with `timestamp`, `profile_name`, `auth_type` and `result: connected | still_offline`, never a key, so "did you reconnect my wifi?" is answered from that record; (6) this decision record. The feature is PC-only: the phone neither shows nor changes it (ARCHITECTURE section 8, JARVIS-API section 204; `/api/wifi-reconnect` is `deliberate` in `tools/check_parity.py`). On a PC where Location services is off, the in-range scan and the radio state cannot be read, so the check reports that and makes no attempt — it never guesses.

- **2026-11-08 — A wrong answer gets one reason, one correction, and one memory card, and both apps read it back (owner ruling Q2):** Right/Wrong on the desktop and the phone now opens one sheet with five plain reasons (wrong fact, out of date, misunderstood, too long, too sensitive) and one optional correction of at most 500 characters; `POST /api/feedback/mark` accepts the optional `reason` and `correction`, and `GET /api/feedback/mark?turn_id` returns both, so a re-shown answer says what was chosen and shows the owner's own words rather than a machine tag. A wrong-fact or out-of-date mark raises ONE existing memory-review card for the first remembered fact the answer used: the owner's correction becomes an update card (`feedback_correction`, labelled "Update the fact" / "Keep it as it is") and no correction becomes a forget card (`feedback_retire`, labelled "Forget that fact" / "Keep using it"), asked for with `retire_cards=1` by every desktop read and by the phone. A misunderstood or too-long answer leaves a manner note and a too-sensitive one a privacy note; nothing is auto-approved, nothing is decided in bulk, and the card is the only decision. The single-decision design was kept over a multi-button queue (the owner's ruling Q2) because replacement words have to be typed for an update to mean anything: a correction present is an update, a blank correction is a forget. The migration smoke test opens a COPY of the live `feedback.db` and proves the old rows and marks still read with the two new columns — never the live file.

- **2026-11-09 — Every shipped patch must be carried by a route the repository can prove:** the owner's ruling Q8 keeps per-patch `DELTA_TABLE` entries as the standard but requires a unit test proving no shipped patch falls outside them - a whole-file SHA was rejected as brittle against CRLF, encoding and comment shifts. `backend/test_patch_delta_coverage.py` parses every `backend/*.patch` and every `(patch, file)` pair on a live-shipped file, and requires one of four proved routes: a `DELTA_TABLE` entry with explicit probes (the five patched base files), the module copied whole (`$SHIPPED`, for a patch the rebuilt modules supersede), the published base already holding the patch (per line, through `selftest.patch_states` - never a whole-file comparison), or the patch's own hunks being byte-for-byte text this repository holds (`backend/_stack.order()` with no invented pre-image). Measured on `85e9e8500` (the wave-13 merge): 180 patches, 180 in `$PATCHES`, 221 live-shipped pairs - 27 delta, 149 base, 27 exact-hunk, 6 whole, 12 exempted, 0 uncovered; `DELTA_TABLE` holds 48 entries, 26 naming a patch and 22 literal deltas with no `.patch`. Wave 14 then added the one `auto-learn.patch` entry (it names two files), so the same suite now measures 49 entries (27 patch-named, 22 literal) and 221 pairs as 29 delta / 25 exact-hunk at this branch's head - the counts moved because the patch stack grew, not because the rule changed. The 12 exemptions are patches whose hunks read the owner's own file and are not in the published base, so no probe can be chosen without a live read and none was guessed: `appearance`, `attention-settings`, `cloud-honesty`, `gate-outcome`, `gate-risk-rows`, `hud-exclusive-bind`, `hud-origin-module`, `initiative-payload`, `limits-read`, `presets`, `retrieve-count` and `show-card-timer`. The list is alphabetically sorted, every entry carries a one-line reason, the count is printed, and an entry that becomes stale (its patch since covered) fails - so it can only shrink. An orphan `.patch` file in neither `$PATCHES` nor `DELTA_TABLE` also fails, and the suite stops rather than reporting a pass on a machine without git. DEF-035 stays open: the deploy's loose single-line fallback still judges the exempted patches, and closing that needs a live read to choose their probes.

- **2026-11-09 — Wave 12: fix the dead skill checks before any feature work, a reversible manual click needs no card but the model's never loses one, the Notion numbers are raised on both apps, and memory may learn without a card per fact:** This wave was shaped by the owner's own words and three Gemini rulings. **(1) Fix first.** Answering the owner's Hermes-skills question found the skill hub's four extra checks built, tested and called by NOTHING; the owner chose "fix it first tonight" on a clickable card, so `jarvis_skills.vet()` now calls `extra_findings()` and the same one scan judges every door, and Gemini Q3 extended the same reasoning to the dormant `skills.lock` writer, which install now writes and uninstall forgets. **(2) The owner's manual-click rule.** The owner said *"if i manually click and change the preset for jarvis, it shouldnt need a card"* and then *"if i manually choose anything in the jarvis app or deskstop program, and its something that i can easily click and change back right away, it shouldnt need a card."* Gemini Q2's fence is what was built: explicit backend allow-lists plus a trusted UI-origin signal, never a blanket route bypass and never a header, body or query field a model can set; the model/chat/voice path keeps every card it had, `[autonomy.tiers]` is unchanged, and deletions, installs/downloads, Lockdown off, app lock, credentials and external writes always ask. A local preset clicked in either app's own preset control applies at once, writes a `preset_apply` receipt naming the preset it replaced, and is one click back from the same menu (Undo on the receipt); Coding keeps its card because its pooled lane unloads both other models for about half a minute, Cloud keeps its card because it chooses where the owner's words go, and a preset asked for in chat or by voice keeps its card because the model asked, not the owner. **(3) The Notion numbers, both owner decisions.** The PC's unpacked ceiling is raised to 4 GB (with the counted cap moved with it, every other guard kept, and every refusal now naming the real numbers plus a free-space preflight) because the owner's 276 MB export was refused at the old 250 MB figure, and the phone's RAW zip cap goes from 250 MiB to 4 GiB with the staging ceiling raised so a full export can be staged - the two numbers still answer different questions. **(4) Memory: learn without clicking, but never silently about the sensitive things.** The owner does not want to approve every memory card; the approved path is the existing reworded-facts switch, turned ON after the next deploy, while the waiting cards stay for sensitive topics, contradictions, facts forgotten before, non-owner words and deletes, and ONE fault banner with a "retry now" button replaces a queue of failure cards; the research's privacy finding - `memory.db` is not encrypted at rest while chat history and backups are - is recorded as an open defect with its own queued fix, not hidden. **(5) Reversal.** The earlier claim that the Alt+Space bar gets no second file door is replaced: the owner asked for the bar too, and its chat command now carries the same attachment argument as the windows. **(6) What the wave-11 deploy field test added.** The one-card-and-download boundary held on the live 0.2.441 install, and the field test's own findings were folded in where they were cheap: the one-preset "better for the Coding preset" sentence now reaches the preset advice before the preset-model ask (a real product failure of the acceptance), and the third-card guard now strips Ollama's ":latest" tag, because the exact-name compare had let the everyday lane warm a second copy of the 30B (the owner's photographed 74%-on-card duplicate, reproduced live). - **2026-11-09 — Wave 13: the Reminders transcript is fixed at the root, GitHub gains ONE carded repository creation and a deterministic truth about what reaches the internet, Creator Mode stages skills but refuses plug-ins, and the pooled-window defect is designed rather than claimed:** the owner's own transcript - *"remind me to call Grandma in 4 days from now"* coming out as 13:00 today, titled with the whole sentence, followed by "I've updated it" over a footer admitting nothing ran - was the first item in Gemini's order for this wave, and it was fixed at the cause rather than the sentence: a day and a week are lengths of time again (not clock times), the three ways of saying "in N days" are one phrase, a relative length without a time of day is a reminder rather than a timer, "next <weekday>" means the same day "on <weekday>" already meant, the title is the action on both roads into a reminder, and a failed change can no longer claim it was done (the answering round holds its words, a done claim is dropped and the tool's own error is said). The same pass makes a reminder's phone-notification flag explicit in its own view and its fired event, so a client can no longer infer it wrongly. **GitHub** then got two things the owner asked and the code did not have: a deterministic, read-only truth about internet reach (four separate answers for web search, reading one page, browser control and GitHub, each saying ON/OFF and quoting the OFF row's own reason, carried into the model's self-portrait digest) and ONE genuinely new capability - creating a repository - behind ONE approval card and nothing else: fixed to the token's own account (never an organisation), a field-by-field body with its own name/description limits, no retry, no push, no delete, no bulk, the token never printed, and GitHub's own words (scrubbed) when it refuses. **Creator Mode** was built to its ruling's scope - "plug-ins and skills" - but deliberately only the skill half is real: a waiting folder, a read-only scan, ONE `modify_own_code` card per item, the pack manager's own scanner and card, a skill that lands TURNED OFF so installing is not enabling, and a plug-in refused in the pack manager's words because a code-trust design does not exist yet. The honest smaller slice was chosen over inventing one. **A broken memory check is one banner, not 200 cards:** the fault is recorded once, `GET /api/memory/fault` answers it, a card-free "Retry now" retries it (it changes no stored fact, which is why it needs no card), a proposal that failed stays unsaved so fail-closed is unchanged, the desktop draws it with a Rust retry command and the phone carries the same fault from `net/MemoryFault.kt` (JARVIS-API section 213) - replacing the queue of up to 200 failure cards the owner asked to be rid of. **The pooled-lane consequence of the wave-11 field test is fixed in code and is still not claimed on the live PC:** the measured 49,152-token window was asked for in a field Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores, so a chat-triggered reload landed at 8,192; the fix is the native preload the Q8 warm and Q6 harness already proved on this PC - before a cold pooled turn the chat path asks the lane natively for `num_ctx` 49,152, proves the loaded window from `/api/ps`, and says one plain line if the warm fails while the turn still dispatches (`pooled_preload()` in `jarvis_agent.py`, `backend/test_pooled_preload.py` 26 checks) - recorded with its measured evidence in the design page, while the acceptance row that must assert `/api/ps` context_length 49,152 **after a cold turn** remains NOT RUN until it is driven on the live PC. **A patched-base fix needs a patch, or it never reaches the owner's PC:** the wave-12 skill-scan caller was written into the published base and into no `.patch`, and `jarvis_skills.py` is one of the five files the deploy never copies - so a correct deploy would have left the live `vet()` judging with `_RULES` alone while the four checks sat in a shipped module nothing called. The delivery chosen is one new last-writer patch (`backend/skill-scan-wiring.patch`: five hunks whose added lines are the base's own bytes and whose context is the live file's) carried by `reconcile_live_backend.py`'s `DELTA_TABLE` and ordered immediately before `plugin-loader.patch`; it is proved against a copy of the owner's live folder (42,416 B -> 50,414 B, the caller and `skills.lock` present, a Hermes-inline skill refused, 28 of 28 functional checks) and pinned by `backend/test_skill_scan_wiring.py`. The post-deploy check that must flip PASS is the live file containing the caller; nothing here claims that check has been run. **Records:** the field-test register now carries the 0.2.441 acceptance honestly (24 rows: 23 PASS / 1 FAIL / 0 BLOCKED, the FAIL fixed in Wave 12 and pending re-test, F2 fixed in code with its live cold-turn row still NOT RUN, F3's duplicate measured and fixed, Q6/Q8 measurements recorded as PASS), the two stale GitHub claim rows are corrected to seven tools and four actions, and the drop-in catalogue's missing Wi-Fi reconnect entry plus its `stack_order` tie are fixed (58 ready modules, every order unique). Wave 13 remains one consolidated pull request after Wave 12, in the order Reminders, GitHub truth, Creator Mode, with the field-test sweep driving its rows only after the wave-13 deploy. **Two presentation fixes, from the owner's own reports on the 0.2.441 install:** the personality list's chosen row is now marked exactly the way the chosen focus preset is marked - the shared `.hud-presets-item.is-chosen` rectangle plus the state in the accessible name only - because the owner asked for a highlight instead of the words "(current)" beside the chosen personality; and the top model chip now repaints from the PC's own preset answer inside the 30-second safety poll, because a preset changed outside the HUD window left a stale model in the chip while the Current Models panel was already right. Both are presentation only: no card, no route, no permission and no gate changed. **F6 was moved into this same wave by the owner's own choice:** the COMPUTE panel's per-lane graphics-card naming ("Loaded now / Resources") had been a named wave-12 follow-up; the owner asked for it in this pull request rather than a later one, so the same wave now walks the model runner's parent chain to the lane's own listening Ollama server (read-only, bounded, no process started) and each loaded lane keeps its own card names while the honest "not reported" fallback stays for a chain the OS will not report. - **2026-11-10 — Jarvis writes the fix itself, one file per card, inside the isolated copy only:** Wave 16B builds the item the 2026-11-10 GitHub record deferred in its own words - the scratch-scoped code-authoring tool that lets fix-and-push write its own fix. The shape is deliberately the smallest one that closes the gap: **no new tool and no new switch** (the surface stays the ten switched-off GitHub tools, and the one switch that already governs the fix flow governs this), and `github_fix_and_push` gains `stage="read"` and `stage="write"` beside `prepare` and `push`. `read` raises **no approval card**, because it opens one file inside the copy, sends nothing to GitHub, uses no token and changes nothing on this PC - the same rule every local read follows - and it is reachable only through the same path resolver the write uses, so it is not a way to read arbitrary disk. `write` is its own action, **`github_fix_write`**, `"ask"` in both shipped `[autonomy.tiers]` files and in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`, so a loosened tier still raises its card; it changes **ONE file** inside the prepared copy and makes **ONE local commit** there, and its card shows the pull request, the folder, the file's path, the exact change as a **real unified diff** and the commit message, and says plainly that no token is used and nothing is sent. The confinement is the module's own, never a prompt's: the folder must resolve under `JARVIS_GITHUB_SCRATCH_ROOT` and carry the prepare stage's `.git` note naming the **same repository and pull request**, so the owner's live checkout and another pull request's copy are unreachable; the path is relative, and `..`, an absolute path, a drive letter, a UNC address, a NUL, a symlink and a Windows junction are refused; `.git` and every file on the **push stage's own credential denylist** are refused; a delete/rename/move/chmod argument is refused rather than ignored; only plain UTF-8 text is changed, and a binary or over-1-MB file is refused; a change too big to show in full on one card (the gate caps a card at 4,000 characters) is refused before a card exists, never shown cut; and `run()` re-reads the file immediately before writing and refuses if it changed since the card was shown - the same TOCTOU pin the merge has. The commit identity travels in git's own `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` environment variables (never argv, never a file), and a failed commit puts the file back and unstages it so the copy is never left dirty. **No ban was loosened:** `NEVER` lost only `edit_file` and `write_file`, which are no longer true because one file inside the copy can now be written, while `NEVER_WORDS` and every other ban (force-push, squash/rebase merge, admin bypass, auto-merge, bypassing a required check, pushing to main, deleting or closing anything, approving a pull request, workflow dispatch, gists) are untouched, and the push still happens only on its own card, still showing the real commits, files and command. Proved by the new hermetic `backend/test_github_authoring.py` (96 checks, real temporary git, no network and no token) and the extended `test_github_tools.py` / `test_github_parity.py`; `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §190.13 is the record of the envelope and §190.4 is corrected where it said no tool could edit or commit code. Not deployed; the phone keeps reads and card decisions only.

- **2026-11-10 — GitHub parity behind one card per action: merge-commit-only
  merge and isolated fix-and-push:** Asked to choose the shape of GitHub in
  Jarvis, the owner picked **"Everything at once"** on a clickable card (Gemini
  ruling Q1, 10:40 PT): a read-only PR cockpit, a card-gated merge, and a
  card-gated fix-and-push. This reverses the 2026-11-03 "Read + actions" and
  2026-11-09 one-create boundary **only behind one approval card per mutating
  action** - there is no standing grant, no bulk path and nothing auto-approved:
  each merge and each PR-branch push raises its own one-shot card, and a
  loosened tier line still cannot run one with nobody asked because both tools
  are in `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`. The merge is **merge-commit only** and
  carries a **TOCTOU pin**: the card names the pull request's exact 40-hex head
  commit, and immediately before the one `PUT` Jarvis re-reads the pull request
  and refuses - sending nothing - if the commit moved, the pull request is a
  draft or not mergeable, a check is still running, or a required check did not
  conclude success; the request body is exactly `{"merge_method": "merge",
  "sha": <pinned sha>}` and no code path can make it anything else.
  Fix-and-push is **isolated-worktree only**: it copies the pull request into
  its own folder under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Jarvis\github-fix` (never the live
  checkout), and the push stage re-reads the live pull request and refuses any
  folder outside that root, a protected branch (`main`, `master`, `release/*`,
  `hotfix/*`), a branch that is not the pull request's own, a dirty tree, a fork,
  any force/delete/mirror flag, and any changed file on the **pre-push
  credential denylist** (the same names, key stems and extensions
  `jarvis_project_read` refuses). The token is never in a git URL, never on a
  command line and never written to disk - the push carries it in git's own
  environment config. **Everything ships off by default**: both new actions are
  `"ask"` in both shipped `[autonomy.tiers]` files, each tool has its own switch
  under Settings, What asks first (off until turned on), and the absolute bans
  that remain are unchanged and total: **force-push, squash-merge, rebase-merge,
  admin bypass, auto-merge, bypassing required checks, pushing directly to
  main/master/release/*, and deleting or closing repositories or branches** -
  `jarvis_github.NEVER_WORDS` is now exactly the sentence that says so. The
  2026-11-10 11:42 PT rulings then fixed the boundary around it (Q1's
  eleven-item polish, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6): a formal pull-request **APPROVE** review
  is permanently banned, because it would satisfy branch-protection
  required-reviewer rules and hand the owner's sign-off to the assistant;
  `workflow_dispatch` and gists are permanently banned too (arbitrary remote
  input execution, and a public-by-default exfiltration sink); the merge stays a
  classic synchronous pinned merge under `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28` with
  no `merge-async` and no merge queue - a branch that requires the queue is
  refused with the sentence that says to queue it on GitHub; and the connect
  surface and `CAPABILITY_DETAILS` carry the fine-grained Personal Access Token
  matrix - Metadata read-only (it also enables reading branch rulesets), Pull
  requests/Issues/Actions/Contents read and write, with **Contents: write** named
  as the one GitHub permission that covers both a merge and a branch push, and
  Workflows (write), Administration, Secrets, Environments and Pages explicitly
  left off. The scratch-scoped code-authoring tool that would let fix-and-push
  write its own fix is deliberately deferred to wave 16B; this wave ships the
  isolated-worktree prepare and the carded push only. The record of the build is
  `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §190.9 and §190.10,
  `backend/jarvis_github.py`, `backend/github-tools.patch` and
  `backend/test_github_tools.py`.

- **2026-11-10 — GitHub full parity, Step 2, card-free reads, and a carded issue close/reopen (owner, 22:30 and 23:00 PT):** the owner's 22:30 ruling "full parity with DeepSeek" added nine GitHub actions above the merge and fix-and-push: a full pull-request read (`github_pr_detail`), opening a pull request for a new branch Jarvis prepares (`github_open_pr`: prepare in the isolated scratch copy, then ONE card showing every commit, changed file, the exact push command and the whole title/body, then push that one new branch and POST the pull request), cancelling or re-running only the failed jobs of ONE workflow run (`github_workflow` - dispatch stays banned), adding/removing labels in ONE request (`github_issue_labels`), editing a pull request's title/body with the exact before/after (`github_edit_pr`), and posting a review that is a COMMENT or a REQUEST_CHANGES but never an APPROVE (`github_pr_review`). At 23:00 the same day the owner answered two questions that changed standing rules: **(A) GitHub reads are card-free** - a read is a GET on api.github.com and changes nothing, so `github_inspect` ships "auto" and the five read tools leave `jarvis_agent.NEEDS_A_PERSON`, while every write keeps its own one-shot "ask" card; **(B) closing ONE issue is allowed, carded** - the old absolute ban on `close_issue` was overturned for a new separate action `github_issue_state` (one issue per card, title shown and pinned, optional reason shown on the card, never a pull request, never bulk, never a delete/transfer/edit, reversible by the same tool), so `close_issue` left `jarvis_github.NEVER` and `bulk_close` joined it - `github_open_issue` still cannot close what it opened, and the removal of a NEVER name is recorded here because that is the one direction that needs a decision on the record. JARVIS-API.md section 216 is the envelope; `backend/test_github_tools.py` and `backend/test_github_parity.py` pin every action, refusal and shipped tier.

- **2026-11-10 — Two read-only pre-push gates, cardless by construction:** the owner's "full parity with DeepSeek on GitHub" order named two abilities Jarvis had only as a person's habit: a review packet before a push and a repository record check. Both are now product surfaces - the model tools `review_changes` and `check_records`, and the deterministic chat sentences "review my branch" and "check the records before I push" - and they are deliberately NOT carded, because a card asks permission for a change and these make none. The decision, in four parts. First, they are LOCAL: they read one git checkout on this PC through fixed read-only git commands and this repository's own twelve checkers, never fetch, open no socket, and never touch the GitHub token, so `JARVIS_REVIEW_REPO` (or the tool's own `path`) is what names the folder, and a stale `origin/main` is reported as stale rather than updated. Second, they are decided under `file_read`'s existing action, `read_files_readonly` at tier "auto" - the same line `project_read` sits on - so no gate action and no approval card were added, and both names sit in `jarvis_asks_first.TOOLS_SWITCHABLE` with neither in the shipped `[tools].enabled`, which is what "off by default, one switch each" means here; the chat sentence names the switch when it is off instead of running anyway. Third, they are NOT rows of `jarvis_github.CAPABILITIES`: every row there is an action that sends the token and therefore asks, and these send nothing - so they are their own pair (`jarvis_agent.LOCAL_REVIEW_TOOLS`) in the same `github` tool group, and the one inventory stays truthful. Fourth, the record check reads the strict rule the owner's order names - ONE `changelog.d/` fragment, ONE decision record, no `CHANGELOG.md` or `docs/DECISIONS.md` rewrite, the docs count when a document was added, every changed `backend/<file>` carried to `jarvis-backend/<file>`, well-shaped claims and defect rows - and a checker that cannot run is NOT-RUN, TIMEOUT or FAIL, never a pass, which is the same rule every field test in this project follows.
