Two defects recorded the same day in the wave-14 follow-up register are fixed here with pins: DEF-063 (the Presets note and the click's announce named only Coding as the carded heavy preset; Medical pauses both other models too) and DEF-064 (the HUD's memory-door line said "decide each card there" while the same plate draws the ONE Keep and posts it from here). Stated limits: the pill and header are proved by headless Chromium and source pins, not by pixels on the installed WebView2 at 1900×1000, and `face-models-rail.mjs` plus `hud-live-read-aloud.mjs` each carried one failure on the pre-change page, unchanged by this work. The branch was rebased onto the merge of PR #1219 (`4a4864712`) with the three duplicate wave-14 HUD commits dropped (two match main's own commits by `git patch-id`, the third is main's `104273ba2` by subject), and the self-code map was regenerated last. **Carried into the code from the same live measurement:** the one line Q3 added to the running install's `jarvis_big_coder._child_env` (`env["LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM"] = "3072"`) is now byte-for-byte in `backend/jarvis_big_coder.py` and its `jarvis-backend/` twin, so a later deploy starts the pooled third lane with the same 3 GB host-RAM prompt cache instead of dropping the cap; the two other lanes' caps live in the PC's own `start-lane.ps1`, which this repository does not carry.

- **2026-11-10 — The phone may approve a tool switch; it is a RISKY card, never a PC-only one:** the owner met the card "Jarvis wants to offer a tool to the AI model" on his phone with only Deny and the sentence "Approve this one on the PC - it needs Windows Hello there", and ruled that the phone may approve tool switches too (screenshot 2026-11-10 22:42 PT). `enable_reading_tool` therefore leaves `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS` and joins the gate's RISKY rows instead - the switch can be turned back off at once, but while it was on the model may already have used that ability, and that use cannot be taken back. The person check the design intends is kept in both places: on the PC the card still asks Windows Hello, and on the phone it needs that phone's own signed approval (a fingerprint or PIN over the one-use challenge), with a phone that has no approval key refused with the existing `no_approval_key` sentence so it can offer to turn signing on. A denial still works from anywhere, and every USE of an offered tool keeps its own "Ask me first" card. The card's words also change: they no longer name calendar/email/notes (it covers every tool the AI can be offered), and the notice NAMES the one tool the card offers - read from the card's own `detail.setting`, validated as a plain tool id and mapped through this project's own labels, so a malformed row falls back to the generic title and no payload text can reach a lock screen. Turning a tool off is still instant and cardless from either app.

- **2026-11-10 — The phone's top strip is split, and History gets a row in More:** the owner asked for the five Home top-strip cards (Waiting for your yes, Emergency stop, Right now, Attention budget and What Jarvis is doing) to stop taking the top of Home, and for past conversations to be easy to reach from the phone. The strip is split by what it is, not by an edit: the two **safety** cards - the approvals queue and the emergency stop - stay on the Home screen, drawn as one compact row from `HudLayout.homeStrip`, because a safety control is never hidden behind a menu; the three **informational** cards open from the app's **More** menu, drawn by `HomeMoreMain` from `HudLayout.moreStrip`. Both halves read the same saved layout document through `HudLayout.visible`, so the `top_strip` id, the owner's arrangement, the presets, the editor and the hide rules are unchanged, and `normalize` still forces a safety card present. More also gains a plain History row opening the existing History screen through the same `onEarlierChats` the status line's link uses; the status line's one-tap link stays, and the History screen's own fingerprint/Show gate is deliberately untouched. This supersedes the 2026-10-30 choice to keep the More menu to the chat's controls alone (which had removed the Earlier chats row): the owner's newer ask puts one informational section and one door back under their own headings.

- **2026-11-11 — The GitHub union ships 0.2.448 as one PR, with checks required per repository, a five-run CI read that refuses a real cut answer, six card-free reads, and the two review gates ON by default in the twenty-name master switch:** the owner's Q-C/Q-G/Q3-Q4/Q-D/Q7 rulings, folded over the 2026-11-10 22:30/23:00 work (16B authoring, 16E review gates, the parity pass, the switch door and the phone card approval) as one tree for the two-repo field test. `github_merge_pr` and `github_pr_scan` now judge checks per repository through one `_check_plan` - the owner's own seven as an unbypassable floor, another repository's own branch-rule contexts, else every check on the carded commit finishing success/neutral/skipped - and a 401/403 rules read refuses with the ruled sentence plus " Nothing was merged."; the cockpit therefore reads a green pull request in the field-test repository as merge-ready instead of "blocked - rust has not reported". `github_ci_status` asks for the newest five runs (`CI_PER_PAGE=5`; `PER_PAGE` stays 20), and a genuinely oversized answer is marked as cut AT THE READ LAYER and refused in plain words instead of being half-shown. All six GitHub reads are out of `NEEDS_A_PERSON` (`github_search` card-free under its own two "auto" actions; `web_research`/`research_authenticated` stay "ask"); `review_changes` and `check_records` are "auto", in both byte-identical shipped `[tools].enabled` lists, in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`, and in the master switch, whose twenty names are the eighteen GitHub tools plus both review gates. HONEST LIMITS, stated rather than hidden: the generic per-repository rule reads page one of the check-run / workflow-run lists only (per_page=100 and the ruled per_page=5 fallback are not paginated, so "every run" means every run on page 1); the 401/403 refusal keeps the ruled sentence verbatim with the module's standard " Nothing was merged." appended; and an existing PC's settings file is never overwritten, so the two review gates reach it as "New - currently off" and through the master switch's one card. The record was corrected to the code in the same pass: CLAIMS C95/C114/C162 and new C164/C165/C166, ARCHITECTURE section 8, backend/README, JARVIS-API sections 190, 43 and a new 218, and `features/features.json` no longer says both that Jarvis never closes an issue and that closing ONE is allowed.

- **2026-11-12 — Code obfuscation is a tool CHECK, and the run is deliberately not built:** PR #1228 asked for a multi-language obfuscation and hardening engine behind one Ask-First card. What it actually shipped was a stack scanner, a plan builder, an executor with no production caller, and six "toolchains" that copied the source files and reported success without running anything; the one JavaScript branch was never called, the "verification" only counted files, and the chat reply told the owner an approval card was waiting when no card had been raised. The salvage keeps only what was true and useful: a read-only check that reports which of the seven known code-protection programs (`javascript-obfuscator`, `terser`, `pyarmor`, `python-minifier`, `r8`, `strip`, `garble`) are installed on this PC, each one's own version line, and the install command when it is missing; and one fixed sentence that says this build cannot obfuscate or harden code, so nothing is run, no card is raised and no file is changed. Every register the fake action had reached is removed with it - the `project_obfuscate` line in both shipped `[autonomy.tiers]` tables, `MUST_ASK`, `HARD_LIMITS`, the asks-first groups, the card-word tables and the four generated contract fixtures - because an action that can never be raised must not appear on "What asks first" or in a card. Two parts of the old design are worth keeping if the run is ever built, and this record is where they are written down rather than lost: source files are never obfuscated in place (the output is an isolated folder), and the owner sees the exact tool, flags and destination on ONE card before anything runs. When that is built it must come back through the real gates - a `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` entry, a `jarvis_gate._TOOL_ACTIONS` mapping and a `_RISK` row, ONE `ask` card through `jarvis_gate.check()`, and a verification that the tool really produced the output rather than counting copied files - not through a plan builder with no caller. Until then the languages are covered by the CHECK only: JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Android, Rust and Go are named as checkable, and none of them is obfuscated by this build. The version probe is given `jarvis_child_env.inherited()`, the repository's allowlist, and is not started at all when that allowlist cannot be built; the old probe handed the backend's whole environment, including `HUD_TOKEN`, `JARVIS_TOKEN` and every `*_KEY`, to each third-party binary it found, which is the exact leak `jarvis_child_env.py` exists to stop.

- **2026-11-12 — The desktop companion's visual half is not built, and the product says so:** the Roamies-inspired companion (PR #1229) ships as one shipped module (`backend/jarvis_companion.py`), a saved-preferences file and seven chat answers. No window of the desktop app and no screen of either app draws an avatar, a guidance overlay, a cursor ask bar or a 3D card, and the module neither reads another program's controls nor recognises text in a picture. Decided on the 2026-11-13 review of that pull request: **the claims go, not the honesty.** Every companion answer starts from "the desktop companion's drawing and screen half is not built in this copy of Jarvis"; the four switches ship OFF because a switch reading ON would be a presence the product does not have; and a save that fails is reported as a failure, never as "now on". The module keeps **no safety list of its own**: `denied_app_reason()` asks the one enforced desktop hard denylist (`jarvis_ui_control.DENY_PROCESSES` / `DENY_WINDOW_TITLES`, through `denied_process_refusal()`) and reduces a full path to the program's own file name first, because the eight-name list this pull request first shipped allowed `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe`, `wt.exe`, `1Password.exe`, `bitwarden.exe` and `keepass.exe` and no caller consulted it. The ten-word `RISKY_WORDS` / `is_risky_action()` pair is removed for the same reason: a bypassable list must never be the thing that guards an action, and with no action here the honest answer is no list at all. **The two change intents are not reads:** `companion_toggle` and `companion_set_style` came off `_PRIVATE_DETERMINISTIC_READS` - they write a settings file, so a private chat now refuses them like every other change, the same rule `read_aloud_set` and `wifi_reconnect_set` are listed under - while the five read intents stay on it and on `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`. The preference file lives in Jarvis's own settings folder (`OPENJARVIS_HOME`, else the two config-folder names, else `~/.openjarvis`), not `~/.jarvis/`, so the suite is hermetic. **The AGPL-3.0-derived geometry and wave are removed, not reworded:** `generate_sphere_points()` and `calculate_wave_displacement()` were line-for-line translations of the Roamies showcase's `showcase/roamies/jarvis.js`, which this MIT-licensed project may not carry, so both are deleted on 2026-11-13 along with the point count they computed, and the overview and the avatar answer now say the geometry and the sound-reactive formula are not here. Recorded here as a "designed, not built" item: the real desktop lane (screen reading, text recognition and a drawing overlay, each behind its own switch and its own card, reusing the enforced denylist) is future work, and no part of the product claims it. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 219 is the contract and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records the one-sided absence; `backend/test_companion.py` is the proof.

  and an honest Settings plate. Nothing runs a model on the phone, no offline store

  `jarvis_gate.record_pending`, none of which exist, swallowed every failure and
  reported success; the transfer route returned two hard-coded model records as the

Window titles, the tray, the HUD, the phone's app label, its notifications and the README's prose use Atlas; the repository name `Epic-Jarvis`, the installer and product identity, `jarvis-desktop/` and `jarvis-client/`, every `jarvis_*.py` module, the install and data folders, `JARVIS_*` environment variables, the `X-Jarvis-Client` header and the release asset names stay as they are, so existing installs keep updating without a migration. Historical records (`CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `changelog.d/`, `decisions.d/`) are not rewritten: a record says what was true when it was written. In-chat wording and the spoken wake word still say Jarvis and are a later pass, and the README states that limit.

- **2026-11-13 — Any file type from the phone, up to 2 GiB, with one constant behind every number:** The owner asked to "transfer any file type through the jarvis android app to my computer ... up to a reasonably large size". This replaces exactly two paragraphs of `JARVIS-API.md` §196 and nothing else: the type allowlist (eight documents plus eight photos) and the 50 MiB cap. **Any extension is now stored as a PLAIN FILE** in `<a listed folder>\From my phone\` - a `.zip`, an `.exe`, a `.dat`, a video, a file with no extension - and the safety shape is unchanged: it is never run, opened, parsed, converted, indexed, OCR'd or shown to a model, the ONE `receive_uploaded_document` card (tier `ask`, in `HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`) is still raised before a byte is written, and the file's name, size and folder are still on the card. A known document or photo extension still has its BYTES checked at `finish` (`%PDF-`, its Office zip members, UTF-8 for text, and the 64-byte photo header), because a program renamed `.pdf` must not be stored under a PDF's name; an unfamiliar kind claims nothing and is not inspected. A `.zip` on this purpose is stored and never unpacked; the Notion purpose's zip is a different door and is untouched. The chat picture path (`ChatPicture`/`goesToPicture`) is untouched too, and a photo on the folder door remains a plain copy. **The ceiling is 2 GiB, and it is ONE named constant** - `jarvis_upload.MAX_FILE_BYTES` - read by the card's own limit line, by the too-big refusal sentence (through `_cap_words`) and by the phone's pre-check (`Upload.DOCUMENT_MAX`, which `UploadTest` parses out of that Python line, so a copy cannot drift); the old `MAX_DOC_BYTES` name remains only as `MAX_DOC_BYTES = MAX_FILE_BYTES`. 2 GiB is achievable in this design rather than guessed: it is 2,048 requests of the existing 1 MiB chunk (each about 1.37 MB of base64 + JSON, a third of the server's 4 MiB `MAX_BODY`), the same loop that already carries a 4 GiB Notion export, and `STAGING_MAX` (4 GiB) holds one full 2 GiB file - two in flight at once are refused with `FULL`, which is the existing behaviour and is said in the module. The reader's own `MAX_DOC_BYTES` (50 MiB) is a DIFFERENT number and is unchanged: a landed document bigger than it is findable by name and simply not opened, and the card says so for that case. The phone's picker is `*/*`, its progress chip now also moves during the one unavoidable measuring read (bytes read), and a refusal shows the PC's own sentence verbatim. **What is not claimed:** no 2 GiB transfer was written to disk in a test - the large-file proof raises the constant to 4 KiB and sends a real 4,000-byte file through begin/chunk/finish - and a file whose name starts with a dot, carries a path, or is a Windows reserved name is still refused, because `jarvis_documents.allowed_path` could never read it once landed.

- **2026-11-13 — A fixed line that arrives mid-answer is dropped, not queued:** when the owner's PC is already speaking an answer, a timer announcement ("Your timer is done.") or a Jarvis Live line is now dropped rather than spoken over it. Deferring it was the alternative and was turned down: every one of these lines also appears on screen (the timer's own toast, the Live strip, the refusal's notice), so nothing is lost by dropping the sound; a timer that fired minutes into an answer is about now, not about the moment the answer ends; and deferring would need a queue of things to say - a second speech path, which would then talk over the NEXT answer instead. This is the rule the focus callout already followed (`playFocusCallout`), now shared by `sayAside`. Stop is the stronger, separate rule fixed the same day: it ends the answer's speech and marks the turn so the rest is never queued.

- **2026-11-13 — The awareness audit's fixes ship together, and VoiceStudio gets a typed switch:** the 2026-11-13 awareness audit scored 8 features across 9 surfaces and measured **39 PASS, 22 FAIL, 11 NOT-APPLICABLE and 9 NOT VERIFIED**; the FAILs were almost all one class - a sentence about a list copied by hand next to a list that had moved. So this change deletes the copying rather than correcting it once: the GitHub capability answer reads `jarvis_agent.GITHUB_TOOLS` / `GITHUB_READ_TOOLS` / `GITHUB_ACTION_TOOLS` and `jarvis_asks_first.GITHUB_TOOLS` plus the live `github_inspect` row at answer time, `JARVIS-API.md` §190.2/§190.6 name the group id and are pinned against the shipped `[autonomy.tiers]` file by `backend/test_github_parity.py`, and the phone's History sentence says both doors that exist. **VoiceStudio's switch is added** - "turn on voicestudio" is ONE `change_own_config` card plus Windows Hello, "turn off voicestudio" is instant and cardless, "is voicestudio on" reads the real file, and its Settings card exists - while **the speaking-voice wiring stays the next wave**: `jarvis_speech.py` still does not import the module, so switching it on changes nothing the owner would hear, and every sentence says so. **The design-only features deliberately get no `features/features.json` rows** (the on-device model plate, the code-protection check and the desktop companion's drawing): a row there is drawn in both apps' Features pages, so a row would be exactly the claim each of those three exists to remove; they are answered by their own deterministic, honest sentences instead, named in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 and `JARVIS-API.md` §219-221, and claimed in `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` C167-C169. Two corrections to the audit itself, measured while doing the work: its GAP-6 ("VoiceStudio is missing from the feature list") was already false on the merged tree - the row was there, with a stale "there is no screen yet" sentence, which is what this change corrects - and its `contract/feature-controls.json` GAP-8 note is a hand edit (nothing in the repository generates that file).

- **2026-11-13 — The required `backend` job is sharded instead of one 90-minute sweep:** The job ran `python backend/run_suites.py` once over every `backend/test_*.py` (75,829 tests), and by 2026-11-13 that step had grown to the job's whole 90-minute cap - measured on a passing run (43549014566, job 132306898351), which took 79m20s with 75m54s in the suite step (618 suites reporting 4,550.8 s), and on PR #1241's run 43547214198, CANCELLED at 90m16s with 88m41s in that same step. Raising the cap to 120 (PR #1247, open) buys headroom but not one minute less per run, so this splits the work: `run_suites.py --shard I/N` slices its own sorted suite list by position (`position % N == I - 1`), the shards fan into the one required check named `backend`, and a shard that selects no suite is a FAILURE rather than an empty green. The shard count has ONE definition - the `matrix.shard` list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; the job name and the runner's total both read `strategy.job-total`. It deliberately does NOT change which suites exist, which are skipped by name, the `backend-windows` job, or any other job, and with no `--shard` the runner behaves exactly as it did before (same suites, same order, same exit rule).

- **2026-11-13 — A storage self-fact is answered from the code or refused, never composed by the model:** the owner asked Jarvis "where are the chat backups stored?" and it answered "Chat backups aren't stored anywhere by default on this PC - conversations live only in the app's memory until you close it or clear them. If you want a permanent record, I can help you copy important chats to a file or set up a reminder to do that regularly." Every clause is false, and false in the direction that matters most: it told him his private history was throwaway while `jarvis_chat_log.py` has kept it on this PC, encrypted, unchanged since his own decision of 2026-09-24 (that module's header: *"chat history, including what is said to Jarvis by voice, is kept on the PC by default, encrypted, with a switch to turn it off"*). The architect's ruling (Gemini, 2026-11-13 22:30 PT, section 5.6) is that a self-fact about **storage, history, privacy or settings** must be answered deterministically from the code, or refused - never composed by the model - and this lane is the `chat_history_storage` part of it. Decided: `jarvis_quick.py` gets one narrow, read-only intent that answers where the chats are kept and what is true right now, from `jarvis_chat_log`'s own `settings()` and its own database path, because a fixed sentence would be a lie the moment the switch is off or the file cannot be read. It names the default, the encryption (AES-256-GCM, key in Windows Credential Manager), the file (`chat-history.db` in `.openjarvis` in the user folder - named without the Windows account name, because the same reply reaches the phone and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s kept-off-a-phone table says a folder that names the account stays off it), the voice transcripts (the words are kept as ordinary encrypted turns; the recording is not), the retention window, and the switch exactly as each app draws it. It is `settings()` and not `status()` on purpose, so answering mints no key and writes nothing. Off is said as off, an unreadable settings file as "cannot keep anything right now", an unopenable file as "cannot say what is in it", and a backup TIMETABLE - which the product does not have - as no such thing, rather than smoothed into the default sentence. One documented shape moved: *"where are my chats stored"* used to be `history_purge`'s (`docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 189.8), which answered it with the measured file path and a paragraph about clearing; the storage questions now get the answer that names the switch, and every clearing, size and expiry shape stays with `history_purge`. What this deliberately does NOT do: it does not answer "is my chat history private" or any other question outside this one subject, it is not added to `_PRIVATE_DETERMINISTIC_READS` (a private chat hands read-only intents to the model, and its sibling `self_knowledge` is not there either), and it changes no route, no card and no app.

- **2026-11-13 — The two required backend jobs get 120 minutes now, and the suite is split after this wave:** Gemini's ruling (§5.1), after PR #1240's required `backend` job was killed at 1h30m16s by the 90-minute cap at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:294` while it was still executing the suites - so a required check failed with no defect in the change and the pull request could not merge. `backend-windows` carried the same cap at `:800` and had already measured 58m41s and 59m43s on adjacent pull requests, two thirds of its budget. Both ceilings move to 120 minutes now, because a two-line workflow change unblocks the wave tonight and leaves roughly half an hour over the slowest run that did finish (1h13m56s). The ceiling is a stop-gap, not the answer: splitting `backend` into two parallel jobs so no single job carries the whole suite is the durable fix and lands after wave 18. No test may be dropped, skipped or moved to a non-required job to fit either number.

- **2026-11-13 — A forget-a-time-frame card carries the count, not every chat:**
  Asked what should happen when Jarvis wants to delete a lot at once, the owner
  ruled: "Show the count, allow it." So the CARD carries the count of facts and
  chats with the date range ("3 facts and 125 chats from 2 to 8 November 2026")
  and the facts' own words while they fit, and the checked list the owner ticked
  from - one click away, unchanged - carries every item in full. This overrules
  the older rule that a card had to list every item in full, and the reason is
  measured, not stylistic: `jarvis_gate` keeps a card's detail as
  `json.dumps(detail)[:4000]`, the HUD disables Approve for a detail that long
  that no longer parses, and the owner's own 125-chat card sat at exactly 4,000
  characters of invalid JSON and expired un-approvable (measured 2026-11-13: 25
  chats fitted at 3,918 characters, 30 took 4,448, and 125 took 14,546). The
  approval itself is unchanged - still a person's yes behind the normal gate,
  Windows Hello on the PC and the screen lock on the phone, still the second yes
  and the 10-minute Undo, still no item cap. A card that would STILL be cut is
  refused before it is raised, in one plain sentence, using
  `jarvis_agent._card_would_be_cut`'s own rule imported from its owner; the
  gate's 4,000 cap and the HUD's cut-off rule are deliberately not loosened -
  they stay the last line of defence.

- **2026-11-13 — Git's endpoint takes Basic auth, not Bearer; GitHub's REST API takes either (measured on the owner's PC):** the live field test of `github_open_pr` (prepare clone) and `github_fix_and_push` (push) failed with "authentication issue" while every GitHub READ worked, and the difference was the header form, not the token. Measured on the owner's PC on 2026-11-13 against `https://github.com/darknight11ish/jarvis-coding-field-test.git`: `git ls-remote` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` exited **128** with `remote: invalid credentials` / `fatal: Authentication failed`, and the same command with `Authorization: Basic base64("x-access-token:" + token)` exited **0** and listed the refs. So `backend/jarvis_github.py`'s `_git_auth_env` now builds the Basic form - `x-access-token` as the user name, the token as the password, base64 of the pair - and the comment beside the function keeps that measurement so nobody "simplifies" it back to Bearer because the REST API accepts it. The token itself is unchanged in every other respect: it stays in git's own `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment (`http.extraheader`), out of `argv`, out of the remote URL, out of the folder's config, and out of every log line and card; the prepare clone, the open-PR clone and both pushes keep going through the one function, and `test_github_tools.py` now decodes what git is really handed (plus a bite-proof that the old Bearer value fails it). Replaced: nothing in behaviour or in the permission model - only the header form the git steps hand over. Not done here: the `599 checks (measured 2026-11-10)` figure in the JARVIS-API section beside it was not re-measured, so it stays dated rather than invented.

- **2026-11-13 — The HUD's "can I talk to Jarvis" boolean is refreshed by every landed status read:** `S.online` stays the one value the face and Send read, and `paintHost` now writes it from a landed `/api/status` read; the alternative - pointing every reader at `S.ollama` and leaving `S.online` as a compatibility field - was rejected because the chip and the face are painted only by `reactor.set`, so that shape would leave the face showing "offline"/asleep until the next turn while the model was already back. Two guards keep that from repainting twice: only a real boolean moves it (a landed read that does not mention the model is not a verdict, and a failed read still says nothing), and it repaints only when the value changed, so boot's own read and the beat's read cannot paint the chip twice for one truth. `S.online` now starts null, because a page that has not had a successful read has not been told the model is down: null reads as not-yet-known in the face state, the offline ring, the chip label and the Send gate (Send tries the PC for real instead of writing a "Jarvis is not connected" sample on a guess), while `S.ollama` remains the PC's field as reported, also used by the one status row and the standing lane warning.

- **2026-11-13 — The HUD's read-aloud asks one piece ahead, Pause acts wherever the read is, and no dormant voice pick stays armed:** three defects an independent review found in the desktop speech code, all fixed in the one player the page already had, with no second speech path, player or window message. The stutter came from asking for each 500-character piece only after the previous clip ended, so the HUD now asks for the next piece while the current one plays - the bar's own `prefetchNextClip` rule, one request ahead at most and the queue's order still the read loop's. The dead Pause came from two halves: the answer menu hid the item while the first clip was being made, and `detach()` had already nulled the audio between pieces, so the page's handler refused. Pause/Resume now act on a clip, on the first clip still being made and in the gap between pieces, using a pause gate the read loop waits on where there is no audio to pause; a press that genuinely cannot act says "Nothing is being read." on the item, never nothing. The armed male-voice rule (`english[0] || mine[0]`, which once chose Microsoft David) is deleted along with the English-filtered list it chose from, because nothing calls the browser voice today: rather than trust a page-only test to keep a dormant rule harmless, an utterance with no voice is refused, which keeps the wrapper's local-voices-only promise (an "Online (Natural)" voice is not chosen either). The rule that forbids David, George and Zira stays, and a new test holds it there; hud.mjs's wrapper check was rewritten to the new rule (no voice is chosen for the caller, a local voice the caller names itself still speaks, an online one is still refused) rather than deleted. Proven by `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-read-aloud-flow.mjs` (6 of its 7 checks fail against `origin/main`'s files; the kept guard passes on both), not yet by a live install.

- **2026-11-13 — A 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature." is GitHub saying the repository has NO branch rules, not that the token is blind:** measured on the live 0.2.448 install during the GitHub field test, on `darknight11ish/jarvis-coding-field-test` PR #1 (head `75044fb8bce6993b79bd98d3a54cc4e498de4600`, `ci` green, mergeable clean). The owner approved merge card `92d7445a479a` and `github_merge_pr` answered *"This GitHub token cannot read branch protection rules for this repository, so Jarvis will not merge it. Nothing was merged."* The branch-rules read had returned 403 with GitHub's plan-limit message - branch rules are a paid feature for a private repository - and `_check_plan` treated every 401/403 as an auth refusal. That was wrong in a direction that blocked a merge the owner had already approved. So `backend/jarvis_github.py` now keeps the 403 body and `_plan_limited_rules` matches GitHub's own JSON `message` case-insensitively (`Upgrade to GitHub Pro` or `make this repository public`); `_check_plan` treats that answer as "no rules exist", exactly like a 200 naming no required contexts, and the generic rule decides - PR not a draft, mergeable, at least one check-run on the head sha, and every check-run completed with conclusion success/neutral/skipped. The merge answer names the free-plan reason in plain words so the owner can check the reasoning. A 401, and a 403 with any other message, still refuse with the existing sentence, and nothing else about the merge gate, the cards or the permission model changed. Not done here: the fix has not been re-run against a live install; the same foreign-repo merge is the retest.

- **2026-11-13 — A notification click is answered on both launch paths, and a toast's own sentence must name a control that can be pressed:** the owner reported that clicking the body of an approval toast did nothing, and expected the ordinary Windows behaviour (open the app, and for an approval open that card). Measured on this PC: the toast is in Windows' store with `activationType="foreground" launch="jarvis-open"`, 34 s later Windows logged "Some toast notifications have been cleared", the app's log records no launch at all, and the installed Start Menu shortcuts carry the AUMID but no `ToastActivatorCLSID` - which Microsoft's table for unpackaged Win32 apps is what makes in-process toast activation impossible. Decided, and this is the rule a later edit should not quietly drop: (1) the app answers its toast's launch marker on **both** paths a click can produce - the single-instance callback while Jarvis is running and a cold start - because answering only one is the exact half-fix the Deny button already had to learn, and the two look identical from the owner's chair; (2) a click that names no card goes through `windows::show_hud` and an approval's goes through `commands::open_approval_in_quickbar` with target `hud`, so a notification reuses the app's existing doors instead of adding a window, a tray icon or a second focus path; (3) an approval toast carries **Open** beside **Deny**, on the same action activation Deny rides and with the same marker as its body, because a sentence that says "open Jarvis to approve" must not point only at a gesture Windows will not deliver; (4) the install-time `ToastActivatorCLSID` (a stub CLSID on the shortcut, or a real COM activator plus its registry entry) is deliberately **not** added by this change: it is installer plumbing that cannot be watched firing from here, and a wrong or stale CLSID outliving the app is the failure mode this module already refuses for Deny. What that leaves, said plainly: a body click still cannot be delivered on this build, so Open is the press that works today, and the body marker needs no further change when the activator lands. Deny's action XML is unchanged, and the owner's other toast buttons' readers are untouched.

- **2026-11-13 — The owner-check skip is a limit of the machine, and an accepted skip is printed:** Gemini's ruling (2026-11-13 20:45 PT, §5.2) said `backend/test_owner_check.py` belongs in `tools/check_claims.py`'s `ENVIRONMENT_SKIPS` in its own small standalone pull request, and never smuggled into another one. The suite skips exactly one check on Windows - the one proving "off Windows there is no Windows Hello, so a risky approval fails closed" - because that proof drives the real Windows Hello path, and on Windows the real path raises a real prompt; the skip is a limit of the machine the suite is running on, not a missing guard, and the same check runs in full on a machine that is not Windows. Without the entry the skip withheld proof from claim C163 (the tool-switch approval card), so the register read red at the owner's desk while nothing was wrong with the code; the entry accepts only that one suite's own sentence. The ruling's other half is behaviour now too: a skip the allow-list accepts still buys the row its proof, but never silence - every run names the suite, quotes the skip line and counts the rows that check did not look at, with or without `-v`, because BLOCKED and NOT-TESTABLE are never passes. The same change closes the second desk red the Lead measured, C101, without a skip: the checker used to start suites with the machine's own network settings while `backend/run_suites.py` forces `OFFLINE_ENVS` on every run, so the Live settings parity suite fetched five model files inside one turn and the empty `memory.db` it created tripped its own "the carded change wrote no settings file yet" check; the checker now forces the runner's same six switches, and the suite is 1042 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed with nothing fetched. C101 was never an environment-skip candidate - its suite exits 1 with a failed check, not 0 with a skip - so the fix is the hermetic environment, not an exemption. The same hermetic rule covers the runner's other switch: a suite run now also leaves no bytecode, because `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (`run_suites.py:1452-1453`) was missing from the checker too, and the desk's second register run was red on D06 for the `jarvis-backend/__pycache__` the first run's suites left behind; a check must not dirty the tree it is checking for the next check.

- **2026-11-13 — Editing any `backend/*.patch` rebuilds `backend/patch-history` in the SAME pull request:** `CLAUDE.md` already said to run `python3 tools/build_patch_history.py` before committing a patch change; what this records is the measured consequence of missing it. The GitHub-union pull request edited `backend/github-tools.patch` and `backend/approval-notice.patch` in four commits without rebuilding the history, so the check "every earlier version of every patch in `git log` is in `backend/patch-history`" failed on `main` at `a6f8496fe` and its required `backend` and `backend-windows` jobs went red; every open pull request based on that `main` then showed the same required-check failure and could not merge, even though none of them touched a patch. A patch edit is therefore treated as a two-part change, the patch AND the history it came from, and the history is rebuilt LAST in the same PR (the same order the generated self-code map and recent-changes module already follow). The history file keeps only versions that were real, complete patches: the tool leaves out four commits whose hunk headers do not match their own lines, because no such text could ever have applied to a backend, and this record keeps that honest exclusion rather than padding the list. Nothing in the live install, the settings file or the product's behaviour changes; this is the repository's record and the required CI gate.

- **2026-11-13 — A settings restore never re-points the pairing token:** the phone's settings backup no longer carries the desktop's address (`host` is excluded from the `jarvis_client` file, and the reader drops it from an older or crafted snapshot too). The reason is a credential, not tidiness: the pairing token lives in `jarvis_secure`, which no backup touches, so restoring an address over the stored one would send a token the phone already holds to whatever desktop the backup named. A restored phone therefore pairs again and the address is typed again, exactly as after a reinstall. The same pass caps the PBKDF2 iteration count a backup file may ask for at the 210,000 rounds this app writes - the count sits in the plaintext header, and the key is derived before the first tag can be checked, so a crafted file must not be able to choose a slower key derivation than the app itself - and corrects two sentences that claimed every failure has its own words and that no partial restore exists: authentication is all-or-nothing, but preferences are written one file at a time, so a write that fails partway may already have restored some settings and now says so.

- **2026-11-13 — The phone's microphone press interrupts Jarvis, ON by default:** the owner asked, verbatim: *"when I use the top mic button in the android app and jarvis is still speaking out from a previous response, I want it to interrupt its response and process the new thing I said. also add this to the settings as a changeable Default"*. So a press of the microphone while Jarvis is speaking now silences the reply at once (the stop word's own `VoiceSession.stopSpeaking()`), drops the old turn the way "hey Jarvis" does (`interruptForWake`'s half: the old job is cancelled, and its `Turn.silenced` latch means `SpeechAhead` asks for and plays no further sentence, so a reply still arriving from the PC never starts again on this phone), and starts listening exactly as an ordinary press does. The phone still does no speech-to-text: the new clip goes to the PC's own voice route like every other press. It is a changeable default as asked: ON, with its own switch in Settings -> Voice, "Stop speaking when I press the mic", this phone's alone (the words are in `voice/MicBargeIn.kt`, the value in `data/ClientSettings.kt`, the row in `VoiceSwitchesPlate.kt`, and Settings search finds it by its printed words). OFF restores the behaviour measured before this change: the microphone greyed while the answer streams, and "Still finishing the last one." once the reply has arrived but its sentences are still playing. This is not a new idea - the desktop's own talk button has always done it (`jarvis-desktop/src/main.js` `startPushToTalk`: `noteCutOff(); stopSpeaking();`, with the comment "Barge-in: holding the mic to talk again is as clear a signal as this app gets that whatever Jarvis was saying is done mattering right now"), so the phone was the half that did not have it. It deliberately does not touch the existing "Interrupting Jarvis" choice (that one is about the phone listening by itself while Jarvis talks), the stop word, the wake word, hands-free, or the `MicOwner` arbitration: the press is the ordinary `begin`, which opens the ordinary `Recorder` and asks `MicNow` first.

- **2026-11-13 — The phone gets its own on-device model engine (E1), behind a switch that ships OFF:** the owner's order of 2026-11-13 23:30 PT — *"build the full android local ai model engine into the jarvis app once off peak hits"* — and his two card answers the same night (a **separate Local AI screen**, and model source **Both**: USB/file import first, in-app download second). This slice is the Kotlin and UI half of E1: `com.jarvis.client.localai` gains the JNI contract exactly as the project plan states it (`LlamaNative`, `TokenSink`), a real `LlamaEngine` that loads `libjarvis_llama` **only inside `create()`** and never in an object initialiser, a Kotlin port of PrivateLM's GGUF header reader (magic, version, every scalar value type, arrays kept as shape only, architecture/block/context/embedding/head counts, file type/quant, the calibrated KV-cache and overhead estimates, a largest-context-that-fits search), a port of its RAM tier table plus a refusal that says in plain words when a model is too big for the phone in the owner's hand, the idle unload / 180-second hard cap with an injectable clock (5 seconds in the first build, corrected to five minutes by the field test recorded below), a models folder under `context.getExternalFilesDir("models")` with a SAF import that copies through a `.part` file, checks free space and never overwrites or escapes the folder, and a Compose screen reached from Home's **More** menu whose permanent label reads exactly *"On-device model: runs on this phone, not your PC"*. The screen never downloads anything, never loads a model by itself, shows each reply's measured tokens/s or the words *"not measured"*, and says on the tile exactly what to tap in the file picker. The chat sends the recent turns in the model's own format (ChatML by default, Gemma and Llama 3 detected from the file name), because the JNI contract takes one prompt string and the model has no memory between calls. The desktop deliberately gets nothing: it already has Ollama on this PC, there is no on-device engine there, and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records the one-sided reason; `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 223 records that **no backend route, field or permission is added**, and `tools/check_parity.py` has nothing to classify. **Measured on the owner's phone, 2026-11-13** (field test, CI-signed APK 0.2.4111 from run 43430672162, head `1e809c3a5`): the app itself was driven, not just the library. Qwen2.5-0.5B, 1.5B and 3B Q4_K_M each answered `Hello, who are you?` on the phone, at **27.1, 13.8 and 7.7 tokens per second** as shown on the screen and matched by the engine's own `generated N token(s) in M ms` log line, and the 3B model was accepted by the RAM tier (about 2.9 GB of a 3.2 GB budget) rather than forced. The in-app **Import** (SAF picker) was not exercised - the models were copied with `adb push` - so that row is NOT-TESTED, not a pass. Screenshots are black because the activity sets `FLAG_SECURE` (correctly), so the evidence is uiautomator XML and logcat. **The field test also corrected this record in two places, and the corrected behaviour is what ships:** (1) the idle unload shipped at PrivateLM's **5 seconds** and that is unusable on a phone - measured `model loaded` 06:15:04.976 and `model unloaded` 06:15:20.870, because the timer starts at load and only a request or typing restarts it, so a person reading the screen or moving a hand to the field lost the model before they could type. It is **five minutes** now, the **180-second per-reply hard cap is unchanged**, and leaving the Local AI screen still destroys the model immediately - that is the memory-saving rule that matters. `LocalEnginePolicyTest` pins 299,999/300,000 ms and the 180,000 ms cap. (2) with the keyboard up the chat plate was clipped at the keyboard and **Send left the accessibility tree entirely** - the tester could only send after pressing BACK - so the chat history stays in the scrolling list while the **composer (draft, Send, Clear) is pinned below it**, inside the app's single root `imePadding()`, and the permanent label is pinned above the list; the draft also gained a **Clear** action because it is `rememberSaveable` and had no way to be discarded except killing the app. `LocalAiShipsOffTest` pins the Clear wiring and the close-on-leave effect, and the phone re-drive of the keyboard fix from the CI-signed artifact of this correction is recorded in the pull request body. `features/features.json` is left unchanged in this pull request even though the screen is now measured: the feature row and the catalogue/awareness entries are the follow-up slice, and the one-sided reason stays in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8.

- **2026-11-13 — The phone may back up its own settings, never the pairing token, and a phone update is checksum-pinned as well as signature-pinned:** the owner approved copying Mobile-Harness's encrypted backup and sha256 manifest under MIT (`COPY-OVER-SPEC-2026-11-13.md`, sections A1-A2), and the two adaptations land together in one PR with `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 222 and a one-sided note in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8. **Backup scope is SETTINGS ONLY, and that is the decision rather than an implementation detail.** The file carries the phone's own settings - appearance, menus, voice and display switches, the app-control list and the notification allow-list - and deliberately nothing else: the pairing token stays in the Android Keystore in its own preferences file (so a restored phone pairs again, which is the property that makes the file safe to keep anywhere), and chats, saved memories, pictures, model caches and logs are not settings. The writer only walks an explicit allow-list and the reader refuses a snapshot naming a file it does not back up, so the exclusion is enforced twice and does not depend on the save path being careful. The container keeps the adapted project's versioned header, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and segmented AES-256-GCM with per-segment AAD, but a password is now required (Mobile-Harness also offered an unencrypted file) and a newer format is refused with its own sentence; the whole file authenticates before any preference is written, so "half restored, then the tag failed" cannot happen. A password shorter than 8 characters is refused when saving and accepted when restoring, because an old file's password is whatever it is. **The updater keeps its existing gates and gains one.** The phone already downloaded its own `client-latest` APK and checked the signing certificate pinned in the app (2026-10-11); the decision was NOT to replace that with AppUpdater but to adapt only the manifest half, so a download must now match the `client-latest.json` that CI publishes beside the APK (size and SHA-256) AND the pinned certificate. The manifest is read before the APK on the owner's tap, so a missing checksum downloads nothing and is reported as "could not check" rather than "up to date"; a mismatch is deleted with the reason; nothing downloads without a tap and nothing installs itself, because the install step remains Android's installer prompt. CI's side: the publish step writes the manifest from the file it just hashed, verifies it names that exact file, uploads it with the APK and keeps it when older assets are deleted; its `versionCode` is `1000000000 + GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`, the same number `build.gradle.kts` gives the build, pinned equal by a test so producer and consumer cannot drift. Both features are phone-only because the artefact and the device are: the file is this phone's settings and the updater installs on Android, and the desktop keeps its own separately coded updater and its own PC backup card (the previous sentence in `ARCHITECTURE.md` saying the phone "does not install or update Jarvis" was stale and is corrected in the same note). No route, no card and no new third-party dependency; a wrong password, a tampered or truncated file and a newer format all fail closed with plain words.

- **2026-11-13 — A photo from the phone now lands in "From my phone" unchanged, as a plain file that no model sees on that path:** The owner's report: on his phone he asked Jarvis to "send this file which was a photo to the computer", and Jarvis answered that it had no access to a standard file system and could not receive or send files between devices. That denial was false about documents and, for photos, it was describing a real gap: the Settings row "Send a document" carried only the eight document kinds, and a picture in chat deliberately takes the separate `ChatPicture` path, which runs vision and covers secrets with black boxes before a model sees it. The owner's capability is "put this photo in a folder on my PC", which is neither of those. So the SAME upload route (`/api/upload/begin|chunk|finish`, purpose "document") and the SAME `receive_uploaded_document` card now also accept `.jpg .jpeg .png .webp .heic .heif .gif .bmp`, and a photo is written into `<a listed folder>\From my phone\` byte for byte unchanged. It is a plain file copy: `jarvis_upload.py` performs only a header check on the first 64 bytes, and nothing opens, converts, indexes, OCRs or shows the picture to a model. WHAT MAKES IT SAFE, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE CHAT PICTURE PATH: the chat picture path is an image path on purpose - it decodes the picture, OCRs it and gives it to the vision model, with secrets black-boxed first - while this path is the same pipe a document takes, so the two must not merge in either direction. `jarvis_attached_file.KINDS` is NOT widened (a photo is still refused as a chat document, `WHY_PICTURE`), and a landed photo stays unreadable to the documents feature: `jarvis_documents.read` accepts only TEXT_KINDS/DOC_KINDS, the index's default kind set is TEXT_KINDS, and the word scan opens TEXT_KINDS only - pinned by `backend/test_upload.t_a_photo_lands_as_a_plain_file`, which lands a real PNG and then proves both readers refuse it. WHAT WAS NOT BUILT AND STAYS NOT BUILT: no new route, no new purpose, no preview, no share target, no second picking surface; the phone's chat "Attach a file" row and `goesToPicture`/`ChatPicture` are untouched, and the 2026-11-05 decision that pictures are refused by the upload allowlist is replaced for photos as plain files only. The phone's row now says "Send a document or a photo" so the owner can tell the two doors apart, and the feature list entry `document-from-phone` says what really happens: documents AND photos go into "From my phone", and nothing is sent to the cloud.

- **2026-11-13 — The quiz's Finish records the pass, it never applies:** The owner reported that the setup quiz could never be finished: Next did nothing at the end of the question list and Finish was never painted or wired, so the app kept saying the quiz was unfinished. The last question's Next now reads Finish, and pressing it sends the same cardless `{"keep_current": true}` note "Keep current settings" already sends - so the pass is recorded as complete without writing an answer, changing a setting or raising a card, and the answers still change only through the two-press Apply. Finish is offered only when every question has an answer and the PC has not recorded the pass yet, so an incomplete pass never offers it; and the next press is decided by one pure rule (`nextStep`) that both the page and the tests call, because a second, page-side idea of the next step is what made the dead end.

- **2026-11-13 — A probe set must name every revision a patch ever had, and an older copy of a block is replaced in place, never skipped and never duplicated:** the 2026-11-13 field test proved the rule this project had been applying since 2026-11-05 ("one probe from every `update` block") is still too weak for a patch that grows IN PLACE, and the live install paid for it. `backend/github-tools.patch`'s block was extended four times while its two probes stayed rows of the original ten-tool block; the live `jarvis_gate.py` carried that older block, so both probes matched, the tool reported `already present: 234; to insert: none`, and 82 of the 174 added rows were absent - including `github_open_pr`, `github_fix_write` and the other Step-2 writes, whose cards then could not be approved (`action_for_tool("github_open_pr") == ("unclassified_tool", False)`). Decided: an entry's probes must include a line from EVERY generation of the patch, not one per `update` block, because an extension appends its rows inside a block whose older rows are already on the live file; and when the live file holds an OLDER copy of the block, the correct carrier is an `adapted_hunks` OLD -> NEW pair that REPLACES it in place - skipping it silently and inserting a second copy are both wrong, and a second copy of `_TOOL_ACTIONS.update`/`_RISK.update` rows is exactly the duplicate this decision forbids. `plan_deltas` retains one fallback: if the OLD block appears zero times AND the patch's own pre-image appears exactly once, the file is a PRISTINE pre-image (an install older than the whole patch) and the patch's own hunk is replayed - no guess, because both counts are checked. Anything else (the OLD block missing and the pre-image missing, or a duplicated OLD block) is still REFUSED by name. The measured old block is carried as `tools/hud-deltas/gate-github-tools-old.txt` (96 lines, byte-identical to the live gate, sha256 3de2f78d...) and the current one as `gate-github-tools-new.txt` (173 lines, the patch's own added block), and `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` rebuilds the measured live shape hermetically, proves the old probe pair PRESENT and the fixed entry ABSENT, carries the upgrade byte for byte, proves the second plan is a no-op, and proves the pristine fallback lands exactly the published base. What this deliberately does NOT claim: it does not cover a future extension that adds rows strictly in the MIDDLE without changing any probed row, and it does not implement the whole-file SHA-256 comparison DEF-035 also asks for - DEF-035 stays open. The desk hotfix applied on 2026-11-13 (rows appended to the end of the live gate, 223,701 -> 234,706 bytes) is a separate manual repair, not this change, and this branch writes no live file.

- **2026-11-13 — A "planned" note, a "where" and a self-stated count are only true if the row or the code says so, so the directory and the counts derive them:** three rules came out of the self-knowledge review's places, labels and counts half. First, the Settings directory's planned note may only be emitted for a row whose OWN contract status is `planned` and whose label is Switchable/Adjustable - the class that claims both a Settings control and a typed path; a `known_gaps` row or a multi-field board is evidence about an older state, not permission to stamp "Still being wired" on a row that is no longer planned, and a Command-Only, Always-On, Settings-Only or PC-Only row must never be told its "typed path" is being wired because its own label says there is no such path. Second, a row's `where` must name the place the owner really taps today (including "there is no switch for this yet" when that is the truth), and a place name that has been renamed in both apps ("First-time setup" -> "Personalize Jarvis") is a wrong place, not a stylistic difference. Third, a count of what the program has is read from the registry that owns it at the moment it is said or checked - `jarvis_agent.TOOLS` for the tool list, `tool_targets()` for the switch rows, `features.json`/the catalogue for feature rows - and never typed into prose, a failure message or a test; a count typed into a page has no owner and goes stale silently, which is how the page came to say 49 settings, 61 tools and 181 features. A recorded gap is cleared only after today's code proves it closed, not because a note elsewhere says so. Nothing about approval cards, permissions or routes changed.

- **2026-11-13 — Settings must not deny a feature the same build opens:** the owner-visible rule is that a Settings plate may describe a phone feature as absent only when the build really has no such screen. The "On-device AI model" plate broke it: it said the feature was not available in this build while the same APK opened a working Local AI screen from Home → More → Local AI, and two documents still said the screen was unproven after it had been driven on the OnePlus `f0a5b32b` on 2026-11-13 with Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B answering at 27.1, 13.8 and 7.7 tokens per second on screen (34.5 and 34.3 with the keyboard up). The plate is therefore rewritten in plain words to say the feature exists and lives there, that it runs a model file the owner supplies on this phone and never sends anything anywhere, and that the file must be imported because nothing is downloaded; it gains no switch, because the Local AI screen owns every control. The Settings search row now quotes the new copy, and the two documents are corrected to state the measurement while the in-app **Import** (SAF picker) row stays NOT-TESTED (the test models were `adb push`ed) and a screenshot row stays BLOCKED (`FLAG_SECURE`). Replaced: the 2026-11-13 sentences that said the public feature list would not change "until this screen has been driven on a phone" and that the tokens/s row "stays BLOCKED until the screen itself is driven" - both conditions have now been met. The measurement lives in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 223 and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; this change adds no route, no download and no permission, and does not regenerate `features/features.json`.

- **2026-11-13 — The to-do list owns the words after the list name:** the owner said "add these things to my to-do list. buy Elizabeth a mint mobile plan." and the model answered that there was no to-do list on this PC. The fast path's to-do grammar required the sentence to end at the list name, so a colon or a second sentence after it matched nothing and the turn reached the model. Three things are decided here. First, the item may come AFTER the list name: "add these to my to-do list: milk and eggs" and "add to my to-do list. call the bank" are the to-do list's own add. Second, when it does, the words after the list name ARE the items, stripped of a leading "and"/"also"/"-" and the trailing full stop, and the placeholder before it ("these things") never decides the text. Third, the `coming-up` row's own `where` now names "add milk to my to-do list" and "what's on my to-do list", so a capability answer drawn from that row says the to-do list is included rather than leaving the owner to infer it from "lists". No new intent, no new feature row (the count stays 182), and what `todo_add` does downstream is untouched.

The summary now has three measured forms - model answering, model not answering, model state unknown - and its `online`/`allOnline` values no longer call an unmeasured model "online". The verdict is the value the existing status read already carries, cached on the row as `ServiceStatus.modelOnline`: no second request, no new background poll, and no model generation, and the check stays the on-demand tray menu row it already was. The sentence `JarvisRuntime.decide` puts up after an approval (`"This cannot be undone."`, or a sibling such as "Inbox tidy: 10 minutes to undo.") now goes through one reusable clear: `UNDO_NOTICE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000L`, one `Job`, and a clear that runs only while the notice is still that same sentence (`compareAndSet`), so an older timer can never wipe a newer, different notice; setting the same sentence again restarts its 15 seconds. This deliberately does NOT apply to error and problem notices, including every other `setNotice` caller: those keep the behaviour they had before and stay until the owner dismisses them or something replaces them, because a failure nobody has read must not vanish. No card semantics, routes, permissions or approval gates changed, and no device was driven.

- **2026-11-14 — A second kind of app the model may build: its own screens, from a validated spec, with the model still writing no code:** The owner asked for *"a real app with its own screens, written by Jarvis"* - not the fixed WebView shape the Android builder shipped on 2026-10-30. Decided: keep the model's pen out of the code and widen what it may DESCRIBE instead. A task's copy may carry `app.json`, one JSON object with six keys and at most eight screens of three fixed kinds (text, list, form); a second FIXED Kotlin activity in the same module reads it from `assets/app.json` at run time and draws it with ordinary Android views, so the generated app still declares no permission, cannot reach the internet, the phone's files or Jarvis, and needs no dependency. The model writes DATA, never code: every key is checked against a closed set, every screen id against a closed pattern, every button against the screens that exist, all of it before a byte of the project is written and before any card is raised. A form saves its values to SharedPreferences on the phone and nothing else; a button opens another screen or shows one short line. The task's own files pick the kind - `app.json` present means native, absent means the WebView app - so no flag can drift out of step with what is there, and a request that passes `assets` or a `title` beside a spec is refused, because the spec is the only source of the app's name, colours and words. The decision worth recording is what is deliberately still out: no navigation stack, no data source, no script, no Compose, no permissions, and no way to RUN it from either app - the four routes have no caller, which this branch records as DEF-068 rather than leaving it to a reader to notice. Proof on this PC: `gradlew.bat assembleDebug` through the module's own `plan_build`/`run_build`, BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 23s, 2,479,127-byte APK, sha256 4BA8FD8718067FE117E391F28E121738D2A3DB98675FD91B99C3727319D9159F; a WARM build, no install, and no screen has ever shown the app.

The copy the PC and the phone own is **not** renamed in this pass, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: renaming whole-word Jarvis inside quoted Rust literals moved 765 words across 109 files, compiled clean, and failed **30 of 1,275** tests - every one a mirror reading a shared fixture (`the Python side builds deepseek's target differently`, `refused must say jarvis_not_running's words`). Those fixtures are generated by 53 `tools/gen_*_cases.py` tools from the backend's own words, so the fixture half is free; the half that is not free is that this repository holds the backend only as **patches**, which cannot be renamed in place without being regenerated against a renamed live backend. - **2026-11-14 — Answer budgets are caps, not costs:** the benchmark's one-answer token budget is a ceiling, not a price: Ollama stops at `done_reason: "stop"` when the answer finishes early, so a larger `num_predict` cannot flatter a model or slow a suite that already has its answer - it only stops the harness cutting an answer off before it starts. The old budgets (64 general, 64 tool-calling, 48 vision, 400 coding) were smaller than a thinking model's hidden reasoning alone: measured on this PC, `qwen3.5:9b` asked "How many days are in a leap year? Reply with only the number." produced 266 characters of thinking, `done_reason: "length"` and an empty response, and every model scored 0/6 general, 0/5 tool-calling and 0/1 vision while every scorecard read `answered ''`. The general, tool-calling and vision suites therefore share `ANSWER_TOKENS = 1024`, coding keeps its larger headroom at `CODE_TOKENS = 1200`, and every suite result and stored scorecard carries `answer_tokens` so the terms are visible beside the score. A cut-off answer is still a failed answer and never a skipped one - what changed is that the scorecard now blames the budget, not the model.

- **2026-11-14 — A new gate row goes into the published base and the repair tool, never into a new patch:** the owner's ruling, and it was reached by measurement rather than taste. `jarvis_gate.py`'s three tables (`_RISK`, `_TOOL_ACTIONS`, `_NO_RULE_FROM_DENIAL`) are a shared surface every earlier patch's hunk context lives in, so a row typed into a literal breaks the patch that anchors beside it (`web-search-grant.patch` refused to reverse: `error: patch failed: jarvis_gate.py:1052`), and a row carried by a *new* patch breaks the ordering that six suites and the `audit` job pin - `unknown-risk-approvable.patch` must stay the last writer of the file, `handsfree.patch` must stay immediately before `web-search-grant.patch`, `_stack.py`'s `RATCHET` pins the walk's cost, and `test_patch_original_text` demands a recorded original version for every patch. The `_stack.py` walk went further than a failed assertion: with the row in the new patch's three lines of context it emitted **another** patch's row twice into its reconstructed tree, which is a silently corrupted stand-in. So the row ships in `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py` inside a `<table>.update({...})` block at the end of the file - the region no hunk claims - and reaches a live install that the patcher refuses through `tools/repair_live_backend_gaps.py`, which is what that tool exists for. The guard that would have caught the smear locally (a patch whose context contains a row another patch adds) is the follow-on, deliberately **not** in this pull request so it cannot hold it.

- **2026-11-14 — GitHub stage-1 parity: three reads widened inside the restrictions that already existed, and a measured 481 KB answer that was silently reported as "Changed files (0)" is fixed:** the four approved changes were `github_list` taking a `state` filter (the issue scope was already there), `github_pr_detail` including the bounded unified diff, `github_ci_status` naming the failing checks with one bounded log excerpt, and the stale strings in `backend/jarvis_tool_profiles.py` corrected. The state filter is a CLOSED set of three names (`open`, the default, `closed`, `all`), validated for every scope before an address is built, refused by name when it is not one of them, and refused rather than silently ignored on `repos`/`runs` - a dropped filter would return a list that is not the one asked for. The diff comes from the `patch` GitHub already sends with each changed file, so it needs NO new request and no new endpoint; it is bounded to 20 files and 60,000 characters with one line naming what was left out, and it goes through the one sanitizer like every other fetched string, so a diff full of a PR author's text stays data. The CI answer's jobs read is one fixed GET under the run's own id (`/actions/runs/{id}/jobs`, made only when the newest run failed), and the log excerpt reuses `_job_log` - the 302 is read, never followed, and the signed address is fetched with no Authorization header. **The field-test finding of the same day (23:17 PT) was fixed in the same change, not filed for later:** PR #1261 read with the correct head commit and base branch but "Number of files changed: 0", while `gh pr view 1261 --json files` reported 61 files. Measured with `gh api` on the owner's PC: `pulls/1261/files?per_page=100` is **481,180 bytes** (61 files, every one carrying its `patch`), the read layer stops at `MAX_BYTES` (200,000) and appends `CUT_MARKER`, a cut answer cannot be parsed, and `_read` returned `(None, "")` - no document and no error - so `_run_pr_detail` read it as an empty list and printed the count of that list. The ruling taken from that measurement: a cut answer is an ERROR, never an empty document (`_read_full`); the changed-files page is `MAX_DIFF_FILES` (20; measured 178,021 bytes for this PR, inside the cap) and is retried at 10, 5 and 1 when even that page is cut; the files count always comes from the pull request's own `changed_files` field; and if every page is cut the answer says so in plain words and still shows the rest of the pull request, rather than claiming zero files. Replaced: the old CI sentence that only said "it failed" and pointed at the fix flow (that pointer now appears only when the failing checks could not be read), and two profile claims the code had outgrown - "closing an issue stays permanently banned: ... there is no code path for it" (the owner overturned that at 23:00 on 2026-11-10: `github_issue_state` closes ONE issue on its own card) and "It never reads the failing log itself - GitHub keeps it" (false since 2026-11-10's fix-and-push flow, doubly false now). Not done here, deliberately: no new tool, action, tier, route or permission; the three READS are still card-free by default with the switchable row as the way to put the card back; only the FIRST 20 changed files are ever fetched (a pull request with more files says how many were not read, and there is no pagination beyond that because nothing in the answer can show them); and the failure log is still only ever the end of ONE check's log, never a whole log or one per check.

- **2026-11-14 — Pooling the phone into this PC's model is rejected:** the owner asked whether the phone's chip could add its computing power to the model on this PC, and the answer is no. Four routes were considered — Exo, Petals, llama.cpp's own RPC backend, and the "tightwad" patterns that put a small model beside a big one — and each fails on a measured fact rather than a preference. This PC has **28 GiB** of graphics memory (RTX 2060 12 GB plus 2 x RTX 2080 SUPER 8 GB, measured with `nvidia-smi` on 2026-11-14), and the everyday 8B model already fits on one card, so there is no shortfall for a phone to fill. A phone-sized drafter runs at single-digit tokens per second, slower than the card it would be helping, and a mesh adds a round trip per batch, so the latency would rise rather than fall. None of those projects supports Android as a node at all. The phone's own Local AI screen also has **no network path and no link to this PC** on purpose, so pooling would be the first thing to break that rule. Shapes C (draft-and-finish) and D (memory digest on the phone) are therefore deferred, not built. The only next shape is **B, automatic labelled fallback**, and only if the owner wants offline continuity: it must fire only when Local AI is on and a model is already loaded, and every answer it gives must carry a fixed label so it can never be mistaken for the PC's model.

- **2026-11-14 — Send to my phone: 2 GB, started from a button:** The owner asked for video, mp3, mp4 and other files to move between the Android app and the desktop "and vice versa", then chose a **2 GiB** ceiling (raised from 10 MiB) and a **"Send to my phone"** button on the desktop, both from a two-option card. The PC → phone half keeps its ONE `send_file_to_phone` card (tier `ask`, still in `HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`), and the card still names the exact file, folder, size and cap. What changes is the transport: the bytes move in 1 MiB slices; the id's life is renewed by every slice that is served; the **last** slice no longer consumes it but holds it for a **60-second grace** that every re-serve re-arms, and the phone's own **receipt** (`POST /api/files/ack`, sent after it has verified the whole file's SHA-256) consumes it, or the grace runs out, whichever comes first. A dropped link therefore no longer kills a large transfer, a lost final reply is retried inside the window, and "once" now means one completed transfer. The button calls a new desktop route that raises the same card for a file the owner picked in a native dialog — a real file, never a directory, still carded — while the model tool keeps its "Folders Jarvis may look in" search unchanged, so the model can never name an arbitrary path. No filesystem path ever appears on a phone route or in a phone answer, and the phone checks the whole file's SHA-256 before anything lands in Downloads. The phone → desktop direction already accepted any file up to 2 GiB since 2026-11-13 and is unchanged.

- **2026-11-14 — A widget's look is three closed lists the owner picks, and see-through is alpha only:** The owner asked on 2026-11-14 for widgets to have their own look, choosing it over proving the existing widget on his phone and over a widget-carrying mini app. So a described widget now carries an `accent` (one of eight named colours), a `shade` (`solid`, `half`, `clear`) and a `contrast` (`normal`, `high`): three closed lists, absent meaning today's cyan on near-black, so a widget saved before this date draws as it did to within a shade - the same near-black at full opacity where it was 86% twice over, and the look's own two near-whites where the theme's were - neither visible on a dark desktop, and written down because "exactly the same" is a claim a screenshot could contradict. The model maps a colour word onto a name and is told to leave all three out unless a look was asked for; plain code checks it, and an off-list value is refused rather than defaulted. The preview's own pickers can change the look before Add, and what is saved is what the owner last looked at. The decision worth recording is the LIMIT, and it is the same one as the arrangements for a different reason: a colour and an alpha are runtime values, so they CAN be per widget, where a layout cannot - there is no fifth arrangement and no free hex, no image, no custom font and no grid. See-through means alpha over whatever is behind the card and NOTHING else, because a RemoteViews layout has no backdrop blur and neither has a webview, so the words never say "frosted" or "glass". Text is never given an alpha. Every colour on the three lists is asserted readable at WCAG AA 4.5:1 on both backgrounds in both contrasts, measured in backend/test_widgets.py rather than eyeballed, because a list of colours is only safe to offer if nothing on it can make a widget unreadable. On the PC translucency was NOT real before this change even though the window is transparent and its CSS already used rgba - the window's own shell painted an 86% fill over everything, so a 50% card composited to about 93% near-black and the shade controlled nothing - so board mode now gives that backdrop away and the card is the only see-through part of the window. On the phone no widget in this app has ever drawn with alpha (all 23 colours in widget/ are FF), so that half ships implemented and unit-checked with its first launcher look still owed. Nothing new is approved: same sources, same five buttons, the same App-lock hiding and the same stale-link gate, no new route, and the arrangement rules are untouched.

- **2026-11-15 — A measured number is a claim about the running lane, so the copy is not what gets edited:** Owner ruling Q7 (2026-11-15) settled the shape of the Coding preset's window disagreement. `GET /api/work` publishes the preset's declared 49,152 tokens (`backend/jarvis_presets.py:229`) while `GET http://127.0.0.1:11450/api/ps`, measured after a chat turn on the live 0.2.456 install, reported `context_length` 8,192 with 13.5 GiB resident and no spill. The chat path was read before anything was recorded, and it does NOT drop or shrink the preset's window: it names 49,152 whenever the chat lane is the pooled port (`backend/jarvis_agent.py:15714-15716`, through `jarvis_presets.lane_num_ctx` at `backend/jarvis_presets.py:1299-1311`), and `/v1/chat/completions` ignores that field, which is exactly why the native `pooled_preload()` exists (`jarvis_agent.py:15631-15681`, called immediately before every round at `:16667`). So the ruling is that a number on the screen is a promise about the runner: the disagreement is filed as the defect (DEF-071) with the measurement, the file:line path and the honest limit that which preload state it ended in is not proven, and neither the preset's 49,152 nor the copy is quietly rewritten to 8,192. The same reading was applied to the second record-only row, DEF-072 - an approved `github_merge_pr` card that merged nothing and reported nothing - whose row names what was measured, the three plan checks it suspects (`backend/jarvis_github.py:2395`, `:2396`, `:2402-2403`) and marks the cause as suspected rather than proven. - **2026-11-15 — The About page's claims totals are generated from the register, not typed (owner's ruling Q4):** `docs/ABOUT-JARVIS.md` quotes the totals in `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` in six places, so every claim change broke that page and every pull request that moved a claim hand-edited the same six spots — `b24634c77`, `f75b34e1f` and `9d70ec02b` are three in a row, and the last exists only because `backend/test_claims.py` caught the page stale at 268 rows / 256 built against a register of 269 / 257. The ruling is that the six numbers are generated, in the shape this repository already uses for the two figures in `docs/README.md`: `tools/gen_about_claims.py` reads `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` and rewrites only the digits inside those six statements (idempotent; `--check` writes nothing, exits 1 and prints every number that differs), `backend/test_about_claims.py` proves the page matches the register and that a hand-edited number in any one of the six is caught, and the page's numbers are the generator's to own. **One definition, not two:** the tool imports `backend/test_claims.py`'s `ABOUT_COUNT_SPOTS` — the table the required `backend` job already uses to fail a stale page — and `tools/check_claims.py`'s register reader, so a second copy of the spots or of the counting cannot drift away from the check that judges them. **What it does not do:** it adds no step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, because the check lives in `backend/test_about_claims.py`, which the required `backend` job already runs, and a workflow step would be a second place deciding when the page is checked; it adds no `docs/CLAIMS.tsv` row, so the register's totals (269 rows, 257 built, 7 open, 5 unverifiable) do not move here; and it changes no sentence of the page, only the digits inside the six statements it already had.

- **2026-11-15 — An awareness answer may only claim what the PC can point at:** eleven awareness questions were run through the live backend and each answer was checked against the machine's own evidence (the device roster, `ollama ps`, `nvidia-smi`, `VERSION`, `jarvis_google_calendar.mode()`, `jarvis_accounts.value`). Two answers failed. *(a) "is my phone connected"* named **Pixel 9** as "your phone ... connected right now" when the phone in use is an **OnePlus** and the roster held two phone records with the same last-seen second: choosing one was a guess, and `paired_status()`'s `reach` field - hard-coded True for every row - was never a liveness check, only a capability.
