The rule this records, for every future awareness answer: **the sentence must name the thing it actually measured** - a record, a setting or a process - and never upgrade a record into a live state. Gaps found and left open, recorded so they are not mistaken for passes: "what models are loaded", "which card runs the model", "what are you doing", "what can you not do", "how many spoken interruptions are left", "is ollama running", "what is the phone model", "are you connected to my phone" and "what is my mailbox" have **no fixed answer** and fall through to the model, where nothing measures them.

The phone mirrors that card exactly — its title, its nine possible lines in the desktop's order, and "Close" — because two apps showing the same conversation must not describe it in two wordings; the words live in `jarvis-client`'s `net/ChatInfo.kt`, transliterated from `history-view.js`, and both halves pin them (`ChatInfoTest` here, `tests/chat-info.mjs` there), so a re-word on one side fails a test instead of drifting. First, WHERE the "i" sits: the phone's row is the owner's own DeepSeek-shaped row of 2026-10-27, whose every secondary action already lives in the ⋮ overflow, so the smallest honest addition is one quiet "i" drawn immediately before the ⋮, in the same tone and the same 48dp target, named "About <title>" for TalkBack like the desktop's `aria-label`, and hidden while a "file it under" banner is up for the same reason the menu is; it opens the one flat Dialog History already draws (the Filters sheet's shape) so the screen keeps one popup style, and it closes on Close, on Back and on a tap outside. Nothing was added to the wire: `/api/history` already sends every fact the card shows, and the phone's `ChatLog.Summary` already parsed `device`, `started`, `updated`, `turns`, `has_voice`, `tainted`, `pinned`, `archived` and `tag_id` — the desktop was the half dropping `pinned` — so there is no route, request, permission, approval card or write, only a `ChatInfo.card(row)` call and one dialog. Deliberately not done: no line naming the chat's kind (the row already carries its mark), no per-row info field (the owner asked for the rows to stay clean), and no re-wording of any desktop sentence — if a word should change, it changes in both halves in one breath.

- **2026-11-15 — "About this conversation" is a small "i" and one compact card, not a wider row:** the owner asked whether chat history, in both the desktop and the phone, has an info menu on each conversation that names *"which device (phone or laptop) and more"* *"without this being overwhelming"*, and chose a small "i" that opens one card which closes itself. - **2026-11-15 — The GitHub layer's answers are refusals, not guesses: a shape before a cap, a check before a green, and the model's own text is refused if it can draw as another line:** An adversarial pass over `backend/jarvis_github.py` on 2026-11-15 (the owner's standing "every feature gets its own audit" rule) wrote `backend/test_github_robustness.py` first and fixed what it proved: 94 failing assertions across eleven defects, plus three proven against real GitHub the same day by a live read verification. Four shapes are what the module now keeps. FIRST, a refusal is one plain sentence and it happens before a request exists - a repository named `owner/..` is a path step in the URL rather than a repository, a number of `"0"` is not a GitHub number (it was accepted as a string and refused as an integer, so the same nonsense had two different answers), and `refs/heads/main`, `HEAD`, `main/`, `main.`, `feature/.secret` and `main.lock` are not the branch a card can name, because a runs filter of one matches nothing and reads as "no CI run". SECOND, the SHAPE of an answer is decided before the read cap: a directory listing over 200,000 characters is still a directory (a 320,215-character `docs/` listing used to answer "the answer was longer than Jarvis reads"), and a cut `pulls/{n}/files` list now says what was left out and how many files GitHub says there are instead of "Changed files (0)", which was a false statement about a 481-file pull request. THIRD, "passed" is a claim that needs every check on the head commit: two workflows run on one commit and GitHub lists them in its own order, so the old `workflow_runs[0]` answer said passed on PR #1263 while `audit` and `backend-shard (3/4)` were red - the pull request form now reads the head commit's check runs, names each one that is not a success, and does not use that word otherwise. FOURTH, text the MODEL supplies is refused rather than sanitised when it carries a character that can make one line draw as another: fetched text is cleaned because somebody else's words must survive, but the card is what a person consents to, so silently rewriting it would post something they never saw. FIFTH, a scan row must name what is not green and must never call a commit "running" when a check on it has already failed: the recognition harness's pinned replay of `6b24a964` (2026-11-15) scored PR #1262's row `blocked - backend finished as failure` while `audit` and `backend-shard (3/4)` were red on that very commit, so every check on the commit is now judged by ONE shared `_check_verdict` and the row names each one that is not a success - at most three names and then "and N more". Its stated limit is part of the decision: the WORD a row carries is still aggregate-by-design, GitHub's own merge state plus the repository's required contexts (Q-C), so a red check the ruleset does not require is NAMED beside the verdict rather than turning a mergeable pull request into a blocked one - claiming blocked there would be a stricter statement than the merge gate itself makes. Two deliberate non-changes belong on the record: an absolute-looking file path is still re-rooted inside the repository (`/etc/passwd` asks GitHub for the repository's own `etc/passwd`) rather than refused, and a sha whose only fault is a copy-paste newline is still pinned as the sha. And one limit is stated rather than hidden: `Retry-After` is read only when the transport supplies headers, which the real `_default_fetch_full` now does and which every test fake may do, so no test had to pretend a header existed.

- **2026-11-15 — A GitHub card names the two hosts the saved key reaches, and a fix-flow card refuses a target it cannot prove before it spends anything:** the owner's Q6 ruling on 2026-11-15 was to codify the closed two-host set - `api.github.com` for the REST calls, `github.com` for the git clone, fetch and push - and to make every card state only the hosts it actually uses. This is that, read off the code rather than typed by hand: the write, prepare and push lines are built from one helper so a card cannot name a host the call does not reach. Two refusals move forward, which is the cheaper half of the same idea: a merged or closed pull request is refused before the clone, and a branch that is not a valid ref is refused before a push card is raised, because a card is a promise that the action behind it can still be done. The 900 s git timeout is evidence, not caution - three measured clones took 257-297 s and the old ceiling stopped the flow preparing this very repository. And a check that has not finished is now said as unfinished: a card that reads "no failing checks" while three are still running is the exact sentence this project treats as a lie, whether the code meant it or not.

- **2026-11-15 — One renderer for the CI answer, parameterised by the evidence, so a branch and a pull request cannot drift apart:** The owner's ruling Q2 of 2026-11-15 found `backend/jarvis_github.py` answering ONE question - which checks are red, which are still running - in two functions, `_ci_words` for a branch or repository read and `_pr_ci_words` for a pull request. Both are now ONE `_ci_words(doc, evidence, *, checks_doc=None, who="")`, called by both call sites in `_ci_result`. The parameter is the EVIDENCE, not a second rule: `who` is non-empty exactly when the question is about one commit, and it both selects the commit sentences and names the commit in them; `checks_doc` carries that commit's own check runs; a branch or repository read passes neither and judges the newest run, because `/actions/runs?branch=<branch>` answers runs over TIME, on different commits. `checks_doc=None` together with a non-empty `who` is a commit whose check runs could not be read, NOT a branch read - that distinction is the one thing the first attempt got wrong, and the old-versus-new equivalence harness caught it before anything was pushed. Everything that decides or names a red check was already shared and stays shared: `_scan_checks` decides failed and running, `_ci_failed_lines` names each red check and shows ONE bounded excerpt of the first failing job's log, and a new `_red_lines` prepares that evidence identically for the three failed-commit sentences. NO user-visible sentence changed: the old module from `HEAD` and the new one were driven over 695 sentence pairs - both forms, every status and conclusion, every evidence shape, every check/runs combination - and all 695 came out identical. They did disagree on 30 of those pairs, and both wordings are kept because the evidence really differs: a pull request with no readable check runs judges every run on its commit ("More than one CI run is on the head commit of ... and at least one did not finish successfully"), where a branch read reports only the newest run; and an unreadable runs answer says "GitHub answered without saying anything about CI" to a branch while a pull request says "There is no recent CI run there to report". Those differences are now one documented parameter instead of two code paths that could each be edited alone, which is the owner's whole point: the two answers cannot drift apart. The proof is `backend/test_github_tools.py::t_one_renderer_answers_both_ci_questions` (10 checks, 5 of which fail against the two-renderer code): exactly ONE CI-word renderer exists and `_pr_ci_words` is gone, BOTH call sites really pass through it (a sentinel-answering stand-in is what both questions answer back, with the pull request case deliberately a red check the old pair never shared), identical evidence gives an identical sentence character for character, and the one failing-detail renderer serves both questions. Local proof on this tree: `test_github_tools.py` 1010 passed / 0 failed, `test_github_parity.py` 705 passed / 0 failed, `tools/check_stale_twins.py` all 342 files matching, `test_base_matches_repo.py` 140 passed / 0 failed, plus `test_github_robustness.py` 511, `test_github_self_knowledge.py` 166, `test_tool_profiles.py` 115 and `test_self_code.py` 95 green. One limit is stated rather than hidden and was deliberately NOT fixed, because this ruling was about two renderers disagreeing and it is a wording change no suite pins either way: with no check runs and exactly ONE red run on a commit, the pull request form still says "More than one CI run is on the head commit of ...", which is a false count about how many runs there are.

- **2026-11-15 — The GitHub tools group is a spoken switch, and the model's door to it is the group only:** the master switch for the twenty GitHub and review tools gets a spoken name (`github`, `the github tools`, `all the github tools`) through the generated `_TOOL_TARGETS` table, its own short state answer ("Right now 0 of the 20 are switched on") read live from `jarvis_asks_first.tools_status`, and a `change_setting` fallback so a model-driven turn can raise the same card. - **2026-11-15 — History's Export writes through ONE narrow Rust command, added to the HUD's existing History set, and Copy stays page-side:** the owner asked for "an export and copy button on the sub menu of each individual chat", and the HUD page has no file access of any kind (no filesystem plugin, no Tauri dialog, and its own POSTs are refused by the shell bootstrap), so the only way to write a file the owner asked for - and to know the full path and number a repeated export instead of overwriting - is a command. `hud_history_export` takes ONE bare `*.md` file name and the already-read Markdown text, never a path; it asks the hidden lists first, writes ONE file inside `app.path().download_dir()` (`%USERPROFILE%\Downloads` on a normal install), refuses a name with a separator, a drive, a control character or a Windows device name, and numbers a repeat " (2)", " (3)" rather than overwrite. - **2026-11-15 — A summary line may not contradict the lines it summarises, and a measured audit belongs in the repository:** the app's Measure block said *"Not measured yet: every number above is calculated"* directly under preset rows carrying their own dated measurements, so the same screen said both "nothing here is measured" and "measured 2026-10-18". The fallback now says what is actually true of that check - nothing has been measured *by it* yet, and a dated line above is an older measurement - which holds whether or not such a line exists. The broader rule: a line that speaks for a block must be written so that every line inside the block can be true beside it. - **2026-11-15 — The merge card reads its own pin, and an approved write's failure is code's to say:** Measured on the owner's PC: the `github_merge_pr` card `07b919e83013` for `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis` pull request #1261 was approved at 23:57:46 PT and nothing merged. The model had echoed a `head_sha` from an earlier scan and it was not the pull request's head (`e496e93c3`, unchanged since 22:42); `_run_merge` compared the live head and refused, correctly, but its sentence said "the pull request moved since you looked" - false - and the only account the owner got was the model's own paraphrase, which invented a duplicate-call rule that does not exist. Three decisions follow. (1) The pin may be SUPPLIED or LEFT OUT: when any of `head_sha`, `title` and `base_ref` is missing or unusable, `plan_merge_pr` makes ONE `GET` of the pull request and pins the head, title and base branch GitHub reports, so the card names the real commit and approving it merges. That cannot weaken the pin - the value read BECOMES the pin, and `run()` still re-reads and refuses if it moved after the card. (2) A supplied `head_sha` that is not the pull request's head is refused before the card is raised, because a card that can never merge is worse than no card. (3) An approved GitHub write whose run fails is reported to the owner by CODE, in the module's own words, inside the answer - a no-op explained only by the model is not acceptable. Deliberately NOT done: reading the pull request on EVERY merge card. That would put a GET in front of every approval and force a fake network seam through every existing planner test (the suite's `NoSocket`); the shape taken catches the measured failure - no usable pin, or a pin that disagrees - without that cost, and `_run_merge`'s refusal is now true either way. Nothing is auto-approved, one card is still one action, nothing is retried, and the merge stays pinned to one exact 40-character commit.

- **2026-11-15 — The spoken-interruption mute has one home, in Brain's Attention budget:** The owner approved the audit's finding of 2026-11-15 that one setting should have one home. The mute switch was drawn in the Inbox, while everything it changes - the remaining count, the daily limit's step controls and the "Muted until tomorrow" pill - lives on Brain's Attention budget plate, so the owner read the state in one place and changed it in another. The switch now lives on that plate beside those numbers, and the Inbox keeps only its count line. What it does is unchanged: it mutes until tomorrow (there is no mute-forever), it keeps the words "Until tomorrow. Anything you asked for is never counted.", its TalkBack name stays "Mute spoken interruptions until tomorrow", and it still calls the same `JarvisRuntime.setMuted`, which the quick-settings tile also uses.

- **2026-11-15 — The pooled lane's turn names its window on Ollama's native endpoint, because `/v1` would not carry it:** The live measurement of the Coding preset on 2026-11-15 left two shapes to choose between, and the measurement itself decides. Shape (b) - keep the OpenAI-compatible call and make the runner it reuses already carry the right window - is already implemented in this repository: `pooled_preload()` sends a native `/api/generate` load at 49,152 before every pooled round, and a 49,152 runner really was resident when the measured turn began (`GET /api/ps` before it). The turn still unloaded that runner and re-created it at 8,192, then refused the 9,794-token prompt with HTTP 400. So (b) is not a new shape to try; it is the code that failed, and no test could honestly promise `/v1` reuses a resident runner when the live counter-example exists. Shape (a) is therefore chosen: on the ONE lane a preset gives a window to (the pooled port, `jarvis_presets.is_pooled_lane`), the turn is translated by `native_chat_body()` and sent to Ollama's NATIVE `/api/chat`, which honours `options.num_ctx` when it loads or reuses a runner - the same field `/api/generate` honours, measured at 49,152 tokens and zero spill on this PC. The number is the window the PRESET names (`jarvis_presets.lane_num_ctx`: 49,152 for Coding, 32,768 for Medical), never a number read back from `/api/ps`: `jarvis_power_switch.lane_context()` can only answer "loaded now", "last seen" or the model's own Modelfile default (`backend/jarvis_power_switch.py:378-388`), so after a failed turn it answers the 8,192 that failure created, and it cannot know how a lane was started. Every other lane keeps its `/v1` request byte for byte, a picture turn keeps it too (its OpenAI content parts are not translated), and a lane whose window really is small names that small window rather than the big one. Nothing about this is silent: a prompt bigger than the window it is about to name is said before the request (`WINDOW_OVERFLOW_LINE`), a window nothing can establish is said instead of guessed (`POOLED_WINDOW_UNKNOWN_LINE`, following the `NoKnownContext` precedent), and the native reply's `prompt_eval_count` is carried into `usage.prompt_tokens` so the existing after-the-fact guard still measures what the model really read. `backend/test_chat_window.py` pins all of it with fakes only, no socket, and fails on origin/main.

- **2026-11-15 — A note's own YAML `aliases:` list is the registry, and an alias beats a file-name lookalike:** The owner reported that "my workout log" could not be found after a create, and that the fallback answer said "I'm not sure where your new note is yet". The decision is to resolve a note by what Obsidian itself already reads, in this order: an exact vault path when the owner actually named a path (a slash, or a `.md`/`.txt` ending), then an exact value of the note's own frontmatter `aliases:` list, then an exact title, then a title that contains the words. The alias step is deliberately BEFORE the title step because the owner's vault holds an unrelated root file called `Workout log.md` while the intended note is `Private & Shared/Workout/Workout Log.md`, whose frontmatter says `aliases: [workout log, my workout log]`; a filename that merely looks like the owner's name must not steal it. Two matches are never guessed - the answer asks which note was meant. The registry travels with the note, needs no index, no model and no state from an earlier conversation, and is read fresh each time by `jarvis_notes_edit.find_name()`. The same decision fixes the two create bugs: a create-shaped sentence is never the daily note's (the tail of a create request went into `2026-11-15.md`), and a title that is really a sentence is refused rather than turned into a file name (the measured file was `Workout Log, pin it, and add using todays date that i used the punching bag.md`, 0 bytes). A dated append ("add to my workout log that ...") files under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading, newest last, keeps the one `edit_vault_note` card and the File Guardian copy, and adds bytes by insertion only. Nothing else is in scope: no heading/block/frontmatter patching and no search index - those are later phases. Proved by `backend/test_notes_create_find_append.py` on a temporary vault, and by a read-only resolution against the owner's real vault.

- **2026-11-15 — The phone's API contracts are proven on the JVM, not on an emulator:** The phone's API-contract suites assert the wire - which route, which header, which body, how many requests one tap makes - and they lived in `androidTest` only because `JarvisApi` took `ClientSettings` and `TokenStore`, both of which need an Android `Context`. A test that needs an emulator is a test that runs in the `Jarvis client` workflow, which is path-filtered on `pull_request` (a pull request that touches no phone file does not start it at all) and which is not one of the seven required checks - so the phone's contracts were proven by a job that a merge cannot be gated on. The decision: `JarvisApi` depends on two one-method interfaces, `HostSource` (`baseUrl`, `baseProblem`) and `TokenSource` (`token`), which `ClientSettings` and `TokenStore` implement and which a test can answer from memory; the three suites live in `app/src/test` and run in the required `phone-unit-tests` job. The seam is two functions wide because those two functions are the whole of what the client asks of either, measured by grepping every `settings.` use in the file - it is not a general injection framework. What the move cost, and must be kept: the tests target `127.0.0.1` rather than `server.hostName` (on a plain computer that is the machine's own DNS name, which `PhoneAddress` refuses as off-network), and the real `org.json` is a test dependency, because `isReturnDefaultValues = true` makes android.jar's stub answer null instead of parsing. The device-only half stays on the device: `TokenStoreTest` still proves the Keystore with the real Keystore.

- **2026-11-15 — Copy a phone cannot act on goes behind a tap, and a caveat that cannot be true on this phone is not drawn:** the audit of the Atlas app on the OnePlus (2026-11-15) measured 801 labelled rows and 52,367 characters of words across 16 screens, and named two shapes to fix first. **(a) A command the phone cannot run is not printed in full.** Brain -> Hardware drew 565 characters of PowerShell on every visit; the plate's own next line already says the line is for the PC and that the desktop app's Copy button runs it. The command now sits behind one "Show the command" / "Hide the command" tap with the pointer always visible - the same discipline Help already keeps ("one line visible, the detail behind a tap") - so reading it on the phone stays possible and the wall of text on arrival does not. **(b) A caveat whose condition is false is not drawn at all.** The Android 17 per-assistant volume slider paragraph is now gated on API 37, because the audited phone reports Android 15 (SDK 35) and the paragraph sent the owner looking for a control that is not in its volume panel. The rule this records: a phone surface may describe the desktop, but it must not present desktop-only text as something the owner can act on here, and it must not describe a platform feature the phone it is running on does not have. Not decided here, and left in the audit: the ten presets' repeated five-block prose, the duplicate interruption/voice-check/notification/backup controls, and the two data contradictions (which card runs the model; "calculated" against "Measured").

- **2026-11-15 — The phone's History Delete uses the carded clear route, and an older PC's delete fails closed:** DEF-047 (Class A, `docs/defect-register.tsv`) found that the phone's Delete posted `POST /api/history/delete`, which raises no approval card (`docs/JARVIS-API.md` 184.6, `jarvis_self_portrait.clear_request`), while the phone's own record said the delete was two-phase with one PC card and nothing deleted until the owner answered - so an irreversible action was presented as gated when it was not. The fix points `JarvisRuntime.deleteHistory` at `POST /api/conversations/clear`, the one id body the route takes, and reuses the `ChatLog.Delete.waiting` handling F6 (2026-11-03) had already built: a 202 `waiting: true` says a card is waiting, the row stays, and the list is read again when the card leaves the queue. **The one new rule this decides:** a 404 with no `ok` body from that route means an older PC that does not have the carded route yet, and that is NOT "already gone" - the phone deletes nothing, says so, and never falls back to the uncarded route, because a fallback would delete with no card and reopen the defect. It deliberately does not change the desktop's own History Delete, which still posts the older uncarded route after its own on-screen confirm (recorded as `desktop-todo` in `tools/check_parity.py`, not claimed as done), and it does not carry the "delete the facts this chat taught" ticks through the card: the PC's card says the facts are kept, so the phone tells the owner the ticked facts were NOT forgotten and points at Memory instead of silently forgetting them after an approval the card said would keep them.

- **2026-11-15 — The phone's feature directory is proven by its generator, not by a count:** `jarvis-client/app/src/main/java/com/jarvis/client/net/FeatureDirectory.kt` is generated from `contract/feature-controls.json`, and until now the only thing watching it was `FeatureDirectoryTest.kt`'s cross-check against the contract's `feature_count` and `label_counts`. A count is not the words: `052072133` ("Jarvis knows every paired device") moved the `devices` row's `where` sentence in the contract and re-ran no writer, so the phone kept describing the old Devices row, and the android-builder row still said "there is no way in yet: no chat sentence, model tool or app button starts it" after the `android_app` tool had become the way in. Both merged silently, because the row count never changed. **What was decided:** the artifact is proven by its own writer - `py -3 jarvis-client/tools/gen_feature_directory.py --check` - and that step now runs in the `audit` job beside the desktop's, so a merge that drifts it goes red on that merge rather than a week later. **What this replaces, and what it deliberately is not:** it replaces a count cross-check as the stale-copy guard; the Kotlin test keeps its count check, which is still the right shape for what it asserts. `audit` is informational and holds no merge, so this is a tripwire and not a new required check, and each failure prints the exact one-line command that clears it. The generator is the only writer: the file was regenerated by it and never hand-edited, and `contract/feature-controls.json` was not touched. The same gap existed one file over - the desktop's `tools/gen_feature_directory.py --check` was gated only indirectly, inside `jarvis-desktop/tests/feature-directory.mjs` in the required `frontend` job, and the PC's feature catalogue by `backend/test_feature_guide.py` in the required `backend` job - so all three writers now have a direct step in the one job whose contract is "reads only the repository".

- **2026-11-15 — A note is computed from the phrase it is about, never stamped from a board (DEF-038):** The desktop's "All features and abilities" list carried "Settings control today; typed path still being wired." on every planned row a multi-field board named, and nothing ever asked whether that row's own sentence already worked - so on origin/main `3beaa66b9` the list promised a gap that had closed on 18 rows, where all 18 example sentences resolved. The rule from now on: a note that says a typed path is not wired is COMPUTED from that row's example phrase through the generator's own `_resolves()`, and printed only while the phrase does not resolve - a board may name a row, but it may not make a promise about that row. The checker holds the rule instead of restating it: `tools/check_feature_controls.py` imports `PLANNED_NOTE` and `_resolves` from the generator it is checking, so there is one copy of the rule and two readers, and a row whose note and sentence disagree fails at the desk rather than on the owner's screen. It is written down because the wording had already drifted once - the drift class DEF-027 closed was back, in the prose - and because the tempting fix is to retype the sentence in the checker, which is how the two copies would start disagreeing again.

- **2026-11-15 — A planned row proves its own gap by re-running its displayed phrases, and the eighteen measured stale rows sit in a ratchet that may only shrink:** DEF-037 recorded that the feature matrix's planned statuses were wrong and that its checker could not catch them; the owner's decision on the fix was "make the checker honest now, fix rows in the phone pass". The honest half is this: a planned row is now asked the same question an enforced row is - do the sentences it shows the owner already change its own control - and a row that answers yes fails the check unless it is one of the eighteen measured that day. The ratchet is deliberate rather than a waiver: every recorded id is reported by name on a green run, a recorded id that stops working fails (the row was fixed, so the id must come out), and any planned row that starts working outside the set fails immediately. The alternative - turning the check red today for a gap already written down in the register - would have made the one check that proves this claim unusable until the bigger row-by-row work lands, which is exactly how a checker earns a reputation for noise.

- **2026-11-15 — the preflight names the desktop's, the backend's and `main`'s commits in ONE row, not three:** the desktop app, the live backend folder and the branch releases are built from can each sit at a different commit, and the deploy that puts them there cannot see the other two — so a half-landed change reads as green everywhere. The ruling (Q8) is one row that says all three short ids on one line: equal ids pass, unequal ones WARN and name which piece is behind, because "they disagree" is not actionable and "the backend is 4 commits behind `main`" is. It reads refs already on this PC only (`git rev-parse` fetches nothing), so an offline PC gets the same answer as an online one, and a folder that is not a checkout or a PC with no git says exactly that rather than naming a guessed sha — the same rule the two ids above it already follow. The ids are compared in full and shown short, because seven characters is what fits a preflight line and the comparison is what decides the verdict. Deliberately not done: no network fetch, no deploy, and no second row per piece — one line is the whole point of the row.

- **2026-11-15 — The ten focus-preset rows open at one line, and each row's prose waits behind its own tap:** the phone audit of 2026-11-15 measured the "Focus presets" plate printing five blocks of prose per row - `what`, the second-worker line, "What it is for:", "What it is worse at:" and the words under them - **9,703 characters across the ten rows with every word out, 1,944 of them for Coding alone**, on a screen whose whole job is to let the owner pick one of ten things. The owner's choice, made the same day, is that a row opens at one line and the rest waits behind ONE tap per preset: the title (with its CHOSEN mark), the `focus` line, `modelLine`, a heavy preset's cost sentence when there is one, the blocker, and the "Use this" button stay visible, while `what`, the helper line, "What it is for:" with `cost`, and "What it is worse at:" with `worse` sit behind a per-row `var show by remember` and a "Why this one" / "Hide why" `Quiet` tap. **The prose is folded, never deleted** - opening a row draws exactly what it drew before, so nothing the contract says has become unreachable on the phone - and the closed list draws 1,752 characters instead of 9,703. Both surfaces that share this list (the composer chip and Settings -> Hardware) fold, because they are the same function; no route, no contract, no test weakened and no desktop surface changed. The same discipline the 2026-11-15 audit already applied to Brain -> Hardware's 565-character command line: one line visible, the detail behind a tap.

- **2026-11-15 — Read aloud carries on when the app is left, including a locked phone:** The owner, using the phone: "when i move out of the jarvis android app on my phone (whether thats just putting it in picture in picture mode or moving to a different app or homescreen, it should continue the read outloud if thats what i selected on the jarvis app. right now it stops it". Asked what should happen when the screen locks, he chose "keep going even when locked". This reverses the ruling of 2026-10-27 ("stop immediately, privacy first"): the activity no longer stops a read on ON_STOP, neither read loop stops for a lock landing mid-read, and a mediaPlayback foreground service holds the process awake with one notification whose Stop talking ends the read - the same door as the app's own button, "stop" said aloud, and Stop everything. The start-time refusals (a locked phone, App lock, a stale link) and every rule that keeps an answer on screen are unchanged; the service is proved on the phone, not in CI.

- **2026-11-15 — The recent-changes module is regenerated on main, not carried by a pull request:** The generated `jarvis_recent_changes.py` was the last file every fragment-adding pull request rewrote, so two such PRs always conflicted, and each conflict costs a full CI round because a conflicted PR gets no run at all. Ruling Q1 had already taken the self-code map out of pull requests for the same measured reason; Q2 takes this file with it, in the same main-only workflow, right after the map is settled. What replaces the freshness demand on a PR is a weaker question that a PR can actually answer - is every bullet the module carries a real bullet of the record, in the record's own order - asserted by `backend/test_self_knowledge_honesty.py`, with byte-exact freshness kept for main behind `JARVIS_RECENT_CHANGES_STRICT=1`. The trade is stated rather than hidden: between a merge and the small refresh PR, the owner's PC answers "what changed" from a module up to one merge old, which the workflow reports on main and the answer never disguises as newer than it is.

- **2026-11-15 — The self-code map leaves feature pull requests, and main carries a snapshot checked after every merge:** the owner's ruling Q1, reached from a measured night rather than from taste. The map records every tracked file, so every pull request - and every pull request owes a changelog fragment and a decisions fragment - rewrote the same 330 KB file, and two pull requests always wrote it in the same place; six landed one night and the map forced a full conflict plus a fresh CI round on every one, turning eight merges into about nine hours. What replaced the old rule (regenerate the map last) is a split with two gates. A pull request keeps the tree COHERENT - every tracked file owned by exactly one subsystem, and every key module, suite and document the generator's table names present - which `backend/test_self_code.py` proves in the required `backend` job and `py -3 tools/gen_self_code_map.py --coherence` runs at the desk; it reads no map and regenerates nothing, and a PR that adds a module edits the `SUBSYSTEMS` table instead of the JSON. `main` carries the map: `.github/workflows/self-code-map.yml` runs `py -3 tools/gen_self_code_map.py --check` after every merge and fails, naming the one command, when the committed map is not exactly what main's tree produces. The snapshot is then one small pull request with only the two map files, because main is protected by required status checks and there is no bot token - a push from a workflow would be an unreviewed change to main, which is the thing the protection exists to stop. The generator now also refuses to WRITE on a dirty tree: its file lists come from the index while the commit it records comes from HEAD, and a map generated during an in-progress merge was measured on main recording a commit that never had the files it listed. What this deliberately does not do: it does not stop checking completeness - the same `assign()` call still refuses a file nobody owns or one that two subsystems claim, and its synthetic proofs are unchanged - it does not weaken the twin rule (one run still writes both copies, and `--check` still refuses when they differ), and it does not let a stale map pass silently: main goes red until the snapshot is re-taken, and `docs/SELF-CODE-MAP.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 20 and `CLAUDE.md` now state the new rule in place of the old one.

- **2026-11-15 — The source commit is recorded beside `VERSION`, and the preflight names MIXED COMMITS instead of blocking:** Owner ruling Q8 (Gemini, Principal Architect, 2026-11-15) asked for each artifact's source `HEAD` sha to be recorded in its manifest/version metadata, and for a clear MIXED COMMITS warning when they differ, after three pieces the owner runs were measured at three commits with nothing saying so - desktop 0.2.458 from `7a8fe7d`, the APK from `2aacc71ba`, and the live backend's `VERSION` at 0.2.456 from `04d4748cf`. **Where it is recorded, and why there.** The desktop's `latest.json` gains a `commit` field (from the workflow's `$GITHUB_SHA`, the same value the release notes already name in prose), because a manifest is the one thing a program reads. The phone needed nothing: `client-latest.json` already carries `commit` and the APK's own `BuildConfig.GIT_SHA` is what its update check already compares. The backend's sha goes BESIDE `VERSION` as `SOURCE-COMMIT`, written by the one tool that writes `VERSION` (`tools/reconcile_live_backend.py`, from the `--ref` commit it already resolves for its ref guard), and deliberately NOT inside it: `VERSION` is the shared release marker the desktop HUD compares character for character ("MISMATCH: the backend 0.2.421, but this HUD expects 0.2.433") and every other reader parses it as a bare version number, so a sha in it would break every one of those reads. The record is deterministic (no timestamp), so a second `--apply` plans nothing, and a deploy that cannot read its commit writes no record at all - it says `SOURCE-COMMIT: skipped (...)` rather than inventing a sha. **The comparison, and its honest limit.** The preflight's new `commits` check (the existing read-only status surface, extended rather than a second one) reads the desktop's start-up log line and the backend's `SOURCE-COMMIT`, and says MIXED COMMITS when two pieces that name a commit disagree; a record older than the `VERSION` it sits beside is not believed, and a piece that does not say is said to not say. It is WARN-only by design - the ruling wants visibility so an urgent single-piece fix is still installable - it raises no card, and it never fetches: the phone's installed APK is therefore reported as not readable from this PC rather than looked up on GitHub, and making the phone report into the PC would be a new feature in two apps, not a record that was already there. Both facts it reports are local: a commit written at build time into the binary, and a commit written at deploy time into the backend's folder.

- **2026-11-15 — Trusted mode's cap counts uses per action, not action names:** the design document's `MAX_TRUSTED_ACTIONS = 20` is written as one number against the whole window, and with an eleven-name allowlist a cap of 20 *action names* can never be reached, so in that reading the number would never bind. The engine therefore enforces 20 USES PER ACTION PER SESSION, with a hard ceiling of 30 and a larger request clamped rather than honoured; `TrustedSession.max_actions` is that per-action number, `actions_taken` is the total across all actions, and the twenty-first use of any one action is refused. The owner confirmed the reading on 2026-11-16 ("20 used of each kind") and asked that the default be changeable in Settings, by chat or in Jarvis Live, so the number one window gets is resolved when it OPENS: the caller's own number for that session first, else the owner's `[grants].max_actions` setting (declared once as `jarvis_limits.LIMITS["trusted_actions"]`, 1..30, shipped at 20), else 20 - clamped at every level. The engine only READS the setting; changing it stays the existing limits route's gate action, and the chat and Jarvis Live sentences that name it arrive with the wiring PR. What it deliberately does not do: it does not raise the cap, it does not give a plan grant a cap (a plan's bound is the exact list it names), and it does not make a spent window reopenable - the cap is per session, so a new window needs a new card.

- **2026-11-16 — A spoken sentence is refused as a note's name, never shortened into one:** the capture path's one name is a Joplin note's title, and it was derived from the first line of the owner's words, cut at 80 characters and closed with an ellipsis - so `Workout Log, pin it, and add using todays date that i used the punching bag` became a note's name, and a long line became a plausible half of one. Decided, with the owner's 2026-11-16 ruling (`for_deepseek_2026_11_16_1625pt_rulings_routing_fence_and_clarify.md` R9: "gate the note writer") behind it: a name is a name, and when the words are not one the capture is REFUSED in plain words that quote them, say whether they are a sentence or an instruction, and ask for just the name - because a truncated title is a wrong note the owner never learns about, while a refusal is one sentence he can act on. The rules are the ones the ruling lists and nothing cleverer: a clause joining word (`and`, `then`, `but`, `plus`), a command verb in the imperative (`add`, `append`, `delete`, `remove`, `pin`, `unpin`, `rename`, `move`, `set`, `remember`, `make`, `create`, `write`, `put` - the first word, the word after a joiner, or one followed by what it acts on), a trailing ellipsis, or more than 10 words / 80 characters. A name that already means one of the owner's notes is refused in the ONE resolver's own words rather than a new vocabulary (`jarvis_notes.resolve_note`, merged the same day: `content_preexists` or its `ambiguous_section` question), and that resolver is not changed - its path tier stays case-sensitive, as the same day's ruling requires. What it deliberately does not do: it does not touch the vault CREATE path, which is where the 37-byte `Workout log.md` and the 0-byte sentence-named note came from - that writer's own gate landed the same day in `jarvis_quick.py` (cc7e84136: "a title must be a name (not a sentence), filed beside the note its name already points at; a collision is a 409"), and this change is the capture path's half of the same rule, not a second guess at that one. What it costs, measured rather than assumed: the duplicate-name check asks the resolver, which walks the owner's 1,001-note vault, so a Joplin plan on this PC takes about 2.0-2.4 s longer (median 2.4 s for a name no note has, 1.97 s for `Workout Log`, which now answers `ambiguous_section` naming both notes); a cheaper check would be a second resolver, which the ruling forbids, so the cost is accepted and written down here instead of hidden. And a capture with no body now writes nothing at all: `run()` refuses an empty Plan as well as `plan()` refusing an empty text, because a Plan built by hand used to make an empty journal file (measured: 6 bytes of block marker, ok True).

- **2026-11-16 — An answer that cannot be read is never guessed:** an awareness question is answered from a real read of this PC or it says plainly that it cannot tell; it never falls through to the model, which cannot measure anything, and it never upgrades what it did read. The 2026-11-15 audit measured eleven questions with **no fixed answer at all** - each one reached the 8B model, which has no way to read a disk, a server or an installed-model list, so whatever it said was invention. This change answers four of them from the read that actually owns each fact: *"what models are loaded"* from Ollama's own `/api/ps` (with **"nothing is loaded right now"** when the list is empty, and the loaded model's name, memory, card share and context when it is not), *"how many models are installed"* from the installed-model list the app already reads, *"what is my disk space"* from the same PC-facts disk read that "how much disk space is left" already uses, so the reply names every drive (the audit's gap was the phrasing; a narrower one-drive answer was dropped rather than added beside the wider one), and *"is ollama running"* from the lane's own `/api/tags` probe - the same read both apps' lane warning makes. Each sentence names the read that answered it, so the words can be checked against the machine. The rule this records is the half the older entries did not cover: **when that read fails, the answer is "I could not read it, so I cannot tell - and I will not guess"**, never a number, a model name or a state borrowed from the configured choice; an empty list that cannot be told apart from a failed read is said as "cannot tell", not as "none". A configured model stays **set to use** and is never called loaded or running (PR #1292's rule), and all four answers are read-only intents, so asking one cannot clear what "cancel that" would undo. Deliberately NOT answered, because the honest source is not on this PC: the phone's own model, whether the phone is connected, the mailbox, which card runs the model, what Jarvis is doing, what it cannot do, and how many interruptions are left - they stay open and are named in the audit rather than filled with a plausible sentence.

- **2026-11-16 — The coding benchmark asks for files and applies them itself:** `tools/bench_coding/` is a measurement tool, and it needs a decision written down because the obvious road is closed: this PC's chat lane has no file-write tool (`shell_exec` is hard-refused as `run_shell_on_host`, and `file_write`/`apply_patch` map to `delete_file`), so Jarvis cannot edit a repository itself. The harness therefore sends the failing file and test as text, asks for the complete file in one fenced block, applies that block inside a disposable `git init` repository that has no remote, and judges the row from the exact pytest command's exit code. It **declines** (never approves) a card that appears during one of its own turns: measured the hard way on 2026-11-16, when a local bug-fix prompt made the model call `github_fix_and_push` with an invented `owner/repo` and PR #1 and then wait 600 s on the card - a no executes nothing, and every declined card's id and action is recorded. It never switches a preset unless `--apply-preset` is passed, and a BLOCKED row is never scored as a pass. It is separate from `backend/jarvis_bench.py` on purpose - that module measures a model's token speed, RAM/GPU placement and context sizes; this measures task outcomes through the whole product (which lane answered, whether the tests passed, what the cloud cost, what was touched) and reads none of `bench.jsonl`.

- **2026-11-16 — The gate's census, and the one browser exception:** Two promises finish the one egress gate. **The census:** `tools/check_egress_gate.py` knew six chatbot API hosts, so a green run meant "nothing among six hosts", not "nothing leaves" - the browser sites, the three keyed web-search providers, `api.github.com`, Google's calendar hosts, the weather, package and map hosts were all invisible. It is now a census: every `.py` under `backend/`, `jarvis-backend/` and `tools/` that names an outbound host must either name `check_egress` in the same file or be on an exact-path allow-list with a written reason, a listed `backend/` path also covers its byte-identical `jarvis-backend/` copy (measured, not assumed), an entry whose file has gone or no longer names a host is reported, and a new unlisted host name fails the run with the file and line. `jarvis_search.py` now asks the gate about the exact address before every keyed search, before the key is resolved; the local SearXNG search deliberately does not, because it never leaves this PC. **The exception:** the browser chatbot drivers type into a company's own web page, which has no API key and no monthly cap on this PC - so the money question could never answer yes and those drivers would be refused for ever. The owner's decision (2026-11-16) is that they may go out when the standing cloud switch is on and Lockdown is off, because the switch being on is their yes. So `check_egress` takes one claim, `no_money_cap="<your own caller name>"`, and the gate accepts it only from the callers named in `NO_MONEY_CAP_CALLERS` (today exactly `jarvis_chatbot_web`, the module every website driver sends through), only when it equals the caller's own name, and only for an address that belongs to no service this PC has settings for - it can never bypass a real monthly cap, Lockdown or the standing switch, and a caller that is not named, or that claims another caller's name, is refused exactly as before. The drivers ask it in `send()` and in `_goto_here()`, and a gate that cannot be loaded is itself a refusal, with nothing typed. If a second kind of caller ever needs this shape that is a new decision, not a new name in the list. What this deliberately does not do: it opens no socket and sends nothing itself, the drivers' own existing checks still run, and the HUD's runtime-built address remains the one path a text census cannot see.

- **2026-11-16 — Favourite is its own note property, never an alias of pin:** the owner's sentence `favourite my workout log note` (and `favorite …`) returned no intent at all, and the owner chose a separate property rather than aliasing `pinned`. So "favourite" writes and removes `favorite: true` in the note's front matter through the same one `edit_vault_note` card, File Guardian copy and Undo that pinning an existing note already uses - one route, no new card, no new permission - and a new note can be created with it ("make a note called X and favourite it", card-free exactly as every new note is). The `pinned` property's behaviour is untouched, so a note can be pinned, favourited, both or neither, and the read-back ("is my workout log note pinned / favourited?") answers each from the note's own front matter. It deliberately does not add a favourite list, a sort, a filter or a new setting: those would be their own decision. Both spellings are accepted in a sentence; the YAML key is always the US `favorite`, and the read-back also accepts a hand-written `favourite:`.

- **2026-11-16 — Repository and pull-request destruction, bulk closing and closing one pull request get their own permanent refusal shapes:** Measured on the owner's live install: `delete the repo`, `delete this repo`, `delete the Epic-Jarvis repository`, `remove the repository` and `close all the pull requests` answered "Yes - with ONE approval card per merge, and merge commit only." because the GitHub merge shape's own change-verb list carried `delete`, `remove` and `close`, and its thing list carried `repo`, `repository`, `pull requests` and `issues`. Gemini's ruling Q5 asks for a deterministic matcher refusal for exactly those sentences. An independent audit the same day found three more still on that "Yes" - `close the repo`, `delete the pull request`, `delete all the pull requests` - and `close pull request 1299` answered as if closing one pull request were a merge. The chat fast path now has three read-only shapes beside `approve`: **destroy** (a repository or pull request noun with delete, remove, destroy, wipe, drop or nuke, plus `close` of a repository, because closing a repository is destruction), **bulk_close** (close or delete with all, every or both, and pull requests or issues), and **close_pr** (close one named pull request). Each opens "No", says what is permanently banned, that no approval card can lift the ban, and that nothing was deleted or closed; bulk names closing ONE issue as the real carded action and says even that never closes a pull request, and close_pr says closing a pull request is not an action Jarvis has - `github_issue_state` refuses a pull request by name - while a merge and a one-issue close are the real cards. The repository ban is not typed in `jarvis_quick.py`: the destroy refusal cites `jarvis_github.NEVER` at answer time, which carries `delete_repository`, `close_repository` and `bulk_close`. `jarvis_grants.BANNED_ACTIONS` does not carry repository destruction - so the approve refusal's source (the grant code) is NOT the source here, and the module's own never-list is. None of the three shapes claims a new capability, raises a card, opens a socket or calls the model; informational how-to questions, the real note, file, to-do and calendar deletions, and the real GitHub sentences keep their own paths.

- **2026-11-16 — A switched-off tool is offered in the answer, not in Settings:** The owner's ruling: Jarvis should be as easy to use as a modern agent harness - abilities on by default, one approval per job instead of per action, and no need to visit Settings to enable a tool. The deterministic answer to "can you create a repository?" ended by naming the one card that would switch its tool on, in another window. `backend/jarvis_quick.py`'s create-a-repository answer now offers that card IN PLACE when the tool is off: it calls `jarvis_asks_first.request_tool_enable`, the SAME function `POST /api/asks_first/tools` calls, so the card is `enable_reading_tool` at tier "ask" - Windows Hello on the PC or the phone's own signed approval, OFF instant, nothing written until a person approves, and the PC-only rule is the route's own. If that card is turned down, the next ask says so ("You declined that card, so its tool stays off"), once, and offers it again. No new action, tier, route, card or permission was added.

- **2026-11-16 — Every GitHub write declares its tier where the card can name it:** Gemini's ruling Q5, Layer 1 — *"Every write/destructive tool and intent MUST explicitly declare its tier (`ask` or `refuse`) rather than falling through to `unknown`"* — is recorded in `backend/jarvis_github.py` (`WRITE_TIERS`, read by `write_tier()` and `describe()`), **not** in `jarvis_gate.py`'s three tables and not in `[autonomy.tiers]`. The reason is the defect the 2026-11-16 write-card audit measured: the gate already resolved every one of the twelve write tools to `ask` through both shipped settings copies, and all thirteen write actions already had their `_RISK` and `_TOOL_ACTIONS` rows — what was missing was the card, which said nothing about the tier, so 0 of 12 named it. A declaration in the gate would have been true and still invisible. `refuse` is a standing ban and is refused BEFORE a card exists, so its sentence is carried by the refusal answer (the APPROVE review, a workflow dispatch, a banned push flag), never by an approvable card; `ask` is printed on the card itself. A `[autonomy.tiers]` row is deliberately **not** added for a banned verb: `backend/test_github_tools.py` refuses a tier line that names one, and a `never` line for a verb that is not a gate action would be a second, drifting truth.

- **2026-11-16 — A finished job may say that it ended:** The rule that "nobody is looking, so the result must not speak" is narrowed, not repealed. A background job the owner started and is waiting on may now announce that it ENDED — one phone notification and one desktop toast, carrying the job's own label and its state and nothing else — because those are the owner's own words today: "can jarvis give me a progress update and send me notifications when I ask on task that takes a while". The job's words still wait to be collected: neither notice shows a result, a param or an error text, and tapping either opens the Work pane or Work tab where the result already is. Progress was already carried on the event bus and is unchanged, and the PC's rule that a `cancelled` job gets no notice is kept. Quiet hours, a foreground-only rule, and any switch for this kind are the owner's call and were deliberately not invented here.

- **2026-11-16 — Moving a background job's priority is the owner's act, and a model may never do it:** The owner asked (2026-11-16) to prioritise background work "through chat and otherwise". A priority change grants nothing - it reorders work that was already allowed to run, changes no capability set, starts nothing, answers no card, and never makes a job run before its own `due` time - so it belongs on the cardless-by-design list beside "the next message's lane" and the one-job schedule row, and no approval card is raised. But it is a lever over the owner's ATTENTION, so WHO may pull it is a policy question, not a UI one. The ruling: only the owner's own sentence (the fixed grammar in `jarvis_quick.py`, which answers before the model is called) and, later, the owner's own UI may set it; a MODEL may not. That is enforced by absence rather than by a check - `jarvis_jobs.set_priority()` is the only writer, `jarvis_quick.py` is its only caller, and this change adds no HTTP route, no model tool and no handler-facing writer. Why refuse a model even though the change is small: a job's label and params can come from outside the PC (the watch jobs read GitHub and their own docstring says their text is never handed to a model), so a reorder tool would be a lever that a watched page or an email could pull over what the owner sees first. If the owner later wants the model to help, the recorded shape is: LOWERING is free, RAISING raises a card - a design round, not this change. Two existing ideas stay deliberately separate: `jarvis_arbiter.py`'s `priority` is a TEXT urgency on an intents row (how loudly a finding is delivered), not this INTEGER order on a jobs row, and the two are not unified here; and "set a job's priority when it is created" is left out, because it needs `create(priority=)` and both start forms. The apps show priority in a later PR; the field is already on `GET /api/jobs`.

- **2026-11-16 — Recalled memory is the owner's own data, not outside text:** The taint latch exists to stop OUTSIDE text - a page, an email, a document, a pasted file, tool output - from widening what Jarvis may do. Recalled facts are the owner's own remembered words, learned from his own words only (the 2026-09-24 decision), so they must not take that latch. Measured 2026-11-16: the HUD's memory-injection branch called `jarvis_gate.latch_taint(why="memory_injected")`, and because the latch is ONE boolean with a label no consumer reads, every note write asked for a card (a new note waited on an `edit_vault_note` card) and a setting change refused itself as "shaped by something outside of your direct input". Fixing it has two doors, both in `jarvis_hud.py`: the memory branch no longer latches, and the request handed to `jarvis_agent.run_local_turn` no longer carries the server's own recalled-facts system turn (the turn watch read a system message there as text the APP sent). The every-turn re-latch moves out of the `elif` so it still extends a REAL outside-text latch on memory-injected turns, keeping the 30-minute sliding window exactly as it was. Memory still stays on this PC without the latch, by the two mechanisms that already did that work: while Jarvis injects memory itself the HUD passes `lanes=[]` to `jarvis_router.choose`, and a cloud turn is stripped to user-role messages only, so neither the recalled block nor the local model's restatement of it can travel. A pasted file keeps its own boundary (the router's `file` gate plus the conversation mark, which the 2026-10-30 decision chose IN PLACE OF the process-wide 30-minute latch, so one attachment cannot keep every other chat off the cloud lane), and a page watch, an email-body read and a document read still latch for 30 minutes with the every-turn re-latch. The fix is in the published base and in NO patch, so it reaches a live install through four literal deltas in `tools/hud-deltas/`, carried by `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py`; `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` proves the four reconstruct the base byte for byte. Proved by `backend/test_note_multihop_taint.py` (memory latches nothing; the note card follows outside text; page/email/document still latch with the 30-minute window and the never-shortens rule; the pasted file still local; the raw payload is the control that makes a memory turn look app-shaped and the filtered one does not).

- **2026-11-16 — A note name is resolved in a fixed tier order, in ONE place, and never falls back to the daily note:** The architect's Wave 1 ruling. `jarvis_notes_edit.py` stays the only vault writer; resolution lives in `jarvis_notes.resolve_note()` and every note tool routes through it, so no two doors can disagree about what a name means. The order is: (1) the exact vault path the owner named (a slash or a `.md`/`.txt` ending is what makes a name a path; case matters there); (2) the file name alone, matched case-insensitively, which is the tier that has to answer on Windows where `Gym.md` and `gym.md` are one file; (3) an exact value of the note's own YAML `aliases:` list, compared case-insensitively and with a leading my/the/a/an and a trailing "note" ignored; (4) refusal, with any near candidates listed. Two matches at one tier are `ambiguous_section` with both candidates named, never a guess. NO TIER TOUCHES THE DAILY NOTE: a name that matches nothing is a refusal, because the measured bug was exactly that fallback (a create request's tail was filed into `2026-11-15.md`). The order is adapted, as a pattern not code, from Vinzent03/obsidian-advanced-uri (MIT), whose `filename` parameter first asks Obsidian's `getFirstLinkpathDest` and only then scans aliases; the refusal vocabulary and the two create options (`create_target_if_missing`, `reject_if_content_preexists`) are adapted, as patterns, from cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server (Apache-2.0) and coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api (MIT). The two options are booleans on `create_target()`/`POST /api/notes/create`, not a second HTTP surface, and `reject_if_content_preexists=False` only allows filling an EMPTY note because Epic Jarvis never overwrites. `find_name()` survives only as a compatibility shape over `resolve_note()`. The vault's `.obsidian/daily-notes.json` is also honoured now - folder, format and template, with the template applied only to a new daily note (a pattern from liamcain/obsidian-daily-notes-interface, MIT) - and a vault without that file behaves exactly as it did before.

- **2026-11-16 — A non-loopback `OLLAMA_URL` is refused at the read and the loopback model answers instead, rather than the value being used or the backend refusing to start:** the three reads (`jarvis-backend/jarvis_models.py`, `jarvis-backend/jarvis_extract.py`, `jarvis-backend/jarvis_hud.py`) now share one function, `ollama_url_on_this_pc()`. It returns the value only when its host is `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1`; otherwise it prints one plain sentence naming the variable and what was wrong, and returns the loopback default. Decided this way because the alternative readings are both wrong for this program: using the value is the defect (the owner's conversations, extracted facts and notes would leave the PC while every document says the model is here), and stopping the backend is a worse failure than the one being prevented - a stale or mistyped environment variable on the owner's own PC should cost him the cloud-looking address, not his assistant. The fallback also matches what the rest of the stack already does for a lane it cannot use (answer locally, spend nothing). Two behaviours were deliberately left exactly as they were: an unset variable still means `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, and an empty one still stays empty - a useless value is not silently turned into a working one - so no PC that never set the variable sees any change. The refusal is deduplicated per distinct value, because all three modules read it at import and three identical lines at every boot would be noise. Recorded with it: a provider's address is now used only when the same resolved lane carries a non-empty key, because that key is a second Credential Manager read and `_auth_headers` would otherwise fall back to Jarvis's own pairing token (see the changelog fragment for the quoted lines).

- **2026-11-16 — One completion count:** Gemini's ruling R7 said to have `jarvis_agent.py` record `completion_tokens` directly alongside `prompt_tokens` and `cached_tokens`, so `speed.jsonl` and cloud cost accounting use one unified source of truth. It now does: the model's own count - `usage.completion_tokens` on the `/v1` wire, and Ollama's `eval_count` on the native one, which `_native_as_chunk` already mapped into that same key - is summed over the turn's tool rounds, returned with the turn, handed to the speed record through `jarvis_speed.note_prompt()`, and written to the row under its own name. For an answer the model counted, the speed row's `tokens` and `token_source` now come from that count (`usage`) instead of this PC counting content pieces (`deltas`), so the figure a speed row shows and the figure `jarvis_chatbot_api.cost_of()` prices as its completion term are one number, from one place. An answer that carries no count records `None` - said as unknown, never written as 0 - and the row falls back to `deltas` with the field absent. Deliberately not done, and not a smaller version of this: the `characters ÷ 3` estimator is unchanged, the estimators are not unified, and no limit, tier, cap or gate row is touched - that is separate work with its own re-pinning cost. What this does not claim: a real local turn is still never priced, because a local lane has no service to charge; the unification is that both readers take one recorded number, not that a local answer now appears on a cloud bill.

- **2026-11-16 — One egress gate, and closed means refused:** Whether a request may leave this PC is now decided in ONE place, `backend/jarvis_egress_gate.py`'s `check_egress(...)`, instead of by each sender for itself. The order is fixed: a loopback address is this PC talking to itself, so it is always allowed and needs no setting; then `local_only=True` refuses, which is how rule 1 - email, files, credentials and stored memory stay on the local model - is carried by a sender that already knows its words must stay here; then Lockdown; then the standing cloud switch (`escalate-cloud.json`, absent or unreadable reads as OFF); then the service's monthly money cap in `chatbot/api-money.json`. "Closed" means REFUSED, not "ask again later": a missing switch file is off, a damaged Lockdown file is on, an unreadable money file refuses, and a host that names no service this PC has settings for refuses, because a cap that cannot be read cannot be a yes. The chatbot's API adapter and the quiz's cloud send ask it about the exact address their socket is about to open, and report an `egress_blocked` refusal in the gate's own words with nothing sent. The two remaining senders - the web search in `jarvis_search.py` and the HUD - are deliberately NOT wired in this change and belong to a second lane. `tools/check_egress_gate.py` lists the web-search sender (both copies) with that reason so the lane cannot miss it; the HUD spells no cloud host at all - it posts to an address the lane data hands it at runtime - which is the limit the checker's own docstring states a text check cannot see, so that one is recorded here rather than in the list. Review found one real bug in the first version of the gate: `_money_refusal` was called with `target` twice, the `TypeError` was caught by the gate's own never-raise belt, and every non-loopback request refused as `config_unreadable` - a gate that refuses everything is exactly as wrong as one that allows everything, and two suites now prove both directions (a refusal sends nothing, and a loopback send really goes). The published-base twin had been left at the pre-fix version too; it is byte-identical again. What this deliberately does not do: it opens no socket and sends nothing itself, it reads no payload word (only its length), and it does not replace the senders' own existing checks - the card, the key pinning and the money check still run where they always did; this is the one question asked immediately before the socket, and the last word on the answer.

- **2026-11-16 — An over-window prompt is trimmed once and then refused, never warned about and sent:** when the prompt estimate (characters ÷ 3, frames included) says a pooled-lane turn is bigger than the window it is about to name, Jarvis now stubs every old tool result but the newest, fits the rest to 60% of the window, re-estimates, and sends only if that fits; if it still does not, the turn ends with one plain sentence — *"Prompt exceeds the N-token local window, even after leaving out earlier turns and old tool results. Shorten the input, chunk the file, or escalate to DeepSeek."* — and no request is made. This replaces the 2026-11-15 `WINDOW_OVERFLOW_LINE`, which announced that the prompt did not fit and sent it anyway; Ollama then dropped the FRONT of the prompt (Jarvis's rules and the earliest turns) and answered, so the warning described the loss instead of preventing it. The reasons for REFUSE rather than trim-again-and-send: the ordinary trimmer has already run by the time this check is reached, so what remains is the rules, the current turn and the offered tool schemas — trimming any of those would delete the exact thing the fix protects; and the estimator under-counts dense text (measured on this PC, 2026-11-16: 8,000 characters of code estimated at 2,672 tokens against Ollama's real 6,013, 2.25×), so a prompt that fits only on the estimate cannot be promised to fit in the model. A refusal is loud, names what to do, and never silently loses a rule; the one trim first is kept because a long chat that can still answer should, and refusing before trying would lose turns that fit after dropping old turns. The same branch clamps `max_tokens` to `min(client value, n_ctx // 4, 8192)`, because `budget()` subtracts it from the window and a huge client value could leave only the 512-token prompt floor. Proven by `backend/test_chat_window.py` (W2: no request, the refusal sentence, and no warn-then-send line left) and `backend/test_agent.py` (one test for the refusal, one for a chat that fits after the single trim). The live install has not carried it yet.

- **2026-11-16 — Three phone paragraphs say it once, and point at the screen that owns the detail:** the phone audit of 2026-11-16 measured three paragraphs on the Android app explaining at length what the screen already draws or what another card already explains, and the rule now applied is that each states its rule once, says where the detail lives, and stops. **Live's start screen**, under the Start button, goes from **402 characters to 186**: it still says when a session ends by itself and that starting Live on a locked phone checks the voice, then points at Settings, Voice. What it no longer re-tells - the "hi Jarvis" cases, the mic press, an unlocked start, and the DEF-033 caveat that an unlocked "hi Jarvis" is still checked - is already said in full on the Voice card (**298 characters**, measured) beside the button that changes the setting, so the caveat stays there rather than in two places. It also no longer states a fixed 90-second quiet length: that is the owner's own setting (`jarvis_live.quiet_seconds`, 30 s to 10 min, 90 s by default), so a static number goes wrong the day it is changed, and the PC already warns before a quiet session ends. **The Focus presets plate's** introduction goes from **378 to 177**: it keeps what a preset changes and the one rule the rows cannot show - a press either switches at once or raises one approval card - and drops three things that live elsewhere: the heavy-preset cost sentence its own row prints above the button, the Cloud-row clause (**the phone draws no cloud row**; it draws only the ten local presets and a read-only line saying cloud is set on the PC, so that clause described the desktop's menu), and the hand-typed "The Fast preset uses the 2080 SUPER", which was a copy of the Fast row's own `modelLine` and would be silently wrong the day the PC moves Fast. **Brain's Settings door** goes from **370 to 111**: it lists none of Settings' contents - the hand-typed list had already fallen behind Settings' own "Jump to:" list, which is drawn on that screen and cannot drift - and instead says the settings are in Settings and the list at the top takes you to any of them. Nothing was removed from the app: every fact dropped from these three paragraphs is still drawn on the row or card that owns it, or sent by the PC when it matters. One JVM test is updated (`VoiceCheckRuleTest`) to pin the Live copy: it may not re-tell the Voice card's cases or hardcode the quiet length, and it must still say the quiet end, the locked-phone check and where the setting is. No route, contract or desktop surface changed, and the phone unit suite is green (3,945 tests, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 52s`).

- **2026-11-16 — A fact that arrived with the request is live; a stored fact is aged, never presented as live:** the phone's own facts (`X-Jarvis-Device`) answer *"what model of phone am I using right now"* and *"are you connected to my phone"* only by that rule. `jarvis_surface` now stores when the facts arrived (`device_age()`), and keeps the newest report any phone has sent this process with its own time (`last_age()`). A fact from THIS request is live - and for "are you connected", the request from the phone is itself the live proof that the phone is reaching the PC. A stored one is returned with its age ("43 minutes ago") and said to be stored, not live. When nothing has arrived, the answer says it does not know yet and names no phone; it does not borrow a pairing record, because a record has a pairing name rather than a model, and PR #1292 already removed a "connected right now" claim built from the roster's `reach` flag, which is a capability and not a liveness probe. A request that is not the phone's still reads the pairing records, but always with the age of their own last check-in and the sentence "a pairing is a record, not a live connection". The rule, for every future awareness answer built on a client header: **a fact that arrived with the request is live; a fact stored from an hour ago is returned with its age and never presented as live** - and if nothing arrived, the answer says so instead of naming whatever the store happens to hold. The same facts could settle the phone's Android version, screen and app build, and "what Android version is my phone" is deliberately left unwired for now: the owner asked for the model question, and every extra matcher is a hijack risk. "Is my phone connected" keeps its existing roster answer.

- **2026-11-16 — A preset the owner clicks is uncarded, the heavy Coding preset included; the chat road still cards:** The owner's sentence, in his own words: *"when i change the model on the jarvis app it still sends me an approval card. that shouldnt happen if i manually press the preset change. only if i ask through chat"*. This EXTENDS the 2026-11-09 manual-click rule (Gemini Q2: an explicit backend allow-list plus a trusted UI-origin signal - a reversible thing clicked in either app's own UI is not carded, and the same thing asked for in chat is) to the HEAVY presets, which that rule had carved out with ONE line: `direct_owner = bool(owner_ui) and not heavy` (`backend/jarvis_presets.py:1840`). A Coding click reached the pooled lane's own `switch_model` card even though the owner had pressed the control, because `jarvis_presets._default_start_lane` (`:2023`) called `jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane(mode="coding")` with no gate, and that lane raises its one card before it unloads anything. The rule now reads: a local preset clicked on `POST /api/work/apply` applies uncarded, whatever its weight; the press answers the pooled lane's card (`_start_lane_for_the_owner`, handing the lane `_OwnerPressed` in the verdict shape a gate returns), so the lane still announces, pauses and loads in the same measured order, and the change still writes the `preset_apply` receipt that makes it undoable - including a return to a heavy preset, which the same click road now restores rather than carding. WHY THE MODEL ROAD DOES NOT CHANGE, on either road: a heavy preset records its model through `_default_adopt`, never `_switch_for_the_owner`/`_default_switch`, because `jarvis_models.switch_to` runs the tripwire's smoke test at the owner's everyday one-card lane - a 14.8 GB coding model would be loaded twice there or evict the model the pooled lane just loaded, and its "did the new model work" answer would be about the wrong lane. WHAT STILL CARDS: the same preset asked for in chat or by voice - `switch_model` through `switch_to` on a named lane, and the pooled lane's own `switch_model` card for Coding or Medical, exactly as before - and the Cloud row on every road. The tier table is not touched (`switch_model` stays `ask`), no request field is read for the uncarded decision, and only `install()`'s POST wrapper, after the origin and token checks, sets `owner_ui=True`. Accepted cost, stated rather than hidden: a clicked heavy preset pauses both lane models for about half a minute while its own model loads; applying another preset is the click back, and the card that used to ask was asking the same question the press already answered.

- **2026-11-16 — One GitHub repository search per language, not one query trying to cover both:** `github_search`'s plan now sends one request per (capability x language) — Kotlin and Java — instead of one query ending `language:kotlin OR language:java`. Decided because GitHub's repository search does not support `OR`: the old form answered `total_count` 0 for every idea (measured 2026-11-16: 0 for the `OR` form, 1,592 for `jarvis language:kotlin`, 1,283 for `jarvis language:java`), so the whole redundancy audit was silently empty. What it cost: one extra outbound request per capability and an approval card one line longer per capability. That is accepted on purpose — the card prints both URLs in full and says "2 request(s)", so the owner is told exactly what will leave the machine, and a shorter card would be a less honest one. One limit that follows from doubling the requests, and is recorded rather than measured: GitHub documents 10 search requests a minute without a token, so an unauthenticated plan with more than five capabilities can now reach that limit; the module already puts a failed request in its `errors` and leaves that capability "unaudited, not clear" rather than reporting it as a clear result, and that unauthenticated path is not measured here because this PC has a token configured. What it deliberately does not change: the search words are still derived locally by `terms()` and are the only payload, the `sort=stars&order=desc&per_page=10` shape and the URL quoting stay as they were, no new service or credential is involved, and the local-only rule is untouched.

- **2026-11-17 — A browser window needs its own switch, separate from "this suite may run":** the four suites that drive `jarvis_chatbot_web`'s visible launch had ONE variable, `JARVIS_ALLOW_VISIBLE_BROWSER_TESTS`, doing two jobs: it let the suite run at all, and - through the suites' own "is Playwright installed?" check - it let a window open. Those two jobs pulled in opposite directions.
