CI needs the first job (the 441 code-only checks) and must never have the second (a required check must never be able to depend on Playwright), and the required `backend-shard` job now does both of the things that used to keep them apart: it sets that variable AND installs Playwright's Chromium for `test_browser_control_live.py`. Measured 2026-11-17 on a green run: all four suites really drove a browser there (486 s, 117 s, 55 s and 12 s, against 0.3 s for a code-only suite), and a Playwright page click had timed out in that job. So the window got its own switch, `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1`, asked for BEFORE the Playwright check, and no job in `ci.yml` sets it - `backend/test_browser_test_guard.py` now fails if one ever does, so the rule is enforced rather than remembered. What it costs the owner, stated rather than hidden: running those four suites by hand to WATCH them now needs two variables instead of one, and the suite prints the second one's name when it skips (`SKIP the real-browser half: JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1 is not set ...`). What it deliberately does not change: a normal `run_suites.py` still skips all four by name (the old opt-in stays unset in the updater and in `apply-patches.ps1`), the 441 code checks still run in both required backend jobs, no route or permission moved, and the suites' code-only halves are untouched. What is not claimed: the guard covers the four suites that import `jarvis_chatbot_web`, not every backend suite that could ever launch a browser - `jarvis_browser_control.py`'s own visible default is pinned separately and this change does not widen that. **Same day, second half - the browser install itself left the required job.** A switch that stops a *window* does not stop a *browser*: `backend-shard` still installed Playwright's Chromium for `test_browser_control_live.py`, so a REQUIRED check could still launch one, and "no job sets the switch" rested on people rather than on a mechanism. The ruling is therefore that required CI must not even be ABLE to launch a browser, and the install was removed. The trade is explicit, not a dropped test: the one suite that needed it is skipped BY NAME in the required sweep when the package is absent (printed, counted, named in `SKIPPED BY NAME` - never a pass), and runs for real in a new INFORMATIONAL `backend-browser-live` job that installs Playwright and Chromium and demands the runner's `ok` line. `backend/test_browser_test_guard.py` pins that no required backend job installs Playwright, that the only two jobs which do are the required `frontend-shard` (its own page tests ARE browser tests - the exception is named, not hidden) and the informational one, and that the live-suite skip is the loud kind. What it costs, stated rather than hidden: one more informational CI job (about three minutes a run), and the live suite no longer gates a merge - its coverage is kept, its vote is not. What it deliberately does not change: nothing required gains a browser, `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER` still gates a desk run, and the desktop page tests keep their browser.

- **2026-11-17 — The phone's client build on `main` must finish, the same way `ci.yml`'s does:** `.github/workflows/jarvis-client.yml:57` cancelled unconditionally (`cancel-in-progress: true`), while `ci.yml:46` deliberately refuses to cancel on `refs/heads/main`; the owner's ruling (Gemini, 2026-11-17, Q4 - "Align `jarvis-client.yml:57` with `ci.yml:46` after P0") was to align the client workflow, and that is the whole code change: the setting the ruling named (line 61 now, after four comment lines were added above it) carries `${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, the same expression, with the comment above it saying why. **The weather it answers was measured the same day:** five merges landed between 22:13:33Z and 22:16:06Z, and the `Jarvis client` runs for the first four (`44187914586` on `c2072ce6d`, `44187942667` on `96f85a3b3`, `44187968003` on `90e818084`, `44187994856` on `2ffe919a7`) were all cancelled, so four merge commits never got a full client build; only the fifth merge (`b9325012e`, run `44188361355`) built, in 20.1 minutes. A cancelled run carries no verdict: it is neither a pass nor a failure, and it can never name the merge that broke the client - the same argument `ci.yml`'s own comment already makes for `main` never being confirmable green. **What it costs, and what it does not buy.** Pull requests still cancel their own superseded runs, because `github.ref` is `refs/pull/<n>/merge` there, so the behaviour this setting was introduced for is untouched; on `main` a build that has STARTED now always finishes, which is the loss being fixed. It does not give every merge in a burst its own build: GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group, and a newer entry replaces the pending one whatever `cancel-in-progress` says (the docs' "any previously pending job or workflow in the concurrency group will be canceled"; measured here in the same wave on `ci.yml`, whose runs for `96f85a3b3`, `90e818084` and `2ffe919a7` were each cancelled about two seconds after the next merge's run was queued, while its run for `c2072ce6d` survived an hour). So the worry that a merge wave queues an hour of client builds does not happen - at most ONE client run waits behind the one building, so the queue cannot stack up - and the honest cost is that the middle merges of a wave still get no build, not that builds pile up. **Why `self-code-map.yml:43` is NOT changed by this ruling:** it also cancels unconditionally, but it is a different kind of check - a 10-minute, informational generated-files check whose answer is about `main`'s HEAD, so only the newest run's answer means anything and superseding the older ones is the correct behaviour rather than the bug; the ruling names only `jarvis-client.yml`, and the same fix does not apply. The other two unconditional cancellers were checked and are not the same shape either: `android-apk.yml` builds on demand only (no merge wave exists to lose), and `desktop-release.yml`'s own header says whichever branch pushed last replaced the owner's download, so superseding is intended there.

- **2026-11-17 — A GitHub target GitHub does not report is REFUSED, never substituted (Q5):** every GitHub request that names a repository is now resolved against GitHub BEFORE its own request is sent — one `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}` for the repository and one `GET .../branches/{name}` for a branch a card names — and a name that is not there is refused in a sentence that prints the name, with nothing defaulted to a guessed repository and no argument on `run()` that skips it. The judgement calls the owner would care about, and why each went the way it did: (1) **REFUSE, never substitute.** GitHub answers a renamed or moved repository with a redirect, and a request could be followed or rewritten to the new name — that would act on a repository nobody named, so a 3xx and a 200 whose `full_name` differs are both refused, the second naming the other repository so the owner can choose it deliberately next time. (2) **Reads are checked too, not only writes.** The extra GET costs one round trip per action, and it buys the naming: without it a 404 on any endpoint is "there is nothing there - or it is private", which describes neither the invented name nor the model's mistake. It also makes the check uniform, so there is no "this tool is exempt" list to drift. (3) **A failure is not a missing repository.** No answer, a refused token, a 5xx or an unreadable body says *"could not check whether ... exists"* — because "there is no such repository" is a claim about GitHub that a network failure cannot support, and the same rule as BLOCKED-is-never-a-pass applies to a name. (4) **`permissions.push` false refuses an ACTION only.** That is the "it exists but it was never your intent" half, and it uses GitHub's own answer rather than the repository's owner, so an organisation repo the owner really can write to still works; a READ of that same repository stays allowed, because a GET changes nothing and refusing it would block looking at a public repository for no safety gain. Missing `permissions` (an answer that proves existence but says nothing about writing) is NOT turned into a refusal — Jarvis does not invent one from silence, and the write's own answer still decides. (5) **A file read's `ref` is not branch-checked.** That argument may be a branch, a tag or a full commit id, and `/branches/` would refuse a perfectly good commit — so the read keeps relying on GitHub's own answer for it, and only a name that is unambiguously a branch (the CI branch and the open-pull-request base) is resolved this way. (6) **The name always comes from the request; an absent name is an ASK before a card, never a default.** `_check_repo` refuses a missing name before a card exists, and says what could not be resolved. There is deliberately NO git-remote fallback: nothing in this backend has a "current workspace" the GitHub tools could read a remote from, and reading whatever folder the backend happens to run in would be the same wrong-repository failure in a different form. If the owner wants a remote-based resolver later, it needs a workspace concept of its own rather than a convenience default bolted on here. It deliberately does not add a new gate action, a new card, a new tool or a new permission: it only refuses earlier and in better words, and `github_create_repo` (which names no existing repository) is not gated. Proven by the new section of `backend/test_github_tools.py` — which fails 7 checks against the pre-fix module — and recorded in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §190.1.

- **2026-11-17 — A note's name is cut at ONE list of instruction boundaries, shared by the create and append readers:** The owner's live sentences handed Jarvis a name made of the sentence's tail: "make a note for me called Mood Log and have this be one of my favorite notes" created `Mood Log and have this be one of my favorite notes.md` with no favourite, and "add to the mood log and make a note for today and put today's date and say that ..." answered that no note was called "mood log and make a note for today and put today's date and say". The boundary list lives in ONE place, `_NOTE_NAME_BOUNDARIES` in `backend/jarvis_quick.py`, and BOTH readers use it - the create reader (`_note_title_and_rest`) and the append reader's name cut (`_note_append_name`) - so the next sentence that swallows a clause is fixed by adding one rule, never by writing a second extractor. The rules added for the owner's sentences are "and make/create ..." (an embedded create instruction) and "and have this ..." (a favourite said as a description); a bare "and" stays inside a title ("Salt and Pepper"). The description form sets the SAME separate `favorite: true` front-matter property that "favourite it" already writes, because the notes store has no other favourite concept and none was invented. The append's words after "that" stay the entry verbatim, with its commas, and the date heading comes from the turn's clock, never from a date word in the sentence. A name that is genuinely absent is still refused with "I could not find a note called ... Nothing was written" and creates nothing - the fix never turns a failed lookup into a create. Proved by `backend/test_notes_create_find_append.py` on a temporary vault.

- **2026-11-17 — One preset's model at a time, and any preset may use all three cards:** Only ONE preset's model may be loaded at a time. Applying a different preset ends the previous one first - the pooled lane is stopped and proved unloaded, or the outgoing model is replaced on the same lane - and nothing is left resident "just in case". Because no preset has to keep its own card's memory free for another preset, any preset may use all three cards where its model warrants it; that is the consequence that makes the rule useful rather than restrictive. This replaces the older design, which reserved one model per card so several could run at once and which parts of `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md` still describe in their dated sections. The rule lives in the rulebook as `CLAUDE.md`'s "One preset's model at a time", the technical statement is at the end of `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md`, and `backend/test_preset_switch_lane_guard.py` is what gives it teeth: it proves the app-click apply path will not answer `ok` when a lane holds another preset's model. The model decision this rule follows is in `decisions.d/2026-11-18-everyday-26b-three-cards.md`: General is `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` at a 32,768-token window across all three cards, and Documents and Browser keep `qwen3.5:9b` at 196,608 because those are the rows that need the long window.

- **2026-11-17 — A preset's speed is shown in the list, dated, and the cautious end of a range is the number:** The owner asked for each model preset's measured tokens a second to be visible in the preset list without opening a menu, expanding a row or hovering. `Preset.view()` in `backend/jarvis_presets.py` now fills `measured.tok_s`, `measured.tok_s_on` and `measured.tok_s_note` from the one live measurement run on this PC on 2026-11-17 (`.dsh-scratch/wave21/preset-truth/REPORT.md`, raw rows `rows.jsonl`), and `tools/gen_work_presets.py` carries it to `backend/fixtures/work_presets.json`, so the desktop HUD and the phone draw the same figure from the same builder. The desktop HUD draws `38.1 tok/s` style in the collapsed row (left rail and the Presets menu's row) and keeps the note as the tooltip; a null `tok_s` reads **not measured**. Where the run repeated a row, the apps show the LOW end of the range and the note carries the range, because a preset list that flatters itself is worse than one that is cautious. The old undated `tok_s` figures are superseded; the other keys under `measured` keep their own dated receipts.

- **2026-11-17 — A preset's measured speed is drawn on its row, and "not measured" is a real answer:** The owner asked for each model preset's measured tokens-per-second to be visible in the preset list without opening a menu. The shared preset contract only ever carried an un-dated `measured.tok_s`; the figure now gets `measured.tok_s_on` (the day it was measured) and `measured.tok_s_note` (the PC's own sentence) beside it in the one `measured` object `backend/jarvis_presets.py` `Preset.view()` builds, which is the same JSON served as `/api/work` to the phone and `/api/presets` to the desktop HUD. Both apps draw it on the row rather than behind a tap. The rule the two halves share: a missing or null `tok_s` reads as NOT MEASURED - the phone draws "Speed: not measured" - never as 0 and never as a pass; and a payload from a PC that has not been updated yet (`tok_s` and no date) still draws the number, with no day and no note, so the two pull requests can land in either order. The visible row keeps the short form (`38.1 tok/s`); the accessibility line spells the unit and the day in words, because a screen reader reads "tok/s" as "tok slash s". No route, approval card or permission changed - this is the same preset read, drawn.

- **2026-11-17 — Note edits stay at tier `ask` and get a `("yes", "local")` risk row, and the unclassified warning says what the gate does rather than what the action is:** `edit_vault_note` is the one action the whole Obsidian editor raises (a whole-note save, an append, a tag change and a carded create), and it had a tier line but no `_RISK` row, so every one of its cards carried the unclassified fallback - which said the action was "treated as permanent and able to leave this PC". The reach half is plainly false: `jarvis_notes_edit` touches no network, no model and no token, by its own docstring and its own routes. The undo half is false too: before a save, an append or a tag change it calls `jarvis_notes.snapshot_vault_before_write()`, and if the File Guardian copy cannot be made NOTHING is written; a carded create records its undo receipt before the file exists and that undo removes exactly the one file. So the comparable rows are `create_logseq_page` (`("yes", "local")`, "delete it and it is gone") rather than `edit_joplin_note`/`edit_logseq_page` (`("hard", "local")`, "the previous text is gone unless you version that vault") - what makes those two "hard" is exactly what the Guardian copy here prevents. **EDITS STAY AT `ask`, AND THE ROW DOES NOT LOWER A TIER:** `edit_vault_note = "ask"` stays in both shipped settings copies, `check()` still raises the one card per save, and the contract that promises that card, the File Guardian copy and the Undo is untouched. `auto` is acceptable only for owner-typed or voice NEW-note creation through the HUD (the card-free create path of #1322/#1342, which never reaches this action's card at all); an edit, an overwrite or a property change keeps its card because the owner was promised one. The row's consequences are the ordinary ones of a classified local, reversible change and they are accepted on purpose: a swipe may now approve an edit (that is what `swipe_ok` means for "yes"/"local") and "What asks first" may offer its switch, because the treatment is now a written decision instead of the unclassified action's maximum friction. **WHERE IT LIVES: the published base's end of file, never a patch.** The row is in an end-of-file `_RISK.update({...})` block in `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py`, because every line inside the literal is some earlier patch's hunk context and the end of the file is the one region no patch claims (the owner's 2026-11-14 ruling). The same reasoning applies to the wording: `UNCLASSIFIED_WARNING`'s definition sits inside `backend/unknown-risk-approvable.patch`'s own hunk, so it is reworded by a second end-of-file override (`UNCLASSIFIED_WARNING = ("Unclassified action - never runs on its own, and a swipe cannot approve it")` plus `_UNKNOWN_RISK` rebuilt from it) and that patch is NOT edited - the base still reverses it out and re-applies it byte for byte. The old line printed the gate's own worst-case record as a fact about the action; the new one says what actually happens (it never runs on its own, and no swipe decides it). The record (`"no"`/`"outbound"`, so `swipe_ok` False, still forced to `"ask"`) is untouched, so a beginning developer reading the card is told what happens, and is never told something the action cannot do.

- **2026-11-18 — A claim that a card was raised is answered by the turn's own card count, and the correction states what is true rather than only denying it:** a new claim family in `jarvis_claims` (`card_claim`, `card_correction`) was added after the field test measured four replies telling the owner "I have raised the approval card" while `GET /api/pending` was empty before and after the turn (DEF-089). The judgement calls, each made against that measurement: (1) **the backing is `_TurnWatch.cards`, not the pending list and not the model's words.** A claim about a card in this answer can only be backed by what this answer raised, so the count the per-turn card budget is already enforced with is reused; there is no list of card ids and none is needed, because a count of one settles it. (2) **`jarvis_gate.pending()` never backs a claim, only chooses the wording.** A card this turn raised has already been answered by the time the answer is finalized, so the live list cannot prove a card was raised; it exists in this check for two reasons only - the correction may say "nothing is waiting for your approval" only when the list really is empty, and a card already waiting from elsewhere leaves the answer alone, because the owner is then not waiting for a card that will never come. (3) **an unreadable turn is never guessed at.** `cards=None` means the caller cannot tell and nothing is corrected; the cloud lane passes an explicit `0` because a cloud lane offers no tools at all and cannot raise a card - a known zero, not an unknown. (4) **the correction must teach, not only contradict.** It says no card was raised in this answer, that (when known) nothing is waiting, that no card was shown in it, and names the one next step - ask again in a new message - because a bare "I did not raise a card" tells the owner nothing true about the state they are in. (5) **the mechanism is the existing one.** The line rides `postscript_lines` / `_claim_corrections` as kind `claim` - the list the local answer and the cloud relay both append - rather than a second checker; the turn's card count reaches it through the same holder that already carries the conversation id for the web-search grant claim. (6) **the exemptions are the module's own, so no honest sentence is corrected:** question, offer, future, condition, negation, "earlier/already", quoted text and code spans are left alone, and one answer gets one line rather than one per sentence - this module's standing rule is that a missed claim is cheaper than a wrong correction. This is a bug fix with no permission, route or approval-tier change: the card itself, its risk wording, its Windows Hello rule and the per-turn card limit are exactly as they were. What this does NOT settle, recorded so the close is not read as larger than it is: the same measured reply also said "This is just a field test - no cards go through right now" on the turn that did raise a card, and that mirror claim (denying cards work while one existed) is a different direction, not corrected here; and a phrasing outside the patterns still slips through, which the module accepts deliberately.

- **2026-11-18 — A card that cannot say what it would change must not be approvable, and the detail is the field that says it:** the owner was shown a live `change_own_config` card about his cloud settings with no detail and a normal Approve, and the desktop HUD had the same shape with "(no detail)" as its body. The judgement calls, all taken from that measured card: (1) **The DETAIL is what the rule reads, not the notice.** `notice.summary`/`notice.full` are built from the action NAME and the risk table by `jarvis_gate.notice_for` - safe by construction on a lock screen - so they can say "change one of its settings" but never which setting or to what. Treating a readable notice as "the card is described" would have left the measured blank cheque passing. (2) **The renderer stopped deleting a detail it can put in words.** `normalisePendingRow` had removed `detail` when it matched the `summary` it derived from the same text; that was true when the card drew `item.summary`, and stopped being true when approval cards read short (c08d768a1, 2026-10-10) began drawing the PC's `notice.summary` instead. One line of text now appears twice on an opened card whose command is also its fallback summary - accepted, because losing the words the owner is agreeing to is the blank cheque. (3) **Refresh REPLACES Approve, rather than a disabled Approve.** DEF-010's lesson (a faded control captioned by a line nobody connects to it reads as a bug) and the ruling that refusing is never held: the card draws Deny on the left exactly as before, and a Refresh that re-reads the waiting queue (a read: approves nothing, never held by a stale link) where Approve would be. (3b) **The notification surface follows the card.** `ApprovalNotificationPolicy` already replaces Approve with Review in Jarvis when its words are redacted or too long; a card whose detail did not arrive is the same case (its notice words name the action, not the change), so it gets Review and Deny there and is never approved sight-unseen; the widget never offers Approve at all (it opens the app), so it needed nothing. (4) **Both apps, one copy of the words.** The phone's `net/CardDetail.kt` and the desktop HUD draw the same sentence and the same action label, and both come from `backend/jarvis_card_words.py`'s `NO_DETAIL` / `REFRESH` through `tools/gen_card_words_cases.py` into each app's contract fixture - the same one-source mechanism `TIMED_OUT` and `BUTTONS` already use; the HUD page cannot import a module, so its own constants are pinned to the module by `tests/card-words.mjs`. (5) **What did NOT change:** the backend's payload, the gate, any tier, route or decision path, the two apps' button order, and the phone's behaviour on every card that has a detail. A card that genuinely carries no detail loses its Approve on both screens - that is the decision, not a side effect.

- **2026-11-18 — a capability row's own name in an ordinary question shape beats a settings lane:** The cloud-settings question lane may answer only sentences that name the setting itself - the escalation SWITCH ("is escalation on?", "what does escalation actually do?", "what can go to the cloud?") or a spend/provider fact - and must never claim a catalogue row's own name used in an ordinary question shape. Two questions proved why on 2026-11-18: "what is cloud escalation?" (the `cloud-escalation` row's id words in "What is X?") and "does jarvis escalate to the cloud?" (its "escalate to the cloud" alias in "Does Jarvis X?") are feature questions, not reads of the switch's state, and both belong to the catalogue row (#1379's sweep required `cloud-escalation 65/65`). The lane is now narrow at the two regexes themselves: the compound "cloud escalation" is not a valid subject for a "what is" question, and the "will you send ... to the cloud" shape requires the WHAT that goes up. This restores the lane's own documented rule ("every feature question keeps the path it had") rather than adding a new earlier matcher; #1379's exact-name lane is untouched because it never sees these two shapes.

- **2026-11-18 — A local turn is never refused for a model choice the router can fix: the lane's own model answers, and the HUD must run that fallback locally:** after the owner's PC produced no answer at all to a private question (gate `taint`, `where: local`) because `model-state.json` named the pooled three-card coder as the everyday model and `jarvis_agent.local_model_refusal` honestly refused to load it on a one-card lane, the ruling is that the model CHOICE is the router's to get right, while the spill refusal itself is untouched. The judgement calls, each made against the measurement: (1) **validate before the turn, against the lane it will really use.** `choose()` asks `jarvis_agent.local_model_refusal` - the very check `run_local_turn` makes before sending anything - with the lane address the HUD itself will use (`jarvis_presets.active_chat_url`, falling back to `OLLAMA_URL`), so router and agent cannot disagree about whether the turn is answerable. (2) **no second copy of "which models are pooled".** The refusal's own `_pooled_model_name` decides which refusal a different model can fix, and the lane tables (`jarvis_big_coder.LANES` by port), the owner's `[intelligence] default_model`, and finally the everyday lane's own row decide the replacement; no model name is typed in the router. (3) **only the fixable class is substituted.** A cloud model named as the local model, or a lane address on another machine, is refused exactly as before - another model cannot answer for a lane that is not this PC, and swapping there would answer a question the refusal is not asking. A fallback that would itself be refused is not used either; the honest refusal then stands rather than a second invalid choice being made. (4) **the route detail must make it diagnosable.** The model asked for, the model really used and the refusal's own words ride in the EXISTING `degraded_from` field (the HUD already carries that key for a cloud lane stepping down), the reason names both models, and the field is omitted entirely on an ordinary turn - tonight this took an hour to trace because the header said `lane: <model>` with no hint it was a saved choice. (5) **a router-only change must never ship, and this is the important one.** The HUD decides "local" as `lane == local_model`; a fallback model name made `use_tools` false and sent the turn to the plain relay, and `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` maps an UNKNOWN lane name to a CLOUD provider (its `DEFAULT_LANE` is DeepSeek - measured: `lane_service("qwen3.5:9b")` answers `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")`). With a saved provider key that is a private prompt leaving the PC: rule 1 broken by a fix meant to protect the owner. So the same PR carries `local-model-guard.patch`, ONE line in `jarvis_hud.py` (`use_tools = ((lane == local_model or decision.inject_memory) and _agent_ok)`); `inject_memory` is the signal because every local decision carries it and no cloud decision does, and a new `Decision` flag would be a second thing to keep in step. (6) **the cloud half is untouched.** A cloud turn is not pulled local, even when the saved local model is a pooled one; the fallback only ever replaces a model on a decision that is already local. (7) **the lane's address is ASKED FOR, never read from the environment.** The router needs the lane address to check the model against it, and it asks `jarvis_models.ollama_url_on_this_pc()` - the one checked resolver #1360 (merged 2026-11-18) put every Ollama address read behind. That suite fails any SECOND direct read of `OLLAMA_URL` in the published base, and it caught this PR's first attempt through a red required shard; the rule is now, in one sentence, **no base module reads `OLLAMA_URL` directly, ever - ask the resolver.** This is a bug fix: no new route, no new card, no tier and no change to what may be sent anywhere. What this does NOT close, recorded so it is not read as larger than it is: `lane_service()` mapping an unknown name to a cloud provider is still reachable from any caller that hands an arbitrary lane name to the plain relay (the HUD's manual-pick path being the one this session could see); the narrowest safe changes would be the HUD asking `lane_state` only for a lane in its own cloud-lane list, or `lane_service` answering nothing for an unknown name - neither was made here, because both need their own measured change rather than a quiet one inside this fix. And PR #1361, merged 2026-11-18, closes the other half of tonight's cause, the preset apply that SAVED a pooled model as the everyday current model in the first place.

- **2026-11-18 — A feature question that quotes an exact catalogue name is that row's question, before any family that shares one word:** The CHAT-GAPS audit left 14 of the owner's 180 measured capability questions missing (166/180 after PR #1377), and four of those answered the WRONG catalogue row - a confident sentence about a different ability, which is worse than a miss. Each of the 14 already said its row's own exact title or alias; no catalogue alias could fix them, because a generic family with one shared word claimed the sentence before the capability lane ran: "interrupt you" is the stop-everything safety phrase; "called" stems to "call" and with "phone" names call-recording; "start ... local model" outscored the quoted restart row; "sound", "reminder", "ring", "read" and "goal" sent the rest elsewhere. **The ruling: an explicit feature question that quotes a row's EXACT catalogue name is that row's question, and it is answered before the generic families** - in one narrow lane (`_named_feature_question`) that takes only exact equality of a row's id, title or alias (never a shared word, a substring or a loose find), placed before `_cap_safety_question` and the reminder / goal / feature-guide / read-a-link families. A shared word may outrank a quoted name nowhere; the priority is the owner's own naming of the feature. The row that used to win each shared word keeps its own question (call-recording, start-the-model-lane, reminder-asks, stop-everything and phone-notifications are pinned), and the audit's three traps stay closed: "can you write a nice email for my boss?" -> None (the writer's path), "Can you send a file to my phone?" -> None (the real tool path), "Can you add 2 and 3?" -> None. Also fixed the exact-name lookup itself: it now tries the question's raw words as well as the spoken normalisation, because "out loud" -> "aloud" (which finds read-aloud) hid another row whose own title literally says "out loud" (read-web-page). Measured with the real matcher: 180/180 measured questions (176/180 with the harness tail kept), and a 5,410-question sweep over every row's aliases, titles and id words in 35 ordinary shapes changed 53 answers, gained 47, regressed 0, on both trees.

- **2026-11-18 — The audit job installs the backend job's Python test dependencies:** Decided 2026-11-18, after PR #1366's `audit` job went red on a real check that the required `backend` job runs. `tools/check_claims.py` lives in `audit` and runs every suite a `test:` row names, so its Python must be the `backend` job's Python: a missing package makes a suite skip, and a skip is never a pass, so the claim reads as a broken BUILD even though nothing regressed. The `audit` job's pip line is therefore now the same package list at the same pinned versions as `backend-shard`'s, and the two are updated together. This is an environment fix, not a relaxation: `tools/check_claims.py` is unchanged, a skipped check still withholds proof, and the Windows-only checks that genuinely cannot run on the Linux runner stay skipped and stay named on every run. Cost was measured before deciding: the install takes 5.6 s on the runner, and the claims step grows only by the checks the packages unlock.

- **2026-11-18 — A capability question is answered from the catalogue, and a "shown, opened or sent" claim has to be backed by the turn that made it:** the owner's own phone ask, *"Can you send a file for me to my PC?"*, was answered *"I can't send files directly"* while the catalogue row `document-from-phone` held the steps and the alias "send a file from my phone to my pc". The judgement calls, each kept narrow on purpose: (1) **"Can you ..." is still not a general capability lead.** It is how the owner asks Jarvis to DO things, and `backend/test_chat_honesty.py` pins that "can you write a nice email for my boss?" and "can you help me create a plan" keep their own paths. The ONE shape this matcher takes is a file transfer toward THIS PC — the measured sentence, and the only direction no tool of ours can start (the phone's own Settings picks the file), so claiming it takes no action away from the model. "Can you send a file to my phone" stays with the model, because `send_file_to_phone` is a real tool that raises its one card. (2) **Direction is evidence, not a veto.** `_cap_resolve` used to return None when the highest-scoring row was the opposite direction; that was right while the catalogue had one file row, and wrong once 2026-11-15 added the phone→PC aliases: `file-from-pc` still wins the score because its id says "file from pc", and it must LOSE to the direction-correct row, never silence it. When no row has the question's direction there is still no honest catalogue answer and the question falls through as before. A question that says "to my PC" now also rejects a row whose own words send "to your phone"; before, only "from my phone" did. (3) **The owner's measured words belong in the catalogue, not in the matcher.** "send a file for me to my pc" was added to `features/features.json` and the generated catalogue was regenerated; an exact match of the question's content words against one of a row's own aliases names that row (function words and order ignored), which is deterministic and is the same route PR #1208 used for earlier measured sentences. (4) **A "shown/opened/sent" claim is corrected in the existing postscript shape, not by a second mechanism.** `jarvis_claims.surface_correction` reads the model's words plus THIS turn's tool steps — the same contract as `unbacked_claim` and `schedule_correction` — and returns ONE line for `backend/jarvis_agent.postscript_lines`, which the local answer and the cloud relay already share. It is backed only by tools that really show/open something (`retirement_whatif` writes its table on the owner's screen by code, `product_check` opens a page in his browser, `conversation_open` opens a kept conversation, and the acting tools that click or type in a real window/app) or really send something (email, a text, the one file to the phone, a GitHub write — a draft is not a send). A question, an offer, a future sentence and anything "already"/"earlier" are exempt, and "I've sent it"/"The file has been sent." stay with the checks that already read them, so one sentence never gets two correction lines. (5) **Nothing gated changed.** No route, no card, no auto-approval, no state read: reading a catalogue is not a gated action, and both fixes answer only a turn no action path had already claimed. The honest limit is written here rather than implied: the catalogue is answered deterministically, but any capability sentence that still resolves to no row keeps the model, and the claim guard corrects words AFTER they were streamed — it does not stop the model from writing them.

- **2026-11-18 — A capability question is claimed by the last lane, in the question's own words, and "can you" is never a generic lead:** The CHAT-GAPS audit measured two numbers that decide this: 74 of 183 catalogue rows are reachable only by quoting an exact name, and "Can you ...?" reaches the catalogue for only 18 of 183 rows - while the local model, which answers what the deterministic layer does not claim, has been measured denying real features ("I can't send files directly"). Two changes follow. **First, the "and" short-circuit in `_explicit_feature_question` is removed.** It returned None before `_FEAT_EXPLICIT` was tried, so every feature question whose subject contains "and" went to the model - 49 catalogue rows, and all six measured owner questions that still fell through. It protected nothing: `_cap_multi_question` already ran earlier inside `_cap_question`, and this lane runs last in `match()` after every action matcher, so a sentence another path owned was never reachable there. The same function now also takes the speaker's frame ("a feature that lets you ...") off the subject, because without that the two of the six that start "lets you/lets Jarvis" became a deterministic "I do not have that one" - still wrong about a row that exists. **Second, three measured false-denial questions are answered from their row, and the mechanism is deliberately narrow.** "Can you send a file from my PC to my phone?" (`file-from-pc`, the mirror of the one-way `_CAP_CAN_YOU_TO_PC`), "Can you read my phone notifications?" (`phone-notifications`, with its off-by-default state) and "Can you add up my spending?" / "Can you check my bank export?" (`spending`) each get a named lead, checked only in `_explicit_feature_question` - the lane that runs after every action matcher - so it cannot take an action path. **A generic "can you ..." capability lead was rejected, and the audit measured why:** it would newly reach 131 rows but would also claim "Can you write a nice email for my boss?" as `email-send`, a sentence `backend/test_chat_honesty.py` pins to the writer's own path. Each lead therefore is only the words of the ONE question it serves, and every widened lead ships with a negative control that must keep the path it had before. **What is deliberately not fixed, and why:** 14 of the 21 measured misses remain. Each is either claimed by another deterministic lane before this one (the reminder family, `read_link`, `goal_capability`, `stop-everything`) or resolves through a neighbouring row inside `_cap_resolve` (attention-budget, also-on-phone/phone-apps, restart-the-model-lane). Those live in functions this PR must not touch - `backend/jarvis_quick.py` is in another lane's diff and the collision rule keeps this change to `_explicit_feature_question` and the `_CAP_*` leads - so they are recorded as the next fix, never claimed as closed. Measured with the real matcher: the six fall-throughs now reach their rows, 7 of 21 measured misses close, and a 4,488-sentence before/after sweep shows 80 newly resolved sentences, two wrong-row fixes (`phone-notifications` -> `phone-apps`) and no action path changed.

- **2026-11-18 — A catalogue row that names a PC-only place must name the phone's own place:** The 2026-11-18 phone awareness audit measured 32 `both` feature rows whose `where` named only a PC Brain tab (`Brain, Work`, `Brain, Memory`, `Brain, Now`, `Brain, Model`, `Brain, Projects`, `Brain, History`) and six more that sent the owner to a Settings card his phone does not draw. The phone's Brain is one scroll with seven headings ("Waiting for you", "What Jarvis knows about you", "What Jarvis is doing", "Money and time", "Your projects and goals", "Your learning", "Jarvis on your PC") and no tabs, so those sentences were honest on the desktop and a dead end in his hand. The catalogue's words now carry both apps' real places in one sentence (`PC: Brain, Work, Today. Phone: Brain, Money and time, Today.`) and say plainly when the phone has no screen for something rather than inventing one. `surface` is `both` only where the phone genuinely draws the feature: `reminder-actions` and `email-drafts` (the phone shows the note and answers the card; the PC writes the file) and `chatbot-money` (the phone reads the spend and the limit; the keys and limits are the PC's, so its label stays PC-Only Setting). A row whose full page is the PC's - `memory-known`, whose by-topic list with the filter box is the desktop's Memory page per `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 - stays `desktop` with its reason, and its `where` now names the phone's same-named heading so the two are not confused. The rule is machine-checked, not a convention: `tools/check_feature_list.py` rule 10 reads the phone's real places from `BrainSections.kt`, `ui/OpenPlace.kt` and `SettingsScreen.kt`, and `backend/test_feature_list.py` holds the five rows the audit ranked most likely to them. No route, screen or behaviour changed; the sources are `features/features.json` (three identical copies) and `contract/feature-controls.json`, and the generated consumers are regenerated by their generators, never hand-edited. This replaces writing `where` from the desktop's own screens alone.

- **2026-11-18 — A claimed suite that exits 0 having passed no check withholds proof from its claim, unless its whole body is a documented environment skip:** the external review's ruling, and the last place a skip could hide. `tools/check_claims.py` read only the skips a suite prints, so a suite that exited 0 having run nothing printed no skip and read as proof - the exact shape the register exists to prevent. The checker now applies `backend/run_suites.py`'s zero-check rule (`passed == 0` is a failure, no allowlist, 2026-10-27) to the one caller that did not run it (`audit` runs the register, and the runner's rule does not run in `audit`), and it takes the counts from the runner's own parser (`run_suites.counts`) rather than a second parser that could drift; this is one mechanism reaching one more caller, not a new one. The ruling's other half is kept: a suite whose whole body is skipped for a documented limit of this machine is the `ENVIRONMENT_SKIPS` case, not a hole, but it must show both halves - the suite's path keyed in `ENVIRONMENT_SKIPS` AND a skip it really printed that the allow-list accepts. An entry records why a skip happened; it cannot document a skip that never happened, so it must not turn a silent suite back into proof. The skip rule itself is unchanged (a printed skip is never a pass), a skip beside checks that really ran is unchanged, and the run now prints how many checks the `test:` rows reported so a green register says what it watched.

- **2026-11-18 — A degrade step may only land on a lane the code has, and the update tool may rewrite that one stale value:** `jarvis_router.degrade()` used to return the next name in `[budget] degrade_chain` whatever it was, and the owner's live file still named `jarvis-bulk` and `jarvis-critic` - two cloud lanes the owner's 2026-10-27 decision removed from the code. The consequence was not a crash but three real cloud attempts where one was intended: `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` maps an unknown lane name to the CHOSEN cloud service, so a 429 on `jarvis-escalate` stepped to "jarvis-bulk", then "jarvis-critic", each a second and third request to the same provider with the same key - and the lane that finally answered was not in the caller's lane list, so `jarvis_hud`'s `if lane in lanes: budget.spend()` did not count the call, and the per-minute/per-day budget that exists to absorb rate limits could be walked around by them. **The decision:** `degrade()` filters the configured chain to the lane names this module can actually serve (`cloud_lanes()` of the caller's own list) plus the local model as the floor, and drops anything else rather than substituting a name; local is still checked first and is still the unconditional bottom. **And the file itself is corrected rather than left lying:** `backend/_apply_toml_tiers.py` - already the one script `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` runs on every update because it is the one thing allowed to write this file - now also replaces a `[budget] degrade_chain` that names something outside the shipped chain and the configured local model (`[intelligence] default_model`) with the shipped chain, preserving every other byte and the line endings, with one backup first and a refusal instead of a guess when the key is absent or written over several lines; an empty chain or one naming the owner's local model is his choice and is left alone. That is a deliberate, narrow exception to the tool's "never touch a key the owner already has" rule, and it is limited to a value that names something the code does not have - a stale schema, not a preference. The router half reaches the owner's PC on the same backend update (a shipped module); the configuration half reaches it through the script the update already runs, and `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` now says a line of his settings file was corrected instead of changing it silently.

- **2026-11-18 — The hybrid/cloud settings are asked about and changed from chat, and no answer claims more than a file says:** the owner asked to be able to ask Jarvis through the phone's chat what the cloud provider and escalation settings are and to change them ("i should be able to ask jarvis through chat on phone to change the provider and adjust these particular settings and get clarity"). The decision has three parts. **(1) The questions are deterministic reads of three files, never the model:** `jarvis_cloud_settings.py` (a new module, shipped whole, called by `jarvis_quick.py`'s fast path) answers "which cloud provider am I using?", "am I on cloud?", "is escalation on?", "will you send things to the cloud by yourself?", "what's my cap?", "how much have I spent this month?" and "what does escalation actually do?" from `cloud-choice.json`, `escalate-cloud.json` and `chatbot\api-money.json`, naming the file and its last-saved date in every sentence, and saying "not set up" in plain words with its meaning when a file is missing - which replaces the old behaviour where several of these went to the model (or to the apps-only spending door) and could be answered from a guess. The answer to what escalation does always carries the refusal list the router enforces (email, files, notes, credentials, stored memory, a picture, the screen, a private question, a pasted secret, a conversation that has read outside text) and the gates that still stop a turn. **(2) The changes add no second mechanism:** the service goes through `jarvis_presets.apply_cloud` (the Presets Cloud row's ONE `change_own_config` card), the standing switch through `jarvis_presets.cloud_escalate` (ON is one card and nothing is written before the yes; OFF is instant and cardless - the existing rule kept unchanged), and the monthly cap through `jarvis_chatbot_limits.change`, the exact function behind `POST /api/chatbot/money` - so the question "can the cap be changed from chat?" is answered by an existing route: a raise is ONE `raise_api_limit` card (tier ask, Windows Hello on the PC or the asking phone's own fingerprint) and writes nothing before the yes, while a lowering is cardless because it only ever spends less. A provider name the PC does not know is refused with the list read from `jarvis_chatbot_api.PRESETS`, and a known name is left to the older cloud-provider door so the two doors cannot compete for one sentence. **(3) The hook is small and in one place:** one matcher call in `jarvis_quick.match()` beside the other cloud/capability answers, one runner block, and two dispatch lines; the read answers are in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS` and `_PRIVATE_DETERMINISTIC_READS`, the change is deliberately not. Stated limits, so nobody reads more into it: the chat answers are read fresh on every call and never cached; "not set up" (no file) and "cannot be read" (a broken file) are different sentences because deleting a file forgets a setting while a broken one must not read as off; no key is ever read (the module never touches `key_saved` or Credential Manager); and the phone needs no client change because the answers and cards ride `/api/chat`. Proof: `backend/test_cloud_settings_chat.py`; docs: `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 229.
