The measured incident: the deploy at `b8de6ef15` reported `RESULT: PASS - backend reconciled` and minutes later the live app answered `GET /api/presets` with 503 and `AttributeError: module 'jarvis_models' has no attribute 'ollama_url_on_this_pc'`. The shipped modules were byte-current; the live `jarvis_models.py` is one of the five patched base files the deploy deliberately never carries, and its copy dated from 2026-10-19, before the published base gained that function in #1360 - so the call raised. The owner repaired it by hand (a documented shim with a `.before-gaprepair-20261118-2015` backup) and the repository must not depend on that repair. So step 2c derives every unguarded name the shipped `.py` modules call on the five patched base files and proves the TARGET folder's copy binds each one - a static `hasattr` (the target source is parsed, never imported: importing live modules would execute them, and a dry run must not). A missing name refuses exit 2 before any write, naming the module, the function and the patch that owns the file; the two ways out are deliberate: apply the patch stack (`scripts/apply-patches.ps1 -BackendPath <live>`) or record the gap by repairing that one live file by hand under a backup. Rejected alternatives: making the deploy carry `jarvis_models.py` (copying the published base over the live patched copy would lose `gpu-offload.patch`'s applied hunks) and requiring a `try/except` fallback in every caller (the shipped modules own their fallbacks; only unguarded calls are requirements, so a compatibility probe like `jarvis_gate.tier_of()` inside `try/except` is not refused). The declared floor is `CROSS_FILE_DEPENDENCIES`, pinned to the shipped modules' derivation by `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py`; each deploy re-derives from the ref's bytes so the list cannot silently go stale. Proved: `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` builds the tonight shape from `jarvis-backend/` by deleting the function (refusal, exit 2, nothing written, no backup folder) and proves the correct base passes in a dry run and an apply.

- **2026-11-18 — The desktop release path is repaired where #1319 broke it, with the strict install kept:** one merge broke the release two ways, and the second was hidden behind the first. (1) #1319 added the bindings pilot's `typescript ^5.9.3` devDependency to `jarvis-desktop/package.json` without regenerating `jarvis-desktop/package-lock.json`; the release workflow's `npm ci` - the only place that reads the lockfile - then refused every main merge from #1319's own merge (`8858a2db8`, 2026-11-16 22:56Z) through #1375 (2026-11-18 17:05Z), all eight with the same `npm error Missing: typescript@5.9.3 from lock file`, so the rolling `desktop-latest` release stayed at 0.2.465 from `589ba09`. (`main` carries eight such runs, not the seven the brief names: #1319, #1332, #1358, #1359, #1365, #1367, #1368 and #1375. A ninth, #1361, was cancelled by the workflow's own `cancel-in-progress` concurrency when the next merge arrived 90 seconds later, so it never reached `npm ci`.) The lockfile was regenerated with the desktop's own package manager, `npm install --package-lock-only` on npm 12.0.2 / Node 22.23.2: 16 lines added, 1 line changed, no dependency version moved. (2) The first `Desktop release` run that got past `npm ci` - a `workflow_dispatch` on the fix branch, run `44403718039` - then died in `npx tauri build` with `failed to find main binary, make sure you have a package > default-run in the Cargo.toml file`: the same #1319 added `src-tauri/src/bin/export_bindings.rs`, so Cargo now has two `[[bin]]` targets and `tauri build` will not guess which is the app. `Cargo.toml` names it, `default-run = "jarvis-desktop"`, which is the fix that error itself asks for; the exporter still runs by name (`cargo run --bin export_bindings`) and nothing else changes. Three things were deliberately left alone. (1) `npm ci` stays `npm ci` - switching to `npm install` would hide the drift the strict install exists to surface, and the strict install is exactly what failed. (2) The workflow's pins (`node-version: "22"`, the action SHAs) are current and not the cause: the runner's npm 10.9.9 installs from the fixed lockfile cleanly, and no workflow change is owed. (3) No new gate was added to required CI even though a lockfile-sync or `tauri build` check would have caught these before merge - the required `frontend` job never runs `npm ci` (it only runs `npm install --no-save playwright`) and only `Desktop release` runs `tauri build`; adding such a gate belongs in its own CI change, not inside a release repair. Until it exists the release workflow itself is the gate, and these nine red runs are the evidence that it fires.

- **2026-11-18 — One preset, one model, one lane: the everyday 26B takes the pooled three-card lane and the second coding lane is retired:** The owner's words are "i dont need a separate coding lane on any preset. each preset should be dedicated to one preset local ai model." So each preset names exactly one model and exactly one lane, the everyday model is `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` at a **32,768**-token window across ALL THREE cards, and the separate coding lane on port 11435 is retired. THE LANE WAS RULED ON BY EXTERNAL REVIEW THE SAME DAY: General must NOT sit on the everyday lane on 11436, because that lane is pinned by its Windows logon task to the single 12 GB RTX 2060 and a 15.50 GiB model there guarantees a spill into system RAM (measured live on 2026-11-18: 15.8 GB resident with only 9.1 GB on the card). General therefore joins the other heavy presets on the **pooled lane** (11450) as `heavy_mode=True, mode="gemma4-26b-a4b"` - the pooled lane already sees all three cards, so the owner gets the model he chose with no change to his PC - and **the everyday lane is NOT retired, because Documents & Notes and Browser & Forms keep `qwen3.5:9b` at 196,608 tokens there** (Fast and Agentic + Vision use it at 16,384); that is why it still exists. THE MODEL AND WINDOW WERE CHOSEN ON QUALITY, NOT SPEED: a blind eight-task battery on this PC on 2026-11-17 scored the 26B 22/24, the 12B 21/24, the 35B 21/24 and the old everyday 9B last at 19/24 with the only app-breaking failure in the run (`.dsh-scratch/wave21/quality-battery/REPORT.md`). MEASURED on this PC on 2026-11-17 ON THE POOLED LANE across all three cards at 32,768 tokens (`.dsh-scratch/wave21/preset-truth/REPORT.md`, every raw row in `rows.jsonl` beside it): **15.501 GiB resident, 14.820 GiB in the cards' memory, 0.681 GiB (4.4%) spilled, 25.4-36.5 tok/s with the LOW end 25.4 as the preset's figure, and a 49.9 s cold load.** THE EARLIER 196,608-token HEADLINE DID NOT REPRODUCE: it claimed 0.92 GiB spilled and 46.10 tok/s, and the same run measured the same model at 196,608 across the pool at 17.501 GiB loaded, 2.385 GiB spilled and 21.2 tok/s, so 32,768 is the shipped window. Fast moved from the retired coding lane to the everyday lane at 16,384. This supersedes the 2026-10-18 presets and the two-lane shape they inherited: `jarvis_presets.LANES` has `main` (11436, the RTX 2060) and `pooled` (11450, all three cards) only, and `jarvis_big_coder.LANES` holds one entry - the everyday lane's `qwen3.5:9b` at 196,608, zero spill on restore - so nothing pauses, restores or starts a second single-card lane. A heavy preset's OWN measured spill is allowed by the pooled mode row the apply's lane read-back uses (`_preset_spill_allowance`: General/Reflective Coach 0.68 GiB, Pictures & Screens 2.24 GiB, Coding/Medical 0), so General's measured 0.681 GiB does not fail its own apply while a worse load still does. **The same tag is also Reflective Coach's pooled model at the same 32,768 window** (from #1358), and General now runs the same measured pooled mode, so the two presets share ONE mode row - acceptable because only one preset's model is loaded at a time; `is_pooled_model()` refuses every pooled model on the everyday lane again, including General's, because the exemption that let it run there went with the lane ruling. **The medical advocate was a consequence nobody had noticed:** it hard-coded `medgemma1.5:4b-it-q4_K_M` on the retired 11435 lane, so the retirement would have broken its default silently; it now asks `jarvis_models.current_model()` and the lane table at call time and types neither a model nor a port. THE LIVE MACHINE IS NOT CHANGED AND DOES NOT NEED TO BE: the everyday logon task keeps exactly the 9B lane it runs today, and the pooled lane is started on demand by the app. `backend/test_presets_lanes.py` pins the presets to `jarvis_big_coder.LANES`, `backend/test_preset_switch_lane_guard.py` proves a lane holding two presets' models is a failed apply, and the stale "one lane per GPU" advice in `recommendations()` was the text that kept the old layout looking necessary - it is replaced with the one-preset-at-a-time rule.

- **2026-11-18 — The favourite flag becomes a resolver tier, asked last, and it selects a note without showing its words:** the owner's `favorite: true` front matter was written on create and by a carded `set_property` edit, and exactly one reader consumed it - the yes/no "is my X note favourited?" answer - so "add this to my favourite note, especially if I made them my favorite" resolved nothing at all. This is the first behaviour that flag has. **The four judgement calls:** (1) **It is a fourth tier in the ONE resolver, not a second resolver** - `path -> basename -> alias -> favourite`, added where `RESOLVE_TIERS` is stated and consumed, so every note tool that already routes through `jarvis_notes.resolve_note` gets it and no door grows its own idea of a name. (2) **It sits LAST** because a favourite is a DESCRIPTION of a note, never its name: any explicit vault path, file name or note `aliases:` value was already asked and won, so a favourite can never override the owner naming a note, and the tier can only turn a would-be refusal into a choice after every real name tier has said no. (3) **It fires only on the favourite words themselves** - "favourite"/"favorite" and their plurals and short forms, which is what `_note_key` leaves after it drops "my/the/a/an" and a trailing "note" - so a plain note question ("garden bucket", "favourite colour") keeps its old refusal and a favourite is never picked for it; the flag is not a fallback for an unknown name. (4) **None is an honest refusal and never a create:** with no flagged note the answer names what was looked for, and `create_target` returns that same refusal even when `create_target_if_missing` is True, because describing an existing note must never produce a new note called `favourite.md`. Two spellings are read (`favorite` and the British `favourite`, so a hand-written note counts) but only the US one is ever written; the value must be true-ish and must be a top-level key inside a front matter that CLOSES, the same rules the chat's own flag reader used on 2026-11-17 when an unclosed block answered "Yes, pinned" for a property the note did not have. **What was deliberately NOT done, and stays a separate change:** the favourite's content is not put in a prompt, nothing ranks or filters by the flag, `/api/notes/list` and both plates are untouched, and no route, card or approval was added - reading a vault is not a gated action. This PR is selection; "favourites as context" is recall, and it is not this PR.

- **2026-11-18 — Uncensored models live only on `general_uncensored`, and General keeps the aligned 26B (the external review's ruling):** The ruling, verbatim: *"Keep aligned `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` (`22/24`, `52.3 tok/s`) on General, and keep uncensored models strictly on the separate `general_uncensored` preset."* What that replaces: the preset was not on General at all before this - it named an abliterated 9B, `hf.co/mradermacher/Huihui-Qwen3.5-9B-abliterated-GGUF:Q4_K_M`, on the one-card everyday lane at 196,608 tokens with a 2026-10-18 receipt - and the uncensored 27B had no preset, only the pooled lane's `creative` mode. The row now names **`orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored:q4_K_M`** on **`lane="pooled"`** (the only lane that can hold a 17 GiB model on this PC) at **`context=32768`**, the window the 2026-11-18 measurement supports, and its `measured` object carries that run: **17.379 GiB resident, 17.379 GiB in the cards' memory, 0.000 GiB spilled, a 47.4-57.1 s cold load and 9.04-13.05 tok/s over seven clean fixed-prompt samples (median 9.99; the low end is quoted)**. **Why 32,768 and not the larger rung:** 49,152 tokens also measured **0.000 GiB spilled** and is the maximum measured zero-spill window, but it buys no quality or tool figure the measurement supports and costs more of every load; 65,536 measured **1.507 GiB spilled**, so that rung fails the project's zero-spill bar outright. **Why this model and not `muse-glimmer-uncensored:30b`:** 15.77 GiB, already local, tools + thinking - but unmeasured here, so its 30B tool behaviour is a guess; the 27B is the one candidate with a full measurement on this PC (0.000 GiB spill at 32,768, **20/24** blind quality, **19/19** tool calls emitted / 18/19 correct, ~10 tok/s). The alternative is described in the row's own words rather than named as the default, and the two MoE candidates still downloading (`huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:30b-a3b`, `TrevorJS/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-uncensored`) are benchmarks for later, never a figure now. **The honesty this row carries, in its own words:** a bigger, uncensored model is NOT automatically better - the aligned 26B on General scores **22/24 at 52.3 tokens a second** against this row's 20/24 at about 10, on three cards instead of one; it drops the second half of a two-effect instruction; and on three deliberately benign probes the uncensored tag changed nothing observable, so nothing is claimed about safety behaviour on material this project never tested. **What deliberately did not change:** General keeps `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` at 32,768 on the pooled lane (the ruling's other half is a pin, not a move); the one-preset-at-a-time rule and the heavy-mode contract stand (the everyday model is paused while it runs, and a model another preset left loaded is ended first); the big-coder route's three mode keys (`coding`, `deep_think`, `creative`) are unchanged, and the preset reaches its model through the preset layer's OWN `general-uncensored` pooled-mode row, derived from the preset row so model and window are typed once. One stale claim is corrected with the fresh measurement: `creative`'s measured sentence quoted **17.7 tok/s**, and the 2026-11-18 re-measurement could not reproduce the stored 17.96 (best 13.05, median 9.99 over two busy runs and seven clean samples), so that sentence now quotes the fresh range instead of standing contradicted beside the new row. Every figure is dated 2026-11-18 and comes from `.dsh-scratch/wave21/research/MEASURE-27B.md`; no live config, lane, port or model was touched by this change, and nothing was downloaded.

- **2026-11-18 — The owner's GitHub reads are answered deterministically, his own repository is resolved from his own words, and ONLY reads may assume it:** the live failure was one sentence - *"What are my open pull requests on Epic-Jarvis?"* - ending in Jarvis asking *"Could you tell me who owns the Epic-Jarvis repository?"* while `jarvis_github.OWN_REPO` held the answer; the model HAD called the tool and the tool refused the bare name (`agent.chain` in `~/.openjarvis/logs/jarvis-2026-11-18.jsonl`: `github_list`, `ran: false`, `outcome: "unknown"`). A second live battery (eight questions, 17:57Z) measured the other half: seven turns called nothing, one called `github_list` and was refused the same way, and *"What is the latest commit on main in Epic-Jarvis?"* was a FALSE DENIAL of access because the tool diet (`TOOL_DIET_DEFAULT = True`) had hidden every GitHub tool from the model - its words matched only `web_search`/`feature_guide`. Decided: (1) **ANSWER THE CORE READS DETERMINISTICALLY.** `jarvis_quick.py` now claims four read-only GitHub questions - the owner's open pull requests (and ready-to-merge), one pull request's checks/failures (PR N), the newest run on main (the read that names a commit), and the unmerged work - from `jarvis_github`'s own planners and `run()`, so there is no model in the loop, no owner/name question, and the token still goes only to api.github.com under the Q5 target check. It is claimed ONLY while the `github_inspect` tier is `"auto"` and a token is saved: with the switchable "Read your GitHub" row back on "ask", the answer declines and the model's tool path raises that card - the fast path can never go round a permission. The open-defect count is deliberately EXCLUDED because another lane owns its deterministic answer this wave; two doors for one question would drift. (2) **RESOLVE ONLY THE OWNER'S OWN REPOSITORY, IN THE TOOL LAYER.** `jarvis_github.repo_from_words` resolves the bare name (case-insensitively, hyphen or space), a self phrase ("my repo", "my open PRs", "this repository") or the full name in any case to `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis`; `_check_repo` applies it to the FIVE READ planners only, and `jarvis_agent._github_repo_call` fills a READ's missing `repo` from the owner's OWN newest typed-or-spoken words (never a setting, an earlier turn or a pasted caption). **(3) WRITES KEEP DECISION #1348, UNLOOSENED.** The owner's ruling 5.2: reads may assume the owner's own repository, writes may not - every WRITE planner still refuses a bare name with exactly today's words and asks for `owner/name`, because a change built from an assumed repository is worse than a question; a full foreign name passes through untouched everywhere. (4) **THE INSTRUCTION AND THE FACT LIVE IN EACH TOOL'S OWN DESCRIPTION** (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, "An explicit action request reaches its gating tool"): every GitHub tool whose schema takes a `repo` states that a bare name is valid AND names the full `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis`, added once in `jarvis_agent.Tool.__init__` so no future tool can miss it, never in the lane prompt; the four read tools also open with the measured "Call this when the owner asks ..." trigger shape (the shape that took `change_setting` from 0/21 to 18/21 calls on this PC), and the tool diet gained the words that were hiding the tools ("commit" on `github_ci_status`, "defect"/"register" on `check_records`). (5) **The remainder is named:** there is no commit-list read, so the latest-commit answer is the newest CI run's head commit and says so; the "how do I merge a pull request" how-to stays with the model (it is not one of the ruling's four read questions). Proven by `backend/test_github_own_repo.py` (176 checks: the measured sentence end to end, the self phrases, the foreign control, reads-resolve/writes-refuse, the descriptions, the card-free read, the deterministic fast path naming real data for all four questions with no false denial, the fast path declining while the read card is on, and the 17:57Z battery's diet offers) with the suites' injected HTTP fake; no real GitHub call, no network and no token read.

- **2026-11-18 — The GitHub read layer pages a long list instead of refusing it, names the newest run's head commit when a branch read is asked for the latest commit, and answers "which pull requests on Epic-Jarvis are ready to merge?" on the deterministic fast path:** the owner's live field battery failed on the deployed b8de6ef15 in three measured places (`.dsh-scratch/wave21/coverage/GITHUB-FIELD-FAIL.md`), and the ruling is that the read returns what it claims rather than either raising the byte cap or hiding the gap. (1) **PAGE, DO NOT RAISE THE CAP.** `MAX_BYTES = 200_000` is a hard cut on ONE GET; a ten-row open pull request list measured 227,073 characters (the field run's ten were reported even larger), so the JSON could not be parsed and the answer was the cut sentence with no number in it - a false-looking "I cannot read your GitHub" about a list GitHub had really sent. Raising the cap would move the same failure by one row, so the fix is `LIST_PAGE = 5` and `_list_pages`: after a CUT, the SAME list is read five rows at a time and joined, de-duplicated by GitHub's own number, up to the `PER_PAGE` rows the single read was allowed to ask for. The same paging serves the read-only PR cockpit, whose header says "At least N open pull request(s)" when it reached `MAX_PRS` (the count is not claimed as the whole list), and a page that was itself cut is salvaged row by row and the answer says it may be short. An ordinary small list still costs exactly one read - paging runs only after a cut - and when even the pages answer nothing usable the cut sentence is still what the reader gets, so nothing silently becomes an empty list. (2) **SAY THE COMMIT THE READ ACTUALLY HAS.** "What is the latest commit on main?" is answered by the branch CI read - the read the quick lane chose as the one that names a commit - and it rendered only how the newest run ended, never the commit, so the field battery's sha check could never pass. `_ci_words`'s branch/repository form now ends with "The newest run's head commit is <full 40-hex sha>: <subject>", and it is said AS THE RUN'S OWN COMMIT: this read does not measure the branch tip, so it must not claim to (measured live 2026-11-18: the newest run's `head_sha` was the same commit `gh api .../commits/main` named, but the sentence is worded from what was read). Changing the branch form also puts the commit in the model's own `github_ci_status(branch)` answer, which previously could not name one either. (3) **READINESS IS A FAST-PATH SHAPE, BUT ONLY ABOUT HIS OWN REPOSITORY.** The field sentence puts "on Epic-Jarvis" in the middle, which `_GITHUB_MY_PRS` does not match, so it reached the model and came back asking for owner/name. A new `_GITHUB_READY` matcher sends it to the read-only PR cockpit (`plan_scan_prs`) - each open pull request's own merge state and checks, the same verdict the merge gate uses, so the answer can only repeat GitHub's - and its middle words accept ONLY phrases naming the owner's own repository ("on Epic-Jarvis", "in my repo", "this repository", "on GitHub"), so a foreign repo named in the sentence falls through to the model, whose tool resolves a real owner/name. Decision #1348 kept by #1382 is untouched: reads may resolve the owner's own repository when he named it without owner/name; writes still refuse an ambiguous name. What this deliberately does NOT do: it does not raise `MAX_BYTES`, it does not add a separate commit API read (the run's own object carries the sha and subject), and it does not put readiness questions about somebody else's repository on the fast path. Tests: `backend/test_github_own_repo.py`'s three new cases fail on b8de6ef15 for exactly these causes and pass after the fix (a list over the cap must still name every row it claims; a latest-commit answer must carry the 40-hex SHA and its subject; the battery's ready sentence must reach the deterministic lane) - 192 passed, 0 failed - plus the neighbouring GitHub suites (robustness 511, parity 705, tools 1167, ci-count 22, self-knowledge 166, off-switch 73, authoring 96) and the base / regeneration / stale-twin / parity / self-code checks, all green.

- **2026-11-18 — The HUD refuses an empty service by name; it never falls back to the local endpoint:** The ruling, quoted: "`lane_service()` returning `("", "")` (never a cloud URL) is right — AND the HUD manual-lane path must explicitly check for `("", "")` and refuse with a clear error naming the invalid lane rather than letting an empty service pass downstream." `jarvis_hud.py`'s `_completions_url()` turns a cloud lane name into a service and an address through `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_state()`; after #1384 that answer is `("", "")` for every name outside `CLOUD_LANES`, and "no address" used to mean "the local lane", so an unknown lane name went to Ollama with the name still on the request - a 503 from an endpoint the owner did not choose. From 2026-11-18 a cloud-intent lane whose service is empty is refused BEFORE any URL is built: a 404 whose body is one plain sentence naming the lane the client asked for ("There is no lane called `<name>` on this PC, so nothing was sent."), with the next step in the same sentence. The 404 is deliberate - it is not one of the degrade loop's `DEGRADABLE` codes, so the refusal cannot become a silent local answer, and `_open`'s existing `except urllib.error.HTTPError` reader is what shows the sentence to both apps. The check is narrow: a local-intent fallback lane (`decision.inject_memory`) is a local model's name, not a lost cloud lane, so it still reaches this PC's Ollama exactly as before. It ships inside `backend/ollama-direct.patch`, where the lane-to-address decision already lives - no new patch, route, wire field or app change.

- **2026-11-18 — Track the lane launcher in the repository and make the repository admit when the PC cannot honour its lane table:** `scripts/start-lane.ps1` is now a tracked copy of the live launcher the owner's Windows logon tasks run, and `tools/check_lane_launcher.py` compares it with the live file, with Task Scheduler, with `nvidia-smi -L`, and - the part CI can prove - with the lane table in `backend/jarvis_presets.py`. The judgement calls, all made against the 2026-11-18 failure (a pull request said the everyday lane on 11436 spans all three cards; CI was green; the machine's task passes one `-GpuUuid`, and a measured load grew the 2060 by 3,713 MiB and the other two cards by 0 MiB each): (1) **A COPY WITH A HEADER, NOT A BYTE-IDENTICAL MIRROR.** The header must say it is a copy, where the live file lives and that editing it alone changes nothing, so the copy cannot be mistaken for the running thing - but then it can never be byte-identical, so the comparison splits at a marked END line and compares only the live body, line for line, ignoring line-ending style alone. The header also carries a machine-readable TASK/GPU table (the two logon tasks' names, lanes, ports, exact `-GpuUuid` values and contexts, and the three card UUIDs), because the `-GpuUuid` that decides a lane's cards is passed by the TASK, not written in the launcher file; without that record the repository half could not be checked off the owner's PC. (2) **THE LANE TABLE IS THE AUTHORITY, AND THE CHECK IS HERMETIC.** The comparison parses (`ast`, never imports) `jarvis_presets.LANES` - the same table the apps render - and compares each lane's `card` claim with the cards its tracked task grants. A lane claiming "all three cards" while its task passes one UUID FAILS and names the exact value it should carry (all three UUIDs, comma-separated, in `nvidia-smi -L` order); a named card must be the card the task pins. The on-demand pooled lane has no logon task, and is NOT judged - comparing it would invent a grant that does not exist - and the run says so rather than passing silently. (3) **"NOT CHECKED" IS EXIT 3, NOT 0 AND NOT 1.** There is no live launcher on a fresh machine or a CI runner, so sections 2-4 print the exact sentence "not checked: no live launcher on this machine" and the process exits 3, never a pass; section 1 is hermetic, so CI still gets a real verdict on the repository half, and `--repo-only` runs only that half. (4) **THE DEPLOY REFUSES THE ONE-STEP.** `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` runs the preflight BEFORE it plans and refuses both the dry run and the apply (exit 2, nothing written) when the repository and the machine disagree, printing "2-step deploy: update the lane task" with the exact task and the exact `-GpuUuid` it should carry; `--allow-lane-launcher-mismatch` is the explicit override and says out loud the disagreement is NOT fixed. A warning was rejected: a one-step deploy that leaves the machine unable to serve the model the repository names is exactly the failure this closes. (5) **NOTHING LIVE WAS TOUCHED.** No task, launcher, lane or model changed - this PR only makes the disagreement visible; when a later change really wants the everyday lane on all three cards, its PR updates the tracked task table (and CI then requires the lane table to match it) and the machine's task is step 2 of the deploy. The live drift check is at the desk: `py -3 tools/check_lane_launcher.py` (measured 2026-11-18: tracked copy, both tasks, all three cards and `jarvis_presets.LANES` all agree), and `backend/test_check_lane_launcher.py` proves every comparison can fail on fixtures, never on the owner's PC.

- **2026-11-18 — lane_service must fail closed: a lane name the table does not know names no cloud service:** The owner's ruling: `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` must never turn a lane name it does not recognise into a cloud request. It used to map any unknown name to `DEFAULT_LANE` (or the chosen provider), so `lane_service("qwen3.5:9b")` answered `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")` and a local model's name in a lane field could have sent a private prompt to a cloud service; the HUD's request builder asks `lane_state(lane)` for the address it will open, and a wrong service there is a real egress. From 2026-11-18 only a name in `CLOUD_LANES` names a service. The empty name is the local signal, and every other name - an old `degrade_chain` entry, a local model's name, anything else - returns `("", "")`: no service and no model. No caller may reintroduce a fallback for an unknown name; `DEFAULT_LANE` stays the default for the empty name and for a real lane while no provider is chosen, never a destination for a name the table does not know.

- **2026-11-18 — A local record is answered from its file, or refused:** when the owner asks a question whose answer is a record on his own PC ("how many open defects are in the register", "what is open", "what is DEF-089"), chat answers from that record's file, deterministically, naming the file and the date it was read. The count is the checker's own count - `jarvis_quick` loads `tools/check_defect_register.py` and calls its `parse_tsv()` rather than writing a second parser - so a wrong count is never smoothed over: a missing file, a missing checker, a malformed header or a malformed row is refused in plain words. The answer is read-only: no card, no write, no model. The file is found through `JARVIS_DEFECT_REGISTER`, then the review gates' `JARVIS_REVIEW_REPO`, then the checkout the backend runs from - never by scanning the owner's folders - so an installed copy with no checkout beside it says the register is not there instead of denying the register exists. This is the first instance of the shape, not a general file-reading tool: it does not make the model read arbitrary files, and no other record is answered this way yet.

- **2026-11-18 — The Ollama address has one resolver, and every shipped module asks it:** `jarvis_models.ollama_url_on_this_pc()` is the only place `OLLAMA_URL` is read, and the seventeen modules that still read the variable - or Ollama's own `OLLAMA_HOST` - directly now call it, so a lane task's exported port no longer decides where a health read, a quiz, a hardware probe or the personality draft asks. `OLLAMA_HOST` is Ollama's bind variable, not the chat's lane, so reading it was itself the 2026-10-25 wrong-port bug; `jarvis_ollama_contract.py` keeps its `OLLAMA_HOST` fallback because `backend/test_ollama_contract.py` pins that read-only probe to the standard library and nothing else, and its one live caller already passes the resolved lane. The rule that follows: a shipped module never reads an Ollama address out of the environment itself - it asks the helper, and `backend/test_ollama_url_routing.py` fails if a new direct read appears in the published base.

- **2026-11-18 — A package install is refused when it would write into the repository, and its leftovers are checked for:** Decided after the 2026-11-18 incident - a delegated agent ran pip with the repository root as its working directory and TMP/TEMP inside the tree, and seventeen `pip-metadata-*`/`pip-unpack-*` folders sat at the root, untracked and one `git add -A` from being committed. `tools/check_package_install_context.py` refuses that context for pip and for uv BEFORE the install runs, names the offending folder and says the fix ("run the install from a scratch directory, or set TMP/TEMP outside the repo"), and has a `--run -- <command>` wrapper so the delegate path can let the guard do the refusing instead of remembering a rule. A context it cannot judge - an unknown manager, a platform that is neither Windows nor POSIX - is printed as "not checked: <why>" and exits 3, never a pass; that is the project's BLOCKED-is-never-a-pass rule, and it is why this guard may not quietly return 0 on a machine it does not understand. `tools/check_package_manager_temp_artifacts.py` is deliberately the second half rather than duplication: a guard that is bypassed must not be followed by silence, so a tracked or untracked root path matching pip's temporary folders, a root `*.dist-info` or a tracked root `node_modules` fails the check, which then names each path and the command that removes it. It looks at the root only, not inside the tree, because a `pip-*` name in a test fixture and a temp folder under the ignored `.dsh-scratch/` are legitimate and the incident's folders were at the root. Both run in the audit job, and the install guard's step sits before that job's own pip install, so a working directory or TMP regression stops the install rather than being discovered after it. No existing check was weakened: the required jobs' behaviour is unchanged, and `backend/test_package_install_guards.py` proves every branch can fail on fixtures it makes and removes.

- **2026-11-18 — The phone may approve the update card with its own fingerprint:**
  The owner asked that the phone be able to ask for the same desktop update the
  PC can already do, with the phone's own fingerprint. The decision is to keep
  ONE action (`desktop_update`, tier "ask", the same card, the same written
  words) and change only WHERE it may be confirmed: it left
  `jarvis_owner_check.PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`, exactly as `raise_api_limit` left it on
  2026-10-11 for the same owner's reason. Nothing about who confirms it was
  loosened - on the PC the card still asks Windows Hello (the action has no
  `_RISK` row, so the gate gives it the worst case and `is_risky` puts it at the
  prompt), and on the phone it needs that phone's signed approval, a fresh
  fingerprint or PIN over a one-use challenge, with `no_approval_key` refused in
  the existing words. A second action name was turned down: the old attempt's
  `update_jarvis` would have been a second name for an ability that already had
  one. What runs after the yes depends on where it was given - a PC approval
  still runs the desktop shell's own `update_both`; a phone approval cannot reach
  that command, so the backend runs `scripts/update-jarvis.ps1`, the repository's
  own both-halves updater, in a detached helper that holds the shared
  `update-in-progress.lock` so the two roads cannot patch the PC at once. This
  entry deliberately does not claim the phone screen: it is the next pull

- **2026-11-18 — Picture conversion: `img2pdf` for the PDF half, `pikepdf` beside it, and one own "ask" action for the file it writes:** The owner asked "can Jarvis convert certain formats of files to other formats? like to pdf from an image and so forth", and the research lane's report settled the tools, so the decisions here are the shape and the guards. (1) **The PDF half is `img2pdf`, never Pillow's PDF writer.** Pillow's `save(..., "PDF")` re-encodes RGB through its JPEG encoder and defaults the page to 72 dpi; img2pdf copies a JPEG's (and JPEG-2000's) own compressed bytes into the PDF, which is the losslessness the feature exists for and which `backend/test_image_convert.py` proves by finding the input bytes inside the output. `pikepdf` (img2pdf's own PDF assembler, QPDF) comes with it and is named in `requirements.txt` as well, because the lock must hold both. (2) **The picture-format half is Pillow, and it must not lie about quality.** PNG/TIFF are lossless; JPEG/WebP/AVIF are lossy and the card and result both say "lossy" and "not identical". Transparency asked into JPEG is flattened onto white and the sentence says "flattened onto white" - the research's finding that the two obvious tools silently re-encode is exactly the failure this sentence rules out. (3) **ONE new gate action, `convert_images`, tier "ask", with no new HTTP route.** The chat tool's ordinary tool-call card is the only permission path; it reuses the existing gate, the existing `my_files` tool and the existing child-program pattern. A new action name was needed because every existing file-writing card is purpose-specific (the notes editor's `edit_vault_note`, `import_notion_export`, `receive_uploaded_document`, `wiki_update`) and its words would be false for a PDF; the module's `prepare()` refuses any tier but "ask" as a belt under the card, so a hand-loosened settings line cannot make a file write cardless. (4) **Never overwrite: a numbered name, an explicit refusal, and `O_EXCL`.** A chosen name that is taken becomes `photo (2).pdf` and the card says so; a path the caller named that exists is refused rather than silently renamed; and the write itself opens the destination with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`, so a file that appears while the card is up is refused too. (5) **Licences and limits.** img2pdf is LGPL-3.0 and pikepdf/QPDF is MPL-2.0: ordinary pip dependencies of a local, non-commercial program, never linked into a Jarvis binary, credited in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` - which also gains the FFmpeg credit a shipped feature had been missing, with the rule that the GPLv3 build on this PC is required and must never be bundled. HEIC is NOT read (the maintained decoder is handed to the phone's own setting instead), the PDF's page size follows each picture's DPI, and this is chat-only with no route of its own.

- **2026-11-18 — A preset apply has to PROVE the lane, and a tripwire guard must never quietly switch the check off:** `apply_preset` now reads the target lane's `/api/ps` through a `verify_lane` seam and refuses - rolling the model record, the lane pointer and the chosen preset back - unless the lane shows the model the preset names, with no CPU spill and at a window no smaller than the preset's own. The judgement calls in that check, all made against the A2 field test (DEF-088: a `general` apply reported success while 11436 served the pooled coder at 8,192): (1) **an EMPTY lane is not a failure.** A preset apply records which model chat should use; Ollama loads it on the next turn at the lane's own window, so failing "nothing is loaded" would red-flag the most ordinary apply there is. Only a model that is not the preset's, any spill at all, a window smaller than the preset names, or a lane that does not answer is a failure - "could not tell" is never a pass. (2) **A probe names the window whenever it can, and never goes silent when it cannot.** Every tripwire request carries `options.num_ctx` from the lane's own configured window; for an address this program does not know as a lane (`OLLAMA_URL` unset means 11434, so every fresh clone and every CI run) the request goes out without the field - `main`'s own request - because a guard that stops the smoke test there is a check disabled by a guard, worse than the gap it closes, and naming a guessed window would force the downgrade instead of leaving Ollama's configured default in charge. The first cut of this refused on "window unknown" and turned `backend/test_reversible_ui_choices.py` red: that suite loads the base model steward with no `OLLAMA_URL`, so the refusal fired and the tripwire it asserts never ran. (3) **A pooled outgoing model is SKIPPED, not re-aimed at the pooled lane.** The alternative - probing it on the pooled address - would still load a stale name there and cannot answer "how did the old model answer" after `apply_preset` has stopped that server; a skip cannot load the wrong model on the wrong card even when the pooled lane is down. (4) **The lane reader is for the real HUD process only.** Two things decide that: `JARVIS_SUITE_RUNNING`, and the process actually running `jarvis_hud.py` (the same test `_warm_on_startup` uses, and the real backend on this PC is `python.exe ...\jarvis_hud.py`). The second half is there because the first was not enough: a suite that loads the base's model steward directly never sets the marker, and the reader answered from the owner's LIVE 11435 mid-test. Inside anything else the default says `checked: false` and that it is NOT a pass; a suite that wants the real reader passes `_default_verify_lane` itself with a fake lane of its own, which is how `backend/test_preset_switch_lane_guard.py` proves it. This is a bug fix with no permission, route or approval-tier change: the two `switch_model` cards, the app-click rule, and the receipt/Undo path are exactly as they were.

- **2026-11-18 — A recording attached in chat is transcribed by `jarvis_media_read`, and its decode is the one thing the attachment reader writes:** the owner's report was that an `.m4a` voice memo could not be attached from the app's chat "Attach a file" row. The cause was not a missing feature but a picker narrower than the PC's capability: the chat row offered the eight document types, while the PC's own audio reader already read `.wav .mp3 .m4a .aac .flac .ogg .opus .wma` for a file in a listed folder. So the chat row now offers exactly those eight (the canonical type plus the aliases a provider really reports, `audio/x-m4a` beside `audio/mp4`; the extension decides before any provider type), and `jarvis_attached_file` routes the bytes to that SAME reader's new bytes door - the local speech model on this PC, never the document converter, never the phone. **Where the bytes go, decided deliberately:** a WAV is decoded in memory with no ffmpeg and no file; a COMPRESSED recording (M4A, MP3, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OPUS, WMA) is copied to ONE private temporary file for the length of the decode only and deleted in a `finally`, because an MP4/M4A keeps its index at the end and ffmpeg cannot decode one from a pipe (measured: a 100 KB non-faststart `.m4a` on stdin produced a 78-byte WAV header and "partial file", while the same bytes through a real file decoded). That copy has a random name, is never the owner's file name, is never indexed or kept, and `backend/test_media_read.py` proves it is gone after a read and after a refusal. This is a deliberate, narrow exception to `jarvis_attached_file`'s "never written to disk" promise, which still holds for every DOCUMENT. **The refusal is the reader's own:** with no ffmpeg the owner reads `jarvis_media_read.NO_FFMPEG` verbatim - no second sentence is invented - and a busy or speechless recording keeps that reader's own words too. **The picker is not `*/*`:** it keeps the rule "every type the PC has a reader for", so a type the PC cannot read is not offered; no offered document type was found unreadable, so nothing was removed. Video is deliberately NOT offered in this row even though the reader can read one (one attachment is at most 2.5 MB, and the row is the owner's voice memo), and the desktop's own attach list keeps its eight document types in its own lane - both said in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 163.6. The read is still decided under the existing `read_files_readonly` gate before a byte is touched, the conversation is still marked as having read outside text, and the wire format is unchanged.

- **2026-11-18 — A suite or probe cannot write the owner's live settings, and the guard reads the project's own marker:** The review ruled, verbatim: "Keep the harness rule (`scratch --config-dir` only) AND add a fail-fast guard so `JARVIS_SUITE_RUNNING` / probe helpers cannot write to `~/.openjarvis/` without breaking legitimate owner-card flows." The incident it answers: a lane admitted it briefly wrote the owner's live config while probing - it turned the escalation switch off and lowered his money cap to $5, then restored both - and while it did, the app showed him a card saying "$5.00 of $5.00" while the money file said $10.00. What was built, and the judgement calls: (1) **the marker is the one the project already uses, never a second mechanism.** `backend/_where.py` already sets `JARVIS_SUITE_RUNNING=1` for every suite, and two shipped behaviours already read it, so the guard reads that same variable; a new "is this a test" flag would be a second thing to keep right and could disagree with the first. (2) **the live folder is the owner's `~/.openjarvis`, resolved from `~`, never from `CONFIG_DIR`.** A process with `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` / `JARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` pointing somewhere temporary is already safe - that is exactly what `backend/run_suites.py` gives every suite - so the guard exists for the target that reached the owner's own folder anyway (a hard-coded default, a resolver that ran before the override was set, or a probe that built the path itself), and an override that names the live folder is still the live folder. (3) **it refuses by raising, never by redirecting silently.** A silent redirect would let a suite that believes it wrote the live path report a pass it never earned, so `refuse_live_config_write(path)` raises `LiveConfigWriteRefused` naming the file, saying nothing was written, and asking for a temporary `--config-dir` / `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR`; it is called before any folder or file is created, so a refused write leaves the owner's folder exactly as it was. (4) **reads stay allowed and the live backend is untouched.** A suite may still read the owner's live settings and ledger - that is how the battery measures - and no shipped module ever SETS the marker, so the live HUD process cannot trip the guard and the owner's card flows that write these files are unchanged; a test without the marker writes and reads the same files normally. It is wired into the writers this branch owns: `chatbot/api-money.json` (`jarvis_chatbot_api._save`, the monthly cap and spending ledger in one file) and `model-state.json` (`jarvis_models`), and `backend/test_live_config_write_guard.py` proves all four arms with the real writers; the guard itself is also asked about the two preset files and refuses both live paths by name. **The honest scope limit:** `escalate-cloud.json` and `cloud-choice.json` are written only by `jarvis_presets.py`, which this lane's brief forbids touching (a parallel lane owns it), so those two writer calls are not wired here - each is one call to the same guard and is a follow-up for that file's owner, and the harness rule (scratch lanes pass a temporary settings folder) covers them in the meantime. The base-only `jarvis_models.py` half reaches the owner's PC on the next base install, the same route every base-only fix takes.

- **2026-11-18 — The egress gate reads code, not prose:** An external review ruled on the egress gate's census: **a docstring or a `#` comment is writing, not egress, and must not be counted as an outbound host mention.** The measured cause: a new module's docstring showed `api.deepseek.com` as an example, `tools/check_egress_gate.py` flagged it, that failed `backend/test_chatbot_api.py` ("every outbound host mention is accounted for") and the whole `audit` job, and the lane's fix was to DELETE the hostname from the docstring - the gate trained an author to remove documentation instead of thinking about egress. So the checker walks `ast` now: a mention is a HOSTS name in a string literal that is code; docstrings (`ast.get_docstring`), any other bare string expression statement, and `#` comments (which never enter the AST) are ignored and counted only in the run's ignored line. The gate is not weakened: a real code string naming a host still fails unless the file names `check_egress` in code or is on the allow-list with a reason, f-strings and literal `+`/adjacent concatenations are folded so a split host is caught where the raw-text scan missed it, and the wiring half is code too - a docstring saying "this asks check_egress" is no longer wiring. The census lost 13 entries whose host lived only in prose (their files are simply not outbound mentions any more), and seven reasons that claimed "comment" or "docstring" while the mention was really code were corrected rather than left as a false account; the material one is `backend/jarvis_model_recommendations.py`, whose entry said "docstring" while its code builds and compares the Hugging Face URL fed to `jarvis_hf_inspect.py`'s fetch. Run on this tree the walk reports 134 files (6 wired + 128 allow-listed over 95 exact paths), 586 code mentions and 213 ignored documentation mentions; `backend/test_egress_gate_checker.py` holds every case on fixture trees plus the real tree's census line.

- **2026-11-18 — The tool diet gets a named-thing floor instead of more hint words:** the owner's live battery (eight questions about his own GitHub repository, 17:57Z) showed the deepest cause of Jarvis denying abilities it has. `TOOL_DIET_DEFAULT` ships ON, and `tool_diet_selection` shows a model only the tools whose hint patterns match its words. Every GitHub tool's hints open with `github` - but the owner names his repository "Epic-Jarvis", not "GitHub" - so "what is the latest commit on main in Epic-Jarvis?" matched only `web_search` ("latest") and `feature_guide` (a settings tool, whose `\bis the .* (?:on|off)\b` hint matched "is the … on" by accident). Two incidental matches counted as a "recognised subject", so the safe full-list fallback did not fire either, and every GitHub tool was hidden. A model cannot call a tool it cannot see, and it then truthfully reported the limitation as if it were the product's. **What was chosen, and what was rejected.** Not more hint words: a hint is a score, so a competing word can beat it, the top-K cap can crowd it out, and every new phrasing would need its own word; #1382 merged first and patched exactly two hint words (`commit`, `defect`), which rescues those two battery questions but not the class - the repository's NAME still matches no hint, and "branches" still matched none (so that question got a 29-tool full-list fallback). Not a description-matching floor either: every GitHub description contains "commit" and "repository" ("it never merges, pushes, commits or deletes"), so that would have added ten tools to one question. The chosen rule is a floor: `NAMED_ACTION_TOOLS` maps the owner's own object words (repository, pull request/PR, commit, branch, defect register, workflow/CI) and his repository's own name (from `jarvis_github.OWN_REPO`, so there is no second copy of it) to the READ tools that answer about that thing; `named_action_floor` adds those to whatever the hints chose, first, and the cap grows to fit them rather than cutting them. Hints are unchanged for everything else, so with no named thing the diet is byte-for-byte the top-K it was. **Why it is safe for a small model:** the floor adds at most the few reads for the things actually named (the battery's worst case is 3 tools, the eight average 3.9 against 7.4 on merged main and 10.8 on the pre-#1382 tree), it never adds a write tool on its own, it never exceeds the owner's enabled list, and it cannot make the list bigger than the diet cap for an ordinary question because it does not fire there - the ordinary controls still trim to 1-2 tools. **Why it does not weaken approval:** it changes only the SHOWN list. `check_call` reads `names`, the allowed list, and `_one_call` puts every call to `jarvis_gate` exactly as before, so hiding a tool was never refusing it and showing one is not running it; no gate table, no tier and no configuration line is touched (every GitHub read is card-free by the existing `github_inspect` auto row and all seven enabled GitHub writes remain in `NEEDS_A_PERSON` and raise their own card; the all-80-tool before/after approval dump is byte-identical). **Honest limits:** the floor only knows the object words in its table; a question that names a GitHub thing in words outside it (a "milestone", a "release", "the head sha") is still dieted by hints alone - the fix covers the five objects the owner's own battery named, not every GitHub noun. It also cannot fix the other half of the same live run: where the tool was offered, the 9B model still chose not to call it or called it with a bare repository name, which is the deterministic fast path's lane (#1382). And a single incidental hint match can still suppress the full-list fallback for a question that names none of the floor's things; a stricter "recognised subject" rule is the next fix for that class. Tests: `backend/test_tool_diet_named_action.py` (83 checks, no source-text pins; 8 fail on merged main's tree, 17 on the pre-#1382 tree), with `test_tool_eval.py`, `test_kv_prefix.py`, `test_short_tool_list.py`, `test_tool_text.py`, `test_folder_restrictions.py`, `test_warm_prefix.py`, `test_agent.py`, `test_live_parity.py`, `test_live_settings_parity.py` and the twin/base/record checks green.

- **2026-11-18 — The capability sweep splits into an every-PR core subset and a full sweep run only when the catalogue changes, and the desktop lockfile check becomes a required gate instead of an audit signal:** both guards are the external review's ruling, and both were measured the expensive way. (1) THE CAPABILITY SPLIT. `backend/test_capability_answers.py`'s 5,410-question reach ratchet caught a real cross-PR break on 2026-11-18 (two PRs each touched `backend/jarvis_quick.py`, each was green alone, and merged they changed each other's behaviour - main is red on "no ordinary shape lost its row", `cloud-escalation 63 < 65`), so the ruling's shape is implemented: every PR runs a CORE subset of 239 pinned cases - one ordinary question naming each of the 184 catalogue rows' own title, plus the 53 sweep answers the capability fix changed (the review's "~230"; its "180" was the live audit's row count), plus TWO dated known losses ("Does Jarvis escalate to the cloud?" and "What is cloud escalation?" now answer `cloud_settings` - tonight's red) that are printed as KNOWN LOST on every run, never counted as passes, and fail the step if any NEW case loses its row; the full sweep runs only when `features/features.json` or `backend/jarvis_feature_catalogue.py` (or its twin) changed. Measured 2026-11-18 (three runs): the suite with the sweep 32-36 s, without it 10.4-12.7 s, the `--core` shortcut 3.8-4.1 s, so the every-PR run is cheaper than before by about 22 s and the exhaustive ratchet is paid only when the catalogue moves. The path filter is computed in the workflow from `git diff` against the pull request's base sha, because ci.yml's `pull_request` trigger deliberately has no `paths:` filter (a filtered pull request would never report a required check) and GitHub has no per-job path filter. A core case is a question the full sweep already asks, generated by the same `_ordinary_shapes`, and `backend/test_capability_core_subset.py` proves the subset relation and that the mode switch fails closed. (2) THE LOCKFILE GATE. #1319 added `typescript` to `jarvis-desktop/package.json` without regenerating the lockfile, and eight `Desktop release` runs failed at `npm ci` for two days; the release-repair lane (#1386) deliberately left the gate to "its own CI change", which is this one. `tools/check_desktop_lockfile.py` makes the same three comparisons `npm ci` makes - a dependency missing from the lockfile's root package, a range disagreement, a missing resolved `node_modules/<name>` entry - plus name/version, with no npm, node or network, and prints `FIX   cd jarvis-desktop && npm install --package-lock-only`. It runs in the REQUIRED `frontend-shard` job (shard 1, about 0.2 s), which fans into the ruleset's required `frontend` check, NOT in `audit`: `audit` is informational and cannot hold a merge, which is exactly how two days passed. The release workflow keeps `npm ci` - `npm install` would hide the drift the strict install exists to surface - and `backend/test_desktop_lockfile_sync.py` proves the check fails on a deliberately desynced fixture pair, passes on the real one, and is wired into the required chain.

- **2026-11-18 — The Wi-Fi reconnect row reads the PC's yes-or-no ONCE, and an unreadable state is never drawn as off:** the owner reported the Settings row saying "The auto Wi-Fi reconnect is already on. Nothing was changed." over an unticked box. Read from the tree before changing anything: the state was ON (the shipped default, with no `wifi_reconnect.json`), and the answer was right - `jarvis_wifi.enabled()`/`state()` return it, the GET/POST route sends it as the JSON boolean `enabled`, and the chat/Live sentences are composed from the same call. The widget was wrong, and it was wrong twice over from one answer: `jarvis-desktop/src/wifi-reconnect-settings.js` ticked the box from `view.on` (a field no answer has ever carried - so `view.on === true` was never true, and the box stayed unticked in every state) while it worded the line from `view.words`. The ruling is that one page may not read one answer two ways: `readWifi()` is now that page's ONLY reader of the PC's yes-or-no, it takes `enabled` and nothing else for the state, `paint()` ticks the box from its `on` and `describe()` words the line from the same `on`, so the tick and the sentence cannot disagree even if a future answer's `words` is stale or wrong. Three consequences are deliberate. (1) **The state word is the page's, not the backend sentence's:** `words` is still the PC's own sentence, but it is now used only where there is no on/off to name (a waiting card, a refused change) or as the last-check detail (`last_words`), because a sentence that can say a state is a second reader. (2) **Unknown is not off:** an answer without a boolean `enabled` is drawn unticked, greyed and said as unknown, and a PC whose saved setting file is damaged (`known: false`) is said as damaged - the same rule the Rust command already applies ("a state that cannot be read is not the same as a switch that is turned off"). (3) **The row's own copy says what it means:** "On to start, as you asked" became "On by default, as you asked; the switch shows whether it is on right now", because the old sentence read as a live state and was quoted back by the owner as one. - **2026-11-19 — A cloud answer is BOUNDED, not truncated, and a twice-failed coding turn gets a third chance at the cloud:** the external review's rulings 6.5 and 6.1, implemented together because both are about the same measured turn. **6.5, in the review's words:** "Add a concise-by-default instruction + a generous safety ceiling (`max_tokens = 4096` for standard escalations, `8192` for coding/deep analysis) - do NOT aggressively truncate hard answers." The measurement behind it: one escalated turn cost $0.002747-$0.0039 and was almost entirely output (2,152 completion against 84 prompt tokens, about 99% of the cost), so cost per turn is a length control - and a truncated hard answer costs MORE, because the owner pays for the retry. Chosen: `jarvis_chatbot_api.cloud_request_body()` is the one composer of a cloud request's messages and `max_tokens`; it sends a concise-by-default instruction as the request's only system message, in front of the owner's newest turn (user turns only, so the cloud lane's privacy cut is unchanged), and bounds `max_tokens` to 4,096 standard / 8,192 coding-or-deep. Those numbers are a ceiling, never a target: the measured turn's 2,152 is well under both, and the bound can only LOWER what the month's money check already priced. The second tier uses EXISTING signals rather than a new classifier - the router's own 0-1 complexity score (0.40 is Stage 1; 0.70 is the top band it already grows answers across) and `jarvis_router.is_coding_turn()`, which reads the Coding preset's own trigger words, a coder model's name, or the caller's tool-in-play answer. It is wired in `_open` in the HUD relay through `ollama-direct.patch`, the one function every hop of the degrade loop builds its request through, deliberately not one caller. The relay's existing cap call is not weakened: the composer records its ceiling on the lane state, and `cloud_request_cap()` can only lower the request to it, so a reasoning-inside lane that was being sent cap + 8,000 room (up to 16,000) is now bounded without ever passing the limit. **6.1, in the review's words:** "Keep the deterministic `complexity >= 0.40` pre-gate as Stage 1, and pair it with a 2-strike / local-failure fallback for coding tasks - do NOT replace it with raw log-probs." Chosen: Stage 1 is untouched; `jarvis_router` gains `note_local_failure(conversation)` / `local_failure_strikes()` / `reset_local_failures()` and a `choose(..., conversation=, coding=)` seam. After TWO local failures in the SAME conversation, a coding turn may pass the complexity stage even under 0.40; everything else still runs, in the same order - the cloud-model, no-lane, Lockdown, taint, image, file, screen, private and pasted-secret gates above it, the budget gate after it, and gate 6's owner-yes/standing-switch requirement at the end. So one failure does not fire it, a non-coding turn never does, and a private turn with two failures still stays on this PC; the count is keyed by conversation so a new conversation starts at zero, the store is bounded and holds counts only. **Rejected, and why:** lowering or removing the 0.40 pre-gate (the ruling keeps it, and a log-prob classifier has no measured evidence here), and putting the instruction in one client or one lane instead of the shared composer (every other escalation would miss it). **Honest limits:** this PR implements the router half of 6.1 - no HUD caller records failures yet, which is a separate change; the 6.5 patch line reaches a fresh install through the patch stack, and the owner's already-deployed HUD needs the usual deploy step (the reconcile delta table was outside this brief). Tests: `backend/test_cloud_answer_bound.py` (29 checks, runtime assertions on the composed request body, no source pins) and `backend/test_router_strikes.py` (35 checks), plus the existing cloud/router/base/records suites green.

- **2026-11-19 — The two hand shims on the live `jarvis_models.py` are temporary debt to clear, NO THIRD SHIM MAY BE ADDED, and the deploy's cross-file guard stays absolute; the clean path is ONE whole-file refresh proved against the published base's own history:** the review ruled on the two shims appended to the owner's live `jarvis_models.py` (2026-11-18: `ollama_url_on_this_pc`; 2026-11-19: `is_pooled_model` + `probe_refusal`) because they were the worked way out the cross-file guard printed, and a worked example is a route that gets followed. Anything else is refused with its reason and nothing is written, including the deploy's own DELTA_TABLE literal repairs. The new file is the current published base plus any patch the target carries that the base does not yet, and the refresh is refused if it would lose a module-level name, drop a patch the base cannot take, fail to bind one of the deploy's declared cross-file names, or not compile. `backend/test_patched_base_refresh.py` proves it on temporary fixtures (a real temporary git repository included) and, with full history, on a fixture built from the REAL published base's history plus the three shim names; the deploy's guard passes on the refreshed file and still refuses when `probe_refusal` is taken back out, so the guard is not weakened. - **2026-11-19 — A machine record that cannot be read is refused, and a search that failed is not a finding:** two failure shapes were measured while pinning the review's ruled gaps, and both are settled the same way rather than by guessing. (1) The monthly money ledger upgraded a missing `months` key and refused a `months` that was not an object, but a month ENTRY that was not an object crashed: `{"months": {"2026-09": "oops"}}` made `money_check` raise `AttributeError`, and `spent_of` too, so a damaged record could break a turn instead of stopping it. The ruling is that `_load()` validates month entries exactly as it validates the three top-level tables, so every unreadable shape is the module's one fail-closed refusal ("an unreadable file must not read as nothing spent") and never a crash. (2) `github_search` reported a search whose every request failed - 403, 429, a timeout - as `ok: true` with no rows; a model reading that can only conclude "nothing exists", which is the one thing a failed search cannot establish. The ruling is that only a search that really ran produces the Redundancy Matrix: a total failure is `ok: false` with one plain sentence saying the audit was not made and why, with no HTTP code and no rows to misread. Neither change touches the rules themselves: a ledger with no `months` key still upgrades (nothing is lost by starting the record at this month), a partial failure still produces a matrix with its unaudited requests named, and `github_search` keeps its own two card-free `auto` actions. Tests: `backend/test_chatbot_api.py`'s rollover-boundary test fails 3 checks on the old module, and `backend/test_github_tools.py`'s `github_search` execution test fails 6 checks on the old agent.

Proved by `backend/test_hud_crisis_route.py` (26 checks, shipping block lifted out of the patch stack and executed - no source pins) with `test_cloud_honesty.py`, `test_wellbeing.py` and the router's taint suites unchanged.

- **2026-11-20 — One reader per row, and a client never claims a state it cannot read:** The two settings state-drift audits (`DESKTOP-STATE-DRIFT.md`, `PHONE-STATE-DRIFT.md`, 2026-11-19) proved a class, not a bug: a screen can paint a control from one store while its sentence comes from another, or paint both once and never ask again while a chat sentence, a second window or a late approval card moves the real value. The rule this PR records is the one the fixes implement. (1) ONE READER PER ROW: the tick/selected mark and the sentence beside it come from the same read, and a row backed by TWO ANDed stores (desktop "Say One moment": this window's localStorage AND the PC's `voice-flow.json`) paints from a reader of both, never from one of them. A failed save repaints the control from the store, exactly as the autostart row already did. (3) A CLIENT NEVER CLAIMS A STATE IT CANNOT READ: the phone draws no switch at all for a state the PC has not answered (`checked = null` + "Couldn't tell", the rule `VoiceSwitchesPlate` already carried for unknown states), never draws an unread hands-free read as "Hands-free is off", derives the focus-preset apply sentence without naming a preset, marks "Current" only while the PC's own live lane agrees with the saved pick, and no longer tells the owner that a PC-only setting is at its shipped default as if that were its value now. Chosen: `jarvis_router.note_local_failure()` is recorded at the relay's real local-failure points in `jarvis_hud.py` - the generic `except` that ends a turn when the relay gives up, the HTTP refusal that cannot step down, and the local answering loop's returned summary with no `finish_reason` - and `reset_local_failures()` is called where a local turn really produced an answer (a plain relay stream that finished normally, and a local turn that returned a `finish_reason`). `choose()` is handed the request's `conversation_id`, so the two-strike count is per conversation and a new chat starts at zero by construction. Nothing about the decision moves: after two local failures a CODING turn may pass the deterministic `complexity >= 0.40` stage under 0.40, every safety gate still runs in the same order (cloud-model, no-lane, Lockdown, taint, image, file, screen, private, pasted secret, budget), and gate 6 still needs the owner's yes or this PC's standing switch - two failures are not a standing permission, and a private turn with two failures still answers here. A cloud lane's failure is NEVER recorded, because a cloud lane's failure is not evidence about the local model; the router's store holds a count keyed by conversation id and no word of any chat; and a broken router is swallowed so bookkeeping can never be the reason a turn fails. **Rejected, and why:** recording in the client or the phone (the count would be per app and would not survive a reconnect), recording every refusal or approval timeout (a refusal is not a failed local attempt; only "the local lane produced no usable answer" is), and adding the recorder to the router's own module (the router cannot see the relay's failure; this is exactly the caller #1408 left out). **Carrier:** `router-strikes.patch` is a NEW patch appended last of the core patches, immediately before `plugin-loader.patch` - not a base change and no `DELTA_TABLE` literal delta, because the seven hunks sit inside regions earlier patches write (the choose call, the two relay handlers, the success paths) so only a patch that runs AFTER them can carry the change without rewriting their outputs; `tools/build_patch_history.py` records no earlier version for a new patch, and `backend/test_patch_delta_coverage.py` classifies it as exact-hunk coverage. **Honest limits:** the owner's already-deployed HUD needs the deploy step; this PR adds no `DELTA_TABLE` rule, so `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` REFUSES by name on that patch instead of silently skipping it (a refusal is the safe direction, and the rule is one small table edit in its own change). Proved by `backend/test_hud_router_strikes.py` (24 checks, the shipping blocks lifted out of the patch stack and executed against the real router - no source pins), with `test_router_strikes.py`'s 36 checks unchanged.

- **2026-11-20 — A check that has not finished is not a failure:** the external review's ruling 5.2, quoted: "(1) `plan_ci` must never classify `pending`/`queued`/`in_progress` statuses as 'failing' - group honestly as pending vs failing vs passing. (2) Read the PR's combined check set (both check-runs and commit statuses on the PR head) to match `gh pr checks`, and update `tools/field_battery.py` to compare against a settled PR and never treat `pending` as a failure." The measured bug was deploy #4's answer about pull request #1424: the owner asked *"What is failing on pull request 1424?"* and the answer said "2 CI runs are on the head commit and at least one did not finish successfully … 2 failing check(s): CI: pending Jarvis client: pending" while `gh pr checks 1424` showed both checks PENDING. Chosen: ONE helper, `_run_verdict`, splits workflow runs exactly as `_check_verdict` splits check runs - a completed run with `success`/`neutral`/`skipped` is fine, a completed run with anything else is FAILED, and a run that is not completed is PENDING (a queued or in-progress run has `conclusion: None`); `_run_split` feeds the failing headline (which now counts only failed runs and says "failed", never "did not finish successfully") and a separate still-going sentence, so a green-checks commit with runs still going says they are still going and a no-check-runs commit with only pending runs says "N CI run(s) are still going: names. Nothing is known about them yet - ask again when they finish." For the combined source, `_ci_result` makes the extra read after the plan's three (the plan is deliberately unchanged: its last step is the check-runs read the pull form is detected by) and `_ci_combined_checks` merges `/commits/{sha}/status` into the check list as check-run-shaped entries; a failed statuses read keeps the check-runs list and says it is check-runs only, because a failed read is not a claim that no status exists. **Rejected, and why:** adding the statuses read as a fourth planner step (it would change the plan's advertised shape and the `steps[-1]` detection); treating `conclusion: None` as red anywhere (the bug itself); calling a pending status or pending run "failing" to keep a simpler two-way split (the ruling names three groups, and "not finished" is not evidence of a failure); and treating an unreadable statuses answer as "no statuses" (a read failure is not an empty result - the same BLOCKED-is-never-a-pass rule the rest of the module follows). The battery side: `gh pr checks` exits 8 while checks are pending and `gh_json` rejected that, so the pending ground truth was thrown away - `_gh_checks` now accepts 0 and 8, reads `name,bucket,state`, the failing question requires a settled PR (gh `fail` and no `pending`), the running question requires pending without failed, and the answer checks match a count as its own number so the `1` in "#1400" cannot pass as a failing check count. Proved by `backend/test_github_ci_count.py` 52, `test_github_robustness.py` 514, `test_github_own_repo.py` 192, `test_github_tools.py` 1199 (after the twin sync), `test_github_parity.py` 710 and `backend/test_field_battery.py` (self-test 37/37); the twin module is byte-identical and the base suites/checkers are clean.

The ruling is that the finish path owns the lane's hygiene: **record the resident model+context before the proof suites, and put it back after them on every ending.** 	ools/update_backend.py reads the lane from GET /api/ps on OLLAMA_URL (loopback only - the update never reaches another machine's models), records it in the backend's own _jarvis-logs folder before the suites, and after them warms the recorded model at the recorded context when the suites left a different one; warming never names a model or context that was not read, and a context-less preload is specifically refused (it would reload the model at Ollama's small default, the measured 2026-10-10 2,048-token bug). One LANE: line says which happened (restored, left alone) or that the lane could not be read and nothing was restored. **The timeout ending is why the record is a file:** the desktop owns the run's bound and can kill the tool mid-suite, so after ANY ending the app runs the tool's own --restore-lane mode from that record; the tool's normal endings remove the record once the lane is back, a failed restore leaves it for that one retry, and the app always removes it afterwards so a stale record can never override a model the owner picks later.
